title: UPDATE: Asian Shares Mostly Higher; Techs Lead In Tokyo, Seoul
text:
(Adds information, quotes, updates/adds market levels)

By Shri Navaratnam and Ga-Woon Philip Vahn

Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES

SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--Asian stock markets were mostly higher Friday with technology plays leading gains in Tokyo and Seoul, while weakness in China's banking stocks dragged the Shanghai market lower.

Investors were encouraged by a third-straight session of gains on Wall Street on Thursday, as well an unexpected increase in U.S. pending-home sales. However, buying was tempered by caution ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for August due later Friday.

"U.S. economic data have been surprising, more than less, on the upside this week," said Philip Wee at DBS Group Research in Singapore. That could be because of "U.S. double-dip worries injecting more-than-usual bearishness into the consensus forecasts."

Japan's Nikkei Stock Average was up 0.4% while Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.2%, South Korea's Kospi Composite gained 0.1% and India's Sensex was 0.2% higher.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was flat, Taiwan's main index gained 1.1% and the Shanghai Composite index was down 0.2%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were two points lower in screen trade.

The Tokyo market was cheered by Wall Street's rise, with tech stocks outperforming after the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.1% Thursday.

However, the market's "gains may be limited since the yen's strength, which is our biggest concern, shows no signs of receding," said Kazuhiro Takahashi, general manager at Daiwa Securities Capital Markets. "We'd like to see how the dollar moves against the yen after U.S. jobs data later today," he said.

Elpida Memory rose 3.2%, Toshiba advanced 1.3% and Sony tacked on 1.7%. Automakers were also rising, with Toyota Motor up 1.4% and Nissan Motor 0.6% higher.

In Seoul, shares were supported by the positive sentiment in markets.

"The U.S. market has turned around from the short-term lows after the ISM (manufacturing) data Wednesday, so the domestic market's moving quickly in line as well," said Hyundai Securities analyst Bae Sung-young.

Tech stocks were broadly higher, aided by an easing of concerns about global growth prospects. LG Electronics rose 3.2%, Hynix Semiconductor added 2.8% and LG Display advanced 3.1%.

Shinhan Financial fell 2.0% on worries about the company's internal governance as the board took steps to remove President and Chief Executive Shin Sang-hoon from his posts.

Shinhan Bank, a unit of Shinhan Financial, said on Thursday it filed a complaint with prosecutors against Shin Sang-hoon and six others and accused them of breach of trust as well as embezzlement.

Banks were struggling in Shanghai after the China Securities Journal said, citing its own statistics, that four of China's five biggest banks reported increases in special-mention loans in the second quarter from the preceding quarter, offering fresh evidence of potentially high credit risk in the local banking system. Bank of China fell 0.6% and China Merchants Bank lost 0.8%.

Special-mention loans refer to loans that have a potential weakness or pose an unwarranted financial risk that, if not corrected, could weaken the asset and lead to higher risks.

China Vanke rose 0.9% after the company said its property sales in August more than doubled from a year earlier to CNY11.99 billion, a record monthly performance for a Chinese property developer.

The Sydney market was led higher by gains in materials, industrials and consumer staples.

Rio Tinto was up 0.4% and BHP Billiton rose 0.3%. Bank stocks were mostly lower, capping the market's gains. ANZ bank was off 0.7%, Westpac was off 1.0% and National Australia Bank fell 1.1%.

Nufarm fell 3.1% after Standard & Poor's placed the company's BB long-term corporate debt rating on negative credit watch, on concerns about liquidity and its ability to improve profitability in fiscal 2011.

In Hong Kong, Sino Land rose 2.3% after the blue-chip property developer said Thursday its net profit for the 12 months ended June 30 rose 63% to HK$6.09 billion, helped by revaluation gains in its investment properties.

Cement shares were leading gains in Thailand on hopes that construction activity will pick up after a Thai court Thursday allowed the resumption of almost all the projects at a controversial industrial estate, almost a year after they were suspended. Siam Cement rose 5.0%, Banpu gained 1.6% and PTT Chemical added 3.4%.

Elsewhere, Malaysian shares were down 0.5%, Singapore's Straits Times Index fell 0.1%, New Zealand's NZX-50 was up 0.6% and Indonesia's share market was 0.9% higher. Vietnam markets were shut for a public holiday.

In foreign exchange markets, the U.S. dollar traded in tight ranges against the euro and the yen as traders waited for the U.S. non-farm payrolls data.

The euro was at $1.2815, from $1.2821 late Thursday in New York, and at Y107.99 against the yen, from Y107.96. The dollar was fetching Y84.26, compared with Y84.21.

"With investors still on edge about the chance of a double-dip U.S. recession, we suspect any disappointment (on the U.S. jobs data) would scupper the recent bond market sell-off, providing headwinds for the U.S. dollar," said Mike Jones, currency strategist at the Bank of New Zealand.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore intervened in the foreign exchange market Friday after the Singapore dollar hit an all-time high against the greenback, a person familiar with the central bank's thinking said.

The person told Dow Jones Newswires that the MAS "went in to smooth the U.S. dollar's fall around S$1.3435."

The Singapore dollar hit a record high late Thursday, with the U.S. dollar sliding to S$1.3425. The previous record was S$1.3438 to the greenback in July 2008. The U.S. dollar last traded at S$1.3471.

Lead September Japanese government bond futures were down 0.01 at 142.20 points, weighed by the Nikkei's gains and Thursday's weakness in U.S. Treasurys. The 10-year cash JGB yield was 0.5 basis point lower at 1.105%.

Spot gold was at $1,249.50 per troy ounce, down $1.80 from late New York Thursday. October Nymex crude oil futures were down 26 cents at $74.76 per barrel on Globex.

title: UPDATE: MAS  Intervenes  After  Singapore  Dollar Hits Record High -Source
text:
(Adds quotes, background) 
 

SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--The Monetary Authority of Singapore intervened in the foreign exchange market Friday after the Singapore dollar hit an all-time high against the greenback, a person familiar with the central bank's thinking said.

The person said the MAS "went in to smooth the U.S. dollar's fall around S$1.3435."

The Singapore dollar overnight hit a record high, with the U.S. dollar sliding to S$1.3425. The previous record was S$1.3438 to the greenback in July 2008.

"They (MAS) will continue to smooth the U.S. dollar's fall for now, but this is a regional issue with widespread weakness for the U.S. currency," the person said.

At 0227 GMT the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.3460. It was the first time since April that MAS has intervened in the foreign exchange market.

The local dollar rose after better-than-expected U.S. housing and employment data overnight eased worries about the health of the global economy, sapping demand for safe assets such as the U.S. dollar and Treasurys.

"They (MAS) expect continued weakness in the U.S. dollar. The basket of currencies that the Singapore dollar trades with will likely go higher in the short term," the person said.

"If that happens the local dollar will further rise and the MAS' role will not be to intervene but to make sure that the rise is orderly."

The central bank uses the exchange rate rather than interest rates as its main policy tool because Singapore's trade flows dwarf the island's small domestic economy.

The MAS also views the Singapore dollar's rise as part of a trend among Asian currencies after China decoupled the yuan from the U.S. dollar in mid-June, the person said. Although the yuan has barely risen, the de-pegging by the People's Bank of China paved the way for other export-reliant Asian economies to let their own currencies gain further, the person said.

The MAS aggressively tightened policy in April by raising the trading band for the Singapore dollar and targeting a "modest and gradual appreciation" for the local dollar, changing its previous policy of zero appreciation.

title: UPDATE: Singapore Dollar Rises To New Record Vs US Dollar
text:
(Adds comments from trader, background on U.S. data)

By Gaurav Raghuvanshi

Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES

SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--The Singapore dollar rose to its highest level ever overnight after better-than-expected data from the U.S. helped ease economic fears and investors returned to assets linked to growth such as equities and currencies.

The U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.3457 at 2359 GMT Thursday, or Friday morning in Asia, after falling as low as S$1.3425 overnight. The previous record intraday low for the greenback was S$1.3438, touched on July 15, 2008.

A person close to the Monetary Authority of Singapore said Thursday that the central bank might intervene in the currency market should the greenback reach around S$1.3440.

Officials of the MAS weren't immediately available for comment on whether the central bank did intervene.

The latest bout of better-than-forecast U.S. housing and employment data have eased worries about the health of the economy, sapping demand for safe assets such as the U.S. dollar and government Treasurys. The market now awaits U.S. non-farm payrolls data due later in the day, which will have a strong impact on the U.S. dollar's performance.

"The Singapore dollar will continue to trade heavy because global risk appetite has improved. There may, however, be a bit of consolidation ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls data due tonight," said a trader at an international bank.

The U.S. dollar may find support near S$1.3440 and face resistance at S$1.3500, he said.

The National Association of Realtors Thursday said its index for pending sales of used homes increased 5.2% to 79.4 in July, surprising economists, who had tipped a decline. Initial jobless claims declined by 6,000 to 472,000 in the week ended Aug. 28.

The reports, along with Wednesday's upbeat manufacturing report out of the U.S. and China, provided relief for investors. Recent data had come in weaker than expected, raising fears of a double-dip recession and deflation.

-By Gaurav Raghuvanshi; Dow Jones Newswires; +65 64154 154; gaurav.raghuvanshi@dowjones.com [ 03-09-10 0020GMT ]

0132 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/HKD down on corporate demand (for local unit), says chief trader at local bank. Tips pair in 7.7700- 7.7780 band in near term. (chester.yung@dowjones.com)

0130 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore MAS intervenes in currency market after SGD rises to record high vs USD, source familiar with central bank's thinking says. MAS "went in to smooth the U.S. dollar's fall around S$1.3435," source says. Adds, MAS "will continue to smooth the U.S. dollar's fall for now, but this is a regional issue with widespread weakness for the U.S. currency." Intervention follows USD/SGD touching 1.3425 overnight (previous record low 1.3438 on July 15, 2008). Pair last 1.3465. (djn.bureau.singapore@dowjones.com)

0127 GMT [Dow Jones] Philippine shares likely to open lower on profit-taking following benchmark PSEi's 2% rise yesterday to 3666.54; market participants also expected to play safe ahead of long weekend in U.S. "But the decline will be limited, due mostly to improved liquidity...our recommendation is to trade within range," says Grace Cerdenia, 2TradeAsia.com research head. Adds profit taking may focus on financial, mining, property names that advanced substantially in recent sessions. Support tipped at 3640, resistance 3680. (rhea.sandique-carlos@dowjones.com)

0125 GMT [Dow Jones] Revision to Japan April-June GDP, due next Friday, may show economy grew at annualized 1.5% clip in quarter, much better than 0.4% rise in government's initial estimate, as MOF survey shows capital expenditure in better shape than expected, says Masamichi Adachi, economist at J.P.Morgan. Ping An (2318.HK) set to open lower on Newbridge Asia's stake disposal; Esprit (0330.HK) may face more post-results selling pressure, but Sino Land (0083.HK) likely to rise a tad on above-view FY results. HSI +1.2% at 20,868.92 yesterday, likely to extend gains today to test 21,000. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0119 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore stocks firmer, mirroring modest gains in other Asian bourses after Wall Street's overnight gains, with STI +0.3% at 2996.02. Technical indicators look healthy with momentum still climbing," says CIMB. Market breadth at 2 gainers for every decliner. Small caps most active, including Genting Hong Kong (S21.SG), +3.3% at US$0.315, United Fiber System (P30.SG), flat at S$0.05, Federal International (F20.SG), flat at S$0.15. Among STI components, notable gainers include CapitaMalls Asia (JS8.SG), +1.4% at S$2.20, Jardine Strategic (J37.SG), +1.2% at US$24.88, NOL (N03.SG), +1.0% at S$1.97. (frankie.ho@dowjones.com)

0119 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/THB lower at 31.13 vs 31.15 late yesterday as capital inflows continue. Court late yesterday ruled 74 of 76 halted projects at Map Ta Phut can go ahead; dealers say this may boost local stocks, THB. "The dollar/baht will likely test THB31.10 support, which is the lowest level hit since April 2008, as fund inflows continue" says Bangkok-based dealer. Foreigners net buyers of THB9.38 billion worth of Thai shares in past 5 sessions. Investors keeping eyes on U.S. employment report for August due later today. Support tipped at 31.05, resistance at 31.20. (oranan.paweewun@dowjones.com)

0113 GMT [Dow Jones] Strong USD/JPY bids from Japanese corporate customers stand at 84.00 which also low touched on EBS in late Asian trading yesterday, says Singapore-based dealer; adds strong selling interest at 84.60/70; but if 84.70 breaks, stops-driven buying may lift pair to 85.00. USD/JPY last 84.33. (jerry.tan@dowjones.com)

The correct version follows:) Korea treasury bonds, bond futures lower, tracking overnight losses in U.S. Treasurys. Daewoo Securities analyst Yoon Il-kwang expects yield curve to flatten until next week's BOK monetary policy meeting as rate hike expectations likely to continue weighing on shorter-end bonds, especially 1-year paper. Says, yield spreads between 1-year monetary stabilization bond and 5-year treasury note as well as spread between 1-year MSB, 10-year note may narrow, in particular. title: *DJ MAS To  Intervene  If  Singapore  Dollar Returns To Record High -Source
text:
2 Sep 2010 03:00 EDT *DJ  Singapore MAS 'On Intervention Watch' - Source

2 Sep 2010 03:00 EDT *DJ  Singapore Dollar Trading Around 2% Above MAS Band Midpoint -Source

2 Sep 2010 03:01 EDT *DJ  MAS To Tolerate Midterm Singapore Dollar Rise If Orderly, In Line With Region -Source

2 Sep 2010 03:01 EDT *DJ  MAS To Stand Pat In October 'Unless Things Change Dramatically' -Source

2 Sep 2010 03:07 EDT =DJ  Singapore MAS On 'Intervention Watch' But Ready For Stronger SGD -Source

SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--Singapore's central bank is poised to intervene in the currency market if the local dollar climbs back to around its record high, a person familiar with the situation said Thursday.

But the Monetary Authority of Singapore is prepared to let the currency rise against the U.S. dollar in the short to medium term if the move is orderly and in line with other Asian currencies, the person told Dow Jones Newswires.

The MAS is "on intervention watch," the person said.

This suggests intervention could be imminent for the MAS, which is thought to have stayed out of the market since April. The U.S. dollar was quoted at S$1.3485 around 0706 GMT, up from the day's low of from S$1.3454 but still close to its July 15, 2008, all-time low of S$1.3438.

The Singapore dollar, up 4% this year against the U.S. currency, has been rising along with peers like the Malaysian ringgit and the Indonesian rupiah, as Asia has rebounded strongly from the global economic crisis and the U.S. dollar has fallen on speculation the Federal Reserve will have to loosen policy further to bolster the world's biggest economy.

In recent days the Singapore dollar has been around 2% above the midpoint of the undisclosed trade-weighted band in which the MAS guides the currency, the person said. "Anything above that will trigger action."

The central bank uses the exchange rate rather than interest rates as its main policy tool because Singapore's trade flows dwarf the island's small domestic economy.

"If the basket of currencies we trade with moves higher against the U.S. dollar, it will be futile to fight the trend," the person said. "But any movement must be orderly. If it's not, the MAS will try to stop the volatility."

The MAS also views the Singapore dollar's rise as part of a trend among Asian currencies after China decoupled the yuan from the U.S. dollar in mid-June, the person said. Although the yuan has barely risen, the de-pegging by the People's Bank of China paved the way for other export-reliant Asian economies to let their own currencies gain further, the person said.

The MAS aggressively tightened policy in April by raising the trading band for the Singapore dollar and targeting a "modest and gradual appreciation" for the local dollar, changing its previous policy of zero appreciation.

The currency's recent rise is dispelling the idea of a further tightening at the next policy review, in October, said the person familiar with MAS thinking. The bank will stand pat "unless things change dramatically."

Singapore's economy grew a blistering 18.8% in the second quarter from a year earlier, accelerating from 16.9% in the first quarter and after contracting last year due to the global economic crisis. The government expects the economy to grow 13%-15% for the full year.

-By Singapore Bureau; Dow Jones Newswires; 65-6415-4150; djnews.singapore.bureau@dowjones.com

(END) Dow Jones Newswires

=UPDATE: NTUC FAIRPRICE, DAIRY FARM BID FOR CARREFOUR SINGAPORE, MALAYSIA ASSETS - SOURCE 

Singapore's NTUC FairPrice and Dairy Farm International Ltd. and Malaysian private equity group Navis Capital have placed bids for French retailer Carrefour SA's Singapore and Malaysia assets, a person familiar with the situation said Thursday. (published 0443 GMT)


 
=2ND UPDATE: BANPU UNIT SELLS 8.72% STAKE IN INDO TAMBANGRAYA FOR $395 MLN 

Banpu PCL, Thailand's largest coal miner by revenue, said Thursday that its wholly-owned unit has sold an 8.72% stake in Indonesian coal miner unit PT Indo Tambangraya Megah in a deal worth $395 million. (published 0609 GMT)


 
BANPU: RESUBMITTED CENTENNIAL BID TO AUSTRALIA'S FOREIGN REVIEW BOARD 

Banpu PCL, Thailand's largest coal miner by revenue, said Thursday it has resubmitted its application to Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board for the full takeover of Centennial Coal Co. . (published 0625 GMT)


 
=WSJ: FORD: 70% OF ITS GLOBAL GROWTH THIS DECADE TO COME FROM ASIA PACIFIC, AFRICA 

Ford Motor Co. expects 70% of its global growth this decade to come from Asia Pacific and Africa, a senior executive said Thursday. (published 0629 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: GENERAL MOTORS MULLS RESTARTING INDONESIA PLANT 

General Motors Co. is considering restarting a production plant in Indonesia with an investment of $150 million, and a decision is expected within the next 90 days, Tim Lee, GM's president for international operations, said Thursday. (published 0531 GMT)


 
=INTERVIEW: GM DAEWOO ON TRACK FOR TURNAROUND THIS YEAR 

GM Daewoo Auto & Technology Co., backed by new models, is on track to post a profit this year, reversing from the previous year's net loss, while being determined to achieving a double-digit percentage market share in the domestic market, the company's chief executive said late Tuesday. (published 0000 GMT)


 
FOSTERS CFO JUMPS SHIP TO PORT, RAIL OPERATOR ASCIANO 

Foster's Group Ltd. Chief Financial Officer Angus McKay has left the beverages group and taken up the same roll at port and rail operator Asciano Group, the two companies said Thursday. (published 0034 GMT)


 
NZ COMMERCE COMMISSION ALLEGES ANTI-COMPETITIVE CONDUCT BY FREIGHT COMPANIES 

The New Zealand Commerce Commission said Thursday that it has filed proceedings in the High Court at Auckland against a number of international freight forwarding companies on charges of colluding on surcharges and fees for air freight forwarding services to New Zealand. (published 0133 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: HARUM ENERGY SETS INDICATIVE IPO PRICE AT IDR5,000-IDR6,300/SHARE 

Coal producer PT Harum Energy has set an indicative price of between IDR5,000 and IDR6,300 per share for its planned sale of up to a 24% stake, or 650 million shares, through an initial public offering slated for later this month, an official at one of the underwriters told reporters Thursday. (published 0551 GMT)


 
GLOBE ASIATIQUE DEFERS IPO DUE TO WEAK GLOBAL MARKET 

Philippine property developer Globe Asiatique Realty Holdings Corp. has decided to indefinitely postpone an initial public offering it had planned to launch on Sept. 15, citing "weak global market conditions," the Philippine Stock Exchange said Thursday. (published 0229 GMT)


 
SAN MIGUEL: MAY INVEST $8 BLN FOR POWER PROJECTS 

Philippine conglomerate San Miguel Corp. said Thursday that its power unit, San Miguel Energy Corp., may invest as much as $8 billion in a project that will integrate a liquefied natural gas facility with power plants. (published 0339 GMT)


 
=WSJ: BAIDU LAUNCHES APPLICATION PLATFORM 

Baidu Inc. has launched an application platform through which developers can distribute applications through a browser, Baidu Chief Executive Robin Li said Thursday at the company's 2010 Technology Innovation Conference. (published 0431 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: NZ COMMERCE COMMISSION: ALLEGES ANTI-COMPETITIVE CONDUCT BY FREIGHT COMPANIES 

The New Zealand Commerce Commission said Thursday that it has filed proceedings in the High Court at Auckland against a number of international freight forwarding companies on charges of colluding on surcharges and fees for air freight forwarding services to New Zealand. (published 0344 GMT)


 
FONTERRA APPOINTS ADVISERS FOR NEXT STEPS IN CAPITAL STRUCTURE CHANGES 

Fonterra Co-Operative Group Ltd. said Thursday that it has appointed advisers for the next step in its capital structure changes, adding that a new trading system that will allow farmers to buy and sell Fonterra shares among themselves will begin in late 2011 at the earliest. (published 0354 GMT)


 
=CINEMAX CHAIRMAN: LOOKING TO SELL NAGPUR MALL PROPERTY FOR INR750M-INR850M 

[ 02-09-10 0713GMT ]

Cinemax India Ltd. is looking to sell its Nagpur mall project for INR750 million-INR850 million and will use the proceeds to repay high-cost debt and for expansion. (published 0419 GMT)


 
DELTA AIR LINES PRESIDENT: STRONG YEN BOOSTING PASSENGER DEMAND 

The president of Delta Air Lines Inc. Ed Bastian said Thursday that the strong yen is helping to boost passenger demand from Japan. (published 0501 GMT)


 
ELPIDA: HAVE DEVELOPED 4-GIGABIT NAND FLASH MEMORY WITH SPANSION 

Elpida Memory Inc. said Thursday that it and Spansion Inc. have developed a new flash memory chip with a simpler cell structure than existing ones, and plans to start mass production next year at its western Japan plant. (published 0503 GMT)


 
ESPRIT LAST FISCAL YEAR NET PROFIT FALLS 11% TO HK$4.23 BLN 

Fashion retailer Esprit Holdings Ltd. said Thursday its net profit for the 12 months ended June 30 fell 11% on weak wholesale business and continued economic weakness in Europe, which accounts for the majority of its revenue. (published 0517 GMT)


 
SINOSTEEL DENIES REPORT AUDIT FOUND POOR FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT 

State-owned Sinosteel Corp. said Thursday a local media report that an investigation by China's National Audit Office found the company made risky investments and had large debt because of poor financial management was incorrect, and that it hasn't received such an assessment from any organization or government department. (published 0438 GMT)


 
METCASH SAYS CONDITIONS REMAIN DIFFICULT; RETAINS EPS GROWTH GUIDANCE 

Metcash Ltd. said Thursday trading conditions remain difficult but it maintained its guidance for earnings per share growth in the current fiscal year ending April 30, 2011. (published 0440 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: ASIAN SHARES HIGHER; FINANCIALS UP IN CHINA, TECHS LIFT TOKYO 

Asian stock markets were higher Thursday as stronger-than-expected U.S. manufacturing data renewed optimism about the global economic recovery. In China, financial stocks were driving the market higher on merger activity, while tech plays and automakers were strong in Japan. (published 0410 GMT)

ENERGY/COMMODITIES:


=UPDATE: WESTERN AUSTRALIA STARTS BROWSE LNG LAND ACQUISITION PROCESS 

Western Australia state said Thursday that it has commenced a compulsory acquisition process for land planned to accommodate the massive Browse liquefied natural gas project. (published 0230 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: RIO TINTO SAYS 4Q IRON ORE PRICE TO FALL 13.3% FROM 3Q 

Rio Tinto Ltd. said Thursday that it expects fourth quarter iron ore prices to fall around 13.3% from the third quarter of 2010 to more "sustainable" levels after several price hikes. (published 0508 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: CNPC: PETROCHINA COMPLETES WORK ON FIRST LNG TERMINAL 

PetroChina Co. has completed construction of its first liquefied natural gas terminal, located in northeastern China's Dalian city, parent company China National Petroleum Corp. said Thursday. (published 0544 GMT)


 
INDIA AUG 26-SEP 1 MONSOON RAINS LIKELY 16% ABOVE AVERAGE - OFFICIAL 

Monsoon rains in India were likely 16% above average during the Aug. 26-Sep. 1 period, a senior official with the India Meteorological Department said Thursday. (published 0617 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: WHOLE-MILK POWDER PRICES JUMP 19% IN SEPTEMBER AUCTION 

Fonterra Co-Operative Group Ltd. said its Internet-based auction for early September saw average whole-milk powder prices jump 18.8% after falling since May, something economists said will increase the chances the dairy giant meets its forecast milk payout for the 2010-2011 production season, pumping billions of dollars into the New Zealand economy. (published 2339 GMT Wednesday) [ 02-09-10 0713GMT ]

title: MARKET TALK: JGBs Likely To Fall If Tokyo  Intervenes  - Analyst
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0057 GMT [Dow Jones] JGBs likely to face downward pressure if Tokyo decides to intervene in FX market to push down JPY, because action would reverse recent downtrend in USD/JPY, Tokyo shares, and because that may increase oversupply concerns as government will need to issue more discount bills to fund any foreign-currency buying operations, says Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities strategist Katsutoshi Inadome; brokerage expects government to directly step into FX market, only if a USD/JPY breach below 80 becomes possible (pair last around 84.52). Lead September JGB futures currently +0.24 at 142.69. (megumi.fujikawa@dowjones.com)

0048 GMT [Dow Jones] S&P/ASX 200 down 0.7% at 4421.7 after hitting 4413.7 amid broad-based retreat following 1.5% decline in the S&P 500, as U.S. economic data continued to disappoint. Australian equities market is showing signs of nervousness, with cyclicals generally weak and defensives outperforming. Banks are down 0.4%-1.6% and Macquarie (MQG.AU) is down 1.2%, while in resources, BHP (BHP.AU) is down 1.6% and Rio Tinto (RIO.AU) is down 1.4%. Among defensives Wesfarmers (WES.AU) up 0.5%, CSL (CSL.AU) up 0.5% and Foster's (FGL.AU) up 0.5%. But S&P/ASX 200 looks to be finding support below the 50-day moving average at 4427 and may regain this level if domestic funds support the market before month end. "Our market looks pretty good," says UBS Head of Sales George Kanaan. "The reporting season was reasonably good. It's just this volatile U.S. market that is pushing us around but it was very thin overnight. I don't expect Asian markets to go too badly today." Expects optimism to return if Wednesday's China PMI and U.S. ISM data show signs of improvement. (david.rogers1@dowjones.com)

0044 GMT [Dow Jones] Kospi off 0.6% at 1749.09, weighed by continued worries about global economic growth that pushed U.S. markets lower. Hyundai Securities analyst Bae Sung-young says market likely supported around 1742 levels for day, to trade in 1710-1770 band for week; "The Bernanke factor wore off in the U.S. after a day, and generally the economic data coming out this week, including U.S. August non-farm payrolls report and ISM manufacturing report, won't look very good. Unless there are definitive new measures to support growth the market's going to remain weak." Notes banks, which posted sharp gains Monday, and tech plays considered vulnerable to weaker 2H10 global growth. KB Financial (105560.SE) off 1.9% at KRW48,550, Woori Finance (053000.SE) 1.8% lower at KRW13,500. Hynix (000660.SE) off 2.9% at KRW21,800. (vincent.lee@dowjones.com)

0042 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/KRW rising towards psychological 1,200 in early trade as concerns over pace of global economic recovery continue to weigh on risk-sensitive currencies like KRW, EUR, traders say. If pair rises to as high as that level, "it would be the fourth time (this month) that exporters deal with KRW1,200 level," says local bank trader. Adds, it's going to be interesting to see whether pair could test 1,200 resistance successfully today but this unlikely scenario if exporters sell as actively as they had been doing in previous occasions. Tips pair in 1,193-1,206 range for rest of session. Players also keeping close eye on USD/JPY as stronger JPY tends to push JPY/KRW higher. USD/KRW last at 1,197.7 vs 1,192.0 late yesterday in Seoul amid Kospi's 0.6% loss. (min-jeong.lee@dowjones.com)

0042 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/TWD likely to rise in 32.050-32.100 band vs 32.060 yesterday, boosted by expected losses in local equities, gains in USD/KRW, but gains will likely be limited due to exporters' month-end TWD settlement demand, says local bank trader. Adds, "the central bank may lift the pair higher in late session" to help island's exporters; would be continuation of suspected pattern of intervention over most of month. (mason.wu@dowjones.com)

0039 GMT [Dow Jones] China shares set to consolidate but biased down following Wall Street's fall overnight amid ongoing worries about sustainability of global economic recovery. Shanghai Composite Index support tipped at 2600 after ending +1.6% at 2652.66 yesterday. "The banks' recent string of fundraising efforts put pressure on the (banking) sector, and since the sector has a big weighting, its weakness will hurt the broader market," says Qian Qimin at Shenyin Wanguo Securities. Xinjiang-based companies may be in spotlight today after China's top securities regulator Shang Fulin reiterated Monday that Beijing will continue to support companies in region to raise capital. Shenzhen index +2.6% at 1158.22. (jean.yung@dowjones.com)

0039 GMT [Dow Jones] Home sale transactions in Singapore likely to fall 30% over next 3-6 months, with some moderation in prices for mass-market projects, following latest government measures to rein in housing market, says Goldman Sachs. Cites doubling of minimum cash payment to 10%, which applies to home owners with outstanding housing loans seeking another property, as probably strongest deterrant. Says restrictions on public housing flats - such as increasing minimum occupation period before owners can sell, requiring private home owners buying resale public housing flats to sell private home - will indirectly affect demand from upgraders for mass-market private housing; "we see the measures casting a shadow on near-term property sales." Rates Keppel Land (K17.SG), UOL (U14.SG), Allgreen (A16.SG), Wing Tai (W05.SG) at Neutral with respective targets of S$3.92, S$4.18, S$1.33, S$1.93. (frankie.ho@dowjones.com)

0035 GMT [Dow Jones] Nikkei down 2.0% at 8963.36 after BOJ's new easing measures fail to curb yen's rise; sentiment also hit by drops in U.S. stocks overnight on worries about U.S. economy; USD/JPY trading below 85, hurting exporters. "Japan is giving investors the impression that it's running out of options to counter market weakness," says Kenichi Hirano, strategist at Tachibana Securities. Adds Nikkei likely to be supported at 8850 today; if USD/JPY (now 84.55) trades below 84.50, losses may widen. Tokyo Electron (8035.TO) off 4.2% at Y4,005, Advantest (6857.TO) off 3.0% at Y1,633, Canon (7751.TO) off 2.9% at Y3,480. ANA (9202.TO) bucking weakness, up 0.6% at Y310 on Deutsche Securities' rating hike to Buy. (ayai.tomisawa@dowjones.com)

0035 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore government bond yields likely down 2-3 bps tracking overnight moves in U.S. Treasurys after global risk appetite wanes. "The positive sentiment lasted just a day and a second read of the U.S. Fed and Bank of Japan statements has only reinforced fears of deepening trouble for the world economy. The flight to safety theme is back," trader at international bank says. Adds bonds at longer end likely to rise more today. Yesterday, 2-year Singapore government bond yield down 1 bp at 0.46%, 10-year also down 1 bp at 2.06%. (gaurav.raghuvanshi@dowjones.com)

0034 GMT [Dow Jones] New Zealand residential building consents excluding apartments, down 5.3% on month in July, weaker than forecast, says ANZ economist Mark Smith; "we expect that residential investment activity will recover, but for this to be pushed back into 2011." Adds, had thought October 1 increase in GST to 15% from 12.5% would encourage some residential work to be brought forward, but "there is very little evidence of this in the consent data so far." Says higher costs of purchasing new dwelling, large supply of existing dwellings on market, ongoing household develeraging, low income growth, moderating trend for net immigration are playing more influential role in constraining residential building activity than previously thought. (lucy.craymer@dowjones.com)

0032 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/SGD higher in Asia after overnight data show U.S. personal incomes rising at slower rate than expected, yesterday's BOJ move to stem JPY rise falls flat. "The markets are once again worried about the faltering global economic recovery, which is fueling risk aversion," says trader at local bank. Expects resistance at 1.3630, support 1.3510. Pair last 1.3561. (gaurav.raghuvanshi@dowjones.com)

0028 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan shares likely to fall in 7650-7700 band, after edging up 0.2% to 7741.20 yesterday, weighed by losses in Asian, U.S. shares, says KGI Securities trader Randy Chang. Adds losses likely led by tech stocks after Hon Hai's (2317.TW) disappointing 1H results, Intel's warning of weak sales in current quarter. Still, "The downside for Taiex is limited as insurers and government funds may buy around 7650," he says. Hon Hai says Monday its 1H net profit +22% on-year, but based on its 1Q net profit of NT$17.99 billion, its 2Q net profit down 6.9% on-quarter at NT$16.75 billion. Company didn't disclose its 2Q net profit.(mason.wu@dowjones.com) [ 08-30-10 2057ET ]

title: MARKET TALK:MAS Won't  Intervene  On SGD At Current Level-Source
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0614 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore MAS comfortable with recent rise in local dollar vs U.S. dollar, won't intervene near current USD/SGD levels, source familiar with central bank thinking says. Also, MAS likely to stand pat at next policy review in October. "The rise hasn't been dramatic and at current levels the Singapore dollar is competitive for our exports," source says, adds, MAS likely won't intervene unless USD/SGD falls "clearly and sustainably closer to S$1.34." Pair last 1.3629 vs 1.3625 Friday close. (costas.paris@dowjones.com)

0609 GMT [Dow Jones] Rallying Aussie bonds defying fundamental analysis, RBA still in hiking bias, says Annette Beacher, senior strategist with TD Securities. "Everyone is just standing back at the moment even as the levels for 3s and 10s is just too low. And there really isn't much until GDP early next month, which might be the chance for the market to get back in," says Beacher. Aussie 3-year up 5 ticks at 95.44, 10-year up 7 ticks at 95.025. (geoffrey.rogow@dowjones.com)

0605 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan shares end higher, led by gains in tourism, airlines, textile firms; Taiex +0.6% at 7941.22; may test 8000 tomorrow; "Taiwan shares are relatively strong compared with Japan and Korea partly because of strength in China shares," says Andrew Teng, assistant vice president at Taiwan International Securities; adds, relatively lackluster performance of index-heavyweights, such as semiconductor makers, financial firms, as well as lower trading volume (NT$119.43 billion vs NT$131.45 billion Friday) indicates sentiment not very strong. Tourism, airlines rise on hopes of more Chinese tourists visiting island. Formosa International Hotels (2707.TW) +7% by daily trading limit at NT$506. EVA Airways also +7% at NT$24.55. Textile strong on hopes for strong demand in 3Q. Carnival Industrial (1417.TW) +7% at NT$12.30. Taiwan shares tipped to consolidate in 7900-8050 range near term. (joy.shaw@dowjones.com)

0559 GMT [Dow Jones] Kospi off 0.1% at 1743.91, erasing most of its earlier losses, tracking strong Chinese stocks on top of eased program selling pressure due to foreign, domestic institutional buying in futures, analysts say. "Amid a lack of fresh momentum recently, investor sentiment and supply-demand conditions are having a greater impact on the market," says NH Investment & Securities' Kim Hyoung-ryoul; tips Kospi in 1720-1760 range at least until U.S. economic data later in week, such as leading indicators, Philadelphia Fed business survey Thursday. Some tech shares recovering from earlier drops, with Hynix (000660.SE) +1.9% at KRW22,020 while LG Electronics (066570.SE) +1.0 at KRW103,500, but financial stocks mostly down on strong program selling, analysts say. KB Financial (105560.SE) down 1.7% at KRW47,900 while Woori Finance (053000.SE) down 2.5% at KRW13,550. (jung-ah.lee@dowjones.com)

0552 GMT [Dow Jones] Benchmark 10-year JGB yield falls to fresh 7-year low as speculation lingers that BOJ may take additional easing steps in near term as concerns grow that Japan's economy may be losing momentum, says trader at Tokyo securities house. After release of weaker-than-expected GDP data earlier in day, "many investors have started to expect that the BOJ could be forced to do something to curb the stronger yen and prop up the economy. Demand for JGBs will likely remain solid for a while." 10-year JGB yield now down 3.5 bps at 0.945%. Lead September JGB futures up 0.29 at 142.68 points. (tomoyuki.tachikawa@dowjones.com)

0549 GMT [Dow Jones] Thai shares down 0.1% at 861.13 at midday break in moderate trade, off intra-session trough at 857.51, with tad down after losses on regional markets, Wall Street while local market closed for holidays Thursday, Friday. Optimism over upcoming Thai 2Q GDP data, companies' dividend payments helps limit downside, says analyst with Far East Securities Weerachai Krongsamsri. "The market's correction will be short-lived," he adds. Thailand's 2Q GDP due Aug. 23. Support tipped at 855, resistance at 865. Among most active, Charoen Pokphand Foods (CPF.TH) +2.2% at THB25.25, Kasikornbank (KBANK.TH) off 2.9% at THB99.50, True Corp. (TRUE.TH) +1.6% at THB6.25, PTT +1.2% at THB253, Bangkok Bank (BBL.TH) off 1.8% at THB134.50. (oranan.paweewun@dowjones.com)

0548 GMT [Dow Jones] The EUR/CHF rate will play a key role in the timing of the next Swiss National Bank interest-rate increase, according to Credit Suisse. "Amid the still very volatile environment, the SNB will likely strive to avoid any additional pressure on the currency pair resulting from narrowing of the interest-rate differential to the euro zone," says economist Fabian Heller. "However, if the economic outlook and market environment proves to be robust in coming months and confidence in the euro returns, an interest-rate hike by the SNB ahead of the European Central Bank remains plausible," he adds. Libor futures contracts show markets don't expect a 25-basis-point increase until the end of 2011, he says. EUR/CHF at 1.3430. (neil.maclucas@dowjones.com)

0547 GMT [Dow Jones] HK short-selling volume +69.5% at HK$2.526 billion, 7.7% of market total, vs 4.8% Friday's midday, suggests HSI's 0.2% rise midday likely a technical correction after index's 4-session 3.3% decline. Sun Hung Kai Properties (0016.HK) tops list with HK$297.41 million after government's fresh measures to curb property prices, while Hutchison Whampoa (0013.HK) in 2nd place with HK$210.43 million. Agricultural Bank of China (1288.HK), HKEx (0388.HK), Sino Land (0083.HK) round off top 5 with HK$133.90 million, HK$122.75 million, HK$119.08 million, respectively. (susanna.tai@dowjones.com)

0542 GMT [Dow Jones] Nikkei 225 September futures down 1.1% at 9170, but well off intraday low of 9080, on slower-than-expected growth in April-June GDP. "Futures have been oversold so dragging them down further entails risk," says Hideki Horikawa, chief analyst at Himawari Securities. Notes technical signals suggest futures index due for rebound to 9300-9400 by end of this week after shedding 4.1% last week. Adds investors also closely watching whether Prime Minister Naoto Kan will hold meeting with BOJ Gov. Masaaki Shirakawa to exchange views on yen's recent rise. (kana.inagaki@dowjones.com)

0538 GMT [Dow Jones] S&P/ASX 200 down 0.3% at 4448.1, continues to recover in late trading. "I think results in Australia and fundamentals in Asia are pretty good," says UBS Head of Sales, George Kanaan. "Outlook statements have been a bit subdued, but results generally aren't missing expectations and you've got underlying dividend support." Notes that companies tied to Asia, such as Leighton (LEI.AU), are performing well. "I think the market has got a good floor at the moment and unless we get a blip down overseas, the market looks pretty relaxed." Continues to expect S&P/ASX 200 to rise to 5000 by year end. (david.rogers1@dowjones.com)

0535 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/KRW continues to trim earlier gains, falling back below 1,190 level as Kospi pares much of earlier losses in afternoon (now off 0.2% vs down 0.8% earlier), triggering bout of stop-loss sell orders on USD. Pair now up at 1,187.4 vs 1,195.2 around noon, 1,183.8 late Friday in Seoul. USD/KRW likely peaked at 1,200.3 for today, trader says. Local bank trader puts support at 1,185. Another local bank trader says, "I'm not sure of which direction to bet on from here," given such volatile trading patterns so far today. Adds, offshore players now quiet after some aggressive buying in morning trade. (min-jeong.lee@dowjones.com)

0532 GMT [Dow Jones] Sliding AUD/USD is going to keep running lower, says Callum Henderson, head of FX strategy for Standard Chartered in Singapore. AUD/USD recently at 0.8922, down from 0.9021 late Friday as economic jitters across globe have traders flooding to safety. "From our perspective, there is more to go in this pullback. The previous pullback went from 0.93 to 0.80," says Henderson, adding that on fundamental level, backdrop of slowing global economy, slowing China, will weigh heavily. Still, Henderson tips support at 0.8840 as particularly robust along way down. (geoffrey.rogow@dowjones.com) [ 08-16-10 0214ET ]

title: Dow Jones Asia-Pacific Top Stories Sked For August 16
text:
Following are the top Asia-Pacific stories featured on Dow Jones Newswires as of 0700 GMT. Not all stories appear on all wires. Please direct any questions or comments to asianewseds@dowjones.com.

MACRO/FOREX/FIXED INCOME:


 
=2ND UPDATE: JAPAN GDP GROWTH SLOWS AS CONSUMPTION, EXPORT GAINS SLACKEN 

Japan's economic growth slowed sharply in the second quarter, falling well short of expectations as stagnant consumption and flagging exports weighed on an economy already hobbled by deflation and a soaring yen. (published 0357 GMT)


 
=DATA SNAP: INDIA WHOLESALE PRICE INDEX UP 9.97% ON YEAR IN JULY 

India's wholesale inflation decelerated to 9.97% in July from 10.55% in June, the government said Monday. (published 0615 GMT)


 
=2ND UPDATE: AUSTRALIA LABOR FOCUS ON ECONOMY, HEALTH AT CAMPAIGN LAUNCH 

Australia's Prime Minister Julia Gillard on Monday kicked off her center-left Labor government's official pitch for a second term in office with a focus on the economy and health care, attempting to carve both out as areas where Labor has the upper hand. (published 0641 GMT)

SINGAPORE MAS WON'T INTERVENE IN SINGAPORE DOLLAR AT CURRENT LEVELS-SOURCE 

Singapore's central bank is comfortable with the local dollar's recent rise and won't intervene near current levels against the U.S. dollar, a person familiar with the central bank's thinking said Monday. (published 0539 GMT)


 
S KOREA JULY IMPORT PRICES DOWN 0.5% ON MONTH; FIRST FALL IN 6 MONTHS 

South Korea's import prices declined in July from the previous month due to a fall in prices of Dubai crude oil and other raw materials, easing inflationary pressures on the economy. (published 0300 GMT)


 
PHILIPPINES' MEDIUM-TERM PLAN DOESN'T ENVISAGE BALANCED BUDGET 

The administration of President Benigno Aquino III isn't looking to balance the budget during its six-year term, but will keep the deficit at a manageable 2% of gross domestic product, the latest medium-term fiscal program of the government showed Monday. (published 0542 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: AUSTRALIA'S BANK OF QUEENSLAND TO OFFER A$750M IN RMBS 

Australia's Bank of Queensland Ltd. plans to offer A$750 million in residential mortgage-backed securities, with pricing guidance on the top tranche much improved from earlier this year. (published 2350 GMT)


 
=PREVIEW: MALAYSIA 2Q GDP LIKELY SLOWED TO 8.4% ON YEAR - POLL 

Malaysia's trade-driven economy likely moderated in the second quarter from the first, in tandem with slower exports, economists said. (published 0242 GMT)


 
=PREVIEW: HK MAY-JULY UNEMPLOYMENT RATE LIKELY STEADY AT 4.6% 

Hong Kong's unemployment rate likely held steady in the three months ended July 31 as a larger work force, boosted by school-leavers entering the job market, offset the increase in the number of new jobs. (published 0226 GMT)

EQUITIES:


 
=UPDATE: CANADA'S AGRIUM BIDS A$1.50/SHARE FOR AUSTRALIA'S AWB 

Australian agribusiness AWB Ltd. said Monday it has received a conditional takeover bid from Canadian fertilizer supplier Agrium Inc. pitched at A$1.50 cash a share, valuing the company at A$1.24 billion, even as AWB continues to implement a share-based merger agreement with GrainCorp Ltd. (published 0233 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: SIGMA TO SELL PHARMACEUTICAL DIVISION TO ASPEN FOR A$900M 

Sigma Pharmaceuticals Ltd. on Monday announced a surprise deal to sell its pharmaceutical division to South Africa's Aspen Pharmacare Holdings Ltd. for A$900 million. (published 0357 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: URUGUAY'S UNION AGRICULTURE GROUP MAKES BID FOR NZ FARMING SYSTEMS URUGUAY 

Uruguay's Union Agriculture Group said Monday it plans to make a full takeover offer for NZ Farming Systems Uruguay Ltd. for NZ$0.60 per share, beating the NZ$0.55 full takeover offer that Singapore-based Olam International made last month. (published 0349 GMT)


 
COSCO INTERNATIONAL: MAY SELL ENTIRE STAKE IN SINO-OCEAN LAND 

Cosco International Holdings Ltd. said Monday it may sell its entire 16.85% stake in Sino-Ocean Land Holdings Ltd., as part of the company's divestment of non-core investments. (published 0500 GMT)


 
CHINA ATTACHES CONDITIONS TO NOVARTIS' ACQUISITION OF ALCON 

China's Ministry of Commerce on Friday approved Novartis AG's acquisition of Alcon Inc., but attached conditions to the deal in the China market. (published 0451 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: GOODMAN TO ACQUIRE MOORABBIN AIRPORT FOR A$201.5M 

Commercial property investor Goodman Group said Monday it plans to buy Moorabbin airport and business park in Melbourne for A$201.5 million. (published 0542 GMT)


 
=2ND UPDATE: GUNNS TO SELL TAMAR RIDGE; EXPECTS FY10 NET A$28M 

Australian forestry company Gunns Ltd. said Monday it would sell its Tamar Ridge wine unit for A$32.5 million, while also announcing an unaudited net profit for fiscal 2009-10 of A$28.0 million ahead of what one brokerage said could be a messy formal full year result scheduled for Wednesday. (published 0337 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: KB FINANCIAL: OVERSEAS EXPANSION THROUGH M&A POSSIBLE 

South Korea's KB Financial Group Inc. said Monday it may consider mergers or acquisitions to expand in overseas markets such as Singapore and the U.S. as the lender searches for new growth engines beyond the highly competitive domestic market. (published 0129 GMT)


 
SAN MIGUEL TAKES CONTROL OF LOCAL FIRM BELL TELECOMMUNICATION 

Philippine conglomerate San Miguel Corp. said Monday its wholly-owned unit, Vega Telecom Inc., has taken control of Bell Telecommunication Philippines Inc. through its acquisition of new shares in three local firms that together own 100% of the local telecom services provider. (published 0158 GMT)


 
CLP 1ST-HALF NET PROFIT RISES 83% TO HK$5.92 BLN 

CLP Holdings Ltd. said Monday its first-half net profit rose 83% from year earlier, partly due to higher contributions from its energy business in Australia. (published 0452 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: NEWCREST FY NET PROFIT DOUBLES ON SALES, COSTS, PRICE 

Newcrest Mining Ltd. said Thursday that net profit for the year ended June 30 more than doubled to A$556.9 million, from A$248.1 million a year earlier. (published 0248 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: LEND LEASE SWINGS TO A$345.6M FY PROFIT; OPERATING RESULT BEATS GUIDANCE 

Lend Lease Group, Australia's largest property developer, on Monday swung to a full-year net profit of A$345.6 million, owing to an absence of the near A$1 billion worth of asset writedowns that marred its previous result. (published 0651 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: CENTENNIAL COAL NET PROFITS DOWN 28% TO A$51.5M ON FOREX, VOLUMES 

Centennial Coal Co. Ltd. said Monday that full-year net profit fell 28% from a year earlier as a strengthening Australian dollar put pressure on export prices. (published 0251 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: BLUESCOPE STEEL FY NET PROFIT A$126M, RESUMES DIVIDENDS 

Australia's largest steelmaker BlueScope Steel Ltd. said Monday it has returned to profitability with full year earnings of A$126 million and resumed dividend payments but warned that short-term conditions remain tough. (published 0548 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: FREIGHTWAYS FY10 NET DOWN 33% BUT 2H SHOWED IMPROVEMENT 

Courier and freight company Freightways Ltd. on Monday said its full-year profit fell 33% but pointed to better performance in the second half as it begins to benefit from New Zealand's gradual economic recovery. (published 0010 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: PYNE GOULD CORP SAYS FY NET PROFIT TO BE 5% HIGHER THAN FORECAST 

Financial-services company Pyne Gould Corp. Monday said its fully year net profit would be around 5% higher than forecast after net operating income strengthened. (published 0320 GMT)


 
UNITECH 1Q CONSOLIDATED NET PROFIT UP 14% AT INR1.80 BLN 

Real estate developer Unitech Ltd. posted a 14% rise in its fiscal first quarter consolidated net profit, helped by higher sales and drop in interest costs. (published 0330 GMT)


 
ALINTA ENERGY EXPECTS A$465M IMPAIRMENT CHARGE IN 2H10 

Debt-laden power generator Alinta Energy Ltd. said Monday that it expects to book a A$465 million non-cash impairment charge in the second half of last financial year. (published 0532 GMT)


 
AIRPORTS OF THAILAND SWINGS TO 3Q NET LOSS OF THB516.2 MLN 

Airports of Thailand PCL said Monday that it swung to a net loss in the third quarter because of foreign exchange losses. (published 0610 GMT)


 
=UPDATE: ASIAN SHARES MOSTLY LOWER; SOFT JAPAN DATA HIT SENTIMENT 

Asian stock markets were mostly lower Monday with weaker-than-expected economic growth from Japan weighing on sentiment across the region, though gains in Chinese shares were helping to stem the losses. (published 0411 GMT)

ENERGY/COMMODITIES:


KODECO HALTS 1 RIG'S PRODUCTION AFTER COLLISION -INDONESIAN OFFICIAL 

Kodeco Energy Ltd. has shut down one of its 14 oil and gas production rigs in a block offshore of East Java after its rig was hit by a container ship last week. (published 0234 GMT)


 
=2ND UPDATE: WOODSIDE STRIKES GAS FOR PLUTO LNG EXPANSION 

Woodside Petroleum Ltd. said Monday that it has found more gas offshore Western Australia state, potentially putting an expansion of its A$13 billion Pluto liquefied natural gas project back on track. (published 0444 GMT)

SINOPEC ENCOUNTERS RECORD GAS FLOW AT NORTHEAST SICHUAN WELL 

China Petroleum & Chemical Corp. has encountered a high flow of natural gas at a well it drilled in Yuanba in gas-rich Sichuan province's northeast, with a record daily output of 1.26 million cubic meters, parent Sinopec Group said in its in-house newsletter Monday. (published 0420 GMT)


 
JAPAN MISSION TO VISIT VIETNAM TO PITCH NUCLEAR POWER TECHNOLOGY 

[ 16-08-10 0706GMT ]

High-level government and industry officials from Japan plan to visit Vietnam possibly later this month to sell nuclear power plants to the Southeast Asian country for the second phase of its atomic power project, a Japanese government official said Monday. (published 0322 GMT)


 
AUSTRALIA'S MACQUARIE TO LAUNCH CROP FUND 

A unit of Australia's Macquarie Group Ltd. on Monday launched a new crop fund aimed at investors looking to increase exposure to the production of grains and oilseeds. (published 0126 GMT)


 
PHILIPPINES FORECASTS 2H FARM OUTPUT TO EXPAND 3.8% ON YEAR 

Philippine farm production in the second half of the year is expected to expand 3.8% from the same period a year earlier, allowing the sector--which accounts for one-fifth of gross domestic product--to at least "break even" for the year, the Department of Agriculture's chief statistician said Monday. (published 0420 GMT) [ 16-08-10 0706GMT ]

title: MARKET TALK: Japan's MOF Unlikely To  Intervene  In  FX  Mkts-Citi
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0520 GMT [Dow Jones] Japan's ministry of finance unlikely to intervene in FX markets, says Citigroup, even though government appears to have heightened vigilance on JPY strength. Notes 2 psychological hurdles - "First, they probably think that other industrialized counties, especially the U.S., are seeking weaker currencies in order to support their economies and prevent deflation and that the currency intervention might be problematic in this context." Also, MoF likely believes currency intervention is difficult when international community is pushing China to increase CNY flexibility. (colin.ng@dowjones.com)

0518 GMT [Dow Jones] Standard Chartered expects benchmark 3-month Hibor to stay low near 0.30% from now until 2012 as it expects first U.S. Fed hike to come only in 2Q 2012 amid uncertain U.S. economic recovery. "We believe that the Hong Kong (and China) recovery story will remain fundamentally compelling to global investors," which will help to lure inflows, keeping interbank liquidity ample, report says. Expects Hibors to start climbing only in early 2012. 3-month Hibor steady at 0.28%.(chester.yung@dowjones.com)

0513 GMT [Dow Jones] India interbank call rate higher as banks cover cash requirements for weekend, but rate may turn lower as most lenders have already covered positions on account of reporting Friday, says trader with state-run bank. Banks have to report cash reserve levels to RBI at end of every fortnight. Overnight call rate at 5.76% vs 5.25% last close. Collateralized lending and borrowing obligation, or CBLO, rate slips to 4.61% vs 5.00% at open, banks avoid borrowing from CBLO window as they have to pledge bonds as collateral. "The RBI has made available two liquidity adjustment facility windows on reporting Fridays, when cash positions of most banks are covered well in advance, so borrowing rates may be subdued," trader says. Tips call rate may slip to 5.00% in session while CBLO support tipped at 3.75%. (khushita.vasant@dowjones.com)

0509 GMT [Dow Jones] China's banking regulator may be losing faith in the country's trust companies, says Heard on the Street, another amber light for foreign institutions considering investing in this sector; increased scrutiny by the CBRC comes amid worries over practice of banks selling loans to trust companies so that they can repackage them and sell them on to investors. That threatens steady source of income for trust companies, which at forefront of financial services innovation in China; part of trusts' appeal till now has been their relative freedom from regulatory scrutiny, but that seems to be changing. See "HEARD ON THE STREET: Losing Faith In China's Trust Companies" (andrew.peaple@dowjones.com)

0458 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/KRW turns lower in afternoon trade on back of improved sentiment in regional stock markets, pushing Kospi higher (last up 1.1%), traders say. Local bank trader tips pair to target 1,182; "if Chinese shares extend gains later, it will be enough to push the pair down to that low level." But another local bank trader expects downside to be cushioned by foreign selling of local shares, while "exporter selling of dollars isn't as strong as it was yesterday." Pair last tad down at 1,185.2 vs 1,186.6 midday, 1,186.2 late yesterday in Seoul. (min-jeong.lee@dowjones.com)

0446 GMT [Dow Jones] Nikkei up 0.2% at 9230.12 vs 9186.32 midday close (down 0.3%); volume low with Japanese "Obon" holiday season in full swing and as investors await string of U.S. economic data and action from Japanese government to stem yen's rise. "If it turns out that the government is just giving lip service (regarding strong yen), markets will test critical 9000 support," says Masayoshi Yano, senior market analyst at Meiwa Securities. Puts next week's Nikkei range at 9000-9300, noting index may rise to 9500 provided BOJ takes additional easing step(s). 18/33 Topix subindexes higher; some flight to domestic demand/defensive issues seen: Fast Retailing (9983.TO) up 0.6% at Y12,890, Eisai (4523.TO) up 1.7% at Y2,994. Panasonic (6752.TO) up 1.6% at Y1,082 after GS ups to Buy. Many exporter shares continued to underperform; Honda Motor (7267.TO) down 1.2% at Y2,765, Fanuc (6954.TO) off 0.9% at Y9,600, Nikon (7731.TO) flat at Y1,495. CSK (9737.TO) down 8.8% at Y299 after brokerage target cut. (kana.inagaki@dowjones.com)

0447 GMT [Dow Jones] HSI +0.1% at 21,120.46 midday, struggles to recover after index's 3-session 3.2% fall, amid uncertainty over global economic recovery after U.S. disappointing jobs data, says Daniel So at Sun Hung Kai Financial. "The index is now struggling at around its 250-day moving average (21,020) and it's unlikely to move much further up or down from that level, as there's still caution over the global economic outlook." Tips near-term support at 20,600. Still, expects upcoming corporate results of China banks, oil plays could help support trading sentiment in local market. Among these, ICBC (1398.HK) +0.2% at HK$5.70, Bank of China (3988.HK) +0.5% at HK$4.04, Cnooc (0883.HK) down 0.2% at HK$12.74, Sinopec (0386.HK) +0.7% at HK$6.15. Volume modest at HK$30.84 billion. (susanna.tai@dowjones.com)

0446 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia shares by midday up 0.4% at 3037.205 in light volume thanks to foreign bargain-buying in select consumer-related, telecommunication stocks, traders say; tip resistance at 3050. "The market is seen trying to recover from recent falls despite sporadic selling by local funds," says trader at Lautandhana Securities. Car maker Astra (ASII.JK) +1.2% at IDR48,100, heavyweight Telkom (TLKM.JK) +1.2% at IDR8,500. Profit-taking hits cigarette maker Gudang Garam (GGRM.JK) down 0.7% at IDR35,300. (edhi.pranasidhi@dowjones.com)

0440 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore shares still mostly higher as bargain hunters return after steep falls this week. Gains, however, generally modest as underlying sentiment remains cautious. "It is unlikely fears of a slowing U.S. economy will go away anytime soon, unless the next batch of economic indicators, especially job numbers, shows a pick-up in growth," says AmFraser Securities strategist Najeeb Jarhom. STI +0.4% at 2939.24 midday, with immediate resistance at 2950, followed by 2969 (Aug. 11 high). Market breadth at almost 2 gainers for every decliner. Genting Singapore (G13.SG) most sought-after stock in market, +10.9% at S$1.42 on 497.4 million shares, accounting for almost a third of overall market volume, on strong 2Q10 results. Wilmar (F34.SG) bucks gains by most other blue chips, off 2.2% at S$6.13, on disappointment with 2Q10 performance. (frankie.ho@dowjones.com)

0440 GMT [Dow Jones] NZ shares heading for positive close, last up 0.3% at 3015.102. "After a bit of downside over the past few days. It has bounced back mainly in reaction to a firmer Australian market today," says Hamilton Hindin Greene broker Grant Williamson. "It is finding a little bit of buying support." Retailers like Pumpkin Patch (PPL.NZ) +1.2% at NZ$1.75, Kathmandu (KMD.NZ) +1.9% at NZ$1.64, benefiting from stronger-than-expected retail sales data. In other direction, PGG Wrightson (PGW.NZ) down 7.1% at NZ$0.52 after FY result, outlook; "Investors are just a touch disappointed that the outlook is not a little bit brighter." Says focus now firmly on corporate earnings due to come "fast and furious" next week. (rebecca.howard@dowjones.com)

0438 GMT [Dow Jones] KLCI +0.6% midday at 1357.40 boosted by bargain buying of selected heavyweights, led by Genting (3182.KU) after its Singapore unit swings to the black. Adds, techs (+2.8%) leading gains despite sector dragging Wall Street overnight. "After six-consecutive days of losses, players are finding some bargains among the chip makers... total market volume (at 554 million shares) is also a little better than of late," says dealer. Says 1360 immediate resistance likely to stay intact as players may turn tad cautious ahead of weekend; support at 1350. Market breadth positive with 391 advancers vs 222 decliners; among actives, Genting +6.0% at MYR8.16, Axiata (6888.KU) +1.6% at MYR4.32, tech plays JCY (5161.KU) +6.1% at MYR1.21, Unisem (5005.KU) +5.6% at MYR2.06. Decliner Nestle (4707.KU) down 0.5% at MYR39.00. (kwan-por.lee@dowjones.com)

0437 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/CNY stays up midday in relatively quiet trade after higher fixing; as concerns over potential central bank-guided flows later in session also kept players from selling USD, say traders. On OTC, USD/CNY at 6.7880 vs 6.7851 last close; tipped in 6.7820-6.7950 band in afternoon. "People are careful not to push the dollar-yuan much lower because the dollar faces strong support around CNY6.7800, given there was suspected dollar demand from state-owned banks close to level yesterday," says Shanghai-based trader at foreign bank. (joy.shaw@dowjones.com) [ 08-13-10 0120ET ]

title: MARKET TALK:USD/KRW Up; Geopolitical,  Intervention  Risks Weigh
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0053 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/KRW breaks 7-session declining streak, last up at 1,163.65 vs 1,160.1 yesterday, on news North Korea fired artillery in contested maritime border, higher chance of BOK intervention being supportive of USD, say market participants. Still, overall conditions continue to point to a lower USD/KRW, so pair unlikely to advance much today. "Given that the direction is still tilted towards the downside, it's just not that easy to buy actively again simply because it's rising now," says local bank trader. Pegs pair in 1,158-1,166 band rest of session. Foreign bank trader tips USD/KRW to stay within 1,160s today, tips robust export settlements to flow in if pair approaches higher 1,160s. (kanga.kong@dowjones.com)

0049 GMT [Dow Jones] S&P/ASX 200 turns down 0.2% to 4584.1 in quiet trading before the FOMC meeting later Tuesday. Index has slipped as low as 4577.7 amid weakness in BHP Billiton (BHP.AU), Westfield (WDC.AU), NAB (NAB.AU). BHP down 0.8% at A$41.21, slightly below its ADR's equivalent close, while Westfield (WDC.AU) down 2.8% ex-distribution, NAB down 0.5% on disappointing 3Q cash profit. But NAB seems well supported on dips and CBA (CBA.AU) is up 0.3% ahead of tomorrow's FY results. "The equity markets are in a holding pattern as they wait to see what the FOMC does in terms of whether they will let the economy continue to chug along or whether they signal quantitative easing," says IG Markets strategist Cameron Peacock. "The Australian share market outperformed on Monday, so it's not surprising to see us underperforming today." Other traders are expecting a break above the June 21 high at 4622 later today, after Monday's break above resistance from last week's high and the 100-day moving average in the 4584-4488 area. (david.rogers1@dowjones.com)

0045 GMT [Dow Jones] FOMC meeting focal point of market and there's significant expectation that Fed will comment on a reinvestment policy for maturing assets, says Greg Gibbs, FX strategist at RBS. But adds RBS U.S. economic research team anticipates that Fed will just allude to a weaker economic outlook. Adds perhaps the one dissenter, Hoenig, will end his objection over extended period language. House says there's room for disappointment in Fed statement that undermines risk appetite if it fails to discuss concrete steps under consideration to enhance its easing policy in some way. (james.glynn@dowjones.com)

0045 GMT [Dow Jones] Kospi +0.2% at 1793.15 as investors remain cautious ahead of Fed meeting outcome while North Korean issues have limited impact on market, analysts say. "Uncertainties remain, but the market hopes the Fed will signal steps to boost U.S. economy, so the index isn't likely to be pressured downward," says Hanyang Securities' Lim Dong-rak; adds, "Many events, such as Fed's results and the BOK's rate review, are planned this week, but they aren't likely to offer a concrete direction for the market, it may just make the market volatile." Analysts say liquidity still abundant with foreigners, local institutions snatching up stocks today. Recent KRW strength also offering "good" excuse for foreigners to buy Korea. Investors calm to news North Korea yesterday fired artillery near contested maritime border; "Unless they (South and North Korea) clash, the impact will likely be limited," Lim says. Kospi tipped in 1790-1800 range today. (jung-ah.lee@dowjones.com)

0036 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan shares likely to extend gains after strength in U.S. stocks overnight, Asian stocks so far; Taiex may test 8100 vs over 3-month high of 8034.49 (+0.9%) yesterday; "Taiwan shares' recent gains have been led by non-technology companies (financial firms, traditional industry companies etc.) and we think that trend can continue because of rising global raw material prices," says Maggie Chien, manager at President Securities. Index tipped 8000-8100 for session. (joy.shaw@dowjones.com)

0033 GMT [Dow Jones] Nikkei up 0.9% at 9654.56 with select exporter shares snapped up on firmer USD/JPY (now 85.98), but light market trading volume expected to continue ahead of BOJ policy meeting result today, U.S. FOMC meeting later in global trading day. "The BOJ will likely not change its policy, but it may indicate a sense of crisis over recent yen strength," which could be enough to boost market sentiment, says Toshikazu Horiuchi, equity strategist at Cosmo Securities. Puts today's Nikkei range at 9550-9700. 28/33 Topix subindexes higher; Disco (6146.TO) up 6.5% at Y5,110, Mitsubishi Materials (5711.TO) up 5.1% at Y249 on solid 1Q earnings/outlook hikes. Tokyo Electron (8035.TO) up 2.6% at Y4,560, Kyocera (6971.TO) up 1.9% at Y7,930. Shiseido (4911.TO) off 0.7% at Y1,951, JX Holdings (5020.TO) down 1.2% at Y477. (kana.inagaki@dowjones.com)

0033 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan 20-year government bond likely to fall sharply on worse than expected 20-year bond auction yesterday, says local bank trader. Central bank sells NT$40 billion worth of 20-year bonds at 1.7890% yield vs 1.7400%-1.7600% band expected, on tepid demand from insurers; "insurers did not seem to be pressing to buy the 20-year bond." But expects insurers to step into market after 20-year yield rises to 1.8000% vs 1.7340% yesterday in when-issued trade. 20-year yield eyed in 1.7500%-1.8000% band for day, 5-year yield tipped in 0.9200%-0.9300% band vs 0.9173% yesterday. (mason.wu@dowjones.com)

0033 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/JPY may fall if BOJ decides not to ease monetary policy at its policy-setting meeting which ends later in day, says Barclays Capital chief strategist Japan Masafumi Yamamoto. House expects no change in BOJ's policy this month as Japan's authorities have been signaling they won't tackle recent JPY strength immediately, he says. Adds, investors to keep close eye on FOMC meeting tonight; if Fed eases its policy or at least signals plans to ease monetary policy in near term, USD/JPY may fall sharply again, he says. Citibank Japan's chief strategist Osamu Takashima says he doesn't rule out USD/JPY's break below 85.00 just yet. Pair last at 85.98. (takashi.mochizuki@dowjones.com)

0030 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore government bonds may fall a tad as Asian stocks should remain well supported, with local stocks possibly outperforming on catch-up rally after market closed yesterday for National Day holiday. However, trader says fall should be subdued after recent rally in yields, which may also limit any impact from Fed announcements later. Focus now on upcoming 20-year bond auction in early September, trader adds. Friday, Singapore's 2-year bond yields were flat at 0.48%, 10-year bond yields up 1 bp to 2.03%, ending week with 8bp gain. (david.roman@dowjones.com)

0023 GMT [Dow Jones] KLCI may rise, taking cues from gains on Wall Street overnight; market's rise however, may be limited near-term as investors await outcome of FOMC meeting later today. "The series of earnings reports coming out over the next two weeks also gives investors a reason to stay cautious for now," dealer says; tips KLCI to remain in 1355-1365 range near-term. Glovemakers such as Top Glove (7113.KU) may be in focus on concerns recent appreciation of MYR will squeeze profit margins. (benjamin.low@dowjones.com)

0022 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/SGD lower at 1.3485 vs 1.3498 late Asia Friday, with market shrugging off final Singapore 2Q GDP reading (on-year growth marginally slower at 18.8% vs 19.3% estimated in July) and likely to focus on BOJ, Fed meetings later today, which should clip downside ahead of cues on upcoming monetary policy trends. Action yesterday subdued, with local market shut for public holiday, but pair still dropped in line with other key Asian pairs, to fresh 2-year low at 1.3453 - that may be key support level today. First resistance tipped at 1.3500. (david.roman@dowjones.com)

0020 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore shares may inch up following Wall Street's modest gains, but investors likely to tone down expectations ahead of Fed's interest rate decision, accompanying statement due later Tuesday. STI not expected to challenge year-to-date high of 3043, while 2963 (higher end of minor breakup gap formed July 23) may offer support on any pullback; ended down 0.4% at 2995.06 Friday (market closed yesterday for public holiday). Analyst at Singapore bank expects limited upside for shares in near term; "while corporate results so far have been OK, they are not fantastic. Economic data so far from the U.S. and even from China don't seem to be pointing to a strong 2011. July's U.S. nonfarm payrolls data, for example, came in worse than expected." Singapore's final 2Q 2010 GDP data +18.8% on-year vs +19.3% tipped by government last month. UOL Group (U14.SG), Bukit Sembawang Estates (B61.SG) may be in focus as companies latest to report June-quarter results. (frankie.ho@dowjones.com) [ 08-09-10 2053ET ]

title: MARKET TALK: USD/SGD Likely Up On Risk Aversion, Cap At 1.3590
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0119 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/SGD flat in Asian morning trade amid conflicting signals for pair, may rise on weaker Nikkei. "The risk environment has turned negative following the U.S. home sales and factory output numbers that have brought back doubts about the strength of the global economy," trader at local bank says. Adds USD itself weaker on speculation over more Fed easing moves to revive flagging economy. Tips 1.3590 resistance, support near 1.3490. Pair last 1.3521 vs 1.3523 late Asia. (gaurav.raghuvanshi@dowjones.com)

0118 GMT [Dow Jones] Thai shares may see some pullback today on Wall Street weakness, also after bourse clocked up 9 straight sessions of gains, with foreigners net buyers for 7 consecutive days. "It looked like the market would go down yesterday, but then buying came in at the end. It just does not seem like there is much selling around," says Andrew Yates, head of sales for international equities at Asia Plus Securities. Market may also find some support among energy plays after crude oil hit $82/bbl for first time since May. Support at 860, resistance at 870. Index closed +0.2% at 864.48 yesterday. (leigh.murray@dowjones.com)

0108 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/KRW recovers 1,170 support, quickly coming off an earlier low of 1,166 amid Kospi's 0.4% fall as participants increasingly wary over possible USD buying intervention by FX authorities, after BOK suspected of having intervened frequently in recent sessions to support USD, traders say. "A bout of short dollar covering kicked in, in the upper-1,160s region," lifting USD, while some offshore players also seen bidding up USD, says local bank trader. Puts cap at 1,173 amid anticipated USD selling by exporters above 1,170. Pair now tad down at 1,170.6 vs 1,171.6 late yesterday in Seoul. (min-jeong.lee@dowjones.com)

0104 GMT [Dow Jones] HSI may fall on profit-taking after recent gains, also tracking weak U.S. cues, says Francis Lun at Fulbright. Tips 21,200 support today, as any falls unlikely major given underlying sentiment still strong, supported by latest corporate results. "Some profit-taking is expected after the recent strong ride, but I still believe the Hang Seng Index could test 22,000 in the near-term." Says both HK, China property stocks may take breather after latest outperformance (Hang Seng Property Subindex +3.4% over past 2 sessions, vs HSI's 2.0%). HSI ended +0.2% at 21,457.66 Tuesday. (susanna.tai@dowjones.com)

0103 GMT [Dow Jones] NZ government says mobile calls to get cheaper now Commerce Commission to regulate wholesale prices charged by mobile network operators for providing services to customers from other network operators. Regulating "will improve competitition in the mobile market and result in lower prices for mobile phone users," says Communications Minister Steven Joyce. But Vodafone NZ, local unit of Vodafone Group (VOD, VOD.LN), Telecom (TEL.NZ) unhappy with news; "the New Zealand mobile telecommunications market is dynamic and active, and to further regulate at this point would only interfere in what is proving to be the most competitive part of the overall telco sector," says Tom Chignell, General Manager of Corporate Affairs for Vodafone NZ. Comments echo Telecom (TEL.NZ) spokesman Mark Watts who says regulation unwarranted, unnecessary. If move forces lower prices will bite into both companies' revenues but could help smaller player 2degrees as it fights to win market share. (rebecca.howard@dowjones.com)

0101 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/THB steady around 32.16-32.165 vs 32.16 late yesterday in Asia, but pair biased downward amid general bearish tone towards greenback after it stumbled against major rivals overnight following weak U.S. economic data, also speculation Fed may push additional measures to boost economy. "It's been fairly quiet this morning, but sentiment is definitely leaning towards a stronger baht," says Bangkok-based dealer. Support remains at 32.10, with Bank of Thailand tipped to step-in to defend that level strongly; resistance at 32.20. (leigh.murray@dowjones.com)
