title: SGX Nikkei 225 Futures End Up On Wall St,BOJ  Intervention
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Nikkei 225 stock index futures traded on the Singapore Exchange ended higher Wednesday, encouraged by Wall Street's resilience overnight and the Bank of Japan's move to push the yen lower against the U.S. dollar, dealers said. 

 The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract closed up 290 points at 9925 points, with 19,254 contracts traded. 

 On the spot market, the Nikkei 225 rose 2.7% to 9939.60 points. 

 Dealers said they saw solid fresh buying supporting the market, amid hopes the selling pressure in U.S. stock markets may be tapering off. 

 Tuesday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 17.30 points, or 0.2%, to 8903.40, while the Nasdaq lost 24.47 points, or 1.6%, to 1555.08. 

 In addition, the Japanese central bank's intervention in the foreign exchange market earlier Wednesday improved sentiment on equities, dealers said. 

 At 0806 GMT (4:06 a.m. EDT), the dollar was trading at Y117.59, compared with Y117.23 late Tuesday in New York. 

 A weaker yen would benefit Japanese exporters. 

 Despite the gains, the market's future direction remains unclear amid the current uncertainty over a possible military confrontation in Asia after the horrifying terrorist attacks against the U.S. last week, dealers said. 

 The Japanese equities markets will continue to take cues from Wall Street, they said. 

 The MSCI Taiwan stock index futures traded in Singapore ended lower, with the benchmark September contract down 3.8 points at 171.3. 

 On the spot market, the Weighted Price Index of the Taiwan Stock Exchange closed up 6.55 points, or 0.2%, at 3781.17 in dealings valued at NT$26.10 billion (US$1=NT$34.518). 

 Both the spot and futures markets for Taiwan equities were closed Monday and Tuesday due to damages caused by Typhoon Nari. 


Selling pressure was heavy after two days of market closure, as
investors tried to catch up with the recent sharp losses on Wall Street
and other regional bourses, dealers said.

title: Emerging  FX  - Mixed bag, yen and c.banks watched.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 19 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were a 

 mixed bag in late trade on Wednesday with the market 

 wrongfooted by intervention from Japan and by local central 

 banks. 

     The regionals had followed the yen firmer early but turned 

 tail when the Bank of Japan stepped in to sell yen on at least 

 two occasions lifting the dollar away from the 117.00 level. 

     This is the second time this week the BOJ intervened to 

 stem the yen's rapid appreciation. However, the action was only 

 a partial success with the dollar unable even to hold 118.00 

 yen. 

     The regional currencies also had to weather central bank

intervention of their own. 

     In the Philippines, the central bank was rumoured to have 

 aggressively sold U.S. dollars to countered losses in the peso 

 caused by demand for the U.S. currency to settle maturing deals 

 in the non-deliverable forward market. 

 The Indonesian central bank also offered dollars to curb 

 the rupiah's slide which resulted from active dollar demand 

 from local banks and companies. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar drifted below the key 1.7400 market after 

 the BOJ intervention prompted dealers to mark the dollar higher 

 and some players to cover short positions. 

 Dealers said there was no sign of intervention from the 

Monetary Authority of Singapore so far, but there was talk the 

 MAS has left dollar buying orders open at 1.7340. 

 Charts show the Sing dollar is trading around its 14-day 

 moving average of 1.7419, and also that there is a gap up to 

 1.7500 left after last week's plane attacks which the currency

 was likely to fill sooner or later. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was a touch firmer at 44.15, but still locked in a 

 tight range of 44.10-44.24 after gains inspired by foreign 

 stock buying were countered by exporter dollar offers above 

 44.20. 

     Foreign investors had been net buyers of Thai stocks since 

 last Thursday. 

     On the macro front, central bank chief economist Atchana 

 Waiquamdee said the volatile world political and economic 

 situation may leave Thailand with lower than expected economic 

 growth in 2002. 

 "If the world situation persists and worsens, we could see 

 a technical recession in 2002, when the economy contracts for 

 two consecutive quarters," she said. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah briefly dropped below 9,700 for the first time 

 since August 2 on the back of aggressive dollar buying from 

 local banks and companies, including one oil importer. 

 But the currency crawled off its lows after Bank Indonesia 

 sold the dollar at around 9,700 and some local firms took 

 profits on the dollar. 

 BI had said earlier on Wednesday that it was considering 

intervening in the foreign exchange market to prop up the 

 rupiah. But dealers said the amount of its dollar sales was 

 small. 

 Deputy central bank governor Miranda Goeltrom also told 

 Reuters there was a "likelihood" that benchmark SBI interest 

 rates would fall further. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso closed lower at 51.40 to the dollar in the onshore 

 market against 51.370 on Tuesday despite central bank

 dollar-selling intervention. 

     Market players needed the U.S. dollar to settle their deals 

 in the NDF market. 

     Dealers in Manila said central bank dollar sales accounted 

 for almost half of the total market turnover on Wednesday which 

 was around $73.50 million. However, the central bank later said 

 they had not intervened. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said separately 

 he was quite comfortable with the current level of the peso. 


    KOREAN WON         -2



    The won ended higher against the dollar as a rate cut by



the central bank and the yen's resilience provided support for



the local currency.



    The won closed at 1,296.50 to the dollar against the



Tuesday's close of 1,296.9.



    The central bank on Wednesday cut its target for the



short-term call rate by 50 basis points to 4.00 percent,



joining a global monetary easing to minimise impacts from U.S.



attacks on the world economy.

title: Emerging  FX  - Roiled as Japan buys dollars for yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 18 (Reuters) - Asian currencies turned 

 mixed in unsettled morning trade Wednesday after the Bank of 

 Japan intervened to buy dollars for yen for the second time in 

 three days. 

     Regional currencies had mostly started firmer  as the 

 dollar tracked losses in the U.S. stocks which ended at 

 three-year lows overnight. 


    But as the dollar drifted off toward 117.00 yen        a



round of buy ordrers hit the market which dealers assumed were



from the BOJ and the dollar duly jumped to 117.75. The Ministry

of Finance confirmed it had ordered the intervention,



signifying how serious their intent was.



    In any case, with global investors more risk-averse after



last week's plane attacks, they are tending to avoid peripheral


currencies.



    Indeed, traders suspect they would be selling Asian


currencies more actively if it were not for the lack of



liquidity in local markets. Instead, they use the much more



liquid markets in the Australian and New Zealand dollars and



sell those as a  proxy.



    SINGAPORE DOLLAR



    The Sing dollar reversed early gains and followed the yen



lower to 1.7405 after the BOJ's intervention.



    Dealers were also wary of possible intervention by the


Monetary Authority of Singapore since many assumed the MAS



might want a weaker currency as a tacit easing in monetary



policy following this week's round of global rate cuts.



    "While the Sing dollar looks set to continue to following



the yen, the market needs to watch for any change of policy by



the MAS after this week's (non-oil exports data) showed exports



falling by early 30 percent year-on-year in August," said



Mansoor Mohi-Uddin, currency strategist at UBS Warburg.



    "Singapore's economy continues to be hit by the slowdown in



the economy globally and so undue currency strength appears



unwarranted," he said.



    KOREAN WON         -2



 The South Korean won firmed to 1,295.0 per dollar, compared to



Tuesday's close of 1,296.9, after the central bank cut interest



rates.



    Bank of Korea trimmed borrowing costs by 50 basis points on



Wednesday, in line with moves by some other countries following



last week's attacks on the United States.


Central Bank governor Chon Chol-hwan said there has not



been upward price pressure from the demand side despite



concerns the attacks could lead to higher oil prices.



    Chon also said that the assault against the United States



would prolong South Korea's economic slowdown.



    Dealers said they expected dollar/won to trade between



1,292 and 1,297 on Wednesday.



    In the non-deliverable forward market, the one-month won



was 1,296.1/97.1 per dollar, against 1,298.4/99.4 late on



Tuesday. The six-month won was quoted at 1,304.9/05.9 against



1,307.4/08.4.



THAI BAHT



The baht also gave up early gains to stand at 44.20 in the



wake of the BOJ's action.



In any case, players were not willing to push the local


currency above 44.00 yet due to fears of dollar-buying


intervention from the Thai central bank.



Meanwhile, Commerce Minister Adisai Bodharamik estimated on



Tuesday that Thai exports were worth around $5.3-5.4 billion in



August and that Thailand should manage to post a trade surplus



for the whole 2001.



Baht funding costs were mostly steady, with the tom/next



rate quoted at 0.25/0.40 satang per dollar and one-month



forward rate at 7/11 satang in the offshore market.



PHILIPPINE PESO



The peso opened at 51.365 to the dollar against the



Tuesday's close of 51.37. Trading was thin, with only $2.00



million transacted at 0120 GMT.



The country registered trade deficit of $66 million in



July. But the trade during the first seven months of this year



remained in surplus.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH The rupiah slipped to the 9,625,



driven by strong dollar demand in the past two days believed to



be linked largely to genuine commercial needs.



One dealer from a European bank said the market looked



"toppish" given dollar/rupiah had risen from 9,200 to 9,600



this week despite the dollar's losses against many regional


currencies in the wake of last week's attacks on the United



States.



    "I think the market will stop around here," said the



dealer.



    "People that have gone long (dollars) don't dare keep their



positions open for long at these levels," he said.



    Dealers have said that they believe the central bank has



made efforts to stem the rupiah's decline though moves had



appeared to be half-hearted up until now.



    Indonesia, home to the world's largest Muslim community



said on Tuesday that it would step up intelligence efforts to



keep terrorists out of the country.



    TAIWAN DOLLAR          The Taiwan dollar remained firm



around 34.45 relative to its position ahead of last week's



attacks on the United States, with some dealers expecting more



U.S. dollar weakness ahead.



All eyes were on how financial markets would fare following



a two-day closure dictated by Typhoon Nari which brought floods



to the island's capital and triggered the deaths of 66 people.



Though sentiment towards stocks was bearish, dealers said



they expected the Taiwan dollar to remain on the strong side of



its recent range.



"The U.S. dollar is likely to remain weak against North



Asian currencies and any impact on stocks will be limited after



the government action," said a senior dealer from a U.S. house.



Taiwan's minister of finance said on Tuesday that the local



stock market's daily downward trading limit would be cut in

title: Emerging  FX -Bolstered as dlr wilts ahead of Wall St.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 17 (Reuters) - Asian currencies edged ahead 

 in early trade on Monday as nervous investors stayed away from 

 the U.S. dollar ahead of Wall Street's reopening. 

     Poor U.S. industrial data released Friday also weighed on 

 sentiment. The data showed industrial production fell for the 

 11th straight month in August, while capacity utilisation fell 

 to lowest level since July 1983. 

 But gains were likely to be capped by wariness of potential 

 dollar buying intervention by major central banks, particularly 

 from Japan which is desperate to restrain the yen - a currency

 closely tracked by the regional currencies. 

 "I don't think Asian currencies will rise much further from 

 here. Many in the market expect the Fed to act today when the 

 markets reopen and major central banks are not going to let the 

 dollar fall like a stone," said a dealer at a U.S. bank. 

 "And if the U.S. strikes back, and we believe they will, 

 I'm sure the market will be more risk averse. In that 

 situation, the dollar is likely to be in demand. We still think 

 this is a good opportunity for the market to accumulate 

 dollars," he said. 

 Money markets in the U.S. have already moved to price in 

 further aggressive easing from the Federal Reserve with many 

 expecting it could even cut later today. 

 The market is also watching the Bank of Japan's meeting 

 later this week amid speculation it may take further steps to 

 show its resolve in stemming deflation and preventing a weak 

 Japan from contributing to a global economic slowdown. 

     Elsewhere in the region, Taiwan's financial markets are 

 closed on Monday as the island braced for Typhoon Nari. 

     Singapore is due to release August non-oil domestic export 

 data at 0430 GMT, with most economists expecting a deeper slide 

 in exports after a 24.2 percent year-on-year contraction in 

 July. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was marked up to 1.7315 in early trade - 

 its best level since January 22. There was still no inter-bank 

 trading, with deals going through brokers. 

 Dealers expected the Monetary Authority of Singapore to 

intervene to stop the local currency from appreciating much 

 past the key level of 1.7300. 

 "There is no good news from the local front but the Sing 

 dollar has strengthened primarily on the back of a firmer yen," 

 said a dealer at a European bank. 

 "Also, we believe local companies are unlikely to be 

 aggressive in buying overseas assets in this kind of 

 environment," he said. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht moved up to the morning high of 43.98 in early 

 thin trade to mirror gains in the regionals as onshore and 

 offshore players unwound long dollar positions. 

     There is still no direct quotes for the baht in the onshore 

 market. 

     Thailand's macro picture remains bleak. A local newspaper 

 quoted the National Economic and Social Development Board - a 

 government think tank - as saying the country's exports were 

 likely to fall over 6.0 percent in 2001. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won tracked a firmer yen higher as players were 

 reluctant to buy the U.S. dollar, fearing steep losses when 

 Wall Street reopens. 

     The local currency opened at 1,290 before edging lower to 

 1.294 compared with the Friday's close of 1,296.3. 

     Gains were likely to be limited by losses in local stocks 

 which has shed 2.62 percent at 0125 GMT. 

     Meanwhile, the country posted a record $100.04 billion in 

foreign exchange reserves as of September 15 compared with 

 $99.03 billion at the end of August. 

     The increase was attributed to steady repayment of foreign 

currency-denominated loans by financial institutions to the 

central bank and a higher conversion value of euro and yen 

 holdings which increased the dollar value in the reserves. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was little moved from levels seen late on Friday 

 around 9,100 as players awaited direction from U.S. markets. 

 Traders were cautious after last week's terror attacks in the 

 U.S. disrupted a meeting between the government and the Paris 

 Club of creditors. 

     "The focus is very much on the U.S.. We are still looking 

 for direction," said a dealer from a European bank. 

     "Some people are dollar bearish because the U.S. economy 

 will suffer more, but there is little to cheer about in the 

 rupiah," he said. 

     The rupiah was seen trading in the range of 9,000 and 9,200 

 while corporate activity was expected to pick up later in the 

 day, dealers said. 

     Indonesia earlier this month asked the Paris Club to 

 reschedule $6 billion in foreign debt falling due between April 

 2002 and March 2004 to ease pressure on the ailing budget.

title: Singapore Dlr Up Late On Broad US Dlr Weakness;Thin Trade
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was higher in very thin trading late Monday, in line with the U.S. dollar's broader weakness against major currencies, dealers said. 

 Around 0755 GMT (3:55 a.m. EDT), the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.7335, down from S$1.7376 late Friday in Asia. According to dealers, it traded between S$1.7310 and S$1.7335. 

 The U.S. dollar opened around its intraday high against the Singapore currency, reflecting losses against the yen and euro late Friday in Europe. 

 Around midday, the U.S. dollar drifted lower to its intraday low, in step with its brief fall below Y117. 

 Subsequently, intervention by the Bank of Japan boosted the U.S. dollar against the yen and nudged it slightly higher against the Singapore dollar as well, dealers said. 

 "The BOJ intervention didn't do much for the dollar/Sing because the market is still nervous about the (U.S.) dollar ahead of the reopening of the U.S. stock market today," said a senior dealer at a European bank in Singapore. 

 Dealers said trading was very thin with most of the trades being dealt through brokers. 

 "There weren't any interbank calls," a dealer said. 

 Market participants expect the U.S. stock market to open sharply lower when it reopens later Monday, following Tuesday's terrorist strikes in New York and Washington. This would pressure the U.S. dollar lower. 

 Adding to the uncertainly about the U.S. dollar are expectations among many market participants that the Federal Reserve may cut U.S. interest rates before the U.S. stock markets reopen. There are also fears that a sharp slide in the U.S. dollar may prompt coordinated intervention by major central banks. 

 Dealers expect the U.S. dollar to trade between S$1.7270 and S$1.7370 over the next few hours and then in a wider S$1.7250-S$1.7400 range overnight. 

 Prices of Singapore government bonds were higher Monday after a rally in U.S. Treasurys overnight and on expectations of a sharp fall in U.S. stocks when U.S. equities market reopen later Monday. 

 A sharp fall in the local stock market and soft local interbank money rates also helped bond prices, dealers said. 

 The yield on two-year bonds was down five basis points at 2.05% and the yield on five-year bonds was down four basis points at 2.73%. 

 At the longer end of the curve, the yield on seven-year bonds was down one basis point at 3.18% while the yield on 10-year bonds was down three basis points at 3.41%.

title: Emerging  FX -Firmer as dollar sags, awaits U.S. cue.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were mostly 

 firmer in early trade on Friday with shakey dollar sentiment 

 undermined further by bearish U.S. consumer confidence data. 

     The University of Michigan consumer sentiment index, 

 released on Thursday, showed a sharp 7.9 point fall to 83.6 in 

 September, its lowest level in nearly eight years. And that was 

 before the terror attacks earlier this week. 

 Cautious market players kept their trading activity to a 

 bare minimum, although there had been few reports of settlement 

 or clearing problems so far. 

 There is still no interbank trading in most markets in the 

 region on Friday, with deals carried out through brokers or 

 electronic broking systems. 

 "The market is waiting for the U.S. stock markets to reopen 

 on Monday to see if they function smoothly, which direction 

 they head, etc," said a senior dealer at an Asian bank in 

 Singapore. 

 "Interbank players in Singapore will reassess the situation 

 again later today, and I believe by Monday or Tuesday we will 

 be able to quote directly again," he said. 

 U.S. stock markets will reopen for business on Monday, 

 nearly a week after an attack demolished the World Trade 

 Center, killing perhaps thousands and triggering longest 

 shutdown in trading since the outbreak of World War I. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was quoted in a 1.7360-1.7385 range in thin 

 trade, tracking the dollar/yen closely amid a dearth of strong 

 local leads. 

 The market is cautious to push the Sing dollar up much 

 higher, fearing the central bank might step in to curb its 

 appreciation due to the country's weak economic outlook. 

 Economists are betting the terror attacks in the U.S. will 

 lower growth rates in Asia and delay economic recovery - a 

 view which puts further strain on regional currencies. 

 At the current level, the U.S. dollar/Sing dollar is 

 hovering just above the oversold line on the 14-day relative 

 strength index, with a reading of 33. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht also edged higher alongside the regionals although 

 corporate dollar bargain hunting capped its gains at around 

 44.15. 

 But like most centers in the region, trading activity in 

 Bangkok was subdued as most interbank players sat on their 

 hands. 

 Meanwhile, Thailand will go ahead with the sale of more 

 Thai Airways shares in November despite their dive to a record 

 low this week following the attacks in the U.S. 

 The government wants to reduce its stake in the national 

 carrier to 70 percent from 93 percent. More than 10 percent 

 could be offered to a strategic partner. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won eased in anticipation of equity-related outflow of 

 dollars and on demand from oil importers. 

 Dealers in Singapore said overall trade was still subdued 

 on settlement worries and as interbank players awaited 

 retaliatory action of the U.S. against perpetrators of the 

 September 11 attacks. 

 Finance and Economy Minister Jin Nyum said interest rates 

 would be kept low and ample liquidity would be provided for the 

 financial system as the attacks were likely delay a recovey. 

 In a briefing to President Kim Dae Jung, he said the 

 government was ready to inject emergency liquidity to stem 

 sharp fluctuations in the won. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar rose in line with the yen and on an 

 expected inflow of dollars from foreign funds that had been net 

 buyers in local stocks, despite recent losses in the benchmark 

 TAIEX index. 

 But dealers in Singapore said the central bank, which 

intervened aggressively in the market on Thursday, was expected 

 to keep the upside capped. 

 Foreign funds were net buyers of 1.49 billion Taiwan 

 dollars worth of local stocks on Thursday, bringing total net 

 buying to 2.46 billion Taiwan dollars over the past three 

 sessions. 

 Amid high expectations of further policy easing, the 

central bank said on Thursday it would hold its quarterly board 

 meeting on September 26 to review monetary policy. 

 Taiwan has trimmed its discount rate and the accommodation 

 with collateral rate eight times since December 2000, bringing 

 them to record lows of 3.250 percent and 3.625 percent 

 respectively. 

 PHILIPPINES PESO 

 The peso edged up to 51.24 per dollar, taking its cue from 

 other regionals but dealers in Manila said dollar demand from 

 corporates and oil importers could weigh it down. 

     They said uncertainty in global markets would continue to 

 keep most interbank players cautious. 

     Energy Secretary Vince Perez said on Thursday the country 

 would suspend exports of petroleum products to ensure stocks, 

 following this week's terror attacks in the United States. 

     The Philippines imports all its crude requirements but 

 exports a small amount of products when refinery output exceeds 

 local consumption. 


    INDONESIAN RUPIAH



    Local corporates seeking dollars for immediate import and



debt payment needs were expected to keep the rupiah weighed



down.



    But dealers in Singapore said fear of central bank

intervention would cap the downside.



    Dealers believe the central bank was in the market on



Thursday at around 9,140 and its dollar sales helped the rupiah



bounce off session low of 9,175. It was hovering at 9,100 on



Friday.



In what was seen as a major positive development, the



government won vital parliamentary approval on Thursday to sell



its majority stake in the top retail bank - Bank Central Asia.



    The vote was seen as a test of relations between President



Megawati Sukarnoputri's new government and parliament.

title: Asian  Currencies  Up Late As Terrorist Attacks Bruise Dlr
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- Asian currencies received a boost late Wednesday, after Tuesday's terrorist attacks in the U.S. sent the dollar reeling in global foreign exchange markets and threatened to smash the already fragile confidence in the U.S. economy. 

 But trading was extremely thin as shell-shocked participants largely stayed on the sidelines, dealers said. 

 The interbank market in Singapore ground to a halt, leaving participants to trade via brokers and electronic broking systems, dealers said. 

 "There's nothing we much we can do," said a dealer at a European bank. "Liquidity is bad. If we're holding big positions, we're just trying to get out slowly." 

 Several central banks in the region - including authorities in Japan, Singapore and Korea - early in the day assured the markets they were prepared to offer additional liquidity to the banking system. 

 Position-squaring dominated trading, as market participants focused on ensuring transaction settlements were going through smoothly. Dealers said there were no reports of any major hiccups so far. 

 Still, "everybody's concerned whether or not the next few sessions we'll see any settlement problems," said a dealer a U.S. bank. 

 The cloud of uncertainty is expected to persist, and the dollar likely to remain wobbly, as observers consider the economic implications of the attacks in New York and Washington and wonder about how the U.S. government would retaliate. 

 Hijacked planes destroyed New York's two tallest buildings, and crashed into the Pentagon, badly damaging the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense. 

 "We don't want to be opportunistic to take advantage of the situation and hammer the U.S. dollar. Emotionally it's wrong, politically it's wrong, even though economically, it's right," said a dealer at a European bank. 

Foreign exchange participants were bracing for a collapse in U.S. stocks when the equity market resumes trading, expected Thursday, dealers said. Trade was suspended Tuesday. 

 Following the attacks, the U.S. Federal Reserve is expected to act swiftly and aggressively to calm financial markets and cushion their blow on the economy, market watchers said. Already, talk of emergency rate cuts of at least 25 basis points, as early as this week, has swirled around the market. 

 But such expectations didn't quell jitters of a likely downdraft in U.S. stocks anticipated Thursday, with most Asian stock markets tumbling Wednesday. Stock markets in Kuala Lumpur and Bangkok were closed Wednesday following the overnight attacks. The impact of the region's equity losses on the region's currencies was, however, muted, with participants focusing on the dollar's fate, dealers said. 

 Barclays Capital said in a research note that while it is too early to conclude definitively on the likely economic and policy implications of Tuesday's carnage, by the same token, "the widespread talk of a global recession and sustained global financial crisis does appear premature, based on current information." 

 Barclays said the dollar's downtrend against Asian currencies "could prove temporary," with the Japanese authorities threatening to intervene to curb the yen's strengthening, and amid fears that Asia's balance of payments would suffer from reduced capital inflows and higher oil prices. 

 Fears of, if not actual, intervention by the region's monetary authorities pulled Asian currencies off their intraday highs, dealers said. 

 Dealers believed intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore pulled the Singapore dollar off its nine-month high of S$1.7260, set overnight following the attacks on the U.S. 

 Some dealers suspected the central bank intervened again Wednesday in Asia, when the U.S. dollar was quoted around S$1.7340. 

 At 0937 GMT (5:37 a.m. EDT), the Singapore dollar was quoted at S$1.7376 against its U.S. counterpart, stronger than S$1.7539 late Tuesday in Asia. 

 Taiwan's central bank bought an estimated US$800 million - around US$300 million in the last few minutes of trading - to push up the U.S. dollar from the intraday low of NT$34.403, said a dealer at a foreign bank in Taipei. 

 The U.S. dollar closed at NT$34.599, down from NT$34.684 Tuesday. Turnover swelled to US$1.27 billion from Tuesday's US$338.5 million. 

 In Seoul, the Finance and Economy Ministry said it would go all out "to ensure market stability through various measures if the won moves sharply from investors' uneasiness." 

 The dollar finished at 1,286.1 won, down from Tuesday's close of KRW1,295.8. 

 On the Philippine Dealing System, the dollar closed at 51.230 pesos, down from PHP51.300 Tuesday. 

 The Thai currency was stronger at 44.435 baht per dollar, compared with THB44.810 late Tuesday. 

 The Indonesian currency was at 9,060 rupiah per dollar, firmer compared with IDR9,095 late Tuesday.

title: Emerging  FX -Bow to dollar, wait on O'Neill.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 11 (Reuters) - Asian currencies stumbled 

 lower early on Tuesday as dollar bulls bought back the U.S. 

currency after Wall Street bounced from the brink overnight 

 while its peers in Tokyo and Europe suffered losses. 

     Analysts said regional currencies were likely to face 

 further downside risks given the yen's bleak outlook and a 

 dearth of good news from the domestic front. 

     "We see recent gains in the regional currencies as a good 

 opportunity to buy dollars on dips. Fundamental stories do not 

 support the regional currencies," said Syetarn Hansakul, 

 regional economist at WestLB in Singapore. 

     "A major risk would come from the yen which gets little 

 help from either trade or portfolio inflows. We expect the yen 

 to drop to 122 in one month and 124 in three months," she said. 

     The regional currencies were mostly range-bound, alongside 

 the dollar/yen, ahead of a meeting between U.S. Treasury 

 Secretary Paul O'Neil and Japanese Finance Minister Masajuro 

 Shiokawa on Wednesday. 

     The market also awaits a string of key U.S. data due later 

 this week, including retail sales numbers on Friday. 


    SINGAPORE DOLLAR



    The Sing dollar lurched lower to 1.7510 as the U.S. dollar



regained its strength against the yen and the euro - both



carry substantial weight in Singapore's trade-weighted basket



of currencies.



Market talk that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS)



was in the market on Monday to support the U.S. dollar at



around 1.7460 also made players reluctant to get too short of



the greenback.



Analysts believed the Sing dollar's recent gains were just



a blip as they were not justified by fundamentals and suspect



the central bank would soon encourage the currency to trade



lower.



    WestLB's Hansakul forecast the local currency would slide



to 1.7550 in one month and 1.7800 in three months.



    KOREAN WON        -2



    The won, which closely tracks the yen, was trading lower at



1,293.5 compared with 1,290.3 at the close on Monday.



    But dealers in Singapore expected some dollar profit taking



to emerge soon as American International Group is



moving closer to buying control of Hyundai Securities



 and the market assumes some sort of flows into won



will result if the deal goes through.



    In the non-deliverable forward market, the one-month won



traded at 1,293/1,295 and three-month at 1,296/1,298.



    PHILIPPINE PESO



    The peso lingered around the 51 per dollar level with the



market focused on moves in other regionals amid a lack of fresh



local leads.



    Dealers in Manila said sporadic dollar buying by corporates



and importers had kept the peso locked in a tight 51.20-51.40



band but few players were showing interest to probe the



downside.



They said in recent weeks the central bank had repeatedly


intervened in the spot and the non-deliverable forward market



to keep the peso from breaching the 51.50 level, a level not



seen since August 13.



    The central bank denies the market talk but has said it



would act to stem speculation and volatile moves.



    THAI BAHT



    The baht edged down taking the cue from other regionals and



dealers in Singapore said rising baht funding costs in the



offshore market could pull the baht lower.



    The yen's overnight losses against the dollar prompted some



offshore players to cover their short dollar positions and to



hedge their recent investments in the local equity market.



    Dealers said the baht may test 44.90, the 50 percent



retracement of its August 1 to September 4 upmove, a break of



which could lead to lower levels beyond the 45 per dollar



boundary.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH



The rupiah bobbed around the 9,000 per dollar level,



weighed down by local corporates seeking dollars for debt and



import needs but supported by fear of central bank

intervention.



Dealers in Singapore said the market was closely watching



the majority disinvestment of Bank Central Asia, the country's



largest retail bank.



    The government expects parliament to approve the



disinvestment in the next couple of weeks.



    Parliament's approval to sell 51 percent stake of BCA to a



strategic investor is seen as a test of President Megawati



Sukarnoputri's commitment ability to deliver on reforms agreed



with the International Monetary Fund.



The IMF resumed lending to Indonesia on Monday, freeing up



$395 million of stalled loans after the government agreed a new



reform package.

title: Emerging  FX  - Yen's losses bruise regionals.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 7 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were on the 

 backfoot late on Friday, put off balance by the wobbly yen. 

     Japan's second-quarter economic growth data gave the yen 

  a tiny initial boost as the contraction was not as bad 

 as expected. But the market then realised it was still a 

 contraction of 0.8 percent, even if it beat expectations of 0.9 

 percent. 

 The yen's tussle with the U.S. dollar dented sentiment 

 towards the regionals, with dealers saying they sensed building 

 confidence among dollar bulls. 

 "People are starting to believe in the dollar/yen move 

 again, so there's a bit of dollar demand against the 

 regionals," said a U.S. bank dealer. 

 "Korea's got foreign direct investment dropping. Taiwan's 

 stock market keeps collapsing. And Singapore, well, the 

currency's too strong. We just need to get the sentiment and 

 the fundamentals to work together, and the dollar should go 

 higher." 

 After Thursday's poor U.S. economic data, there was 

 lingering doubts as to whether the dollar was seeing a 

 turnaround. The market was awaiting August employmemt data from 

 the United States, due later in the day. 

 THAI BAHT 

 Dollar demand from local corporates drove the Thai baht 

 lower, with losses in the yen aggravating its falls. 

 Singapore dealers said local corporates were looking to 

 hedge their dollar needs, and were actively looking to pick up 

 the dollar in the spot and forward markets. 

 A U.S. bank based in Singapore was spotted aggressively 

 snapping up dollars, catching local players short on dollar, 

 dealers in Bangkok said. 

 They added that news the Bank of Thailand had tightened 

 supervision of currency remissions and transfers did not have 

 an impact on the market. 

 Baht funding costs were rising with the one-month rate 

 quoted at 7/10 satang per dollar offshore, and -2.5/-1.0 satang 

 onshore. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 U.S. dollar bulls chased the Singapore dollar lower as the 

 yen limped through the Asian day. 

 Dealers said the U.S. dollar was struggling in early trade 

 as a European bank dumped some $100 million in the market. But 

 a local bank was spotted bidding for the U.S. unit just past 

 the 1.75 mark, driving it higher. 

 The yen's fall in the afternoon brought more pressure on 

 the Sing dollar. But it managed to avoid the key 1.7540 level, 

 which daily charts showed is a resistance level for the 

 greenback from a trendline starting on August 21. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar faced a sea of troubles, including weaker 

currencies from trade rivals Korea and Japan, the tumbling 

 local stock market and poor trade data. 

     It ended the day at 34.656, against Thursday's 34.616 

 close. 

     Singapore dealers said Taiwan's central bank had been 

 selling U.S. dollars sporadically during the day, but were not 

 spotted in the afternoon. 

     Taiwanese trade figures for August came in worse than 

 expected, with imports falling 36.5 percent year on year 

 against forecasts of a 26.4 percent dip, and exports down 25.8 

 percent compared to expectations of a 22.4 percent fall. 

     The Finance Ministry later said exports would not see 

 on-year growth until April 2002. 


    KOREAN WON         -2



    The won took its cue from the yen, giving up early gains



and touching a four-week low of 1,290.5, as players scrambled



to cover their short dollar positions.



    Singapore dealers said players panicked after the yen fell



through the 121 mark, sending exporters to the sidelines.



    Export-related inflows and dollar offers by some offshore



players had pushed the won higher earlier in the day.



    On the macroeconomic front, August foreign direct



investment data showed a decline of 17.2 percent on the year,



threatening a government target of $15 billion for the year.



    However, external liabilities continued declining for the



12th consecutive month, and by end of July were at $125.4



billion against $127 billion in June and $136.3 in December



2000.



PHILIPPINE PESO



The peso edged lower with a rise in dollar demand from



corporates and importers, prompting interbank players to build



long dollar positions.



    But some equity-related inflows and fear of central bank

intervention limited the downside.



    Volume was subdued in lacklustre pre-weekend trade, with a



total of $77.20 million traded by the end of onshore trade



compared to $96 million on Thursday.



    The government said it had concluded a deal for a private



placement of 15-year bonds worth a total of at least $250



million with Credit Suisse First Boston.



   National Treasurer Sergio Edeza said the amount raised would



be used to finance the budget.



    INDONESIAN RUPIAH



    The rupiah eased to hit a session low past 9,100 as the



market gave a cold shoulder to the draft budget for 2002, the



first to be unveiled by President Megawati Sukarnoputri.



    Fears of central bank intervention and dollar sales by a


Singapore-based bank pushed it back to settle just above the



9,100 mark.



    Dealers in Jakarta said the budget had no surprises and



some of the assumptions looked too optimistic.



    But Jakarta's official creditors, the IMF and the World



Bank, said the draft had struck the right balance between



prudence and stimulating growth.

title: Emerging  FX  - Retreat as dollar bolstered by NAPM.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 5 (Reuters) - Asian currencies ceded ground 

 in early trade on Wednesday after much stronger than expected 

 August U.S. manufacturing data prompted market players to buy 

 back the dollar, which they had sold actively in recent weeks. 

     The National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) 

 said its monthly index rose to 47.9 in August, up from 43.6 in 

 July and beating economists' forecasts of 43.9. 

     "The dollar/yen remains the major lead in the market that 

 people follow. But the dollar will need to break convincingly 

 above 120 for the Asian currencies to get out of their recent 

 ranges," said a dealer at a European bank in Singapore. 

     The market was now eyeing Japan's April-June gross domestic 

 product data and U.S. unemployment data for August, both due on 

 Friday. Local media reported Japan's Cabinet Office told policy 

 makers on Tuesday the GDP shrank by 1.2 percent in that period. 

     Otherwise, Korea will release its August producer price 

 index at 0300 GMT and the Philippines is scheduled to publish 

 its August consumer price index at 0100 GMT. 


    SINGAPORE DOLLAR



    The Singapore dollar mirrored the yen's losses against the



dollar amid a lack of local leads.



    Dealers said dollar offers by some U.S. banks around



1.7480-1.7490 helped the Singapore dollar bounce off its early



low of 1.7495, but overall the pressure was on the downside



with local players favouring the U.S. dollar.



    A convincing break of 1.75 was possible if the yen falls



past the 120 mark with some support expected at around 1.7530,



the August 23 low.



    THAI BAHT



    The baht lost ground on broad-based dollar buying from both



offshore and onshore players after the strong NAPM data set off



rounds of dollar buybacks.



    But exporters' dollar offers around 44.25-44.30 should help



slow down the dollar's rise, dealers in Bangkok said.



    "People have been chasing dollar since last night. The



rebound might be sustained in the near-term if Japan's GDP



numbers come in worse than expected," said a dealer at a U.S.



bank in Bangkok.



Demand for the dollar pushed baht funding costs higher,



with the one-month forward rate edging up to 4/7 satang per



dollar offshore and -2.7/-2.2 satang onshore.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH



The rupiah edged up above 9,000 helped by early dollar



sales by offshore players amid wariness over central bank

intervention.



Dealers in Singapore said Friday's draft for the 2002



budget, which is likely to give clues to government plans to



fix the troubled economy and talks with the Paris Club of



creditor nations starting on Monday, was likely to attract



attention.



    Jakarta will seek rescheduling of $6 billion in foreign



debt with the Club to ease pressure from debt repayments.



    PHILIPPINE PESO



    The peso opened slightly lower at 51.20 compared with the



Tuesday close of 51.15, tracking the regional currencies.



    The country's August annual inflation came in at 6.3



percent against 6.8 percent in July.


Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said the



lower-than-expected inflation would give the bank more



flexibility in interest rate policy, but added the bank did not



need to lower the rates immediately.



TAIWAN DOLLAR



The Taiwan dollar slipped a notch in line with the yen,



with renewed U.S. dollar buying interest in the non-deliverable



forwards market keeping the greenback firm in the spot market.



Singapore dealers said interest in buying U.S. dollars was



perking up in both the spot and NDF markets after a long lull.



They added further falls in the yen could spur the market to



take more long U.S. dollar positions against the Taiwan dollar.



But dealers were still wary of the central bank, which has



been on both sides of the market and kept the Taiwan dollar



within a narrow range 34.463-34.686 since August 3.



KOREAN WON -2



The won gave up some ground as it followed the yen south,



with falls on the local bourse also driving its retreat.



    Still, Singapore dealers said the won's losses were an



early reaction to the softer yen and lower stock prices.



    They said trading interest in the market was still minimal,



and expected dollar offers from exporters to emerge around



1,285.

title: Emerging  FX -Riding on yen's coat tail, US data eyed.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 4 (Reuters) - Asian currencies retained 

 their gains early on Tuesday as the highly correlated yen 

 advanced further against the dollar despite Japan's poor 

 economic fundamentals. 

     Some currencies were at their best levels in weeks as 

 market participants continued to pare down their long dollar 

 positions. 

     Dealers said the yen's strength was a combination of doubts 

 over the U.S. economic recovery, funds repatriation to Japan 

 ahead of end-September book closings, and declines in foreign 

 portfolio investments by Japanese investors. 

     Morgan Stanley Dean Witter said Japanese investors had 

 gradually decreased their investments in foreign assets over 

 the past three weeks because the recent continuous declines of 

 the Nikkei had reduced their risk appetite. 

     The market was watching out for the U.S. NAPM survey due 

 out on Tuesday to see whether it confirms the improvement in 

 manufacturing data reported on Friday. 

     Elsewhere in the region, the Philippines published its 

 latest exports data and Hong Kong will release its July 

 external trade figures at 0800 GMT. 


    SINGAPORE DOLLAR



    The Singapore dollar followed after the yen, though the



market was wary of possible intervention by the authorities.



    Dealers and analysts say the local currency has been



trading around the upper half of its neutral band, which means



the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) would be more likely



to buy U.S. dollars to cap the Sing dollar's gains.



    A European bank dealer said the MAS was suspected of buying



U.S. dollars late last week around 1.7370, which is also the



100 percent retracement of the U.S. dollar's rise from February



27-July 16.



    The MAS issued a survey on Monday which showed economists



expect the city-state's economy to contract by 0.6 percent this



year due to the sharp downturn in the electronics cycle.



    THAI BAHT



    The baht struggled to break convincingly above 44.00 as



corporate demand for the dollar and fears of central bank


dollar bids above that level capped its gains.



    Dealers said if the dollar dropped further against the



baht, there was a good chance the central bank might step in to



buy the dollar on dips either to top up the foreign reserves or



to repay debts.



    The market was also cautious about buying the dollar



actively after the central bank said on Monday it would review


forex trading supervision rules to prevent money laundering.



    The remark followed the discovery by police last week of a



suspected money laundering operation, allegedly involving



individuals working at a Singapore bank in Bangkok.



    KOREAN WON         -2



    The won rose slightly as it rode on the yen's coat tails,



with an early rise in local stocks giving it an added boost.



    But Singapore dealers said the market lacked the drive to



push the won higher as offshore players opted for the



sidelines.



    "There's just no determination out there to test the



dollar/won's downside. We definitely need a bigger move in



dollar/yen," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.



    He added players were not concerned about possible central



bank intervention as the authorities were probably comfortable



with the cross rate with the yen and won . It was



quoted at 10.77/10.79 at 0045 GMT.



    INDONESIAN RUPIAH



    The rupiah was expected to stay under pressure from local



corporates' dollar demand for debt payment and import needs.



    But dealers in Singapore said rupiah's downside was limited



amid fears of intervention by the central bank aimed at keeping



the rupiah on the right side of the 9,000 mark.



    However, lack of support from the central bank could pull



the rupiah down to around 9,200, a multi-week low seen last



week.



    PHILIPPINE PESO



    The peso was expected to linger in a narrow range around



the 51 per dollar mark amid a lack of fresh trading cues.



    Dealers in Manila said most corporates were staying on the



sidelines, waiting for the authorities to push the peso higher.



    However, interbank players were reluctant to take short



dollar positions amid a lack of dollar inflows and an expected



rise in demand as the import season peaks in September.



    TAIWAN DOLLAR



    The Taiwan dollar edged higher in line with a steady yen



but equity-related outflows and the central bank were expected



to cap significant gains.



    Foreign investors were net sellers of 1.64 billion Taiwan



dollars worth of local shares on Monday, bringing the net



selling to 5.86 billion Taiwan dollars over the last five



sessions.



However, the recent strengthening of the yen has prompted



players to bail out of long dollar positions. The market tracks



movements in the yen as Taiwan competes with Japan in several



export markets.

title: Asian  Currencies  Mostly Dn Late; Mkts Seek Dlr Direction
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- Most Asian currencies were slightly weaker, languishing in tight ranges late Monday as fears of raising the ire of the region's central banks kept the dollar buoyed, dealers said. 

 As Japanese officials stepped up their verbal intervention to keep a rein on the local currency's recent strength, the dollar stayed afloat against the yen, in turn keeping the U.S. currency supported against most of its Asian counterparts, dealers said. 

 Suspected bouts of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore in London trade Friday, when the U.S. dollar skidded to as low as S$1.7370, also pressured the Singapore dollar, dealers said. 

 Fears of provoking the monetary authorities in South Korea, Taiwan and Thailand also restrained the movements of their respective currencies, which had surged Friday as the dollar floundered on increased despondency over the U.S. economy, dealers said. 

 The region's bleak economic fundamentals don't justify the currencies' recent resilience, which has been inspired by the yen, analysts said. 

 At 0742 GMT (3:42 a.m. EDT), the dollar was quoted at Y118.81, little changed from Y118.80 late Friday in New York. 

 With the direction of the dollar still murky ahead of a slew of potentially market-moving data this week, participants were also wary of building any major positions, dealers said. 

 The U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management index of manufacturing will be issued Tuesday, and the August employment report Friday. Japan is scheduled to announce its second-quarter gross domestic product data Friday. 

 "Markets are quite undecided as to what the next direction for the dollar is," said Thio Chin Loo, a regional currency strategist at BNP Paribas. "There are mixed signals on the U.S. economy." 

 U.S. economic data issued last Friday, including the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index and July factory orders, came in better than market expectations. 

 "The market, which is a bit confused right now, needs more weak data to justify the dollar sentiment," said a dealer at a European bank. 

 With U.S. markets closed Monday for the Labor Day holiday, trading in the region's foreign exchange markets was subdued. 

 The Singapore dollar skirted around the S$1.7400 level against its U.S. counterpart most of the day, following suspected buying in the U.S. currency by the local monetary authority in London trade. 

 Late in the day, the U.S. dollar inched higher to S$1.7413, above S$1.7374 late Friday. 

 Thio at BNP Paribas noted that the Singapore dollar, which has been the main beneficiary in Asia from the yen's recent advance, is relatively strong compared with most of its regional peers, which have largely been rangebound. 

 "If the Singapore dollar does outperform against the other currencies, the chances of the MAS coming in will increase," she added. 

 The Thai currency was marginally weaker at 44.075 baht per dollar, compared with THB44.025 late Friday, with participants unperturbed by the central bank's new foreign exchange reporting requirements for financial institutions, which take effect Monday, dealers said. The requirements are intended to curb speculation on the baht and damp volatility. 

 The baht also ignored a local newspaper report Monday that the Government of Singapore Investment Corp. has signaled to Thai authorities that it isn't interested in investing in Thailand's matching-fund scheme at present. 

 Hopes that the Singapore government's investment arm would participate in the equities fund had in recent weeks stoked expectations of foreign fund inflows, contributing to the baht's recent strength. 

 Dollar demand by local corporations needing to repay their foreign debt continued to weigh on the Indonesian currency, which was at 9,055 rupiah to the dollar, compared with around IDR8,860 late Friday. 

 In Seoul, the dollar finished at 1,280.1 won, slightly higher than KRW1,278 Friday. 

 On the Philippine Dealing System, the dollar closed at 51.040 pesos, higher than PHP50.935 Friday. 

 The New Taiwan dollar resisted the region's downward draft, finding respite from exporter's dollar sales and sluggish demand for the U.S. currency by importers, dealers said. 

 The central bank had bought U.S. dollars to offset the local currency's appreciation, in Taiwan's apparent bid to maintain the price competitiveness of its exports, dealers said. 


The U.S. currency ended at NTS$34.538, lower than NT$34.554 Friday.

title: Singapore Dlr Up Late; Hits 28-Wk High On Yen, Euro Rise
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was sharply stronger late Friday, hitting a 28-week high against the U.S. currency, as it tracked a stronger yen and euro, dealers said. 

 Around 0830 GMT (4:30 a.m. EDT), the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.7370 - a 28-week low - down from S$1.7473 late Thursday in Asia. 

 The U.S. dollar opened lower in Asia and fell sharply in early trade, in line with its fall below Y119. The euro's rise above US$0.9150 also helped push the U.S. dollar lower against its Singapore counterpart, dealers said. 

 Interbank market participants and a U.S. investment house were the main sellers of U.S. dollars in the morning, a dealer said. 

 Subsequent light U.S. dollar buying by some local banks as well as a European and U.S. bank - suspected to have been a feeble intervention attempt on behalf of the Monetary Authority of Singapore - provided some support to the dollar below S$1.7380, the dealer added. 

 "The dollar-yen looks heavy and therefore the dollar-Sing is also looking soft," the dealer said. 

 Dealers noted that with U.S. dollar stop-loss orders lined up below Y118.50, the U.S. currency could test Y118.30 support later Friday or next week. Such a move would push the U.S. dollar past its initial support at S$1.7350, toward the next support level at S$1.7320. 

 Meanwhile, the U.S. dollar's upside is expected to be capped at S$1.7440, dealers said. 

 Prices of Singapore government bonds were mostly higher Friday, boosted by a stronger Singapore dollar. 

 Bonds opened flat and were thinly traded before lunch with most of the gains occurring in the afternoon session, dealers said. 

 The yield on two-year bonds fell two basis points to 2.18%, while the yield on five-year bonds fell one basis point to 2.87%. 

 At the longer end of the curve, the yield on seven-year bonds fell one basis point to 3.28%, and the 10-year yield fell one basis point to 3.55%.

text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 30 (Reuters) - Asian currencies retreated in 

 early trade on Thursday as the dollar recouped some lost ground 

 after the U.S. reported its economy continued to grow in the 

 second quarter. 

     The government said the U.S. economy grew at a modest rate 

 of 0.2 percent in the second quarter -- its slowest pace in 

 more than eight years and well below a previous growth reading 

 of 0.7 percent. 

     Despite the dollar rebound, some dealers doubted if the 

 latest round of what they believed was dollar correction had 

 come to an end. 

     Merrill Lynch said its recent global investor survey showed 

 exposure to the dollar had fallen to its third-lowest level in 

 the 12-year history of the survey, while investors had not 

 reduced exposure in any other major currency. 

     However, this impact on the yen could be limited due to 

 Japan's economic problems. Its top financial diplomat Haruhiko 

 Kuroda said on Thursday the current yen level was not 

 reflecting economic fundamentals. 

     Since most Asian currencies tracked the yen closely, the 

 dollar correction might have only a mild impact on them as 

 well, dealers said. 

     Elsewhere in the region, the market is eyeing fresh 

 economic data for trading direction. The Philippines will 

 release its second quarter gross domestic product data later in 

 the day. 

     On Friday, Hong Kong will publish its second quarter GDP 

 data, and Thailand will announce its monthly key economic 

 indicators. 


    SINGAPORE DOLLAR



    The Sing dollar ambled aimlessly in early trade, with



dealers expecting it to move within a recent 1.7450-1.7550



range ahead of the European Central Bank's meeting later in the



day.



    The euro carries substantial weight in Singapore's



trade-weighted basket.



    Dealers said news that SingTel           would soon



finalise a deal with Cable & Wireless Optus Ltd could



cap the local currency's upside in the near-term.



    SingTel said on Wednesday its US$9 billion bid for Optus



would be declared unconditional by August 30.



    Although the news has largely been discounted by the



market, dealers said they were not sure how much more the



company might need to buy from forex market to cover the deal.



    THAI BAHT



    The baht edged lower as some U.S. names chased the dollar



from 44.20 in early trade to cover positions after the dollar



perked up overnight.



    But dealers in Bangkok said the dollar was likely to



struggle to breach 44.30 where dollar profit taking and



exporter offers would emerge.



    Baht sentiment remained poor. The central bank on Wednesday



cut its forecast for economic growth this year to 1.5-2.0



percent from a previous projection of 2-3 percent due to a



slowdown in exports.



    Despite the forecast downgrade, the central bank kept its



benchmark 14-day repo rate unchanged at 2.5 percent.



    INDONESIAN RUPIAH



    The rupiah was on the wrong side of the 9,000 mark weighed



down by dollar demand from local corporates for debt



repayments.


Singapore dealers said Wednesday's central bank

intervention to support the currency was likely to keep players



cautious but they added players would continue to test levels



beyond 9,200.



Meanwhile, the benchmark one-month SBI certificates rate



rose to 17.67 percent in Wednesday's auction from 17.61 in the



previous auction. Dealers said that also indicated the central



bank would continue to support the currency.



The auction results came after the IMF warned Indonesia



against lowering interest rates too quickly given a steadily



rising inflation now at above 13 percent.



KOREAN WON -2



With the yen back on the wrong side of 120, the won edged



towards the lower end of its recent 1,275-1,292.1 range where



it has been trapped since August 3.



The won has been caught between a tug of a war between



exporters' dollar sales and fears of central bank intervention.



Dealers said the market was wary of testing the won's upside as



the authorities are believed to be keen on protecting the price



competitiveness of Korea's exports.



Looking ahead, the market was keeping its eye on July



industrial output data and August consumer price index, both



due on Friday.



TAIWAN DOLLAR



Gains on the local stock market and month-end exporters'



dollar sales sent the Taiwan dollar slightly higher.



But the market was wary of central bank intervention after



the bank was suspected of selling U.S. dollars on the market in



late trade on Wednesday.



With foreign exchange reserves of over $110 billion, the


central bank has been active in smoothing over volatility in



the exchange rate.



PHILIPPINE PESO



Local corporate dollar demand was expected to drag the peso



towards 51.30.



But Manila dealers said they suspected the central bank may



seek to protect the currency around that level. They added,



though, the bank was also believed to be buying dollar on dips



through major foreign banks to pad its forex reserves.



"They're keeping it within a band, and trading has come



down to what they can tolerate on the peso's downside," said a



local bank dealer in Manila.



    Still, with import season coming into full swing in



September, dealers said the peso would continue to weaken.



    The market was also watching out for second-quarter GDP



data due later in the day. A Reuters poll showed economists on



average forecast 2.25 percent growth on the year.

title: Asian  Currencies  Mostly Up Late On Yen; Baht Leads Rise
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- Most Asian currencies received a boost from the yen's vigor late Friday, with the Thai baht leading the rise as it snapped out of its recent range to trade at five-month highs. 

 With the yen still ambling in familiar territory, emerging Asian currencies are expected to remain in limbo in the near term, observers said. 

 "There's no clear view, no real trend to pick," said a dealer at a European bank. "You can't go long Asians given the weak fundamentals." 

 At 0855 GMT (3:20 a.m. EDT), the dollar was quoted at Y119.80, little changed from Y119.78 late Thursday in New York, but lower than Y120.31 late Thursday in Asia. 

 The Thai baht grabbed the limelight, as dollar sales by offshore U.S. banks and investment houses triggered stop-loss orders when the U.S. currency broke below THB44.500 and finally THB44.400 - a critical support level that had held up for the most part of day, dealers said. 

 Late Friday, the dollar was quoted at 44.315 baht, its lowest level since end-March. Late Thursday, the dollar was much higher at THB44.630. 

 As the baht found support from the yen and the Singapore dollar, the absence of much-feared intervention by the Thai central bank emboldened offshore participants to unwind their long dollar positions, dealers said. 

 Thai corporates also appeared to have pulled out their bids for dollars from the market, removing a source of support for the U.S. currency, dealers said. 

 "Onshore corporates are net long dollars," said the dealer at the European bank. "It will take a long time before they come in to buy, maybe at around THB44." 

 To a lesser extent, dealers also attributed the baht's advance to remarks by Finance Minister Somkid Jatusripitak that the Government of Singapore Investment Corp. has expressed an initial interest in setting up a joint fund with the Thai government. 

 Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra had suggested to his Singapore counterpart, Goh Chok Tong, during a visit this week to Singapore that the Government of Singapore Investment Corp. consider jointly investing with his government in a Thai equities fund. 

 The equities fund would try to draw foreign investment by matching it with government contributions. 

 The apparent receptiveness to the idea has propelled Thailand's benchmark stock index by 2.3% Friday. 

 Against the Singapore dollar, the U.S. currency skirted around the S$1.7500 level, failing to make much headway below that level, even when the U.S. dollar broke below the critical THB44.400 support against its Thai counterpart, dealers said. Market participants were wary of getting the Monetary Authority of Singapore's hackles up, they added. 

 The U.S. dollar was quoted at S$1.7498, lower than S$1.7560 late Thursday. 

 Exporter dollar sales combined with the yen's resilience to prop up the South Korean won and the New Taiwan dollar, dealers said. 

 But foreign equity outflows - the Taipei stock index plunged 3.4% - and U.S. dollar purchases by Taiwan's central bank wiped out a bulk of the New Taiwan dollar's earlier gains, dealers said. 

 In early trade, the New Taiwan dollar hit an intraday high of NT$34.596 against the U.S. currency. 

 The New Taiwan dollar ended at NT$34.625 per U.S. dollar, marginally stronger compared with NT$34.629 Thursday. 

 In Seoul, the dollar finished at 1,281.20 won, down from KRW1,283.80 Thursday. The threat of central bank intervention tempered the won's advance, dealers said. 

 The Indonesian currency was slightly stronger at 8,690 rupiah per dollar, compared with IDR8,725 late Thursday. 

 Corporate dollar demand dented the Philippine peso slightly, dealers said. 

 The dollar closed at 51.050 pesos, a shade higher than PHP51.000 Thursday.

title: Emerging  FX -Boosted by dlr retreat after Fed's cut.
text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 22 (Reuters) - Asian currencies moved to higher ground with the yen early on Wednesday as the dollar fell after the Federal Reserve cut interest rates for the seventh time this year to boost the U.S. economy. 

 The Federal Open Market Committee lowered its benchmark federal funds rate by a quarter-point to 3.50 percent, as had been widely expected, and indicated it was poised to do more to boost the world's largest economy. 

 "Sentiment has been shifted to one of frustration. People have been trying to walk across the valley to the other side of the recovery and they are just a bit tired. They are now beginning to disbelieve in the recovery because the hard data don't seem to support the recovery yet," said Clifford Bennett, senior currency strategist at BNP Paribas in Singapore. 

 Comments by Japanese Finance Minister Masajuro Shiokawa that he was not considering intervening in the foreign exchange markets for now also sent traders rushing to buy back yen, which they sold earlier due to fears of intervention. 

 Dealers expected the regional currencies to track the yen higher, but with gains capped by Asia's weak fundamentals. 

 On the data front, Singapore is due to release July consumer price data on Thursday and industrial production on Monday. 

SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was weighed by fears of intervention after the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) was rumoured to have been in the market to check rates during London trading. 

 Dealers said the currency was caught between dollar bargain hunting from U.S. and Australian names and offers by funds and other foreign names. 

 They expected its downside to be supported by a firmer yen and the dollar's weak tone. 

 "While (the Sing dollar) was overbought in relation to the worsening domestic outlook, it can still overshoot on the upside given the bearish sentiment for the dollar, although on a three to six month view the Sing dollar is expected to trade in a 1.78-1.80 range," said DBS in a note. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was steadier, beholden to the regional currencies amid a dearth of strong domestic leads. 

 Dealers expected it's upside to be capped at 44.40 for now where corporates were likely to pick up the dollar on dips. 

 The 44.40 level is also a key technical level because it represents the 38 percent retracement of the dollar's February 2-April 9 rise. 

 Baht funding costs were easier offshore, with the tom/next rate quoted at -0.18/-0.17 satang per dollar while the one-month rate was quoted at 1.5/3.0 satang. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won found inspiration in the yen's gains and clambered higher, though falls in local stocks capped its rise. 

 It was quoted at 1,283 against 1,283.8 late on Tuesday. 

 Pessimism over the U.S. economy was also likely to counterbalance the impact of the stronger yen, as the United States is the main destination for Korean exports. 

 While domestic consumption was able to keep the country's economy growing in the second quarter, a central bank official said a recovery in the electronics sector and the U.S. were key to Korea's rebound. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar inched higher along with the won and yen, but was expected to remain within its recent range of 34.50-34.70 because of central bank intervention. 

 Taiwan's central bank has been spotted on both sides of the market to prevent volatility in the exchange rate. 

 Analysts say the authorities want to keep the Taiwan dollar competitive to sell the island's key electronics exports. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso marched in step with the stronger regionals, but local corporate dollar demand below the 51 level was expected to limit its rise. 

 Manila dealers said the market was still suffering from a dearth of dollars, which added pressure on the peso when interbank players covered their short dollar positions. 

 But they said continued dollar sales from the central bank have kept the peso at the higher end of its recent range. 

 The central bank said it was likely to keep rates steady despite the Fed cut at its weekly policy meeting on Thursday. 

 It added that it would consider hiking reserve requirements again. The bank has already hiked reserve requirements by four percentage points to shore up support for the peso by draining liquidity in the market. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was locked in an 8,500-8,550 range in early thin trade as the market looked for fresh incentives. 

 Its downside was underpinned by Bank Indonesia-engineered tight rupiah liquidity, bearish sentiment towards the dollar, and hopes for an agreement with the IMF. 

 President Megawati Sukarnoputri was on her Southeast Asian tour to drum up support for her new government. Diplomats said Megawati's decision to go on a regional tour was aimed at displaying confidence in weathering the troubles at home.

title: Asian  Currencies  Mixed Late Amid Renewed Pressure On Dlr
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- Asian currencies were mixed late Wednesday, as renewed pressure on the dollar helped them sustain their recent gains despite the region's grim economic outlook, dealers said. 

 The Federal Reserve's decision Tuesday to trim short-term interest rates by a quarter percentage point was widely expected, and had little impact on Asian currencies. 

 Instead, the market focused on the Fed's statement accompanying its action, which suggested that the U.S. economy hasn't responded to the central bank's attempts to spur growth. The Fed's latest move marked the seventh cut this year, bringing interest rates to their lowest level in seven years. 

 The Fed also indicated it was more likely to lower than raise rates in the future, saying risks were "weighted mainly toward . . . economic weakness" rather than inflation. 

 "The repeat of the June statement emphasized the fact that business capital spending continues to weaken, suggesting that no upturn is in sight for the high-tech industry that fuels the region's exports," Bank of America said in a report. 

 Repeated verbal warnings by Japanese officials against excessive yen strength did little to offset the pressure on the dollar, which slid overnight following the Fed's announcement. 

 At 0820 GMT (4:20 a.m. EST), the dollar was quoted at Y119.69, slightly higher than Y119.55 late Tuesday in New York. The dollar was at Y120.68 late Tuesday in Tokyo. 

 Despite the yen's resilience, fears of central bank intervention prevented the South Korea won from breaching past KRW1,280 to the dollar, dealers said. 

 In the case of the Singapore dollar, talk of intervention by the local monetary authority overnight kept the U.S. currency supported above S$1.7500, dealers said. 

 In Seoul, the dollar finished at 1,282.70 won, down from KRW1,283.80 Tuesday. 

 After the market closed, the South Korean government said it has reached an agreement to sell large stakes in Hyundai Investment Trust & Securities Co. - and its units, Hyundai Investment Trust Management Co. and Hyundai Securities Co. (Q.HDS) - to a consortium led by American International Group Inc. (AIG). 

 The government's Financial Supervisory Commission will hold a press conference Thursday. 

 The deal is expected to bring $800 million to $1 billion worth of inflows into South Korea, supporting the won, some analysts said. 

 The U.S. dollar's weakness against the yen and the euro failed to inspire the Singapore dollar, dealers said. 

 Speculation by some dealers that the Monetary Authority of Singapore had checked the local dollar's advance when it climbed to as high as S$1.7475 in New York trade Tuesday kept the U.S. currency afloat above S$1.7500 Wednesday, dealers said. 

 The U.S. dollar briefly received an additional boost late in the day, jumping to around S$1.7540, on the Australian government's approval of Singapore Telecommunication Ltd's (P.SGT) A$14 billion-plus takeover bid for Australia's second-largest telecommunications group, Cable & Wireless Optus Ltd. (A.CWO). 

 But the U.S. currency failed to sustain its gains, and subsequently retreated to S$1.7525, weaker than late Tuesday's level. 

 "There were keen sellers around the S$1.7450 to S$1.7550 level," said a senior dealer at a European bank. 

 The Thai baht was the main beneficiary of the dollar's weakness against the euro and the yen, dealers said. 

 The Thai currency strengthened to 44.52 baht per dollar, compared with THB44.745 late Tuesday. 

 After riding on the coattails of the yen's gains earlier in the day, the New Taiwan dollar lost ground as it yielded to foreign equity fund outflows, which contributed to a 1.7% slide on the local bourse, dealers said. 

 The U.S. dollar ended at NT$34.603, higher than NT$34.586 Tuesday. The U.S. dollar had touched an intraday low of NT$34.496. 

 Concerns over Taiwan's sluggish economic fundamentals will likely continue to weigh on the local dollar, observers said. 

 The Ministry of Economic Affairs said Wednesday Taiwan's July export orders sank 16.8% to US$10.8 billion, sharper than the average 14.3% year-on-year drop the market had expected. 

 Taiwan's July industrial output fell 10.4%, compared with a 11.3% decline in June. The data was mostly in line with expectations of a 10.1% drop. 

 Renewed fears of a further increase in local banks' reserve requirements shored up the Philippine peso, dealers said. 

 Somewhat alleviating the market's jitters, Deputy Central Bank Governor Amando Tetangco said later in the day an increase in banks' reserve requirement was only "an option" for draining excess liquidity from the financial system, should it be causing inflationary pressures. 

 The dollar closed at 50.91 pesos on the Philippine Dealing System, down from PHP51.25 Tuesday. 

 The Philippine central bank appeared to have bought dollars as the currency retreated, to replenish its reserves and smooth the peso's volatility, dealers said. 

 Elsewhere, corporate dollar demand weighed on the Indonesian currency, which slipped to 8,650 rupiah to the dollar, compared with IDR8,545 late Tuesday, dealers said.

 early on Friday as fears of intervention by Japan took away 

 some of the yen's strength.

positions on the local stock market's early fall and wariness



that authorities may try to cap the local currency's rise.


Singapore dealers said Thursday's rumours of intervention


after a state-run bank was spotted buying dollars had already



made players cautious.

interest rates stay low. Dealers said most of those factors



had

Monday.

the dollar and people are happy with the positions they have,"



said an NDF dealer in Singapore.
