title: Emerging  FX -Rangebound as dlr bulls pause.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 28 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were trapped in a tight range late on Wednesday as the market took stock of the latest developments both outside and inside the region. 

 An earlier more bullish mood brought about by a firmer yen and surprisingly strong consumer confidence figures from the U.S. proved elusive. 

 U.S. consumer confidence level increased to 117 in March from February's 109.2, and upward revision from 106.8. The average forecast from economists was for a decline to 104.50. 

 "That's the first piece of good news in a long time. But the market will need more evidence to prove the U.S. economy has reached bottom before there will be a meaningful turnaround in Asian currencies," said Syetarn Hansakul, economist at WestLB in Singapore. 

 "In the near-term, I think there is room for further downside for the regional currencies," she said. 

 The Sing dollar went through a choppy session, trapped between fears of central bank intervention and speculation on and actual outflows as funds sold SingTel shares to buy Cable & Wireless Optus stocks. 

 Indonesian rupiah was clouded by political uncertainty, but the downside was capped by central bank intervention. 

SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was a bit out of sync with other regional currencies, hitting 1.7955 - its worst level since August 31, 1998 - after a brief break earlier in the day. 

 It was weighed by speculation of rising dollar demand following SingTel's successful bid of Optus. There was talk one telecom company bought up to US$200 million on Wednesday alone. 

 Dealers said some funds were selling SingTel shares and buying Optus to take advantage of SingTel's options offered to the latter's shareholders. 

 But the downside was underpinned by fears of central bank intervention. 

 "But I noticed people were quick to take profits once the Sing dollar poked below 1.7950. We still think that's the level the central bank could come in to intervene," said a dealer at a European bank. 

 THAI BAHT The baht kept a softer tone as local companies bought U.S. dollars to meet the end-month payment of their U.S dollar loan. One dealer in Bangkok estimated his bank saw them bid at 44.30-33 throughout the day and at least US$10 to 15 million orders were executed to the loan payment. 

 But the baht was refusing to retreat despite such pressure, in part because of the steady yen. 

 Dealers said 44.45 resistance for dlr/baht proved too high as it failed to break for the last two sessions. 

 Also supporting the baht was firmer baht funding cost in the offshore market. One-month forward rate rose to 15/18 satang per dollar from 12/17 on Tuesday. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won edged up as a firmer yen and foreign buying of local stocks prompted trimming of some dollar longs. Dealers said expected month-end inflows from exporters also kept dollar bulls at bay. 

 But the trading range was tight and volumes were subdued amid undented pessimism over the slowing economy and uncertainty over direction of the yen. 

 Korea posted a month-on-month rise in current account surplus in February because of slowing imports, taken as another signal of slowing domestic demand. 

 February industrial production data is due on Thursday. A Reuters poll of 10 economist forecast output to remain flat from previous month, but rise by 5.3 percent year-on-year. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar nudged up in line with gains in the yen and won but its upside was capped by the central bank intervention in an effort to maintain the island's export competitiveness. 

 Japan and Korea compete with Taiwan in several key export markets. 

 Dealers said month-end exporter inflows and settlement of recent foreign buying of local stocks have kept the Taiwan dollar firm. 

 However dealers said there was some caution in the market ahead of the central bank's quarterly policy meeting on Thursday. A Reuters poll of 10 economists and bankers showed all expected the bank to cut the key rates to boost economic activity. 

 The discount rate stands at 4.25 percent while the accommodation with collateral rate is at 4.625 percent. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 Bank Indonesia was heard selling a moderate amount of dollar at 10,400-10,420 in a thin and listless market to support the rupiah which was weighed by political uncertainty. 

 There was also talk that it had asked state companies to sell the dollar on Wednesday if the rupiah dropped sharply. 

 Dealers said the move indicated the central bank was nervous about political development following President Wahid's disappointing response to a parliament censure. 

 Bank Indonesia also guided the benchmark one-month SBI rate higher to 15.58 percent at the auction from 15.24 percent last week to drain liquidity from the market.

 The dollar mustered some strength against the yen amid expectations of further safe haven flows to the U.S. But, with the end of the Japanese fiscal year nearing, the yen could show some resilience thanks to repatriation flows. 

 Analysts said the regional currencies were likely to find some near-term support as the market was long dollars, making it vulnerable to corrections. 

 A steadier yen and possible gains on local bourses following Wall Street's stronger performance on Friday could spark unwinding of long dollars. 

 The domestic front was quiet, with Indonesian and Malaysian markets closed for public holidays. 

 But the Singapore dollar was under pressure after Singapore Telecommunications Ltd. made a formal bid for Australia's second largest telecoms carrier Cable & Wireless Optus Ltd. . However, analysts said most of the hedging for the deal was probably already completed. 

 The euro was still depressed after European Central Bank member Ernst Welteke sounded a hawkish note on Friday, fueling concerns the ECB could be sacrificing growth because of inflation fears. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar recoverd slightly after wallowing beneath 1.7940, a level not seen since August 31, 1998. 

 The latest upset was caused by news SingTel has made a bid for Australia's Optus at up to US$8.63 billion, what would be the largest foreign acquisition ever by a Singapore company. 

 "This is obviously a knee-jerk reaction to news, which is too big to ignore," a European bank dealer said. 

 Dealers said the earlier fall was intensified by stop-loss orders placed at 1.7900 in thin trading. 

 However, the market was wary of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 Charts showed the dollar/Sing was in overbought territory, with a 14-day relative strength index at 80.78. 

 But dealers expected profit-taking would bring the dollar back no further than 1.7850. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was on the defensive, cowering just above 44.46, its lowest level since March 1998. 

 Dealers said the mood was bruised by the Sing dollar, which was nearing all-time lows. 

 Some dealers said the baht came under pressure after the Bank of Thailand said the country was due to repay $700 million to the IMF in the first quarter of this year. 

 But others said the news had limited impact on the currency as Thailand could pay the debt from foreign reserves, as it did in March. 

 The one-month forward rate in the offshore market eased to 22/27 satang per dollar from 39/50 on Friday. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 Indonesian financial markets were closed to celebrate Muslim New Year and will resume trading on Tuesday. 

Currency strategists in Singapore said they expected the rupiah to be supported around 10,500 this week after state-run Bank Restructuring Agency (IBRA) stepped up its dollar sales on Friday to around $40-50 million. 

 IBRA started converting $500 million from recent asset sales on Thursday and dealers expected dollar offers to continue this week. 

 After IBRA converts those dollars, dealers said there was not much the government can do to support the currency. 

 Bank Indonesia governor Sjahril Sabirin said on Friday he was not sure if interest rates would be hiked at the SBI auction this week as the rates were already at a 20-month high. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won weakened on the back of a softer yen, though its downside was likely to be capped by profit-taking on dollar. 

 Analysts said while the won is expected to slip further in the long term due to the yen's poor outlook, the market was still long dollars despite Friday's correction. A turnaround in the yen could spur the market to shed some of its long dollar positions. 

 Korea competes with Japan on a number of exports, making it vulnerable to the yen's movements. 

 In addition, the Korean economy has been showing signs of a sharp slowdown due to increasingly sluggish external demand. 

 The Finance Ministry said on Friday it would follow a low interest rate policy in order to spur growth. The central bank will meet on April 6 for its monthly monetary policy-setting meeting amid growing concerns over inflationary pressures. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso opened lower at 49.25 per dollar in the onshore market compared with Friday's close of 49.135. 

 Dealers in Manila said the currency was weighed by dollar demand from importers, who became more active in dollar buying after it poked above 49.00 as they feared the peso may drop further. 

 Otherwise, the peso's direction mostly hinged on regional currencies, they said. 

Central bank said last week the country's net portfolio investments totalled $23.3 million up to the second week of March this year. 

 February saw a net outflow of $13.7 million compared with a net inflow of $31.40 million in January. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar edged lower in line with the yen, though the central bank was likely to cushion its fall. 

 In addition to the watchful central bank, hopes that the worse was over for U.S. technology stocks was also providing support for the local stocks, and in turn, the Taiwan dollar. 

 However, the market was also abuzz about a possible rate cut from the Taiwan central bank, which said earlier it would hold a board meeting on Thursday. 

 The bank has made three rate cuts since late December, bringing its discount rate and accomodation with collaterol rate to 4.25 percent and 4.625 percent, respectively.

title: ANALYSIS-Singapore dlr fall may force MAS hand.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 26 (Reuters) - A sharp fall in the Singapore dollar to two-and-a-half year lows could soon force the interventionist hand of the Monetary Authority of Singapore - even as it is seen becoming more relaxed about a weaker currency. 

 A struggling Japanese yen, gloom about Asia's prospects this year and the largest foreign takeover by a Singapore company have all helped push the Sing to where the market believes it is close to the top of the acceptable trading band for the MAS. 

 Analysts expect the de facto central bank will make its presence felt if the Sing dollar tries to move past Monday's low of 1.7945 to the U.S. dollar - its lowest since August 31, 1998. 

 "On the normal effective exchange rate basis, the dollar/Sing dollar is moving at the top of its band, and I don't think it will break 1.7950," DBS Bank currency strategist Philip Wee said. 

 "The Authority might come in to intervene." 

 Monday's low came as Singapore Telecommunications Ltd said it was going to spend up to $8.4 billion to buy Australian company Cable and Wireless Optus Ltd - even though it is likely that most, if not all, of the foreign exchange component of the deal was carried out some time ago. 

 SPEED OF FALL A CONCERN 

 It is not only the outright level of the currency but the speed of its fall that has the market on intervention alert. 

 The Singapore dollar has fallen 1.15 percent against the dollar over the last week. In comparison, the yen has fallen 0.65 percent and the Indonesian rupiah has rallied 0.40 percent. 

 "The fall has been very rapid and that's why the market has to be cautious," UBS Warburg currency strategist Mansoor Mohi-uddin said. 

 "No central bank wants to see currency volatility." 

 The Sing is monitored against an unpublished trade-weighted basket of currencies, which include the dollar, the euro, the yen and other regional currencies, to ensure its competitiveness. 

 The MAS intervenes occasionally to make sure that the Sing dollar does not get out of sync with trading partners, both in terms of outright level and the velocity of its moves. 

 But the Singapore dollar is not alone in its woes - the yen has hit 22 month lows, the Australian dollar is at record lows, and the rupiah, Thai baht and Korean won have all fallen to levels last seen in the Asian economic crisis of 1997/98. 

 The Sing is down about 3.5 percent since the end of 2000, which compares favourably with falls of over eight percent in the yen and rupiah, and a 12.5 percent fall in the Aussie. 

 END OF TIGHTENING CYCLE NIGH? 

 The MAS announced on February 22 that it was sticking to its tightening bias to ward off inflation - a decision which surprised some given the global trend to easier monetary policy. 

 At the time, the MAS noted the trade weighted Sing was in the top half of its policy band. It was then trading around 1.7400. 

 The Authority said it would review its stance by mid-year or sooner, and even though the tighter bias could stave off currency volatility in the near term analysts believe monetary policy will soon shift to neutral to help counter weakening external demand. 

 Accordingly, the MAS is expected to become more tolerant of a weaker currency in order to keep the economy growing strongly. 

 Economists polled by Reuters recently forecast economic growth in 2001 of 5.3 percent - just over half the 2000 growth rate of 9.9 percent. 

 "The exchange rate remains Singapore's key counter cyclical tool. In our view, there is an 80 percent chance for a policy shift from gradual appreciation to neutral before mid-year," said Liang Chia-Lian, analyst at Merrill Lynch. 

 "Specifically, we are revising our end 2001 exchange rate forecast to S$1.80 from S$1.76 previously," he said.

 SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--Heavy selling of U.S. dollars by U.S. banks helped the Singapore dollar rebound sharply from a 38-month low early Monday against its U.S. counterpart. 

 Traders say the Monetary Authority of Singapore, the island-state's de facto central bank, wasn't responsible for the rise in the local dollar. Analysts expect the MAS is poised to curb the slide in the Singapore dollar for fear it will spark inflationary pressures. 

 At 0130 GMT (8:30 p.m. Sunday EST), the U.S. dollar was S$1.7890, down from an early high of S$1.7939, a level not traded since January 1998. 

 A chief dealer at a European bank in Singapore said U.S. institutions likely sold U.S. dollars to take profit amid speculation the MAS might step in, and on a "buy the rumor, sell the fact" strategy in relation to Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.'s (P.SGT) takeover bid for Australian-based Cable & Wireless Optus Ltd. (A.CWO). 

 The bid, which was launched Monday, values Australia's second largest telecommunications company at up to A$17 billion, and might require Singtel to exchange local dollars for foreign currency. 

 The trader said there are "no signs" of local banks selling U.S. dollars that would normally be associated with MAS action. 

 MAS indicated recently it would provide foreign currency liquidity to prevent any volatility in the Singapore dollar in the event of any one-time capital flows arising from mergers and acquisitions. 

 This along with a report issued last week by Singapore's DBS Bank, which said MAS might intervene around S$1.7900 unless the U.S. dollar breaks above Y125, is fueling intervention fears. 

 DBS is one of a number of local banks that traders say sometimes act on behalf of the MAS. 

 The European trader expects the U.S. dollar will find support at S$1.7850, and meet resistance at S$1.7950 and then at S$1.8000.

title: Emerging  FX  - Easier on dollar strength, regional gloom.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 23 (Reuters) - Asian currencies eased 

 early Friday as safe-haven flows from bearish equity markets 

 and a weaker outlook for the yen kept the dollar strong. 

     However, weekend short covering in recently battered 

 regional stock markets and wariness of central bank

intervention could prompt trimming of long dollars. 


    A 3.69 percent gain on the technology-laden Nasdaq	  ,



which rose only in the final minutes of trade, heightened hopes



tech stocks have bottomed out and may help lift tech-sensitive



North Asian bourses.



But with the yen expected to test much lower levels and



most regionals facing their own economic and political woes,



players still preferred to take refuge in dollars.



In early Asian trade, the yen was around fresh



22-month lows against the dollar. The euro also looked



feeble after hitting three-month lows overnight on concerns



about euro zone growth after a weak reading in Germany's Ifo



business survey.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH



The rupiah was supported by fears of central bank

intervention and dollar sales by IBRA, which said on Thursday



it had started converting $500 million from recent asset sales.



    Dealers said IBRA sold around $20 million into the market



on Thursday and might be selling again on Friday.



    "The expectation of such conversion is limiting dollar's



upside for the moment as corporates await better levels to



buy," said IDEAglobal.com in a research note.



    "But it will continue to require both the subsiding of real



end-quarter corporate dollar demand and more visible political



stability before dollar/rupiah bias has hope of sustained



reversal," it said.



On the political front, President Abdurrahman Wahid said on



Thursday he had no intention of resigning since to do so might



trigger the break-up of Indonesia.



At least 10 people were killed in the latest round of



ethnic riots in the country's Kalimantan province where



hundreds died last month.



KOREAN WON -2



The won slipped to new 28-month lows as the yen teetered



closer towards 124.



While rising local stocks cheered up gloomy sentiment a



bit, the won's fate still laid in the hands of the yen. Verbal


intervention by officials so far this week has proven



fruitless, as dealers said those comments were not backed by



concerted intervention.



    However, analysts warned of a possible technical correction



for the dollar as the market was long on it.



    Charts showed the won still trapped in oversold territory



with a reading of around 84 on the 14-day relative strength



index.



    Looking ahead, though, analysts were still calling for a



weaker yen. JP Morgan said in a research report it saw the won



bottoming out around 1,330 by end-June, citing the global



economic slowdown, the limping tech sector and weaker yen.



PHILIPPINE PESO



The peso fell in line with weaker regionals, prompting



corporates to cover their future dollar requirements.



Dealers in Manila said there was some profit-taking in



dollars around the 49 level. But with no major factors



supporting the peso, a breach of the level was on cards.



    They said the central bank's monetary easing was further



incentive to mark down the peso.



    The Philippine central bank cut its key overnight rates by



50 basis points effective on Friday.



    The cut takes the overnight borrowing rate to 10.0 percent



and lending rate to 12.25 percent.



    While the bank said it may ease further if the Federal



Reserve continues to cut rates, it added that it was watching



inflation numbers.



    TAIWAN DOLLAR	



    Despite an overnight rise in U.S. tech stocks, the Taiwan



dollar was still playing catch-up with the weakness in the yen



and won.



    While the market shrugged off recent economic data,



analysts said weaker-than-expected export orders and industrial



output in February illustrated the extent at which Taiwan's



economy was slowing.



    JP Morgan forecast in a research report the Taiwan dollar



would reach 33.2 by end-June.



    SINGAPORE DOLLAR	



    The Sing dollar turned tail to hit fresh 31-month lows of



1.7905 overnight, as aggressive local bank selling triggered



stop-loss orders around 1.7860-80.



    Dealers owed the underlying weakness to weaker regional


currencies and to speculation SingTel will seal a



deal to buy Australia's Optus soon.



    The Sing dollar was only getting marginal support at



1.7990, last seen in August 31, 1998. A break of this bulwark



could open the way to all-time lows of 1.8150, hit on January



8, 1998, according to Reuters data.



But a swift and steep slide of the Sing dollar raised fears



of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of


Singapore.



Dealers said the Sing dollar may rebound to around



1.7820-30 as players were likely to take profit on dollar.



Charts showed the local currency was oversold with a 14-day



relative strength index reading of 77.56



THAI BAHT



The baht cowered just above four-month lows of 44.46, with



the government saying the weaker currency was not a cause for



concern.



Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said on Thursday the



baht's weakness reflected a slowing world economy rather than



domestic problems.



    Analysts said repatriation by foreign investors to cover



losses at home and political risk also undermined the baht.



    Thaksin was indicted in December by the National Counter



Corruption Commission for failing to declare some of his



assets.



    If the Constitutional Court upholds the ruling, Thaksin



faces a five-year ban from politics, which could throw domestic



politics into turmoil.



    Baht funding costs offshore firmed to 50/70 satang per



dollar from 20/35 on Thursday.



    Tight offshore baht liquidity and exporters' dollar selling



could provide some marginal support, analysts said.

title: Emerging  FX -Clouded by ailing yen, Wall St gloom.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 22 (Reuters) - Asian currencies retained their bearish tone in early trade on Thursday as investors continue to look for good levels to buy the dollar amid gloom befalling Wall Street and the yen. 

 Dealers said they expected the yen to stay pressured as players take advantage of Japan's ultra-low interest rates, depressing regional currencies. 

 "Overall, the dollar is still pretty well-bid. External and domestic developments argue for long dollar positions," said a dealer at an Asian bank in Singapore. 

 "Some might be taking profits due to fears of potential central bank intervention, especially in Korea and Taiwan, or because the market is a bit long of dollars. But I don't expect the dollar-buying trend to reverse anytime soon," he said. 

 Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs is due to publish data on February export orders and industrial output at 0230 GMT. 

 In January, the island's export orders were down 4.62 percent year-on-year while industrial output fell 13.98 percent on-year. 

 The Philippine central bank is to hold an interest rate-setting meeting later in the day. Its top official said on Wednesday the monetary board was likely to cut key overnight rates by 50 basis points at the meeting. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was faced with the familiar depressing sight of a struggling yen and falling U.S. technology stocks. 

 UBS Warburg said in a research note the market was targeting 1,316, which is close to the 62 percent Fibonacci retracement of the dollar's fall between September 27, 1998 and January 10, 1999 on a weekly chart. The bank said its long-term target was 1,400. 

 But it warned that there was a possibility of a correction on a turnaround in the yen or central bank intervention. 

 While officials warned against further falls in the won on Wednesday, they did not seem to follow through on those comments with concerted intervention. Analysts said the government was likely to tolerate a weaker won, despite inflationary pressures, as Korea competes with Japan on a number of exports. 

 The won's 14-day relative strength index showed the dollar was overbought with a reading of over 75. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was likely to struggle amid a weaker yen and bearish sentiment towards the local bourse after the Nasdaq's overnight fall. 

 However, the market was expecting the central bank to step in to cushion the currency's fall. Taiwan has around $110 billion in foreign exchange reserves, and the central bank interevenes frequently to smooth out any volatility in the exchange rate. 

 Analysts have said despite this intervention, the Taiwan dollar should weaken given a slowing economy and softer yen. 

 Taiwan will release February industrial output and export orders at 0230 GMT. 

 Economists polled by Reuters on average expected industrial output to grow by 10.73 percent on year while export orders are expected to expand by 10.8 percent on year. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 Fears of central bank intervention kept a lid on the rupiah's falls, but strong corporate demand for dollars amid Indonesia's volatile political climate continued to weigh. 

 Bank Indonesia hiked interest rates again on Wednesday as part of ongoing efforts to stem weakness in the rupiah. At its weekly SBI note auction, the benchmark one-month rate rose to 15.24 percent from the previous week's 14.97 percent. 

 On the political front, Indonesia's defence minister Mahfud M.D. said on Wednesday President Abdurrahman Wahid was ready to step down if parliament found he had violated the constitution. But he later backed away from his statement, saying Wahid would only resign if there were constitutional reasons. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar had no reprieve as aggressive dollar buying from British banks and offshore speculators knocked it down to fresh two-and-a-half year lows of 1.7850. Dealers said bears were cautious to push the Sing dollar lower, in part because charts showed dollar/Sing in overbought territory with a 14-day relative strength index reading at 79.09. 

 They said uncertainty over SingTel's bid to buy Australia's Optus and some concerns of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore to support the Sing underpinned the downside. 

 THAI BAHT The baht kept a softer tone after selling from local banks and foreign players triggered stop-loss dollar orders at 44.15, pushing it to four-and-a-half month lows around 44.24. 

 Weakness in the Sing dollar and the absence of exporters' bids for baht were threatening the next technical support of 44.435, the 38 percent Fibonacci retracement level of its steep January 19-April 5, 1998 drop. 

 Offshore baht funding costs firmed, with the one-month forward rate at 12/15 satang per dollar compared with 6.9/9.9 on Wednesday. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso nudged lower against the dollar alongside the yen and other regional currencies, hovering below 48.70. 

 Dealers said the market seemed to have factored in the likelihood of the central bank cutting overnight rates further by 50 basis point later in the day. 

 Despite narrowing interest rate differentials between the peso and the U.S. dollar, the peso's downside should be limited due to improved political sentiment, they said. 

 "If the peso dips further, it would be because of the weakness in the yen and other regional currencies. Domestic situation is quite calm now and that helps," said a dealer at a European bank in Manila. 

 "We noticed that the switching from local peso deposits to foreign currency deposits by locals, which is one of the major factors that affects the peso, has tapered off," he said.

title: Singapore Dlr Sets New 31-Mo Low As USD Advances In Asia
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar fell to a new 31-month low late Thursday as the U.S. dollar continued to advance against most Asian currencies. 

 Around 0812 GMT (3:12 a.m. EST), the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.7870, up from S$1.7810 late Wednesday in Asia, and higher than its previous 31-month high of S$1.7850 reached overnight. 

 Dealers said the U.S. dollar gained on broad-based buying, but its gains against the Singapore currency were capped by fears of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 "I'm very hesitant to buy at these levels because the dollar is looking overbought and I'm concerned about MAS intervention," a dealer at a European bank said. 

 Earlier Thursday, two local banks offered to sell U.S. dollars around S$1.7845-S$1.7850, but the offers were unlikely to have been made at the central bank's behest, a dealer said. 

 "The market's long (and) it would have been vulnerable to a selloff if it had been the MAS," the dealer said. 

 In a research note, Singapore's DBS Bank said the U.S dollar was trading near the upper limit of MAS' undisclosed policy band, and that U.S. dollar bulls should note there's scope for a "substantial downside correction." 

 The MAS manages the Singapore dollar exchange rate against a trade-weighted basket of currencies of the country's major trading partners and competitors. It maintains the trade-weighted exchange rate within an undisclosed band. 

 DBS estimates that the MAS band currently ranges between S$1.7610 and S$1.7880. 

 Unless the U.S. dollar firmly breaches 125 Japanese yen, market participants shouldn't expect it to break above S$1.79 as the MAS may likely intervene around that region, DBS added.

S$1.7800-S$1.7880 range overnight.

text:

title: Emerging  FX  - Mixed after Fed cut, wavering yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 21 (Reuters) - Asian currencies slipped early Wednesday, finding cold comfort from Wall Street's disappointment over the Federal Reserve's rate cut and the softer yen. 

 However, regional currency markets were generally long dollars, especially against the Singapore dollar and Korean won. Any turnaround in the yen may convince players to bail out of long dollar positions, giving Asian currencies a short-term boost, dealers said. 

 The Fed cut rates by 50 basis points on Tuesday, bringing the federal funds rate to five percent and the discount rate to 4.5 percent. It also signaled it was ready to take necessary action at any time. 

 A Reuters poll showed 17 out of 25 primary dealers of U.S. government securities polled after the Fed cut expected another 50 basis point by the next Fed meeting on May 15. For the POLL, double click . 

 But the size of the cut disappointed Wall Street, which had been clamouring for a bigger cut. The technology-laced Nasdaq fell by 4.8 percent, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 2.4 percent. 

 Those falls were expected to pressure tech-senstive equity markets in Taiwan and Korea. 

 On the major currency markets, the yen saw early gains slip away and the euro managed to rachet up more gains against the dollar. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was under pressure at around 1.7740, having hit lows of around 1.7760 overnight. 

 Dealers said underpinning the downside was persistent speculation SingTel might drop its bid to buy Australia's Optus . 

 "But until there is clear news here, the market seems unwilling to offload its large U.S. dollar longs," Mansoor Mohi-uddin, regional currency strategist at UBS Warburg in Singapore, said in a research note. 

 Dealers said some U.S. investment banks were unwinding long positions, piled up in the run up to March 16 highs of 1.7780. 

 The Sing dollar has lost 2.5 percent since the beginning of the year, in part because of the weaker yen and other regional currencies. 

 That, analysts say, lessened the market concerns about possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won opened lower as disappointment over the size of the Fed's rate cut and concerns over the prospect of a U.S. recovery worked through the local stock market. 

 The weaker yen and bearish economic data also weighed on sentiment. Dealers said the won was expected to consolidate in the near term as the market was very long of dollar. 

 "But the dollar's bullish trend is intact. Charts show the dollar/won is still trapped in the uptrend channel which started on February 20," said a dealer in Singapore. 

 The market was unnerved by news of Korea's fourth quarter growth shrinking on quarter for the first time since the second quarter of 1998, the nadir of the Asian financial crisis. 

 Analysts said although Korea may avoid technical recession as its economy is likely to grow moderately in the first quarter this year, its gross domestic product might contract again the April-June period. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht dangled just above the 44.00 level as the market continued to favour the dollar despite disappointment over the Fed's rate cut. 

 Uncertainty over the U.S. economy, the weak yen and Thailand's gloomy economic outlook all kept a lid on the baht. 

 "There's not much good news around. The dollar looks a bit overbought and we spotted some profit taking at around 44.00. But I expect dollar bulls to pick it up on dips to 43.80," said a dealer at an Asian bank. 

 Dealers said the market's reaction to news that the government would unveil a new fiscal stimulus package in April was muted. 

 "Looking at their fiscal position now, I think there's little room for the government to increase its spending. The delay of value-added tax (VAT) increase would stretch the government's coffer a bit," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bangkok. 

 The one-month forward rate was quoted at 6.9/9.9 satang per dollar offshore and -10.50/-10.25 satang onshore. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso eased after the central bank indicated its desire to follow the Fed rate cut with its own. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said he expected the Monetary Board at its meeting on Thursday to ease key overnight rates by 50 basis points. 

 The overnight borrowing rate now stands at 10.5 percent and the lending rate at 12.75 percent. 

 The central bank has cut its key rates by 450 basis points after raising them by 400 basis points in October to defend the weak peso . 

 Dealers said they expected the peso to trade in a range of 48.50-48.80 with the downside capped by expected dollar inflows from exporters. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was holding above 10,500 in a market wary of further central bank intervention. 

 Chief economics minister Rizal Ramli said on Tuesday he had asked the Indonesian bank agency to convert $500 million in asset sales to help the rupiah. He also said he had requested that the central bank act more decisively to support the rupiah. 

 Bank Indonesia has been intervening regularly in the market, either directly or through state banks. It has also recently raised its benchmark one-month SBI rate to 14.97 percent and its intervention rates in the rupiah money market by 50 basis points. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was flat in early trade, as the market puzzled over Wall Street's fall, the indecisive yen, and Taiwan's dimming economic prospects. 

 Charts showed the U.S. dollar was hugely overbought against the Taiwan dollar, with a reading of around 95 at 0047 GMT. 

 However, sentiment towards Taiwan was still bearish given its dependency on exports to the U.S. 

 Looking ahead, Taiwan will release February export order data and industrial output on Thursday. Recent Reuters polls showed economists on average expected a 10.8 percent on year rise in export orders and a 10.73 percent on year rise in industry output.

title: Emerging  FX  - Range-bound ahead of Fed decision.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 20 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were a mixed bag early Tuesday as profit-taking in dollar/yen provided some support but uncertainty ahead of the Federal Reserve policy meeting kept their recent ranges intact. 

 The yen had hit 22-month lows on Monday after the Bank of Japan announced it would set a target of keeping bank reserves at around five trillion yen - a "quantitative easing" that would allow interest rates to fall back to virtually zero. 

 Players heavily long in dollars later decided to book profits as the dollar neared overbought territory on the 14-day relative strength index while speculation increased on how deep the Fed would cut the interest rates. 

 A Reuters poll on Monday showed the market almost evenly split over whether the Fed will cut interest rates by 75 basis points or 50 basis points. 

 The Bank of Japan has been under intense political pressure to counteract deflation after controversially abandoning its zero interest rate policy last August. 

 But skepticism that the move would solve Japan's more serious structural problems would keep the yen under pressure which would keep sentiment dampened for other Asian currencies. 

 The euro was steady with overall trade in majors thinned by a local holiday in Japan. Players in Asian currencies would also tread cautiously ahead of the Fed rate decision. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing Dollar was holding above 1.7700, with the market focusing on the outcome of SingTel 's bid for Australia's Optus . 

 "With the market still looking long of U.S. dollars we are concerned that any withdrawal by SingTel will lead to the U.S. dollar coming off sharply here," Mansoor Mohi-uddin, regional currency strategist at UBS Warburg said in a research note. 

 Bears had piled up sizable U.S. dollar long positions on speculation SingTel would buy the Australian company at around $7 billion. 

 The market was still less wary of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, which threatens the 1.7800 support, dealers said. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was on a healthy tone, holding above 44.00 after offshore players took profits on their U.S. dollar long positions. 

 But analysts said the slowing economy and political risks pointed to a distress for the Thai stock market, thereby for the baht. 

 Dealers said the dollar was facing resistance at 44.150, with a break of this bulwark opening the way to near the November 26 high of 44.435, which also marks the 38 percent retracement of its steep January 18-April 5 1998 drop, on a weekly chart. 

 The one-month forward rate in the offshore market eased to 8/13 satang per dollar from 10/12 in late Monday trading. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won recovered from a fresh 28-month low in line with gains in the yen but trade is likely to remain subdued ahead of the Fed rate decision. 

 Profit-taking in dollar/yen and overnight Nasdaq gains prompted players to trim their dollar longs against the won. 

 Bank of Korea will release the preliminary 2000 gross domestic product growth data at 0300 GMT. A recent Reuters poll showed economists on average expect the Korean economy to have contracted by nearly one percent in the fourth quarter from the third quarter. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO The peso was steady, aided by the steady yen and a mild recovery in January imports. 

 Philippines imports rose to $2.47 billion in January from $2.24 in December but it was still below year-ago levels. 

 Economists said the bounce from December showed a slowdown in exports, due to tapering world demand for electronics products, could soon be reversed, at least temporary. 

 Dealers in Singapore said players were looking levels to sell the U.S. dollar above 48.50, which would underpin the peso. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was down as markets braced for protest rallies planned in the day by supporters of President Abdurrahman Wahid who is facing increasing pressure to step down amid corruption allegations. 

 Fears that the rallies led by the 40-million strong Nahdlatul Ulama, Indonesia's largest Muslim organisation, could add to the violence plaguing the country for the past several months were likely to keep the rupiah under pressure. 

 Analysts said given the political situation, moves like interest rate hikes and intervention in the currency market was unlikely to give a lasting support to the rupiah. 

 Bank Indonesia said on Monday it would raise interest rates this week due to concerns over inflation and added that it had continued to intervene in the currency market to support the ailing rupiah. 

 The rupiah's recent fall through 10,000 to the U.S. dollar has unsettled officials, fearful that imported inflation could raise prices for Indonesia's millions of poor and spark more social unrest across the embattled country. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was hovering close to 32.80, its lowest since January 9 but dealers said rise in the yen and gains in U.S. tech stocks was likely to keep the downside limited. 

 They said expected central bank intervention and foreign inflows in the domestic stocks market, with foreign investors buying T$8.327 billion in the last four sessions was also likely to provide support. 

 However, trade was likely to remain subdued with most players staying cautious ahead of the Fed policy meeting.

title: Emerging  FX  - Languish, with all eyes on BOJ, Fed.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 19 (Reuters) - The dollar dominated Asian currencies early Monday, but was held in check by a cautious market ahead of two key central bank meetings this week. 

 The Bank of Japan will hold a monetary policy board meeting later in the day amid growing speculation it may return to the zero interest rate policy only six months after abandonning it. 

 Whatever the outcome, few in the market expect the yen to benefit as it struggled to stay off 22-month lows. And the euro continued to come up short as the market's concerns over Japan and the U.S. spilled into Europe. 

 There was also some focus on a Washington summit between Prime Minister Yoshiro Mori and President George W. Bush amid Japanese media reports that they were likely to agree to tolerate a weak yen. 

 The U.S. Federal Reserve will meet on Tuesday, and is widely expected to cut the federal funds rate, which currently stands at 5.50 percent. 

 A recent Reuters poll showed the market was split as to how deep the cuts would be, with 13 out of 25 primary dealers of U.S. government securities expecting a 50 basis point cut, while 12 expected a 75 basis point cut. 

 While further easing by the Fed would encourage most regional central banks to continue with their own rate cuts, the outlook for the region remained gloomy given slowing external demand. 

 Last week's OPEC meeting also produced more bad news for Asia as the cartel decided to reduce crude oil production by 1 million barrels a day. 

 With the exception of Indonesia and Malaysia, Asian countries are net importers of oil. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah remained entrenched below the 10,000 mark despite wariness about dollar sales from Bank Indonesia. 

 Analysts said OPEC's decision to cut oil production was a positive development for Indonesia, but added that domestic political worries were likely to keep the rupiah's upside capped. 

 In the latest round of violence to hit Indonesia, at least 10 people were killed in Aceh province after Jakarta vowed last week to carry out a limited military crackdown against separatist rebels in the region. 

 The central bank said on Friday it might further raise key interest rates to ease inflationary pressures arising from the weakening rupiah and reiterated it would keep intervening in the forex market to help the currency. 

 The Asian Development Bank said on Saturday it was prepared to lend Indonesia between $600 million and $1.2 billion a year over the next three years, provided Jakarta pressed ahead with key policy reforms. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar hit fresh two-and-a-half year lows around 1.7765, a level not seen since September 1998, taking its cue from the weaker yen, Aussie and the euro. 

 Dealers said trading was rather thin, making it easier to push the Sing dollar lower. 

 Speculation that SingTel may not reach an agreement to buy Australia's Cable & Wireless Optus as expected, on Monday, added to the Sing dollar's woes. 

 Dealers expected the Sing dollar to return to 1.7730 in the short-term as charts showed it was in oversold territory, with a 14-day relative strength index reading at around 83.63. The market is less wary of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore because the weakness in the Sing dollar has been in tandem with other regional currencies. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso remained the wrong side of 48.00 in early offshore trade, in line with weaker regional currencies and the yen. 

 Markets in Manila were keeping a close eye on the Fed's meeting on Tuesday, as the Philippine central bank has indicated it was awaiting the Fed's next move before cutting rates further. 

 The bank left its overnight borrowing and lending rates steady last week at 10.5 percent and 12.75 percent respectively. 

 The government said at the weekend a planned bond issue backed by future income from state-controlled agencies could raise at least 56 billion pesos to help plug the budget gap. 

 The government is forecasting a budget deficit of 145 billion pesos, and has been told by the IMF that maintaining fiscal discipline was key to ensuring further economic progress. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was a breath away from 1,300 in early onshore trade, weighed down by a softer yen ahead of the Bank of Japan's policy meeting and expectations of a rise in oil prices after OPEC's weekend production cut decision. 

 Korea imports almost all its oil requirements and competes with Japan in several export markets. 

 Analysts said Nasdaq weakness and uncertainty ahead of the Fed meeting on Tuesday were also likely to keep players cautious. 

 Mansoor Mohi-uddin, UBS Warburg's regional currency strategist, said with DRAM prices unlikely to rise much in the near future, the long-term target for the won was at 1,400. 

 Stepping up its rhetoric to help the battered won, the Finance Ministry said in a statement "the won's excessive sensitivity to the movements of other currencies was not desirable", and it was closely watching the market. 

 It added there were no problems with the supply of dollars in the forex market as the trade account was in surplus while more foreign direct investment inflows were expected this month. 

 THAI BAHT The baht was down near four-month lows of 44.00, a victim of the weaker yen. 

 Charts showed the baht in oversold territory, with a 14-day relative strength index reading at 73.61, but dealers expected it to test 44.15 in line with the bruised yen. 

 The market was awaiting the release of fourth quarter gross domestic product data, due later on Monday. 

 A Reuters poll showed the Thai economy was expected to grow around 3.00 percent year-on-year in the fourth quarter compared with 2.6 percent the previous quarter. 

 This would mean growth of about 4.2 percent for the whole of 2000, the same level achieved in 1999. 

 Dealers said any upward surprise in the figures could help trim losses. 

 The one-month forward rate in the offshore market was quoted at 8/11 satang per dollar by 0113 GMT. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR The Taiwan dollar was held hostage to the ailing yen, kicking off the day at 32.73 - its worst level since January 8 - after the yen fell to a fresh 22-month low earlier. 

 Weak DRAM prices also weighed on sentiment. UBS Warburg said DRAM oversupply was likely to drag on until the second quarter as producers seemed reluctant to cut back on output despite global gluts. 

 The market is awaiting February export orders and industrial output data, due on Thursday, for further clues on the state of the economy. 

 Dealers expected the Taiwan dollar to be underpinned somewhat by news of foreign investments rising 40.98 percent in January-February, with major flows going into retail, insurance and publishing.

title: Emerging  FX -Bewitched, bothered, bewildered by yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 16 (Reuters) - Emboldened by the yen's fresh bout of weakness, dollar bulls dragged regional currencies lower on Friday with the Singapore dollar and Korean won suffering the worst blows. 

 With the yen stumbling below the 122.00 level, the won drooped to a fresh 28-month low and the Sing dollar was driven to 30-month lows, hurt by both the yen and struggling euro . 

 Regional currencies were also contending with persistent talk of U.S. funds decamping from local bourses and converting to send funds home to compensate for U.S. stock losses. 

 Given the pervasive gloom hanging over regional currency markets, jawboning by the authorities barely had any impact. The Korean and Indonesian central banks tried to talk up their currencies to little avail. 

 Looking ahead, the market was focused on the Bank of Japan's monetary policy meeting on Monday and the Federal Reserve's meeting on Tuesday. While the Fed is expected to ease its federal funds rate by 50 basis points, speculation is mounting that the BOJ may return to a zero interest rate policy. 

 On the domestic front, Thailand is expected to issue fourth quarter gross domestic product data on Monday. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was trapped below 10,000, despite steady dollar sales from Bank Indonesia (BI) and state banks. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said the central bank was spotted selling a small amount of dollars earlier in the session. State banks were estimated to have sold around $20 million on behalf of the authorities. 

 "Just the same old story, BI tries to sell dollars, but the corporate demand (for dollars) is just too much," said a dealer at a foreign bank. 

 Trading was cautious after news on Thursday that Standard Chartered Bank was fined nearly $900,000 for a breach of forex curbs. The bank said on Friday the fine was excessive, calling the breach operational errors. 

 BI later said it may revise the penalty. It also said interest rates were likely to rise further to curb inflationary pressures stemming from the weak rupiah. 

 At its weekly note auction on Wednesday, the central bank's benchmark one-month SBI rate rose to 14.97 percent from the previous week's 14.83 percent. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar got little solace in afternoon trading and was pinned near 1.7730, just off two-and-a-half-year lows of 1.7740 hit overnight. 

 Its weakness in tandem with the yen and the euro lessened concerns about possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, as both currencies carry substantial weighting in the Sing dollar's trade-weighted basket of currencies. 

 Dealers said the Sing dollar could test as high as 1.78 in offshore market, when bears could take advantage of thin trading conditions. 

 Singapore's non-oil domestic exports for February are due on Saturday. A Reuters poll of 10 economists showed the headline number rising seven percent on the year in February, thanks to a falling currency and a lower base. 

 THAI BAHT The baht was pinned near its day lows around 43.98, taking its cue from the weaker yen. 

 But dealers said dollar offers from Thai exporters lined up around 44 were supporting the downside. 

 The one-month forward rate in the offshore market was 5/10 satang per dollar, down from 8/13 earlier in the day. 

 The bleak mood was further bruised after the central bank suspended an unnamed financial institution from the local repo market for 10 days after it breached currency reporting rules. 

 Analysts estimated the Thai economy grew around three percent in the fourth quarter compared to a year earlier, bringing 2000 annual growth to 4.2 percent. The figures are due for release on Monday. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso finished at its session high of 48.50 after running into onshore dollar sales from a market long of dollars. 

 After gapping down at the open and slipping to a low of 48.73 on the back of yen-inspired weakness in regional currencies, the peso kept within a fairly narrow range. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said the bank was sticking with its peso forecast of 46-48 to the dollar for this year. 

 He added that it was possible for the overnight borrowing rate, now at 10.5 percent, to fall below 10 percent, hopefully in the first half of 2001. 

 Socio-economic Planning Secretary Dante Canlas said gross domestic product growth should average 4.7-5.2 percent in the next three years. He said the GDP forecast for this year remained 3.8-4.3 percent. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won ended not far from a 28-month low of 1,294.5 as the yen's slide prompted offshore players to hedge against further falls in the won. 

 Depressed Korean stocks and dollar buying in the non-deliverable forward market also weighed on the won. The one-month dollar/won NDF was quoted at 1,293/94 in late trade against 1,291.2/91.92 earlier while the six-month was at 1,296.5/98.5 versus 1,294.7/94.95. 

 A Korean government official's comment expressing disapproval of the won's trend of tracking the yen lower failed to lift the currency as it was not backed by actual intervention. The official said Korea was more concerned about a weak won leading to a rise in consumer prices than it was about boosting export competitiveness.

 The Taiwan dollar slipped to a two-month closing low of 32.683 on the back of the losses on the yen and won.

title: FX  ASIA: Weak Yen Holds Singapore Dollar To Ransom
text:
A Dow Jones Newswires Column



SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- Currency contagion pushed the Singapore dollar
to its lowest level since September 1998 Friday, as U.S. dollar bulls
continued to gore the euro, yen and other Asian units.


 With the Monetary Authority of Singapore appearing reluctant to defend it against such strong negative forces, in coming weeks the Singapore dollar will likely continue to be held to ransom by a weak yen, in particular, as the Bank of Japan grapples with its policy options to help avert a recession. 

 The Singapore dollar overnight fell below the psychologically important level of S$1.77 against the U.S. dollar as the yen plummeted below Y122, for the first time since July 1999, on speculation that the U.S. wouldn't resist a weaker yen to stimulate growth in Japan. The euro fell below S$0.90 for the first time since December. 

 After a brief recovery from its early morning low of S$1.7720, the Singapore dollar fell to an intraday low of S$1.7740 at 0712 GMT as banks and companies resumed buying U.S. dollars. This is the currency's lowest level since hitting S$1.7785 on Sept. 3, 1998. 

 A weak Thai baht and Indonesian rupiah - which initially held up around IDR10,000 before falling below IDR10,350, - also contributed to the Singapore dollar's fall. 

 Bank of America currency strategist Simon Flint said that as long as the yen continues to weaken, the Singapore dollar will drift lower, punctuated by brief period of respite, and "we'll see plenty of (U.S. dollar) buying on dips." 

 At the same time, DBS Bank researchers noted that while the Singapore dollar will stay weak, there also scope for a "substantial" recovery if the negative sentiment toward the yen abates. 

 At home, too, there is little news to cheer the Singapore dollar as large government-linked companies eye overseas acquisitions and the domestic economy slows in line with the downturn in the U.S. economy and global electronics demand. 

 On Thursday, Singapore's Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said that while the government is, "for now", maintaining its 2001 economic growth forecast at 5% to 7%, it is closely monitoring global and regional economic developments that have "clouded" the island's growth prospects. 

 "If the anticipated V-shaped recovery does not come about (in the U.S.), there will be rougher times ahead for Singapore and the rest of the world," Lee said, adding that "We also need to watch the global electronics downturn." 

 In a sign of a rapidly slowing Singapore economy, data released late Thursday sowed that January retail sales rose by a dismal 3.8% on-year, lower than analysts forecasts of a 15% to 18% rise, sharply below 19.3% growth in December. The data indicated that slowing consumer spending may knock the government's hope that strong domestic demand will help offset slowing external demand. 

 Given the current external and domestic situation, the island's central bank will most likely keep currency intervention on hold, especially since the Singapore dollar is relatively stronger on a trade weighted basis, Bank Of America's Flint said. 

 The MAS manages the Singapore dollar exchange rate against a trade-weighted basket of currencies of the country's major trading partners and competitors. It maintains the trade-weighted exchange rate within an undisclosed band. 

 According to a DBS Bank research note, the Singapore dollar has likely appreciated 0.4% year-to-date on a trade-weighted basis (or compared with currencies of major trade partners) while having depreciated 2.2% against the U.S. dollar on the spot market. 

 "The point we are trying to get across is that the MAS' policy of a strong (trade weighted) currency doesn't mean that the Singapore dollar must rise in nominal (or spot) terms," said Fong Cheng Hong, head of research at DBS Bank. 

 According to DBS estimates, the U.S. dollar's recent surge has pushed up MAS' policy band to S$1.7540-S$1.7810 from S$1.7310-S$1.7570 at the start of the year. 

 DBS says the policy band can shift to a higher S$1.7590-S$1.7860 range if the yen and euro continue to plunge.

title: Emerging  FX  - Beaten down by yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 15 (Reuters) - Dollar bulls jumped into Asian currency markets early Thursday as dollar/yen pushed towards 121 despite repatriation by Japanese companies ahead of fiscal year-end this month. 

 There was also talk that some U.S. funds are selling stocks in the region and sending money back home to make up for losses in their domestic markets. 

 Sentiment was also hurt by the rupiah, which was struggling the wrong side of 10,000 with intervention upstaged by political gloom and strong corporate demand for dollars. 

 Going forward, dealers expected the regional currencies to trade at the lower end of their recent ranges in the near-term as a turnaround in fundamentals was not likely to happen soon. 

 "The dollar/yen punched through 120 for 121 in New York on Wednesday. That, in combination with persistent U.S. equity jitters, should maintain strongly supportive dollar/Asian currencies environment," said IDEAglobal in a research note. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht slid to 43.79 in early trade, its worst level since January 2, as both offshore and onshore players actively bid for dollars in the wake of the yen's renewed weakness. 

 But it was likely to be supported by high baht funding costs in the offshore market, where one-month forwards rose to 10/13 satang per dollar from 6/9 satang late Wednesday. 

 Charts showed the dollar/baht was still trapped in an uptrend channel that started on February 15. 

 On the fiscal front, Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said Wednesday preliminary estimates showed Thailand may post a budget deficit around 200 billion baht in 2001/2002 Oct-Sept fiscal year against an expected 105 billion baht in the current year. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLARS 

 The Sing dollar lapsed to around 1.7660, after an offshore drop knocked it down to 1.7680, a fresh two-and-a-half year low. 

 Dealers reported U.S. names were selling to repatriate funds. 

 The Sing was also feeling pain from the weaker yen, another stumble in overnight U.S. stock markets, and burgeoning mergers and acquisition activity which entails overseas purchases. 

 Singapore brokerage Vickers Ballas Holdings said on Wednesday it was looking for more acquisitions both in Singapore and elsewhere in the region. 

 Any dire performance by the Straits Times Index would further bruise the mood, dealers said. 

 A local bank dealer said speculation of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore should keep the downside to 1.77. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was the wrong side of 10,000, with little respite in sight. Bid/ask spreads were also unusually wide, quoted at 10,150/300 at 0125 GMT, which indicated a reluctance to trade. 

 Persistent state bank selling of dollars, believed on behalf of the central bank, kept the rupiah away from 30-month lows seen earlier in the week. 

 The rupiah also benefited slightly from expectations that the Indonesian bank agency would convert some $345 million from its sale of palm oil plantations to a Malaysian company. 

 But local corporate demand for dollars amid Indonesia's turbulent political scene continued to pressure the currency. 

 Indonesia also received a warning from one of its major lenders. Tokyo warned late Wednesday that Jakarta's backsliding on reform could hinder loans from Japan. 

 Japan's total aid disbursement to Indonesia up to March 2000 was 3.92 trillion yen. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was likely to feel pressure on the back of the yen's falls. 

 But dealers said the central bank was ready to defend the local dollar to slow its fall. The bank was spotted selling dollars on Wednesday around 32.55, and was expected to come in around 32.60. 

 Given the weakness in the yen, dealers said there was some renewed interest in the Taiwan dollar non-deliverable forward market. At 0036 GMT, the one-month Taiwan dollar was at 0.10/13 and the three-month was at 0.28/31. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 Falls in the yen and the Korean stock market dealt a two-fisted blow to the won. 

 For the past few weeks, the won has been tracking the yen closely as Korea competes with Japan on a number of exports to the U.S. Korea also exports a sizable amount to Japan as well, making the won even more vulnerable to the yen's movements. 

 Meanwhile, the local bourse dropped more than three percent at the open in reaction to significant falls on Wall Street as concerns over a gloabl economic slowdown hit a fever pitch. Any signs of foreign fund outflows were likely to further dampen sentiment towards the won. 

 However, dealers said dollar selling by exporters may help slow the won's decline. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso ceded ground to 48.34 compared with Wednesday's close of 48.20. 

 Dealers say the general weakness in regional currencies, depressing stock markets and solid corporate demand for the U.S. dollars dogged the peso. 

 However, they said the downside was supported around 48.45 due partly to fears of intervention by the central bank. 

 "I don't think BSP would come right away at this level, but any dips on the peso should be met by BSP," a Manila dealer said.

title: Emerging  FX  - Worried by soft yen, regional gloom.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 15 (Reuters) - Asian currencies failed to escape the fury of dollar bulls late Thursday with the yen still faint and the regional outlook remaining decisively gloomy. 

 Despite a bounce in downtrodden Tokyo stocks, concerns over Japan's economic disarray continued to haunt the yen . Ratings agency Fitch placed 19 Japanese banks on negative review on Wednesday, sending investors running for dollar cover. 

 U.S. funds were also reported to be scurrying home after another day of heavy losses on Wall Street, driving some regional currencies lower as they sold off local stocks and converted the proceeds into dollars. 

 Dealers also blamed the weakness in the Indonesian rupiah as damping sentiment towards the region. Local corporate dollar demand kept the ailing rupiah below 10,000, despite wariness over central bank intervention after news Bank Indonesia fined Standard Chartered Bank 9 billion rupiah for violating recently installed foreign exchange curbs. 

 Meanwhile, the euro remained under pressure, faced with not only its inability to capitalise on woes in Japan and on U.S. equity markets, but also falls on European bourses. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was trapped in a tug-of-war between central bank intervention which kept the market cautious, and strong corporate demand for the dollar. 

 Dealers said Bank Indonesia intervened through two state banks which were estimated to have offered up to $20 million before midday. 

 The rupiah was also underpinned by news of the central bank fining Standard Chartered Plc's Indonesian operation for allegedly breaching tough new foreign exchange rules. 

 "That news and wariness of intervention has lent support to the rupiah. People in the market believe the central bank won't let the rupiah fall through 10,200," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Jakarta. 

 "But at the end of the day, you have genuine strong dollar demand, and genuine concerns over a poorly performing leader who refuses to step down. State companies which the government urged to sell dollars are still net buyers," he said. 

 Before the news of the fine spread in the market, dealers said the dollar looked well-bid after local media reported comments by Finance Minsiter Prijadi Praptosuhardjo that the sale of palm oil plantations to Malaysia's Kumpulan Guthrie was not final. He was reported as saying parliament should have been consulted. 

 Expectations that IBRA would convert some $345 million in the market from that sale had helped support the rupiah on Wednesday. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso lurched lower but was still trapped in its recent range, weighed by weak regional currencies and dollar demand from a state utilities company, dealers said. 

 The currency was wedged in a 48.33-48.49 range. Trading volume was relatively brisk, with around $148.50 million traded compared with $66 million on Wednesday. 

 "One state company has been in the market since yesterday to buy the dollar to service debt. The amount was quite big relative to the turnover," said a dealer at a European bank in Manila. 

 The central bank left its key overnight rates unchanged at 10.5 percent for the borrowing rate and 12.75 percent for the lending rate. 

 The bank has cut rates by 450 basis points since December after raising them by 400 basis points in October to defend the peso in the face of a political crisis. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar had little reprieve in afternoon trading, sliding to fresh two-and-a-half year lows around 1.7700. 

 "We've been seeing funds out of New York and Europe sold the Sing dollar moderately to get out of the stock market," a European bank dealer said. 

 The Straits Times Index was off its worst but still near its lowest level since April 1999, having lost around nine percent since the beginning of the month. 

 Dealers said the flow of funds and bleak outlook for the yen pointed to a weak Sing dollar, but fears of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore would slow its decline. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht sank to its lowest level since January 2 as corporate and interbank players continued to buy the dollar in the wake of a weak yen, despite high baht funding costs offshore. 

 Dealers said one hedge fund had been asking around for prices, but it was not clear if it took any positions against the baht. 

Central bank governor Chatu Mongol Sonakul said on Thursday the baht was not depreciating too quickly. His remark was interpreted by the market as implying the bank was not disturbed by the baht's recent losses and would let it fall further. 

 Chatu Mongol also said that one bank had been barred from participating in the local repo market - where financial institutions get cheap funds - for 10 days after it breached forex regulations. 

 Separately, Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said Thailand was unlikely to face another economic crisis and fresh baht instability. But his remark failed to stop the market from selling the baht. 

 The one-month forward rate in the offshore market eased to 6/11 satang per dollar from 10/12 satang earlier, but was still high compared to last week's range. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar fell under the weight of the soggy yen, but the central bank helped it off its lows. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the central bank was spotted selling U.S. dollars around the high of 32.615. 

 Local banks in Taipei quickly followed suit, helping bring the Taiwan dollar back to 32.55. 

 But the U.S. dollar remained well-bid on the offshore non-deliverable forward market, with the one-month at 0.125/140 at 0826 GMT against 0.10/13 earlier in the day. 

 "Investors are taking long dollar positions in the NDFs because the fundamentals for Taiwan are expected to weaken," said a dealer at a European bank in Singapore. 

 Taiwan relies heavily on its high-tech exports and is now faced with a limping technology sector, a slowdown in its largest export market - the U.S. - and a weaker currency for one of its biggest competitors - Japan. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was off its lows but still weak after hitting a near two-month trough of 1,290 per dollar on the back of the sagging yen and early losses in Korean stocks. 

 Dealers said further falls were contained by exporter dollar sales and fears of government efforts to limit the won's slide, as was the case when it hit 25-month lows of 1,293 in January. 

 Bargain-hunting in Korean stocks also cushioned the won somewhat, but with foreign investors selling a hefty 55 billion won worth of local shares, dealers expected it to remain weighed. 

 Labour Minister Kim Ho-jin estimated the unemployment rate for February would be five percent or 1.069 million people, but he expected the number of jobless to fall to 980,000-990,000 in March. February data is due next week. 

 Korea's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate was 4.1 percent in January and 3.9 percent in December.

title: Emerging  FX  - Steady, but bears poised to pounce.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 13 (Reuters) - Asian currencies held onto the stronger end of their recent ranges late Tuesday, though bearish sentiment towards the yen and U.S. equities threatened to knock them over. 

 Dramatic falls on U.S. equity markets overnight grabbed the spotlight, and forced most major regional bourses lower. That added some pressure on regional currencies. 

 Analysts said two consecutive sessions of major falls on the technology-heavy Nasdaq did not bode well for Asian economies and currencies, particularly those dependent on electronics exports such as Taiwan, Korea, and Singapore. 

 "Asia from an external perspective continues to suffer. The chain reaction from the exporters, to producers to domestic economies is already coming through...if anything we've not seen the worst yet," said Craig Chan, regional currency strategist at ING Barings in Hong Kong. 

 Making matters worse, the yen was still out of favour due to concerns over the Japanese economy. 

 While it regained some ground during Tuesday's session, traders attributed this to Japanese firms and banks trying to cover losses by converting proceeds from foreign assets, not to renewed confidence. 

 The euro slipped, unable to make much of the troubles facing the U.S. and Japanese economies. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah found its feet below 10,000 as the central bank and the government showered the market with verbal and actual intervention to prop it up after Monday's slide to 30-month lows of 11,210. 

 Local dealers estimated the central bank spent around $30 million intervening in the market on Tuesday compared with around $12 million on Monday. 

 Meanwhile, chief economics minister Rizal Ramli said the government would support all the central bank's efforts to boost the rupiah. 

 But he said there was no need to impose capital controls or to force exporters to repatriate their dollar earnings. 

 "The intervention makes the market very cautious. There won't be (strong) dollar buying that we saw in the past few sessions for some time," said a dealer at one foreign bank in Jakarta. 

 "But the rupiah would creep lower...gradually because dollar demand is still pretty active," he said. 

 Dealers said the market was unmoved by Foreign Minister Alwi Shihab's comments late Monday, expressing hope about the prospect for progress in talks with the IMF. 

 They said players wanted to see hard signs of progress towards the disbursement of a long-delayed $400 million loan. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar chalked up modest gains in the afternoon to pop above the 1.76 mark, having fallen more than one percent in a week to lows of around 1.7630. 

 The Sing dollar got some solace as the yen and rupiah recouped losses in afternoon trade. 

 Traders also cited dollar sales by local banks, which spurred talk the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) might be intervening to smooth the Sing dollar's drop. 

 They said that was enough for the market to shrug off a distressing three percent drop in the Straight Times Index , but the outlook for the Sing dollar remained less than rosy. 

 "Singapore is the prominent tech economy. A slowdown in the global technology cycle should contribute to downward momentum in the first and second quarter," a European bank analyst said. 

 This might encourage the MAS to shift its monetary policy bias to neutral from tightening, he added. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht rose and held above 43.70 as the calmer yen and rupiah gave investors a much-needed excuse to pare their very long dollar positions. 

 But it ran into resistance from offshore and onshore dollar buying at around 43.62, dealers said. 

 The market reacted cooly to a newspaper report that Thailand and Japan were close to concluding a bilateral currency swap agreement in the next few months. 

 "Perhaps investors might need more details to determine what kind of implications the agreement would have on the market," said a dealer at a local bank in Bangkok. 

 The offshore one-month foreward rate eased slightly to 4/9 satang per dollar from 6/10 satang earlier as players unwound their dollar holdings. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was wedged in a narrow 48.10-48.21 range, tracking regional currencies in the absence of strong local leads. 

 It finished at 48.16 in the onshore market on Tuesday, slightly off its opening 48.15 and Monday's close of 48.145. 

 Market turnover was moderate, with $130.80 million traded compared with $138.8 million on Monday. 

 On the political front, President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo said new peace talks between the government and the communist National Democratic Front (NDF) would start on April 27. 

 Meanwhile, a local newspaper reported that the government expected tax enhancement measures and higher earnings from privatisation to bring the estimated budget deficit of 145 billion pesos down to 80 billion pesos. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won managed to recoup some lost ground as the yen fended off 20-month lows. 

 That spurred unwinding of long dollar positions, helping the won off a day low around 1,284. 

 Dealers said the dollar faced stiff resistance around 1,290 - a level it last hit on January 18 - as exporters were looking to sell dollars below that level. 

 However, with uncertainty lingering over the yen's outlook and the Korean economy, analysts said the won still faced an uphill battle in the coming months. 

 "With the U.S. economy likely to experience a U-shaped recovery rather than a V-shaped rebound, Korea's ecconomy will continue to slow," said UBS Warburg in a research note. 

 It has a near-term forecast for the won of 1,300 and a long-term forecast of 1,400. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar succumbed to the yen's recent losses and faltering regional currencies. 

 While the tech-heavy stock market resisted the Nasdaq's fall, the local dollar was under pressure from foreign fund outflows. Dealers in Taipei estimated that the foreign exchange market saw an outflow of around US$100 million on Monday. 

 Dealers in Singapore said Taiwan's central bank was spotted defending the local dollar past 32.50. 

 "Around here is going to be a little tough (for the U.S. dollar)," said a dealer at a U.S. bank. "If the yen manages to strengthen a little from here, we're going to have a hard time." 

 Chartists pointed out that the 14-day relative strength index for the Taiwan dollar showed the U.S. dollar was overbought, with a reading of around 85 at 0823 GMT.
