title: Emerging  FX  - Struggling along as good news eludes.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 13 (Reuters) - Asian currencies dragged their feet lower in early trade on Tuesday as the beleaguered yen and the battered Indonesian rupiah undermined regional sentiment. 

 The yen, already down 3.0 percent against the dollar this month, pushed to a fresh 20-month low overnight on mounting political uncertainty and Japan's bleak economic outlook. 

 In Indonesia, fears of central bank intervention could provide some support for the rupiah, but in the absence of fundamental change, analysts said they did not expect to see a meaningful turnaround soon. 

 The country's impasse with the IMF involving $400 million in vital funds is far from being resolved. This could jeopardise a $5.8 billion debt rescheduling deal with the Paris Club of official creditors. 

 A fund spokesman said in Washington that it expected to have future discussions with Indonesian authorities but there were still some major issues to be overcome. 

 Analysts and dealers expect regional currencies to retain their bearish tone in the near-term. 

 "Looking forward, we continue to be most bearish on the yen. For Asian currencies, we remain bearish especially on the baht, and the rupiah," said a DBS report. 

 "The Sing dollar will continue to face downward pressure due to a weaker yen and regional currencies," it said. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was underpinned by fears of intervention by the central bank which jumped in to sell up to $12 million in the market on Monday to shore up the sagging currency. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the market was also cautious that the central bank might soon tighten its grip on foreign exchange trading to halt a slide in the rupiah. 

 "I doubt very much if Bank Indonesia would resort to full-fledged capital controls. They might instead do something to force exporters to sell their dollars. The market seems a bit cautious at this point," said a Singapore dealer. 

 "Otherwise, the rupiah could creep lower...it could reach 12,000 because there is no good news whatsoever either from the economic or political front," he said. 

 The Indonesian central bank has repeatedly said it is committed to a free exchange rate regime. 

 President Abdurrahman Wahid, whose leadership is being heavily criticised, said on Monday he would not step down, adding that the country would fall apart if he did. 

 Although Indonesia's spat with the IMF drags on, many believe the Fund will not abandon the country. However, it is expected to stick to its guns on reforms. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht pushed below the 43.70 mark alongside other regional currencies as foreign names bought dollars in both spot and forward markets. 

 Dealers said the baht might soon test 44.00 but not without rounds of dollar profit-taking. The dollar was looking overbought with a reading of 76 on the 14-day relative strength index. 

 But it should find some support at around 43.50 where the market is likely to buy the U.S. currency on dips, dealers said. 

 "There is no strong local lead at the moment, so the baht seems to be tracking the regional currencies. The weaker yen and the ailing rupiah have spurred dollar demand and hedging activity," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in Singapore. 

 The one-month forward rate was quoted at 1/3 satang per dollar offshore and -11.5/-9.0 satang onshore. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar kept a softer tone to stay just below a three-and-a-half month low of 1.7620. 

 Dealers said investors unloading the Sing dollar because they expected local equities to follow the U.S. stock markets, which again took a dive on Monday. 

 Weakness in regional currencies and the euro compounded its woes, they added. 

 "We see various parties are selling. Singapore, Hong Kong, Tokyo, everyone," a European bank dealer said. 

 Dealers said 1.7690 was now within sight, a level not seen since September 1998. 

 Analysts said the market was not too concerned about the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) intervening to support the Sing dollar, given that its decline was in line with weakness in the currencies of its trading partners. 

 One analyst said there was growing speculation the MAS would revise their stance to neutral from a tightening bias soon, which meant the central bank would guide the Sing dollar lower. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was depressed by losses in the local stock market, the weaker yen, and poor economic data. It opened at 1,284.0 against Monday's close of 1,278.4. 

 The benchmark KOSPI , whose performance usually affects sentiment in the currency market, shed 3.14 percent at the open as investors were unnerved by hefty losses in the Nasdaq overnight.

title: Emerging  FX  - Depressed by yen, rupiah wretched.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 12 (Reuters) - Asian currencies started the the week on a glum note as doubts over the leadership in Japan and Indonesia came to a head, battering the yen and the rupiah. 

 The rupiah fell past 11,000 for the first time since September 24, 1998 as companies and banks rushed to buy dollars amid mounting concern about the political and economic outlook. 

 Analysts predicted it could slide further, barring capital controls or a significant improvement in the political situation. 

 "If the rupiah continues to go at its current pace, I think the government would come up with fresh measures...ie, one form of capital control or another. In that case, it could pick up to around 10,000," said Andrew Fung, head of Asia Pacific treasury research at Rabobank. 

 "Barring that, there is a possibility that it could go to 13,000. I still think the rupiah should trade above 10,000, but sentiment is driving market dynamics at this point," he said. 

 The Thai baht traded at the lower end of its recent range as good news on the national asset management company, soon to be established to tackle non-performing loans, was clouded by the yen and the rupiah. 

 The Sing dollar slipped past 1.7600 which had been expected to be the Monetary Authority of Singapore's intervention threshold, sparking speculation it could test 1.7650. 

SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar trailed off to three-and-a-half month lows of 1.7620 to the dollar on relatively healthy turnover. 

 Weakness mainly owed to the Indonesian rupiah, which tends to move the Sing dollar when it moves sharply. Singapore and Indonesia have traditionally had close investment ties. 

 Dealers said the lagging stock market following the Nasdaq sell-off and the weaker yen dampened sentiment. They added that Sing dollar selling partly owed to talk of Singapore Telecommunications making a bigger-than-expected bid for Cable and Wireless Optus . 

 Dealers said the Sing dollar was unlikely to fall much beyond 1.7620, a low last seen in late November, due to jitters over intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso trimmed losses to end at around 48.07 per dollar, having fallen to around 48.25 earlier in the day. 

 "That was a knee-jerk reaction to the falling rupiah and the yen. But the sell-off didn't last because we have a relatively stable economy and now the political situation is better off," a trader at a local bank said. 

 He added the peso should settle into a snug range of 47.00 to 48.50 in the short term. 

 "We need to see a firmer stock market, more offshore demand and more foreign investment for the currency to break the range trading," he added. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won continued to be weighed by weakness in the yen and declines in local stocks, gapping down at the open and hitting a an early low of 1,280.1. 

 Exporter and state bank dollar sales near that level kept it from falling any further but dealers expected limited upside as foreign investors remained net sellers of Korean equities for the third straight session. 

 The benchmark KOSPI ended 3.66 percent lower as foreigners unloaded tech shares following the Nasdaq's 5.35 percent drop on Friday. Bank shares were also sold on disappointment with a decision by Korean creditors to support the cash-starved Hyundai Group. Data released on Monday offered little cause for cheer, with the current account surplus almost halving on the month in January to a provisional $684.4 million. 

 Analysts said the faltering semiconductor sector, a main export segment, would keep pressure on the economy. 

 J.P. Morgan said it would cut its 2001 growth forecast for Korea to 3.5 percent or lower from four percent as weakness in the electronics sector remained a concern despite improvements in consumer and business sentiment and industrial output. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah hit a 30-month trough, before verbal and actual dollar-selling intervention by Bank Indonesia prompted a bounce. 

 Mounting concerns about the government's inability to contain ethnic violence and revive the economy, and the fate of IMF loans spurred dollar demand from banks and local companies in a thin market. 

 News of the closure of three gas fields by Exxon Mobil Oil Indonesia in northern Aceh on Friday due to security concerns added to the gloom as the Indonesian economy relies heavily on oil and gas exports. 

 The rupiah extended losses after deputy central bank governor Anwar Nasution said BI had limited ability to defend it. 

 That remark was later countered by another BI deputy governor who said the central bank would continue intervening to support the currency and had adequate reserves to do so. 

 Dealers said BI backed its comments with actual dollar sales worth around $5-$10 million, causing the rupiah to bounce above the 11,000 level. 

 "It's almost a one-way market. Bank Indonesia and state banks were among few dollar providers. Exporters are not selling," said a Jakarta dealer. 

 "If it goes on like this, I bet the central bank will do something. I don't think it will be a capital control. They might be looking into ways to force exporters to bring in dollar revenues," he said. 

 Chief economics minister Rizal Ramli said 8,000 was an acceptable level for the rupiah. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was wedged in a narrow 43.55-43.75 range. Investors were reluctant to take profits on the dollar due to gloom in the rupiah and the yen, but they were not willing to build on their already long dollar positions either. 

 The market welcomed news that the soon-to-be-established national asset management company would buy up to 250 billion baht ($5.74 million) of bad loans from private banks at book value net of loan loss reserves. 

 It had earlier said it might absorb as little as 120 billion baht at discounts. 

 "The news seems to be benefitting bank and finance shares more than the baht. I guess people will be watching how efficient and transparent the AMC is and the rate of loan recovery," said a dealer at a European bank in Bangkok. 

 "The baht didn't move much today. The market is already pretty long of the dollar, but at the same time there is no compelling reason to buy the baht either," he said. 

 Baht funding costs offshore nudged up, with the one-month forward rate rising to 1.5/2.5 satang per dollar. TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar slid to its lowest level since January 30, edging closer to 32.50 per dollar on declines in local stocks and a depressed yen. 

 The market was keen to test its downside after Friday's close below 32.40, which prompted speculation the central bank had moved its line of defence back to 32.50. 

 Taiwan shares ended lower for the third straight session as heavyweight electronics shares were hurt by the Nasdaq's drop.

title: US Dollar Above S$1.76; First Time Since Nov 27
text:
- - 12/03/01 03-58G



0358GMT


 SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--The U.S. dollar rose above S$1.76 Monday - the first time since Nov. 27 when it hit a high of S$1.7608, dealers said. 

 The U.S. dollar's gains against the Singapore currency follows its rise above 11,000 Indonesian rupiah and Y120. 

 "Everybody is buying (U.S.) dollars and I don't rule out reaching S$1.77 later today and S$1.78 near term," a dealer at a European bank in Singapore said. 

 At 0415 GMT (11:15 p.m. EST Sunday), the U.S. dollar was at S$1.7616 - its highest level since reaching S$1.7785 on Sept. 9, 1998. 

 Dealers said there were no signs of either the Monetary Authority of Singapore or local banks selling U.S. dollars to stem the local currency's decline. 

 Dealers said that U.S. dollar's 13% rise against the rupiah Monday and the possibility that it may rise above Y121 later in the day are the likely reasons why the MAS has so far refrained from defending the local dollar. 

 Last week, the MAS said it would intervene to smooth out volatility in the Singapore dollar, particularly if the weakness arises from merger and acquisition outflows, such as Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.'s (P.SGT) A$17.5 billion bid for Australia's Cable and Wireless Optus (A.CWO). 

 A DBS Bank research note, issued earlier Monday, provides possible clues for lack of any MAS action so far to defend the Singapore dollar. DBS said that any intervention by the central bank will help curb short-term volatility, "but won't preclude a further weakening of the domestic currency." 

 The government-linked bank, which is also Singapore's largest, said that with weak economic data expected in the first half of this year, the Singapore dollar's value will largely be determined by the regional currency situation and U.S. dollar demand from large Singapore companies seeking to acquire overseas assets. 

 The European bank dealer said that if the U.S. dollar succeeded in staying above S$1.7620 during the remainder of Asian trading Monday, it could break the S$1.7650 resistance level and possibly test S$1.77 during London trading. 

 "We expect a surge in buying when London comes in later," he said. 

 A break above S$1.77 could, in the near-term, propel the U.S. dollar to S$1.78 - a level not seen since August 1998. 

 At 0529 GMT (12:59 a.m. EST), the U.S. dollar was quoted at S$1.7635.

title: Bank Indonesia  intervenes  directly to buy rupiah.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 9 (Reuters) - Bank Indonesia intervened directly in local currency markets on Friday, selling an estimated $20 million to defend the rupiah around the 9,920/30 level, dealers in Jakarta said. 

 "We saw Bank Indonesia intervening directly in the market this morning at 9,920/30," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Jakarta. 

 "There's genuine demand for dollars out there, and Bank Indonesia is the only supplier of dollars in the market. There are no other suppliers," he added. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said several state banks were also spotted in the market selling dollars. State banks have tended to sell dollars on behalf of the central bank in recent sessions. 

 The rupiah was quoted at 9,935/45 to the dollar at 0211 GMT, against levels of about 9,925 late on Thursday. 

 Heavily indebted local companies have been buying dollars in order to repay or service foreign debt. 

 Dealers have noted that buying has picked up steam in recent sessions as the end of the first quarter approaches and amid growing worries over Indonesia's shaky political and economic outlook.

 The U.S. dollar's recovery from its intraday low was also aided by buying likely related to government-linked Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.'s bid for Australia's Cable & Wireless Optus, dealers said. 

 "The dollar/sing is looking quite well bid and I won't be surprised if it tests S$1.7600 tonight because no one wants to go short into the weekend, especially with the rupiah tanking," a dealer said. 

 However, market participants will be cautious in bidding up the U.S. dollar after the Monetary Authority of Singapore's said earlier this week that it would intervene to smooth out currency volatility arising from merger and acquisition related activities, dealers said.

title: Emerging  FX  - Clouded by yen, outlook bearish.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 8 (Reuters) - The beleaguered yen towered over Asian currencies in late trade on Thursday, prompting more analysts to revise down their near-term regional forecasts. 

 The yen remained weak but was off fresh 20-month lows hit earlier in the day after Finance Minister Kiichi Miyazawa said Japan's fiscal condition was on the brink of collapse. 

 Although it managed to poked above 120 in late trade and lifted most currencies from their intraday lows, overall sentiment remained bearish. "A weak yen policy would trigger a new round of competitive depreciation, given the high dependence on external demand and electronics in the region," said Gerard Teo, economist at ABN AMRO Bank. 

 "We have modestly adjusted the currency forecast profiles for some regional currencies given the weaker yen," Teo said in a report issued on Thursday. 

 ABN AMRO lowered its end-March forecast for the Korean won to 1,280 from 1,250 previously, and for the Taiwan dollar to 32.50 from 32.00. 

 The Indonesian rupiah slid to 9,915 - its worst level since October 7, 1998 - as robust corporate demand for the dollar outweighed offers by state banks. 

 The Philippine peso was briefly jolted by the central bank's 50-basis-point rate cut, but managed to stand above the 48 level. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso ended virtually unchanged from Wednesday's close, but sentiment towards the currency was fraying. 

 Dealers in Manila said it dipped in line with the yen and the Thai baht, adding there was still a perception in the market of the similarities between the Thai and Philippine economies. 

 While many dealers were still expecting the peso to appreciate due to the better political climate, they said the bearish sentiment towards regional currencies was catching. "The peso was starting from a weak position, anyway," said a dealer at a European bank in Manila. 

 The central bank's decision to cut rates did surprise some in the market. While the bank was widely expected to ease rates in the future given the slowing economy, some players were expecting the rate cut after the Federal Reserve's meeting on March 20. 

 The Philippine central bank cut its key overnight borrowing and lending rates by 50 basis points, bringing them to 10.5 percent and 12.75 percent respectively, effective from Monday. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar revisited overnight lows around 1.7595 to the U.S. dollar on broad-based selling in light of the yen's fall. 

 The yen is believed to make up between 10 and 15 percent of the trade-weighted basket of currencies against which the Singapore dollar is managed. Dealers said a breach of 1.7595, which the Sing dollar has touched thrice but not broken since November 27, could expose it to further losses towards its late November lows at 1.7615/20. 

 But that level was expected to be a firm support unless the yen weakened radically as the Sing dollar has not slipped beyond that point since September 1998. ABN AMRO left its end-March forecast for the Sing dollar unchanged at 1.75, but revised its end-June forecast to 1.76 from 1.74 previously in light of the weaker yen. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was lower after another session spent tracking the yen's fading fortunes. 

 Korea and Japan compete on a number of exports, especially those headed for the U.S., which makes the won beholden to the yen's movements. 

 However, despite the yen's breach of 120, the won's losses were capped in a market already heavily long of dollars. Dollar profit-taking helped the won off its day low of 1,279.0. 

 Chartists said the dollar was bumping against the 70 mark on the 14-day relative strength index, easing slightly from an over 70 reading earlier in the day. 

 The market took in stride the Bank of Korea's decision to hold its key overnight call rate steady at five percent for March. The move was widely anticipated, though analysts said they expect further rate cuts given Korea's slowing economy. TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar fell back slightly on the back of the yen's losses, but stayed above the 32.40 mark thanks to intervention by the central bank. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the bank was spotted in the market selling U.S. dollars when the local dollar slipped past 32.40. A dealer at a U.S. bank in Singapore estimated the bank spent around $100 million in its defence on Thursday. 

 ABN AMRO cited the weaker yen, less aggressive easing by the central bank than originally expected and slowing foreign fund inflows as reasons for its lowered Taiwan dollar forecasts. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah hit its lowest level since October 7, 1998 as political and economic gloom spurred corporate demand for the dollar which outpaced offers from state banks. 

 Dealers said the country's mountain of debt, social unrest, problems at the central bank, political disunity, and deepening conflict with the IMF continued to weigh on sentiment. 

 On the macro front, Salomon Smith Barney said Indonesia's weak imports of capital goods and some raw materials signalled a poor economic outlook. 

 "Recent depreciation of the rupiah has not helped exports to rebound, but has hurt imports," it said in a report. 

 But it expected inflation to creep up in March and April on the back of bad weather conditions, the government's imposition of sales tax on luxury goods, and upcoming adjustments to domestic fuel prices. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht crawled above 43.60 as high baht funding costs offshore forced some players to unwind long dollar positions. 

 The one-month offshore forward rate rose to 5/7 satang per dollar earlier before easing to 3/6 satang on the back of dollar offers. Onshore rate of the same tenor was slightly firmer at -10.25/-9.75 satang. 

 But dealers said the baht was unlikely to firm beyond 43.40 this week given keen demand to buy the dollar on dips. 

 On the political front, Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said on Thursday he knew who was behind the bombing of a Thai Airways plane he had been due to board, but the mastermind might never be caught due to a lack of evidence. 

 News of the explosion dampened baht sentiment earlier this week as some foreign investors believed the incident raised Thai political risk.

title: Emerging  FX  - Steady, thanks to dearth of factors.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 7 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies were enjoying a breather early Wednesday amid a dearth of fresh factors and dull activity on the major currency markets. 

 However, that calm may be broken later in the day with the Thai government set to announce the details of its planned asset management company. Optimism over the AMC was damped recently after reports that it would fall short of initial promises. 

 The yen , which had been the dominant factor in regional markets in recent sessions, see-sawed in early trade. While most analysts are calling for a weaker yen in the coming months, it was drawing support from exporters' dollar sales, fund repatriation, and a market already long of dollars. 

 Meanwhile, the euro held onto most of its gains from overnight trade. 

 The technology-heavy Nasdaq's 2.87 percent rise may lift sentiment towards North Asian bourses, with possible spillover for their currencies if foreign investors turn up. Foreign funds bought substantial amounts of Korean and Taiwan shares on Tuesday. 

 On the data front, Taiwan will release its February trade balance at 0245 GMT. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah did not stray far from its levels of late Tuesday, though local corporate dollar demand was expected to pressure it. 

 Dealers in Jakarta have said state banks have been selling dollars in order to cap the rupiah's slide. 

 Jakarta markets received a rare bit of good news on Tuesday when an Economics Ministry official said a team from the IMF was expected to arrive on Thursday. 

 Talks between the IMF and Jakarta have been deadlocked recently over issues ranging from central bank independence to regional autonomy. A mission from the IMF would be an important first step for Jakarta in securing the release of a delayed $400 million loan from the Fund. 

 Bank Indonesia said late Tuesday it was closely monitoring the offshore rupiah non-deliverable forward market. The bank's governor Sjahril Sabirin added that the impact, so far, has not been worrying. 

 At 0043 GMT, the one-month NDF rate was quoted at 10,000/10,050 while the six-month was at 10,650/10,850. 

 Dealers in Singapore said volume had picked up in recent weeks, though trading was still cautious due to wariness over Bank Indonesia. A dealer at a U.S. bank said interbank players were continuing to deal with transactions of no more than $2 million, which was one of the terms banks originally agreed upon at the market's creation. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar nudged up as players returning from a holiday on Tuesday decided they were too long of dollars. 

 With the yen and Thai baht steadying, dealers said the market was looking to take profits on the dollar around 1.7560/80. 

 The Sing dollar was also supported by Tuesday's local press report quoting the Monetary Authority of Singapore as saying it was prepared to intervene in the market to balance out any impact of local companies buying assets overseas. 

 "The market is pretty long and there is no strong incentive at this point to further add the dollar to those positions," said a dealer at an Asian bank. 

 "Having said that, there are lots of people out there who would seek to buy the dollar if it dips to 1.7530-1.735. I bet the market will move in a narrow 1.7530-1.7580 range in the near-term," he said. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won opened higher at 1,262.9 compared with Tuesday's close of 1,264.8 as sentiment was boosted by the steadier yen and gains in the stock market. 

 Foreign investors bought a net 32.5 billion won worth of local shares in early trade on Wednesday. 

 However, dealers said the inflows to the stock market were likely to have limited direct impact on the won as more and more investors were seeking to hedge their positions in the belief economic troubles in Japan would pull the won lower. 

 The market is focused on the central bank's policy meeting on Thursday. Nine of 10 economists polled by Reuters predicted the bank would leave its short-term rate target unchanged. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The Thai baht firmed as players covered short positions ahead of the government's annoncement of its AMC plan. 

 Initial news of the AMC plan had bolstered local markets, but recent reports of the plan falling short of initial promises have left some investors disappointed. 

 Moreover, dealers in Singapore said sentiment towards the regional currencies, including the baht, was still bearish. They added 43.20 was still strong support for the dollar. 

 Chartists said dollar/baht had been in an uptrend channel since February 13, and a break below 43.20 would move it out of that channel. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was slightly stronger on the back of improving sentiment over the island's tech sector. 

 At 0118 GMT, local stocks were up 2.12 percent, following the Nasdaq and Philadelphia Semiconductor Index's gains overnight. Dealers said foreign fund inflows have provided major support for the local dollar. 

 Dealers in Taipei said the central bank was spotted in the market on Tuesday buying U.S. dollars to cap the local dollar's gains. With a fragile yen and a weaker yen, analysts said the authorities were likely to become more concerned with Taiwan's export competitiveness. 

 Taiwan will issue its February trade balance at 0245 GMT. A recent Reuters poll showed economists on average expect Taiwan to post a US$25 million surplus against US$546 million in January. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was quoted at around 47.61/47.67 in early trade in a quiet market, with no deals done more than half an hour after the domestic open. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said on Wednesday he saw the peso averaging 46 per dollar if the U.S. economy could achieve a soft landing. He did not provide a time frame. 

 Salomon Smith Barney said in a report there was scope for the peso to strengthen to 46 if the outcome of the May congressional election favoured President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo. 

 Analysts said with the steadier peso, the central bank was likely to cut its key overnight rates further - a move that could drive the benchmark 91-day T-bill rate below 10 percent. The next monetary policy meeting is on Thursday.

title: Singapore Dlr Lower In Late Trade; Mirrors Weaker Yen
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was lower against its U.S counterpart late Wednesday, mirroring a weaker Japanese yen, dealers said. 

 Around 0907 GMT (4:07 a.m. EST), the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.7571, up from S$1.7536 late Monday in Asia. It traded in a S$1.7544-S$1.7572 range Wednesday. 

 Singapore's markets were closed Tuesday in observance of the Hari Raya Haji, a Muslim festival. 

 The U.S. dollar opened higher but fell in opening trades on selling by a large local bank. But it soon recovered and rose in line with its gains against the yen, dealer said. 

 The U.S. dollar is expected to remain bid in the wake of a weak yen and on foreign exchange outflows to fund acquisitions by large Singapore companies. 

 However, the U.S. dollar isn't likely to be bid sharply higher following a recent statement by the Monetary Authority of Singapore that it will intervene in the foreign exchange market to smooth out volatility arising from merger and acquisition-related outflows. 

 Dealers said they expect the U.S. dollar to trade in a S$1.7530-$1.7580 range overnight. 

 On the bond market, prices of Singapore Government Securities ended lower, but off their intraday lows, on nervous selling triggered by the price of the 10-year bond falling below the key psychological level 108.00. 

 The consequent rise in bond yields pushed interest rate swaps higher, which, in turn, generated additional selling pressure on bonds, dealers said. 

 Higher money market rates also encouraged bond selling. 

 Light buying toward the close of the session helped bonds close off their intraday lows. 

 The 10-year bond yield ended four basis points higher at 3.60% and the seven-year yield rose two basis points to 3.43%. 

 The yield on the five-year government paper was unchanged at 3.01% while the two-year bond yield was up one basis point at 2.11%. 

 In the interest rate swaps market, the most liquid seven-year yield was at 3.51%, compared with 3.48% Monday. The spread between the two-and 10-year swaps was at 125 basis points, resulting in a steep swap curve. 

 On the interbank money market, the overnight and term rates rose on the back of a weaker Singapore dollar, dealers said.

title: Emerging  FX  - Granted reprieve with steadier yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 6 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies found a stronger footing late on Tuesday as the yen crept back up against the dollar after several Japanese officials expressed concern over its recent decline. 

 Analysts also said the market was heavily long of dollars, and the comments spurred covering of yen positions. 

 The euro was also slightly damped by the yen's recovery. 

 But analysts said concerns over the Japanese economy, which many see as tottering close to the brink of a serious downturn, remained firmly in place. JP Morgan forecasts the yen to hit 120 by end-March and 122 by end-June. 

 Indeed, Bank of Japan Governor Masaru Hayami said the pace of Japan's economy was slowing and its outlook was uncertain. 

 In the meantime, North Asian currencies, the Thai baht, and the Singapore dollar all rode on the yen's coat-tails on Tuesday. 

 Indonesia's bleak political scene continued to defeat the rupiah, which slipped back towards 9,900. 

 Trading throughout the region was quiet as Singapore markets were closed for a public holiday, limiting offshore interest in Asian regional currencies. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar firmed slightly in line with the yen in light offshore trade as local markets were closed for a public holiday. They will re-open on Wendesday. 

 A local newspaper report quoting the Monetary Authority of Singapore as saying it would intervene to damp excessive exchange rate movements, including those linked to mergers and acquisition flows, also supported the local dollar. 

 Dealers have attributed the Sing dollar's recent weakness in part to heightened speculation over Singapore Telecommunications' possible bid for Australia's Cable & Wireless Optus . 

 An Australian paper reported on Monday SingTel was almost certain to win the bidding for Australia's second largest telephone firm. That report quoted an unnamed source. 

 Vodafone Group Plc and Telecom Corp of New Zealand are the other bidders for Optus. PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso gave way to corporate dollar demand after hitting an early high of 47.54 per dollar, but dollar offers above 47.80 limited the downside. 

 The Supreme Court's ruling upholding Gloria Macapagal Arroyo's presidency continued to be supportive, but dealers said the peso was likely to face a near-term barrier at 47.50. 

 Salomon Smith Barney said the peso could rally further to 46 per dollar if the outcome of the May congressional elections favoured Arroyo. 

 But it added that the central bank was unlikely to tolerate a much stronger peso due to concerns about export competitiveness. 

 "Between 46-47 is the dollar/peso range where we believe the BSP may enter the market and arrest the peso's appreciation," Salomon said in a report. 

 Separately, the central bank said on Tuesday it hoped to conclude the syndication of a three-year term loan worth $740 million by March 15. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won benefitted from the firmer yen, exporter dollar sales and equity purchases by foreign investors, gapping higher at the open after Monday's close at a six-week low of 1,273.3. 

 That put the dollar back into neutral territory on the 14-day relative strength index after Monday's spurt above the overbought mark of 70. 

 Analysts expect the yen to remain a key driver for the won, given that both countries compete in export markets. 

 "Bank of Korea officials target the won cross rate at roughly 11 against the yen," said Craig Chan, regional currency strategist at ING Barings in Hong Kong. Yen/won was at 10.64/66 at 0840 GMT. He noted that non-deliverable forward won rates indicated the market expected the spot rate to remain broadly steady over the next six months to a year. 

 "That is reflective of the credibility of the BOK and also the strong balance of payments which we are continuing to see." 

 The BOK holds its monthly policy meeting on Thursday. Nine of 10 economists polled by Reuters expected the central bank to keep its short-term interest rate target unchanged at 5.0 percent after recent data showed mixed signs on the state of the economy. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The Thai baht recouped some lost ground after the yen's rebound triggered profit taking in the dollar. Trade was subdued as Singapore - its major offshore trading centre - was closed. 

 Lack of progress in a probe into a bomb attack on a plane Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra was due to board over the weekend caused those who overbought the dollar to cut long positions pending further developments, dealers said. 

 Investigators established the fire was caused by a bomb explosion, but have not said whether the blast was an attempt to assassinate Thaksin. 

 Baht funding costs were mostly steady, with the one-month forward rate quoted at 3/5 satang per dollar offshore and -10.50/-9.75 satang onshore. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was jostled around a tight range of 9,850-9,875, caught between local and foreign banks' dollar buying and state banks' dollar selling. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said local and foreign banks were buying dollars on behalf of corporate clients. 

 "It doesn't matter what the state banks sell, genuine demand is still there," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in Jakarta. 

 The dealer added the rupiah found some solace from an Economics Ministry official's comments that an IMF team was expected to arrive in Jakarta on Thursday. 

 The mission is seen as an important step for Jakarta towards securing the release of a delayed $400 million from the IMF. That loan was delayed in December due to concerns over a number of issues ranging from central bank independence to regional autonomy laws. 

 Stalled negotiations between the IMF and Jakarta have weighed heavily on already depressed sentiment towards the rupiah. 

 Rating agency Moody's Investors Service downgraded its outlook for Indonesia to stable from positive, citing political problems and Jakarta's relations with official creditors. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR The Taiwan dollar gave up earlier gains and closed at the day's low of 32.362 after the central bank stepped in to buy the U.S. dollar. 

 Dealers said a steadier yen and foreign equity funds provided support for the local currency in early trade. Taipei shares rose after the central bank's surprise rate cut late Monday, its third in three months. 

 UBS Warburg expected the Taiwan dollar to trade in a 32.350-32.450 range in the near future given that equity sentiment remained firm. 

 "But with the yen weak, local exporters are losing competitiveness and the CBC will be forced to let the Taiwan dollar (ease) again in months ahead," it said.

title: Singapore MAS To Control M&A-Related  FX  Volatility:Report
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Monetary Authority of Singapore will intervene in the foreign exchange market to smooth out volatility arising from a large demand for U.S. dollars when a local company makes a sizable foreign acquisition, the Business Times reported Tuesday. 

 The central bank's comments come a day after the U.S. dollar hit a three-month high against the Singapore dollar. The local unit fell on concerns that a successful bid for Australia's Cable & Wireless Optus Ltd. (A.CWO) by Singapore Telecommunications Ltd. (P.GST) would create a large demand for the U.S. dollar. 

 The U.S. dollar hit a high of S$1.7555 in intraday trading Monday before closing Asian trading at S$1.7533. 

 "MAS recognizes mergers and acquisitions by local companies may cause heightened volatility in the S$ (Singapore dollar), even though they have no impact on the fundamentals of the Singapore economy," the newspaper quoted the MAS as saying. 

 "MAS will intervene if necessary to dampen excessive S$ exchange rate movements, including movements arising from funding of corporate M&A activities." 

 Singapore Telecom which is 80% government-owned, has emerged as a favorite to acquire Australia's second-largest phone company. Other bidders include Telecom Corp. of New Zealand (NZT) and Vodafone Pacific, part of Vodafone Group PLC (VOD). 

 Singapore Telecom could make a formal bid for Optus as early as this week, a person close to the transaction said Monday. 

 Officials from Singapore Telecom recently met the head of Australia's competition agency and didn't confront any potential problems, a person close to the transaction in Australia said. 

 SingTel's board is expected to put the finishing touches on a bid at its next board meeting. The company isn't believed to be too keen on offering a premium of more than 15% for Optus, valuing a bid at about A$16.7 billion. 

 The MAS said deals like the possible Optus purchase will involve selling some Singapore dollars, but such transactions won't lead to any changes in monetary policy. These transactions won't lead to changes in the undisclosed band within which the local currency's value is determined either. 

 The MAS uses the value of the Singapore dollar - determined against a basket of currencies - when implementing monetary policy.

title: Singapore Dlr Lower In Late Trade; MAS Fears Cap USD Rise
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was lower against the U.S. dollar late Monday, tracking a weaker yen, but its downside was capped by fears of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, dealers said. 

 Around 0808 GMT, the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.7474, up from S$1.7448 late Friday in Asia. The U.S. dollar traded in a narrow S$1.7468-80 range with trade light due to a public holiday in Japan. 

 The U.S. dollar opened higher following its gains in London trading Friday after the Bank of Japan surprised markets by trimming its overnight deposit rate by 15 basis points to 0.35%. 

 The move was symbolic, and is expected to do little to stimulate the country's flagging economy. The yen fell to Y117.74 to the U.S. dollar after the announcement, from its opening level of Y116.70 Friday. 

 On Monday, the yen fell further to a low of Y117.92, dragging the Singapore dollar and most Asian currencies lower. 

 However, the Singapore dollar's downside was contained by fears that the MAS may intervene to defend the local unit if it fell S$1.7490-S$1.7500 to the U.S. dollar. 

 "I think intervention is unlikely around S$1.75 given a weaker yen, corporates are still selling (U.S. dollars) around S$1.7490," a chief dealer at a European bank said. 

 The U.S. dollar is expected to trade in a S$1.7450-S$1.7500 range overnight, dealers said. 

 On the bond market, prices of Singapore government securities soared to new highs as interest rates eased further. Expectations of strong demand at a seven-year bond auction due later this month also fueled buying in the tenor, a dealer said. 

 The 10-year Singapore government bond yield fell seven basis points to 3.48% and the seven-year yield ended six basis points lower at 3.24%.

 All yields ended at record lows.

 In the swap market, interest rate swaps eased following lower bond yields. 

 The 10-year interest rate swaps fell four basis points to 3.66% while the seven-year fell six basis points to 3.38%. The spreads between the two- and 10-year interest rate swaps widened, resulting in a steeper swap curve. 

 On the interbank money market, the overnight offered rate eased after the weekend while terms rates eased amid flush liquidity and prospects for a marked slowdown in the local and global economies.

title: Emerging  FX  - A touch firmer before FOMC meets.
text:
SINGAPORE, Jan 30 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies were slightly firmer late Tuesday as market players headed for the sidelines ahead of the Federal Reserve's two-day meeting, starting later in the day. 

 Trading in regional markets was generally quiet, as investors exercised caution ahead of the meeting. A recent Reuters poll of top Wall Street bond dealers showed a unanimous expectation of a 50 basis point cut, given Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's recent somber comments on the slowing U.S. economy. 

 Analysts were generally of the opinion that another rate cut by the Fed would be good news for the region, as it will increase global liquidity and allow regional central banks to also ease monetary policy. 

 Some added that while U.S. growth is expected to slow sharply in the first half of the year, the Fed's expected easing should help spur growth during the second half. 

 "Prospect of a 50 basis point Fed rate cut (Wednesday) is strengthening the second half of 2001 U.S. recovery story," Standard Chartered Bank said in a daily research note. 

 This week will also see the release of a spate of U.S. economic data. U.S. consumer confidence data for January is scheduled to be issued on Tuesday, advance fourth-quarter gross domestic product data on Wednesday, and the January employment report on Friday. 

 The euro lost some of its lustre as investors bet the Fed would secure not only a soft landing for the U.S. economy, but a rapid re-acceleration as well. 

 Even the yen managed a four-week high against the single currency, pushing the dollar down to test major support at 116.15 yen , before it climbed back up in late Asian trade. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah spent most of the day on the wrong side of 9,400, though relative political calm staved off further weakness. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said local banks shed some long dollar positions early in the session as state bank sales of around $10 million late Monday caught many short on rupiah. 

 However, the rupiah found it difficult to break the 9,400 resistance given local corporate demand for dollars and fears the political situation in Jakarta could turn violent. 

 The Indonesian parliament will decide on Thursday the course of action to take on two financial scandals linked to President Abdurrahman Wahid, which may ignite a brewing political battle between Wahid and his critics. 

 Large demonstrations on Monday sent shivers through Jakarta's financial markets as players fretted over possible violence between Wahid's supporters and his detractors. 

 The country's defence minister warned on Tuesday the military could seize power if political leaders did not end their bickering. President Wahid appeared on national television on Tuesday to plead his innocence and cool tensions. 

 KOREAN WON -2 The won was unable to extend its gains beyond an early high of 1,258.0 per dollar as importers bought dollars in a thin market, where most players were keen to unload long positions ahead of the Fed meeting. 

 There was little immediate reaction to news Korea's industrial output slowed for a fourth straight month, but analysts said mounting evidence of a flagging economy strengthened the case for a rate cut by the Bank of Korea. 

 Industrial production fell a seasonally adjusted 2.7 percent in December from a month earlier due to a contraction in consumption, facilities investment and weak domestic sales. 

 Earlier this month, the Bank of Korea left the overnight call rate target steady at 5.25 percent, in what was seen as a sign of its commitment to corporate reform. 

 But many analysts are now predicting a 25 basis point cut at its next meeting on February 8. 

 "We think that more active use of fiscal policy will be required by the government to try and soft land the economy," HSBC said in a research report. 

 "Consequently we remain bullish dollar/won to 1,400 before a rebound in H2 on dollar weakness, and also look for the BOK call rate to fall 100 basis points this year," it said. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar struggled to maintain its early firmness, but succumbed to short covering of U.S. dollar positions in late trading. 

 Dealers said the Sing dollar made slight gains at the opening mostly on the back of the firmer yen. 

 However, lingering weakness in the euro weighed on the local dollar. The Sing dollar is managed against a trade-weighted basket of currencies, of which the yen and euro are believed to be major components. 

 But, trading was generally cautious, with dealers unwilling to take large positions ahead of the Fed's rate decision. 

 The local dollar traded in a relatively tight range of 1.7430-1.7476. Dealers said the U.S. dollar's gains continued to be capped around 1.7500 due to concerns about possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. They added there was selling interest around that area as well. 

 The MAS said last week it was reviewing its 2001 inflation and growth forecasts given the negative external environment and would release a monetary policy statement in February. 

 This sparked speculation it might shift to a neutral stance from a tightening bias, but dealers were still worried the authorities may frown upon any big downward movement in the local dollar. 

 Chartists said the daily chart showed dollar/Sing in an uptrend channel since December 22. 

 Looking ahead, dealers said they expected the Sing dollar to consolidate around this area, with the session's low of 1.7430 seen as resistance. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was supported within a narrow range for most of the day as offshore players bought it against other regional currencies like the Singapore dollar. 

 But the upside was capped on dollar demand from local corporates and importers which pulled the baht down to its day low of 42.75. 

 The baht funding cost in the offshore market also rose with one-month quoted at -4.0/-1.0 satang from -6.5/-4.0 earlier in the day. 

 But dealers said sentiment was improving on expectations the winner of the January 6 polls Thaksin Shinawatra would be able to give Thailand a stable government. 

 A senior economist at HSBC said he expected the baht to firm to around 40 per dollar by the end of 2001 from 42.7 this week and around 44.0 a few months ago. 

 Global banking giant HSBC saw the Thai current account surplus narrowing to 5.2 percent of gross domestic product in 2001 from 6.7 percent in 2000 and 9.1 percent a year earlier. 

 Thaksin said a baht exchange rate of slightly over 42 per dollar was acceptable and would not be too strong for exports. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso fell to its day low of 49.65 before closing at 49.60 as demand for the dollar rose from importers and corporates seeking to cover their month-end inventory requirements. 

 Earlier in the day the peso touched a high of 49.15, compared to Monday's onshore close of 49.48. Turnover was down to $110.55 million, from $126 million on Monday. 

 Dealers said the absence of the central bank, which had been buying dollars to meet foreign debt commitments, and some residual of remittances from overseas workers had helped the peso rise in early trade. 

 The central bank has repeatedly denied making dollar purchases to repay loans and bond maturities estimated at around $400 million falling in January and February. 

 The peso was lifted from around 50 to a dollar on Monday as overseas worker remittances flowed into the market after the Chinese New Year holidays in the region last week. 

 Dealers said the peso was likely to trade in a broad 49.00-49.75 range in the coming days. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar firmed up, helped by a rising yen and gains in local stocks, but its upside was capped by central bank intervention. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the central bank was spotted buying dollars at around the 32.40 level to keep the currency from appreciating too much, especially against the yen and the won. Japan and Korea compete with Taiwan in several export markets. 

 The central bank was believed to have intervened on Monday too, to prevent the local dollar strengthening past 32.50, but its absence early on Tuesday emboldened the market. 

 Dealers said strong foreign portfolio inflows and hopes of a rally after a widely expected cut in U.S. rates were likely to support the Taiwan dollar.

title: Singapore Dlr Dn Late, MAS Action Suspected, Cos Buy USD
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was weaker against its U.S. counterpart late Tuesday on suspected intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, the de facto central bank, and corporate demand for U.S. dollars, dealers said. 

 Around 0901 GMT (4:01 a.m. EST), the U.S. dollar was trading at its intraday high of S$1.7326, up from S$1.7298 late Monday in Asia. 

 The U.S. dollar opened lower, hitting an intraday low of S$1.7277, in line with its weakness against most Asian currencies, particularly the yen. 

 The U.S. dollar's early decline attracted local companies, mostly importers, to start buying the U.S. currency midmorning, and the buying intensified in the afternoon, dealers said. 

 "Most of the buying was through local banks and there is talk that some of it could have been on behalf of the central bank," said a dealer at a U.S. brokerage. "This would have been a good opportunity for them (central bank) to intervene, if indeed they did," the dealer added. 

 The MAS rarely comments on its interventions in the foreign exchange market. In recent weeks, the MAS has been suspected of buying U.S. dollars to prevent the excessive strengthening of the local currency. 

 The MAS said late Monday that Singapore's official foreign reserves at the end of December stood at US$80.36 billion, up 2.9% from November. Market participants say the increase in reserves likely reflects recent U.S. dollar buying by the MAS. 

 Dealers expect the U.S. dollar to remain capped at S$1.7330-40 overnight, with initial support around S$1.7300 and then at S$1.7270. 

 On the bond market, prices of Singapore government securities fell on profit-taking following the steep overnight fall in U.S. Treasurys, dealers said. 

 The yield on the 10-year Singapore government bond ended five basis points higher at 3.82%, the seven-year bond yield rose five basis points to 3.61%, the five-year yield rose one basis point to 3.35% and the two-year bond yield rose by one basis point to 2.78%. 

 In the money market, the overnight offered rate was slightly higher but most other interbank rates edged lower amid greater lending interest. 

 Dealers said the impact of last week's 50 basis points rate cut by the U.S. Federal Reserve has trickled through to the Singapore money market, but rates aren't expected to fall sharply as they are close to historic lows.

title: Emerging  FX -Uninspired by 2nd Fed cut, yen weighs.
text:
SINGAPORE, Jan 5 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were mostly easier in early trade on Friday after the U.S. Federal Reserve's second discount rate cut in two days failed to excite the market. 

 Players chose to focus instead on the beleaguered yen which slid to a 16-month low, as well as on domestic political and commercial leads. 

 The Fed on Thursday cut the largely symbolic U.S. discount rate by an additional quarter percentage point to 5.5 percent, just one day after it surprised the market by slashing its key federal funds rate by 50 basis points and discount rate by 25 basis points. 

 The move occurred after the New York close, leaving little room for U.S. markets to react. 

 "In theory, the cut should provide some support to Asian currencies in the immediate term. But again, there are lots of other factors that are driving the regional currencies, especially the Southeast Asian ones," said Syetarn Hansakul, economist at WestLB in Singapore. 

 "And there are some in the market who now suspect the surprise move by the Fed might indicate something is going terribly wrong somewhere, or the economic situation in the U.S. is much worse than previously anticipated," she said. 

 Dealers expected the dollar to retain its toehold above 116 yen as Japan's sluggish economy came into focus amid fading euphoria over the Federal Reserve's rate cuts. 

 The euro held comfortable above 95 cents and 110.00 yen , supported by growing optimism about the outlook for European economies compared to Japan and the U.S. 

 Markets are keenly awaiting the U.S. employment report for December, due at 1330 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters see non-farm payrolls adding 102,000 jobs after adding 94,000 in November. 

 The unemployment rate is expected to inch up to 4.1 percent from a 4.0 percent reading in November, and would be the second straight month it has risen. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was under renewed pressure as local equities slipped on the back of more losses in U.S. technology shares. 

 While the won had mustered some strength on Thursday, there was good support for the dollar just below 1,250, where buying interest, especially from local oil importers, kicked in. That onshore dollar demand was expected to remain in Friday's session. 

 Dollar buying in the non-deliverable forward market overnight, particularly in the shorter-dated tenors, also pressured the spot exchange rate. The one-month won was at 1,272/74 compared with 1,241 late Thursday. 

 And the won's near-term prospects were dimming, analysts said. Despite the initial cheer from the Fed's rate cut on Wednesday, Korea is more affected by the direction of U.S. economic growth rather than the direction of interest rates, said Mansoor Mohi-uddin, currency strategist at UBS Warburg. 

 With that in mind, the implication of the Fed's rate cuts - that the authorities have become increasingly concerned about U.S. growth - was hurting the won, he said in a research note. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar weakened as players bought the U.S. dollar back after overselling it on Thursday, with the yen's fall past 115 intensifying buying interest for the U.S. unit. 

 The yen is believed to have accounted for around 15 percent in Singapore's trade-weighted basket of currencies which the Sing dollar is managed against. "Yesterday, the Sing shot up to 1.7270 where dollar demand kicked in again as some became short. There was also fear of MAS intervention," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore. 

 "Looking at trade flows today, I think the Sing's upside will be capped at 1.7300 where dollar bargain hunting orders are lining up, while the support is seen at around 1.7380 - a level the market failed to break last night in New York," he said. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was still straddling the 9,500 mark, with local corporate demand for dollars expected to keep the dollar buoyed. 

 While Indonesian rates have been creeping higher over the past several months, mainly to defend the rupiah, central bank deputy governor Miranda Goeltom said on Thursday it would not seek an excessively tight monetary policy. 

 However, central bank governor Sjahril Sabirin said earlier on Thursday the bank would not cut rates following the Fed's move to lower key U.S. interest rates. 

 Sabirin faces a long-awaited graft trial on January 17 on charges that he was involved in the Bank Bali scandal . 

 He returned to work late last year after spending nearly six months in detention over his alleged involvement in the scandal, which caused international lending agencies to suspend loan disbursements to Indonesia and destroyed the re-election chances of former president B.J. Habibie. 

 Indonesia's Attorney General's office also questioned a former central bank governor Soedrajad Djiwandono on Thrusday about billions of dollars of controversial loans made in the late 1990s. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was softer against the dollar despite the second Fed rate cut on Thursday which was overshadowed by the ailing yen and political uncertainty. 

 But the unit found some support around 43.50 where a Singapore name and a European name out of London emerged to offer the dollar. 

 Thais will be voting to choose the new government on Saturday. However, analysts reckon the general elections this weekend will not put an end to the political uncertainty gripping the country but merely prolong it. 

 Telecoms tycoon Thaksin Shinawatra is still well ahead in most opinion polls despite being indicted by Thailand's anti-corruption agency for failing to declare some of his wealth. 

 The concern is that Thailand could plunge deeper into political uncertainty if Thaksin becomes the next premier because he will be removed from office if found guilty by the Constitutional Court. 

 One-month forward rate was quoted at -3.0/-1.0 satang per dollar offshore and -13.2/-11.5 satang onshore. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso slipped past the 51 per dollar mark in early offshore trade in line with weakness in other regional currencies and dealers in Manila said the currency could test lower levels on uncertainty ahead of the Thai general election. 

 "We think the peso can test 51.50-60 as there will be some nervousness in the market ahead of elections in Thailand," a dealer at a local bank in Manila said. 

 Philippine markets closely watch movements in the Thai baht as Thailand is considered to be a competitor in exports. 

 The dealer said the central bank was unlikely to change its key overnight rates in its weekly policy meeting later in the day, given poor inflation data released early Friday. 

 Consumer prices rose 6.6 percent year-on-year in December, against a rise of 6.0 in November, higher than market expectations of a 6.4 percent rise. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura on Thursday said the bank would discuss a 50-100 basis point rate cut at Friday's meeting. The benchmark overnight borrowing rate now stands at 13.5 percent and lending rate at 15.75 percent. 

 Analysts said lower interest rates were needed to boost the stagnant economy but could also fuel inflation already on the rise because of a weak currency and high energy prices. 

 Dealers said news the Equitable-PCI Bank had suffered considerable withdrawals of funds after being embroiled in the impeachment trial of President Joseph Estrada would also keep sentiment depressed. 

 Equitable has handed over documents to the trial court which have indicated the presence of a 500 million peso trust account allegedly opened by Estrada. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar dipped below the 33 per dollar mark, depressed by a weaker yen and won but dealers said fears of intervention by the central bank limited further losses. 

 They said a higher opening of the local stock market, helped by a second cut by the Fed in its discount rate, also kept players from pushing the local dollar lower. 

 Analysts said easing concerns of a hard landing in the U.S. would help sentiment, but Taiwan's slowing growth and exports and a weak financial sector were likely to weigh on the currency. 

 The central bank on Thursday said the cuts in U.S. rates would help stabilise the local dollar and allow Taiwan to keep monetary policy loose. 

 Taiwan will release its December consumer and wholesale price indices at 0300 GMT. November CPI rose 2.26 percent year on year while the wholesale price index up 2.51 percent.

title: Emerging  FX -Firmer, but Fed rate cut cheer fading.
text:
SINGAPORE, Jan 4 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies held their ground late Thursday, though they gave up early, showier gains as markets considered the implications of the Federal Reserve's surprise rate cut. 

 The Fed cut its key federal funds rate by 50 basis points to six percent on Wednesday amid increasing signs of a harder than expected landing for the U.S. economy. It also cut its more symbolic discount rate by 25 basis points. 

 While global markets, particularly equity markets, were relieved by the much-hoped for easing, some analysts said the earlier than expected cut showed the Fed had fallen behind the economic curve. 

 Others said there was a whiff of desperation about the move, which may point to a more dire economic outlook for the U.S. 

 Regional currency markets, with the exception of Indonesia and the Philippines, joined in the initial euphoria over the rate cut with the Korean won and Thai baht leading. 

 Dealers in Singapore, Bangkok, and Hong Kong said the slight rebound in regional currencies was more due to narrowing rate differentials than the prospect of rate cuts by regional authorities. 

 While analysts expected North Asian central banks to follow suit with their own monetary easing, lower interest rates would do little for the more severely hobbled economies of Indonesia, the Philippines, and Thailand - all of which are wracked by political turmoil as well. 

 "The beneficiaries (of the rate cut) will be those currencies sold off due to the concerns over global economic growth, being the Taiwan dollar and Korea won," said David Simmonds, regional currency strategist at Citibank in Singapore. 

 "But it (the rate cut) doesn't impact the elections in Thailand, nor the impeachment trial in the Philippines. Nor does it address the enormous political complications in Indonesia." 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won managed to end on a stronger note despite paring early gains as local importers bought dollars, taking advantage of its low levels. 

 Gains on the local stock market boosted the won, with foreign investors buying a net 395 billion won worth of shares on Thursday. 

 Foreign direct investment in Korea for the full year 2000 rose one percent on year to hit $15.7 billion, with the government saying foreign direct investment could top $15 billion this year if labour issues were settled and corporate restructuring carried out. 

 That, however, has been the problem, analysts have said. Korean financial markets have been roiled in recent weeks by a raft of external and domestic problems - from slowing global demand for exports and firm oil prices to the agonisingly slow corporate reform process and a spate of labour union strikes. 

 While an easier monetary policy would help Korea deal with an expected economic slowdown, a number of issues remain, especially corporate and financial reforms, analysts said. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was weaker, having ceded all of its earlier gains, and then some, as U.S. names covered short dollar positions. 

 A dealer at a European bank in Singapore said a large foreign investment bank based in Hong Kong was also spotted buying dollars in late Asian trading. 

 The baht, along with other regional currencies, had rejoiced over the Fed's rate cut, and firmed through the psychological 43 level earlier in the day, triggering stop-loss dollar sales. 

 Dealers in Bangkok said the baht had initially benefited from a narrowing differential between Thai and U.S. interest rates. The central bank, however, said later its interest rate policy would not be affected by the U.S. rate cut. 

 Thailand has maintained a low rate policy to boost sluggish domestic demand. 

 But local companies as well as offshore players snapped up dollars at the intraday lows, dealers in Singapore said. 

 Deputy Finance Minister Pisit Leeahtam said earlier in the day the baht would recover after the January 6 elections, supported by Thailand's strong fundamentals. 

 Deputy Prime Minister Supachai Panitchpakdi chimed in, saying thin volumes were aggravating the baht's recent volatility. 

 While some dealers in Bangkok said the market had already priced in a victory by Thaksin Shinawatra's Thai Rak Thai (TRT) Party, concerns over continued political uncertainty were lurking. Thaksin was indicted last week of corruption charges, and faces a five-year ban if found guilty. But a final court decision could take months. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar held its gains as the stock market built on early Wall Street-driven momentum to end nearly five percent higher, further encouraged by parliament's adoption of Taiwan's 2001 budget. 

 The Fed rate cut also helped, with the central bank saying it would help stabilise the local dollar and allow Taiwan to stick to a loose monetary policy. 

 It did not specify whether Taiwan would follow suit with more cuts, a week after trimming the discount rate 0.125 percentage point to 4.625 percent. 

 Parliament adopted the government's 2001 budget, whittling away T$32.66 billion after a marathon session plagued by political wrangling. 

 It authorised spending of T$1.5755 trillion, a moderate four percent rise over 2000, but two percent below the T$1.6082 trillion proposed by the cabinet. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar shed its gains as players took profit on the local currency after it failed to break 1.7250 on fears the Monetary Authority of Singapore might intervene soon to curb its rapid appreciation. 

 But dealers expected it to be well-supported around the current level on talk Solectron Corp , which bought a 33 percent stake in Natsteel Electronics , was still unwinding up to $300 million to acquire the Sing dollar. 

 Meanwhile, Singapore's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) for December showed a reading at 52.5 percent, down 2.8 points from the previous month. 

 The composite index is based on indicators measuring orders, production, inventories and stocks of finished goods. 

 On the monetary front, analysts said they did not expect the the Fed's rate cuts to affect Singapore's interest rates much, partly because the MAS had started tightening its foreign exchange policy since last year. 

 "The central bank, through its forex operation, is taking liquidity out of the system which would prevent interest rates from falling," said Vincent Low, fixed income strategist at Merrill Lynch. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The onshore peso market ended a breath away from the 51 per dollar mark, giving up early gains as political and economic uncertainty depressed sentiment. 

 It reached a day high of 50.79 from Wednesday's close of 51.04 following gains by other regional currencies on the back of the Fed rate cut and Nasdaq rally. 

 Dealers said a turnaround in the U.S. economy would ease some of the pessimism on the economic front as the U.S. is the largest consumer of Philippine electronics exports. 

 Exports in the first 11 months of 2000 grew 7.8 percent against the year-ago period to $34.582 billion. In November alone, exports came in at $3.317 billion against $3.075 billion in November 1999. 

 But the central bank said the country posted a balance of payments deficit of $532 million in the first nine months of 2000, a sharp deterioration from its surplus of $65 million in the first eight months. 

 Dealers said political uncertainty, as the impeachment trial against President Joseph Estrada drags on, was likely to keep sentiment negative. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said the Monetary Board would discuss a 50-100 basis point cut in key overnight rates at its Friday meeting. 

 But analysts said the bank faced a dilemma as rate cuts were needed to stimulate the economy, but the peso was likely to suffer from increased liquidity. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah firmed back past the 9,500 level as some players trimmed long dollar positions ahead of a review process with the IMF on the next letter of intent starting on Friday. 

 Some analysts expect the IMF to finally give a go ahead to the next tranch of loans to Indonesia despite an initial delay. 

 Late last month, local media reported the Fund might not issue fresh loans of around $400 million until the passage of key amendments to central bank laws. 

 The disbursement of funds from the IMF - which agreed to loan Indonesia $5 billion over three years to help mend its crisis-hit economy - is tied to a series of economic reforms. 

 But dealers said strong corporate demand for the dollar was likely to keep the rupiah below 9,500 in the near-term.

text:

 - Korean won -2 hovers in choppy trade around 1,263 day low as lack of expected dollar selling by local banks encourage offshore players to pull it down. 

 - But some dealers still expect central bank support in 1,265-70 range. 

 - Sentiment also helped on end of seven-day strike by Kookmin Bank and Housing and Commercial Bank staff against merger agreement of the two banks. 

 - Six-month NDFs rise to 1,260/63 from early 1,251.5/53.5. One-year NDFs at 1,262/65 from 1,253.0/55.0.

 - November output up 6.4 percent year-on-year, but down from a 29 percent year-on-year gain in November 1999. 

 - Government statement said gross domestic product 2001 target between five to six percent, against current year's estimated growth of 9.3 percent. 

 - Commerce ministry sees trade surplus down to $10 billion in 2001 from $12 expected in 2000. 

 - Thai baht depressed on political uncertainty and modest dollar demand from corporates but month-end exporters' inflows help cap downside at around 43.40. 

 - Tuesday's anti-graft tribunal indictment of January 6 poll front runner Thaksin Shinawatra deepen uncertainty on post-election scenario. 

 - Thaksin faces five-year ban from politics but constitutional court needs to confirm indictment which may take months and raises possibility of throwing out elected prime minister if Thaksin wins. 

 - Baht funding cost also easing offshore with one-month forwards at discount of -3.0/1.0 satang per dollar from premium of 5.0/9.0 on Thursday. 

 - Indonesian rupiah slips in offshore trade in line with other regional currencies. Onshore markets closed for Eid Al Fitr holidays. 

 - Dealers in Singapore said offshore players selling rupiah on recent declines in baht and the Singapore dollar. 

 - But fears of central bank intervention likely to cap downside at around 9,600 level. 

 - Singapore dollar moves in narrow 1.7295-1.7330 range with downside capped by year-end exporters and local corporates. 

 - Dealers said players expect Monetary Authority of Singapore to start pushing Singapore dollar higher next week after release of 2000 gross domestic product growth data early next week. 

 - Official estimate at 9.5 percent year-on-year. Reuters poll in early November projected 9.42 percent. 

 - Analysts said relatively strong performance of the Singapore economy to encourage authorities to push Singapore dollar higher against trade-weighted basket. 

 - Philippine peso hovers around 50 level in lacklustre trade as market awaits fresh leads when impeachment trial against President Joseph Estrada resumes next week.
