title: FX  ASIA: Singapore Dlr Falls As Data Signal Recession
text:
A Dow Jones Newswires Column



SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- Mounting evidence that Singapore's economy is
heading into a recession hurt the Singapore dollar Wednesday, and
analysts expect the currency to weaken further before recovering by the
end of this year.


 The Singapore dollar fell to S$1.8213 to the U.S. dollar, from S$1.8174 late Tuesday on data showing that Singapore's industrial output fell 10.9% on year in May. The fall was much sharper than a revised 0.7% contraction in April, and steeper than economists' forecasts of a 6% to 8% contraction in May. 

 Analysts say the data point to a high probability that Singapore's gross domestic product will contract in the second quarter from the first quarter, following a 11.3% quarter-on-quarter contraction in the first quarter. This would put the economy in a recession, defined as a quarter-on-quarter contraction in two consecutive quarters. 

 The Singapore currency was also hurt by a weaker yen and by reported comments from National Trade Union Congress chief Lim Boon Heng, that Singaporeans must brace for a longer-than-expected economic slowdown. 

 Hui Chin Chong, a currency strategist with JP Morgan Chase, said she expects the Singapore dollar to fall to S$1.8300 by end-July before recovering to S$1.8000 by year- end, largely on the back of an expected recovery in the euro and yen later this year. 

 In the near-term, apart from a sharp slowdown in the local and global economies, the Singapore dollar will remain pressured by an estimated US$9.5 billion in outflows arising from overseas acquisitions by Singapore companies, Chong said. 

 Singapore Telecommunication's Ltd.'s (P.SGT) bid for Australia's Cable & Wireless Optus (A.CWO) and DBS Group Holdings Ltd.'s (P.DBS) bid for Hong Kong's Dao Heng Bank account for the bulk of these outflows. 

 Standard Chartered Bank's three-month forecast for the Singapore dollar stands at S$1.8400, and it too expects a recovery to S$1.8000 by year-end. Research form IDEAglobal expects the local currency to weaken to S$1.8300 in the third quarter. 

 At 0529 GMT, the U.S. dollar was quoted at S$1.8210, with reports of a possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore capping its upside at S$1.8220. 

 The latest data and Lim's comments come on the heels of last week's news of a sharper-than-expected 9% year-on-year contraction in Singapore's key non-oil domestic exports, due to a 10.9% fall in electronics exports and a 5.9% decline in the exports of non-electronic products. 

 The electronics sector output in May plunged by 20.1% from a year ago as a result of the slowdown in the U.S. economy and reduced global appetite for electronic products, Singapore's leading export. In April, electronics production fell 8.5% from a year ago. 

 Analysts expect industrial production and non-oil exports to fall further in June following a spate of profit warnings by local and U.S. technology companies, and with no apparent signs of a turnaround in growth. 

 "Industrial production is expected to continue to worsen in June, meaning that second quarter GDP (year-on-year) growth" will slow to 2% from 4.5% in the first quarter, IDEAglobal said in a research note, adding that the May manufacturing performance was Singapore's worst in 10 years. 

 "This would bring the economy very close to, if not already into a... recession, which would occur if growth (slows) to 1.8% on year in the second quarter," IDEAglobal added. 

 Singapore's DBS Bank said it expects GDP to grow by a mere 1% to 1.5% year-on-year in the second quarter, suggesting a recession. 

 Standard Chartered Bank strategist Julian Jessop said recession appears inevitable as his bank expects the second quarter GDP to contract 0.7% from the first quarter. 

 Analysts expect the government to lower its current 3.5% to 5.5% GDP forecast for 2001 when it unveils its advance estimate for second-quarter GDP growth on July 10. The advance, or flash, estimate is based on data from the first two months of the quarter. 

 The expected revised forecast range is 2.5%-5%. 

 Analysts say that while the data should prompt the Monetary Authority of Singapore to ease its monetary policy bias from moderately tight to neutral, the central bank may not want to do so publicly. This would likely result in a reaffirmation of its policy stance at the next scheduled review in July. 

 "If they haven't changed it (policy) already, I'm not convinced they'll do it in the middle of the year," Jessop said.

title: Emerging  FX -Yen recovery, c.bank talk help pare falls.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 22 (Reuters) - Asian currencies trimmed 

 some early losses late on Friday, helped by the yen's 

 bounce off a two-month low and talk that some central banks 

 were in the market to defend their currencies. 

     Dollar profit-taking ahead of the key resistance level of 

 125 and option-linked dollar sales helped the yen recover from 

 124.74 hit early in the day to be around 124.40 in late trade. 

     However, analysts said Japan's grim economic outlook would 

 keep the yen shaky, with consequences for regional currencies. 

     Suspected intervention pushed the Singapore dollar and the 

 Philippine peso off their lows, while fears of central bank

 action limited losses in the Korean won and in the Taiwan 

 dollar. 

 Activity was subdued ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's 

 policy-setting meeting on June 26-27, when it is widely 

 expected to cut interest rates by at least 25 basis points. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar clambered off its intraday lows of 1.8225 

 on the back of speculation that the Monetary Authority of 

 Singapore (MAS) was in the market to shore up the currency. 

 Dealers said they suspected MAS - the city state's de 

 facto central bank - had been in the market since Thursday, 

 chasing the local currency from 1.8235 and on Friday from 

 1.8225. 

 "We can't get any confirmation yet, but it definitely 

 looked and felt like it. No one else seems to be doing anything 

 except for one European bank and one local bank which the MAS 

 normally trades with," said a senior dealer at a European bank. 

     Despite the rebound, the Sing dollar remains confined in 

 the U.S. dollar's uptrend channel which dates back to May 24. 


    PHILIPPINE PESO	



    The peso also closed off its intraday lows of 52.42 on the



back of rumours that the central bank was in the market to sell



around $30 million.



    But cental bank governor Rafael Buenaventura denied having


intervened to shore up the peso.



    "We could intervene if necessary, although we have not



found it necessary yet," he said, but added that the level of



the peso was causing some concern.



    He also said that the central bank would not lower or raise



overnight interest rates in the near term.



    KOREAN WON	   -2



    The won edged towards the stronger end of Friday's



1,308-1,302.4 range due to the yen's rebound, hopes for foreign



investment flows and fears of central bank intervention.



    Dealers in Singapore said exporters and some interbank



players were seen selling dollars around 1,308 on fear a test



of 1,310 may invite central bank intervention.



    However, dollar demand was intact on equity-related



outflows and speculation that the central bank might soon cut



its key interest rates after it downgraded the growth outlook



for the year. The next BOK policy meeting is due on July 5.



THAI BAHT



The baht was strait-jacketed as players sat out ahead of a



meeting between commercial banks and the central bank on



Monday.



The central bank is expected to seek views from commercial



banks on how to streamline reporting rules for non-residents



trading the baht.



Baht funding costs eased slightly as players took advantage



of the recent rise, but they generally remained high. The



one-month forward rate was quoted at 14/19 satang per dollar



offshore and 2.5/6.5 onshore.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH



The rupiah was locked in a 11,350-11,360 range, in a



paper-thin market. Dealers in Jakarta said trading volumes were



well below $100 million, against usual volumes of $150-250.



The market warily watched the murky political scene as



President Abdurrahman Wahid again warned he may call early



elections if the parliament moves towards impeaching him.



TAIWAN DOLLAR



The Taiwan dollar closed at 34.434, near key support at



34.50. The currency was wedged between support from the central



bank and U.S. dollar demand mainly from foreign equity



investors.



    Bearish economic data and uncertainty surrounding the yen



also encouraged players to hold on to their U.S. dollar longs.



    Taiwan May industrial output declined 8.2 percent on year



while export orders dropped 13.96 percent from same period year



ago. Dealers said figures came in slightly better than market



consensus, but were still discouraging.



A senior official at Ministry of Economic Affairs said



Taiwan's export orders were expected to show year-on-year



declines through the rest of 2001.

title: Emerging  FX  - Pressured by yen, wary on outlook.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 21 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were easier 

 in early trade on Thursday, taking their cues from the yen's 

  overnight decline to five-week lows against the U.S. 

 dollar. 

     The yen dipped to just a shade off the 124 mark, its lowest 

 level since May 16, in New York trade after White House 

 economic adviser Lawrence Lindsey was reported as saying 

 further declines in the yen could be expected due to Japan's 

 structural reforms. 

     The more tech-sensitive North Asian currencies may find 

 some solace in the Nasdaq's near two percent rise in an 

 otherwise grim economic scenario at home and abroad. 

     No fresh clues on the state of the sagging U.S. economy 

 came out of the Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's 

 testimony to the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday. 

     However, his comment that inflation was not an immediate 

 worry raised hopes of an interest rate cut when the FOMC meets 

 next week. 

     A majority of Wall Street analysts, 17 out of 25, still 

 believe the cut may not be more than a quarter of a percentage 

 point. 

     In the region's Southeast, players will continue to look 

 warily at the hostage saga in the Philippines, talk of higher 

 interest rates in Thailand, and the violence-prone politics of 

 Indonesia. 


    KOREAN WON	   -2



    The won edged lower in line with the softer yen, but the



downside was seen limited on hopes of more investment-related



inflows and a firmer tone at the local stock market tracking



the Nasdaq's gains.



    A senior Korean official said on Wednesday the country



expects inflows of up to $8 billion in foreign direct



investment in the second half of the year.



    But added settlement of stocks sold by foreign investors in



recent sessions would continue to pressure the won. Foreign



funds sold a net 127 billion won worth of local stocks on



Wednesday.



    Dealers said dollar demand was likely to stay intact at



around 1,290-95, with near-term trading expected within a



1,290-1,320 range.



    SINGAPORE DOLLAR	



    The Sing dollar slid to fresh six-week lows of around



1.8225 on the back of a softer yen, having spiralled all the



way from highs around 1.8150 on Wednesday.



    Dealers said fears of possible intervention grew as the



latest drop put the Sing dollar just half a cent away from



around 1.8270, the level the Monetary Authority of Singapore


was believed to have intervened at in early May.



    Charts showed the dollar was overbought, with a 14-day



relative strength index reading at 74. This indicates some



scope for correction.



    But others noted the Sing dollar's weakness was largely due



to the yen and in line with other regionals, thus reducing


intervention risks.



    THAI BAHT	



    The baht hovered around 45.30 as the yen slid further,



still pretty much confined in dollar/baht's uptrend channel



which started on June 6.



    But its downside was limited by wariness over higher



interest rates or further tightening of disclosure rules which



would push baht funding costs up.



    The one-month forward rate rose to 18/25 satang per dollar



and the 12-month rate was quoted at 130/180 satang as market



participants covered positions ahead of mid-year book closings.



    The central bank had earlier this month raised its



benchmark 14-day repo rate to 2.5 from 1.5 percent, hoping the



move would deter outflows by slowing down foreign debt



repayment and persuading banks to reduce their foreign asset



holdings.



    Recently, there were rumours that the central bank might



raise the rate again. Although the Bank of Thailand has denied



this, the market was not quite convinced.



    PHILIPPINE PESO	



    The peso was on the defensive at 52.15 having recovered to



51.85 on Wednesday after it touched near a five month low of



52.33. Profit-taking from both local and foreign banks of long



dollar positions in an overbought market had sent it higher.



     Fears of possible intervention has kept it stumbling



further beyond 52.20 for now.



    Talk circulated in the market on Wednesday a U.S. bank sold



around $20 million from 52.30 on behalf of the central bank,



but it was denied by governor Rafael Buenaventura.



    The Philippine military said late on Wednesday it had



pinned down Muslim guerrillas holding Filipino and U.S.



hostages in the south and it should not take long for the



captives to to be rescued.



    But this proved cold comfort to dealers as the military has



said in the past it was close to ending the saga and failed.



    INDONESIAN RUPIAH

positive developments on the IMF front should help support it.



    The IMF said on Wednesday it was optimistic Indonesia's



willingness to revise controversial bank law amendments would



end a six-month deadlock on a vital $5 billion loan programme.



    The international institution froze its aid programme to

    In the money market, Bank Indonesia's benchmark one-month

    SBIs are issued by the central bank as a tool of draining



liquidity from the market.



    TAIWAN DOLLAR

    Dealers in Singapore said with the yen testing the 124



level players may hold on to their U.S. dollar longs on hopes

local dollar.



Though the Nasdaq's rise will help sentiment,



equity-related outflows will continue to weigh on the local



dollar. Foreign investors' local stocks sales in the past five



sessions were estimated at a net T$1.44 billion.

title: Emerging  FX -Hostage to fickle yen, Argentina eyed.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 19 (Reuters) - Asian currencies kept an easier tone late Tuesday on uncertainty over the yen's near-term outlook, but weathered any fallout from Argentina's introduction of a special exchange rate for exporters and importers. 

 The yen recovered sharply from one-month lows against the dollar after Bank of Japan governor Masaru Hayami said intervention was needed if forex rates move too rapidly. 

 Hayami also said Japan should not drive the yen lower because of its potential impact on neighbouring countries and given a surplus on Japan's current account. 

 The comment pushed the yen up to around 123.35 from around 123.60, but analysts said its outlook remained grim due to worries about Japan's faltering economy. 

 There was little reaction to Argentina's decision to expand its dollar peg to include the euro for exporters and importers, in a bid to make its goods cheaper for foreign buyers. 

 The move caused much confusion and a sell-off in Latin American markets on Monday on fears it would lead to a dismantling of Argentina's 1991 convertibility system, which is widely credited with bringing economic stability to the country. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO The peso slid to five-month lows of 52.38 as corporates scrambled to buy the dollar on the weaker yen and concerns about the unsolved kidnapping problem in the southern Philippines. Manila dealers said players were still keen to buy the U.S. dollar, even with charts showing it was heavily overbought, unless the government resolved the hostage crisis. 

 "We'll take any excuse to buy the dollar. And we know the central bank can't afford to intervene with their small reserves," a local bank dealer said. The central bank's international reserves stood at $14.44 billion at end-April. 

 But others said the central bank might take the opportunity to intervene given the market was heavily long of dollars. 

SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar finally burst through the 1.8180 support, hitting five-week lows of 1.8194, following the fragile yen. 

 Dealers said U.S and European banks were aggressively buying the U.S. dollar in the afternoon, triggering stop-loss dollar orders at 1.8180. It later recovered some ground with the yen. 

 They expected prospects for a weaker yen to pressure the Sing dollar, with some dealers now doubting the authorities would intervene until it hits 1.8230-50, levels it has not seen since rebounding from 11-year lows of around 1.8270 in May. 

 It was pulled off those levels when the Monetary Authority of Singapore sold U.S. dollars in the forex market, later confirming it had intervened. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht held up well against the dollar, mostly due to higher funding costs offshore, which were driven by persistent fears of higher interest rates. 

 Dealers said despite reassurance from the authorities that the central bank had no plan to increase interest rates soon, the market was not convinced. 

 Moreover, concerns over potential fallout from Argentina also jacked up baht funding costs on expectations demand to borrow the baht to buy the dollar could soon pick up. 

 The one-month forward rate in the offshore market rose to 20/22 satang per dollar from around 8/10 satang late last week. The 12-month tenor edged up to 140/160 satangs. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 News of a bomb blast in Jakarta and another clash between police and students protesting fuel price hikes dragged the rupiah to a two-week low of 11,385 per dollar. 

 Five people were wounded when a powerful bomb exploded at a boarding-house in a Jakarta suburb while police fired teargas to disperse 100 stone-throwing students near a university. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said dollar profit-taking by interbank players and some export-related inflows beyond 11,350 capped its downside. They said there was no sign of the central bank but players were cautious a test of 11,400 may invite intervention. 

 There was little immediate reaction to chief economic minister Burhanuddin Abdullah's comment that the government was willing to revise proposed changes to central bank law, a key obstacle to releasing long-delayed IMF loans. 

 Underscoring the confusion on the economic front, the chief of the statistics bureau said price hikes in key sectors would push 2001 inflation above a revised budget target of 9.3 percent, approved only over the weekend. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won tracked the yen lower, ending at 1,304.9 per dollar, its weakest close since May 16. 

 Sentiment was also weighed by expected equity-linked outflows. Foreign investors, who were net sellers of local stocks for the third consecutive session, sold 172.1 billion won worth of shares on Tuesday. 

 The market shrugged off a remark by a senior official from a government think-tank calling for the central bank to cut interest rates in the second half of the year to boost the sagging economy. 

 The central bank left its overnight call rate target steady at 5.0 percent for June, citing growing inflationary pressure. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was a shade off its session low of 34.43, weighed by equity-related outflows and pessimism over the economic outlook. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the central bank's active presence in the market prompted some dollar profit-taking but overall sentiment was glum. The U.S. dollar was also looking overbought, with a 14-day relative strength index reading of 80.27. 

 May export orders, due on Friday, were expected to confirm the grim economic picture, with economists polled by Reuters predicting on average a 14.34 percent on-year decline after April's 6.63 percent drop.

title: Emerging  FX  - Yen weighs, market eyes Argentina.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 19 (Reuters) - Asian currencies retained their bearish tone in early trade on Tuesday as the yen languished near one-month lows and the market eyed the potential impact of Argentina's currency plan on emerging Asia. 

 The yen , which is tracked closely by most regional currencies, slid to 123.52 overnight after the Bank of Japan's monthly report said the slowdown in the economy was intensifying. 

 It recouped some lost ground after Finance Minister Masajuro Shiokawa said on Tuesday he thought the overnight moves in dollar/yen were "quite big", adding however, that he could only monitor them for now. 

 Argentina's decision to introduce a special exchange rate for exporters and importers, by expanding its dollar peg to include the euro, was also being warily eyed after it sparked much confusion and a sell-off on Latin American markets overnight. 

 Investors fear the move could be a step toward dismantling Argentina's 1991 convertibility system which pegs the peso to the U.S. dollar and is widely credited with bringing economic stability to the country. 

 But analysts expected the impact on Asia to be limited and mainly psychological, with Philippine sovereign bonds looking the most vulnerable due to their significant weighting in the JP Morgan Emerging Market Bond Index Plus (EMBI-Plus). 

 Otherwise, local factors offered little support to regional currencies, with the Philippines' January-April trade surplus shrinking as both exports and imports declined. This followed Monday's news that Singapore's non-oil domestic exports for May fell a nominal 9.0 percent year-on-year, worse than the market's consensus of around a six percent decline. 

 And political uncertainty continued to plague Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar was on the defensive at 1.8160 due to the weak yen. 

 It has avoided a break of 1.8180 thanks largely to dollar sales of around $100 million by a European bank late on Monday, stirring talk the orders may be linked to an M&A deal. 

 Dealers said sentiment for the Sing dollar soured after weaker-than-expected non-oil exports data for May, which raised risks of a technical recession for the trade-driven economy. 

 They said European banks were keen to push dollar/Sing above 1.8180, a level it has failed to break for the past five sessions on fears of possible intervention. Singapore's central bank confirmed it had intervened in forex markets last month when the local dollar hit 11-year lows of around 1.8270. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso floundered to fresh six-month lows of 52.22 on concerns about possible spillover damage on emerging markets from Argentina's currency plan. 

 The country has a significant weighting in the EMBI-Plus, which widened 25 basis points to 758 basis points late on Monday, representing the heightened risk. 

 Manila dealers said the unsolved kidnapping saga in the southern Philippines and the weaker yen also added to the gloom, but they expected fears of possible intervention to keep the peso above 52.50. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was trapped in a tug-of-war between a weaker yen and confusion over forex and interest rate policy. 

 Dealers said players were cautious after the central bank said it had not abandoned plans to tighten disclosure rules, but it just needed more time to work out how to do it. 

 Some investors also kept a low profile ahead of a verdict on Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra's graft case, which is expected by August. 

 On Monday, Thaksin made an emotional 20-minute speech to the Constitutional Court to defend himself against charges he deliberately concealed assets. He denies wrongdoing, but if found guilty would be banned from politics for five years. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was a shade above the 11,300 level amid worries Monday's transport strikes against last week's 30 percent hike in fuel prices may spread to other cities after some regional authorities raised bus fares. 

 The strikes were mostly peaceful apart from some clashes between students and police in Jakarta in which several protestors were injured. 

 Dealers said players feared the protests may get more violent, but the rupiah might remain relatively insulated as most interbank players were showing little trading interest and dollar-starved local corporates were also keeping a low profile. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was hurt by a weaker yen and expected equity-linked outflows after foreign investors sold a net 232 billion won worth of local shares in the past two sessions. 

 But its downside was cushioned by hopes of inflows from Hynix Semiconductor's $1.25 billion global depository receipts issue. 

 The Bank of Korea said the debt default ratio fell to 0.21 percent in May from 0.28 percent in April due to reduced fallout from bankrupt Daewoo Group companies and Samsung Motors. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 Uncertainty about the yen's near-term direction and the Nasdaq's overnight fall to six-month lows were expected to keep the Taiwan dollar under pressure. 

 The local stock market is already reeling from first quarter profit warnings from electronics companies at home which have triggered net selling by foreign equity investors. 

 However, some profit-taking was possible on U.S. dollar longs, as charts showed an overbought U.S. dollar with the 14-day relative strength index reading at 79.17. 

 The Taiwan dollar has been in a downtrend against the U.S. dollar since May 21 when it slipped from a high of 32.91. Currency analysts believe the decline was engineered by the central bank to help the island's sagging exports.

title: Emerging  FX  - Fretting over yen, US outlook.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 18 (Reuters) - Asian currencies headed south early Monday as the yen weakened and U.S data over the weekend showed the economy was far from a recovery. 

 The data and more corporate profit warnings depressed Wall Street, which will impact the region's tech-sensitive markets. 

 The Nasdaq ended down for the sixth straight session finishing the week with an 8.4 percent loss, its biggest weekly decline this year. 

 The yen was wobbling near the 123 mark in early Tokyo trade, after a decline to three-week lows against the dollar in New York on Friday with the focus on Japan's poor economic outlook. 

 Both Japan and the U.S. are Asia's main export markets. 

 The regional currencies can expect little help from domestic factors with Singapore likely to announce weak May non-oil domestic export data due to worsening global technology demand. Thailand's state think tank announced first quarter GDP growth of 1.8 percent, below analysts' already bearish forecasts of 1.94 percent growth. 

 Markets are also eagerly awaiting Thai Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra's speech in the constitutional court to defend himself against allegations he deliberately concealed some of his wealth when he was deputy prime minister in the late '90s. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The Thai baht held below 45.30, within its week-old range as investors eyed Thaksin's speech due around 0630 GMT, at the close of his graft trial. 

 A verdict is not expected until July or August. If found guilty of deliberately concealing his assets, he will be banned from politics for five years. 

 Thaksin told reporters on Saturday he was not considering fixing the weakening baht to the dollar, denying remarks from a leading economist that forex policy amounted to a virtual peg. 

 Ammar Siamwala, economist at a private think-tank, told a local newspaper the government had an ideal level in mind for the baht, as evidenced by the fact the central bank had both bought and sold dollars on several occasions since the new governor was appointed two weeks ago. 

 Meanwhile, uncertainty persisted over the Bank of Thailand's forex policy, with the bank saying it had not abandonned efforts to curb speculation by non-residents, but wanted to hear the views of commercial banks before introducing further controls. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won touched an early low of 1,303, last seen on May 21, on worries over the direction of the yen and U.S. tech stocks. 

 Dealers in Singapore said players scrambled to beef up their dollar longs as Korean stocks got off to a weak start. 

 They said most interbank players had recently trimmed their dollar longs as the won, helped by a steadier yen, equity-related inflows and talk of foreign direct investment deals, had managed to stay above the 1,300 level since May 29. 

 However, hopes General Motors would soon reach a deal to take over Daewoo Motor and expected foreign investments in Hyundai Investment & Trust Securities and Hynix Semiconductor will keep the won's downside limited. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah retained its bearish tone but was well within its two-week-old 11,000-11270 range as a fuel price hike and ensuing violent protests upstaged news the World Bank was set to approve a $320 million loan to Jakarta. 

 Thousands of protesters rallied in the city of Bandung on Saturday and hundreds of bus drivers went on strike, angered by the government's decision to push ahead with a 30.1 percent fuel price hike. 

 Indonesia is Asia's only OPEC member. It had some of the world's lowest fuel prices but at a huge cost in subsidies which the financially ailing government can no longer afford. 

 The World Bank said on Sunday it would approve a $320 million community development loan for Indonesia later this month as part of its $1.2 billion, three-year aid programme. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar stumbled to 1.8178 from 1.8105 late on Friday, tracking the lower yen. 

 Dealers said U.S. names were bidding for dollar/Sing but fears of possible intervention by the authorities encouraged them to take profits at 1.8180. 

 Any dips in the dollar were expected to be met by fresh bids by European banks at around 1.8130 as the market awaited trade data, due at 0430 GMT. Non-oil exports fell 1.2 percent on-year in April. PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso buckled to 51.75, its lowest since January 19, compared with 51.59 late on Friday. 

 Manila dealers said the falling yen and the unsolved kidnapping saga in the southern Philippines encouraged foreign banks to bid aggressively from 51.60. 

 Officials said on Sunday they feared Muslim rebels had killed one of three American hostages they are holding along with more than 20 Filipinos since May 27. 

 Dealers said fears of possible intervention might emerge around 52, but players were looking to take profits at around 51.75 given a 14-day relative strength index reading showing the dollar was overbought at 81.19. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said on Sunday there was little room left for aggressive rate cuts due to the weakness of the peso and inflation pressures. 

 Socio-economic Planning Secretary Dante Canlas said he expected annual inflation in June to rise slightly to 6.7 to 6.8 percent from 6.5 percent in May due to higher consumer spending related to the start of the school year. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 Pressured by a softer yen and worries over the tech sector's second quarter earnings, the Taiwan dollar touched a low of 34.43 early, where central bank intervention prompted trimming of U.S dollar longs. 

 Dealers in Singapore said players were still seeking U.S. dollars and a test of 34.50, last seen on May 28, was possible if the yen weakened further later in the day. 

 They said second quarter profit warnings by tech companies in the U.S. and at home would further dampen sentiment already depressed by poor economic data for the first quarter.

title: Emerging  FX  - Yen rebound provides relief.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 15 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were mostly steadier in early trade on Friday as the yen recouped some lost ground after U.S. manufacturers called for the government to relax its strong dollar policy. 

 Dealers expected market activity to be subdued ahead of the U.S. consumer price data due out at 1230 GMT for clues on what the Federal Reserve policy makers might do when they meet on June 26-27 to decide on the direction of interest rates. 

 Market participants were also reluctant to move aggressively before the Bank of Japan completes its two-day policy meeting on Friday. Political pressure has been building on the central bank to further loosen its already ultra loose monetary policy following data showing the economy had unexpectedly shrunk 0.2 percent in the first three months of this year. 

 "U.S. data continues to show weakness in the U.S. economy and thus for global growth prospects. Moreover, the yen looks set now to weaken further towards 130 against the dollar," Mansoor Mohi-uddin, currency strategist at UBS Warburg, said in a daily note on Friday. 

 "As such, we remain bearish on Asian currencies and out long term targets remain 35.00 for the Taiwan dollar, 1400 for the Korean won, 47.00 for the Thai baht and 1.8500 for the Singapore dollar," he said. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR The Taiwan dollar was at 34.39, within striking distance from 34.50, 32-month lows hit on May 28. 

 Gloomy prospects of the domestic economy has put the Taiwan dollar under pressure from offshore selling, triggered by a CSFB report earlier this week which forecast it to fall to 35.5-36 in three months. 

 UBS Warburg said in a research note the Taiwan dollar might fall to 35 in the long term once the next target of 34.5 is broken. SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar edged up to 1.8138 in listless morning trading from 1.8157 late on Thursday. 

 Dealers said speculators including U.S. funds liquidated their long dollar positions following the firmer yen. 

 But they added many players were keen to buy the U.S. dollar on dips at 1.8130 to take profits at 1.8180, level the market fears the Monetary Authority of Singapore might intervene to support the Sing dollar. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht moved in a narrow range amid political uncertainty as the market watched political development ahead of Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra's graft trial on Monday. 

 Thaksin, who was elected at a landslide in January, is being tried by the Constitutional Court for failing to declare all this wealth when he was a minister in 1990s. He denied any wrongdoing. If found guilty, he can be banned from politics for five years. 

 The trial will be concluded on Monday but the verdict might be delivered in July or August. 

 Pressure groups have organised political rallies in various form to support him, and press for an acquittal. 

 Analysts said if the court stuck solely to the question of whether he deliberately concealed his wealth, Thaksin's chance of survival would be slim. 

 But if the judges brought into consideration the public sentiment, he is likely to be acquitted. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won opened a touch firmer, drawing support from a steadier yen and expected inflows. 

 Momentum should be sustained on if Hynix Semiconductor is successful with its planned $1.25 billion global share offering. 

 But its upside is likely to be capped by Nasdaq-inspired losses in the local stocks and doubts over the country's economic outlook. 

 The one-month won on the non-deliverable forward market was quoted at 1294.7/1295.6, and the six-month at 1304/1306. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was expected to stay within a narrow 51.20-51.60 range, with gains in the yen and a steadier baht supporting the downside, and dollar bids by corporates and importers capping the upside. 

 Dealers in Manila said the underlying sentiment was bearish on the peso given the kidnapping crisis and the recent downgrade of growth estimates by the government. 

 But a lack of fresh leads and with charts showing the dollar overbought, most players were seeking to book profits on dollar gains. 

 The 14-day relative strength index (RSI) showed a reading of 77.61 for dollar/peso last seen in late April when the pair rose from a low of 50.25 to touch a high of 51.45 against the dollar. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was little moved from its tight range around the 11,250 mark with trading interest minimal on a lack of any major development on the political front. 

 Dealers in Singapore said steadier regionals may limit the downside but the rupiah was unlikely to stray far from the current 11,200-11,350 range. 

 "The rupiah is simply simmering down. No one seem to be interested in it any more. Maybe a major political event will provoke some trading interest," said a dealer at a European bank in Singapore. 

 The dealer said most players in the market have squared their positions in anticipation of an early and peaceful exit of embattled President Abdurrahman Wahid. 

 "But nothing is happening and its not clear if things will turn out the way market wants them to," he said.

title: Emerging  FX  - Yen helps, but U.S. data worries.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 14 (Reuters) - Asian currencies held their recent ranges early Thursday, helped by a steadier yen but warily eyeing U.S. data released overnight that showed the global growth engine was still sputtering badly. 

 U.S. retail sales, closely monitored as a proxy for overall consumer spending, nudged up just 0.1 in May percent after an upwardly revised 1.4 percent gain in April. 

 Consumer spending, which fuels two-thirds of economic activity is threatened by increasing layoffs by U.S. companies. 

 The Federal Reserve's monthly Beige Book showed economic activity little changed or slower in April with weak manufacturing, and layoffs increasing. 

 Taking advantage of the bearish U.S. data, the yen recovered from its three-week lows and the euro reached a one-week high also aided by intervention fears. 

 But dealers doubted the yen would make further gains ahead of the Bank of Japan's two-day policy meeting starting on Thursday. The BOJ is facing political pressure to take further easing steps to avoid a recession. 

 BOJ Governor Masaru Hayami said on Thursday he saw no need for new monetary policy steps as the recent fall in stock prices and slowdown in output was within expectations. 

 For more evidence of U.S. sluggishness, markets will watch out for the May Producer Price Index, first-time claims for jobless benefits for the week ended June 9 and business inventories for April, due later Thursday. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar opened higher at 34.274 on the back of a steadier yen before market bearishness dragged it lower again. 

 "With a foreign bank calling for 36.00 for the Taiwan dollar and offshore funds speculating that the authorities will engineer a one-time devaluation to 40.00, the onshore market panicked yesterday," said a UBS Warburg note. 

 "And with U.S. dollar demand remaining good, the market is likely to keep dollar longs and will now target 35.00," it said. 

 Dealers said the central bank was in the market on Wednesday to support the local currency by selling the U.S. dollar as it reached 2-= week lows, but its intervention was sporadic. 

SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar was stuck just above 1.8150 after hitting a month low of 1.8180 on Wednesday where players unwound U.S. dollars on fears of central bank intervention. 

 Dealers said rumours Canadian Celestica Inc was making a takeover bid for local electronic contract manufacturer Omni Industries could support the Singapore dollar and they predicted a range of 1.8150-1.8180 for the day. 

 But overall, players were looking to snap up U.S. dollars on dips given a cloudy growth and export outlook. The market will also stay cautious ahead of April retail sales data due Friday. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah held steady around 11,250, extending the past week's consolidation, as corporates stayed out and offshore and interbank players trimmed dollar longs on a growing perception embattled President Abdurrahman Wahid would step down peacefully. 

 It was also supported by expectations parliament would approve a revised budget and hopes an IMF team would visit Jakarta to review progress on economic reforms next week. 

 In a fresh sign of mounting political pressure on Wahid, his deputy snubbed the inauguration ceremony for new ministers appointed after the latest cabinet reshuffle. 

 The new chief economics minister said on Wednesday the rupiah was undervalued and should be in a 9,000-10,000 range. 

 The rupiah has crept higher against the dollar since it touched a low of 12,215 on April 26. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was wedged below 45.30 as players unwound some dollar longs after the central bank announced it had scrapped a plan to impose tighter reporting guidelines on non-resident trading in the currency. 

 Prior to the announcement, commercial banks had complained that an official form the central bank required them to fill out for this purpose was complicated and not practical. 

 However, the baht's downside was supported by rising funding costs and news the government asset management company would be up and running in July to tackle Thailand's bad asset problems. 

 In the offshore market, the one-month forward rate rose to 10/15 satang per dollar in early trade while the 12-month tenor remained firm at 105/120 satang per dollar. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was little moved from Wednesday's onshore close of 51.31 and dealers expected a narrow range of 51.20-51.40. 

 Dealers in Manila said worries about the fate of Americans kidnapped by a Muslim rebel group and concerns about growth and export prospects would keep underlying sentiment bearish. 

 But a lack of dollar demand from corporates and importers and trimming of stale dollar longs by interbank players were likely to limit its downside. 

 President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo said on Wednesday the government had lowered its 2001 gross domestic product growth target to 3.3-3.8 percent from 3.8-4.3 percent, partly due to the impact of kidnappings in the rebel-infested southern islands. KOREAN WON -2 

 The won opened a touch firmer after the yen recouped some lost ground and a nationwide labour union strike lost steam as workers at Korean Air and hospitals returned to work. 

 The won has been in an uptrend since early April on expectations of foreign direct investments. 

 But with the yen weakness expected to continue, UBS Warburg said offshore players would be encouraged to buy the dollar and it expected the next target to be 1,320.

title: Emerging  FX  - Rangebound on uncertainty in majors.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 8 (Reuters) - Asian currencies bobbed within their recent ranges on Friday as players held back from taking aggressive positions amid uncertainty about the direction of major currencies and thin weekend conditions. 

 However, given the unabated flow of poor economic numbers and more deterioration expected in the second quarter, most players were keen to buy the dollar on dips with no fresh domestic leads to make them think twice. 

 The Bank of Thailand failed to stir the market when it raised its key 14-day repo rate by a full percentage point to 2.5 percent. Markets had been expecting higher rates since the sacking of the central bank chief last week over his insistence on a low rate regime. 

 The Philippine central bank denied talk of intervention sparked after two foreign banks, usually active on its behalf, were spotted buying upto $40 million earlier in the day. 

 The tech-sensitive won and Taiwan dollar were broadly steady following overnight rises in U.S. tech and semiconductor indices. 

 The Singapore dollar was helped by recent gains in the yen and euro , following losses in sterling . 

 The pound stumbled to 15-year lows for the third day as traders bet a victorious Labour Party would push for Britain's early entry into the euro. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was stuck at around 45.10 amid speculation the central bank's decision to raise its key interest rate may be followed by fresh forex curbs to stem capital outflows. 

 Analysts said the rate hike in itself was too small to have an impact on the capital flight estimated at $2.36 billion in the first quarter. 

 Thai officials have repeatedly denied plans to impose capital controls or to enforce postponed reporting requirements soon. 

 Contradictory comments induced more confusion with Finance Minister Somkid Jatsuripitak saying the rate hike would encourage banks to lend more and attract more deposits while Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said rates were still too low to have impact. 

 Fears of new forex disclosure rules, fresh restrictions on currency trade and higher rates have kept the baht firm against the dollar since it touched a low of 45.85 on April 9. 

 But dealers said the central bank's dollar buying intervention on Wednesday when the baht hit a high of 44.68 has made players wary of testing the upside. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah hugged an 11,200 session low on local corporate demand for the dollar which prompted interbank players to book profits on the rupiah's recent gains. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said the political situation was still tense with players cautious amid rumours President Abdurrahman Wahid would sack the military chief. 

 But speculation Wahid may quit peacefully had also not died. Those rumours have helped the rupiah gain ground against the dollar from a low of 12,215 touched on April 26. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso slipped to hit a low of 50.96 despite denial by the central bank it was in the market buying dollars to boost its reserves or for foreign debt repayment needs. 

 Dealers in Manila said two foreign banks that were executing the dollar purchases were usually active on behalf of the central bank and the amount, estimated at $30-40 million, was too big to be associated with a corporate client. 

 However, some interbank players were seen booking profits on the dollar's gains from around 50.90 while corporates and importers kept to the sidelines for most of the day. SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar was confined to a well-worn 1.8060-1.8110 range amid a dearth of new leads and no fresh corporate dollar demand. 

 Narrowing price action in the dollar/Sing has led to the formation of a constricting triangle on the weekly chart following the dollar's steep month-long rise from March 4. 

 While the charts suggest an upside break for the U.S. dollar, dealers said wariness of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore would cushion any falls towards 1.82. 

 The MAS sold the U.S. dollar heavily in forex markets last month, even admitting it had intervened, when the Sing dollar looked set to slide further after hitting new 11-year lows near 1.8270. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won gained from a robust 3.4 percent bounce in local stocks as chips and financials rallied on an improved outlook for the semiconductor business and signs of progress on corporate reform. Korea's semiconductor exports make up about 10 percent of GDP and a third of total exports. 

 Foreign investors bought a net 221.1 billion won worth of shares on the Korean stock market on Friday after selling a net 26.8 billion in the past two sessions. 

 But importer dollar demand capped the won's gains at 1,283.1 for the day. 

 Despite its two-month-old firming trend on rising hopes of foreign direct investment inflows, the won has had trouble sustaining a rise above the 1,283 level, which marks the 62 percent retracement of the dollar's February 21-April 4 rally. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was a shade higher from late Thursday levels as the local stock market tracked gains in U.S. technology and semiconductor indices overnight. 

 The 1.42 percent rise in the benchmark TAIEX raised hopes of fresh foreign equity-linked inflows. 

 However, recent poor economic data and parliament's failure to approve key financial reforms kept sentiment depressed. 

 And with the central bank seen active on both sides, trading interest was also quite low.

title: Emerging  FX  - Docile in ranges but firm yen helps.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 7 (Reuters) - Asian currencies idled around recent ranges early Thursday while the market pondered over two major driving factors at the moment, the yen and baht. 

 The yen firmed against the dollar as it made gains against sterling. The pound was struggling ahead of the British general election amid talk a Labour government would adopt the euro but at the same time engineer a much competitive exchange rate before conversion. 

 But the yen's gains were relatively minute, and analysts expect it to flag given the stagnant Japanese economy. 

 Southeast Asian currencies have also been tracking the Thai baht, which was steady after it veered from a high of 44.74 to a low of 45.31 on Wednesday. 

 The Bank of Thailand threw another curve ball at the market, which had been bailing out of dollar longs given uncertainty over new reporting rules and fears of higher interest rates and possible new restrictions on forex trade. 

 But the central bank said on Wednesday it would delay the implementation of the rules, and Bangkok and Singapore dealers said there was talk the bank was buying dollars to cap the baht's rapid gains and bolster forex reserves. That spurred players to cover their short dollar positions. 

 Analysts said the bank's change of heart added more confusion and was another blow to foreign investor confidence. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was stabilising above 45.30 in a market that was growing increasingly wary of the Bank of Thailand. 

 New forex reporting rules and worries over possible new restrictions and higher interest rates had driven the baht to a high of 44.74 on Wednesday, its best level since March 30. 

 But talk that the BOT had bought dollar at 44.80 and the bank's decision to delay the implementation of the new reporting rules sent the baht past 45 again late Wednesday. 

 Singapore and Hong Kong dealers said players were uncomfortable with pushing the dollar/baht past Wednesday's high of 45.31. 

 But they added the baht was well-supported around 45, given local corporate dollar demand and the rumours of BOT intervention to support the dollar. 

SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore trailed after the firmer yen, but kept with a thin range of 1.8115-1.8120 as the market rooted around for fresh trading cues. 

 Dealers said the Sing was seen drifting around 1.8100, with some local players buying dollar on dips towards that level. 

 But the dollar/Sing's gains were limited to around 1.8130/40, close to the intraday highs on Tuesday and Wednesday, as U.S. names were spotted selling dollar around that level. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was expected to stay within its recent 50.50-50.80 range amid wariness over kidnappings by Muslim rebels and on rising local corporate dollar demand. 

 A steady yen and the baht were likely to limit losses. 

 The central bank's monetary board was also expected to lower key overnight interest rates after a slower than expected rise in May consumer prices index. 

 The overnight borrowing rate is now at 9.0 percent and lending rate is at 11.25 percent. 

 However, dealers said a 50 basis point cut has already been priced in. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won dipped as trade resumed after the Memorial Day holiday on Wednesday. 

 Singapore dealers said sentiment was glum on overnight profit warnings by J.P. Morgan Chase & Co and Hewlett-Packard Co and ahead of a preliminary report on quarterly earnings by computer giant Intel Corp due later in the day. 

 But they added the firmer yen was likely to lend support. 

 The Bank of Korea was widely expected to hold its key overnight call rate at five percent on inflation concerns at its monthly policy meeting later in the day. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar edged down on expected losses at the local stock market in line with the Nasdaq's fall overnight. 

 Singapore dealers said further depressing the sentiment was the opposition-dominated parliament's failure to approve key financial reform bills. 

 However, with some help from the yen on the downside and the central bank on guard on both sides, the Taiwan dollar was not expected to stray far from its recent 33.95-34.10 range. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah hovered above 11,200 thanks to the relative quiet on Jakarta's turbulent political scene. 

 But the rupiah's gains were expected to be capped around the 11,000 level given strong local corporate dollar demand and caution ahead of a special impeachment session in August. 

 The currency has been creeping higher this week on hopes President Abdurrahman Wahid will be forced out of office without much violence. 

 However, analysts say while the rupiah is expected to spike higher with Wahid's probable departure, the currency would later come under pressure given Indonesia's limping economy.

title: Emerging  FX  - Steady on local factors, eye on yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 6 (Reuters) - Asian currencies steered a steady course early Wednesday thanks to local factors, though they were mindful of the yen's direction. 

 So far, domestic cues have played out to regional currencies' advantage. The Indonesian rupiah kept its firmer tone as the market hoped President Abdurrahman Wahid would soon be ousted. 

 In Thailand, comments by the new Bank of Thailand governor Pridiyathorn Devakula, which indicated that interest rates would rise, boosted the baht. 

 But the yen slipped slightly against the dollar in overnight trading, and any further falls could dent regional currencies. 

 Recent U.S. data also showed continued weakness in the economy, with productivity falling, labour costs rising and activity slowing in the manufacturing and service sectors. 

 Analysts have said one of the conditions needed for Asian currencies to strengthen was a recovery in the U.S. economy, which has yet to show itself. 

 Markets in Seoul were closed for a public holiday and will re-open on Thursday. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was firmer despite the softer yen, extending gains to 44.80, its highest level since March 30. 

 Bangkok dealers said U.S. names and offshore banks began buying the baht late Tuesday on speculation of tighter forex rules effective on July 2 and expectations of higher rates. That triggered stop-loss dollar selling at 45.30, pushing the baht above 45. 

 But charts showed the dollar/baht was heavily overbought, with a 14-day relative strength index reading at 17.23, suggesting room for correction. 

 The cabinet formally approved a plan to establish a state-run Thai Asset Management Corp (TAMC) to buy bad loans from banks, which also gave the baht a marginal boost. 

 Finance ministry officials have said they expected TAMC to buy up to 1.35 trillion baht worth of non-performing loans from banks, of which about 1.1 trillion would come from state-owned or nationalised banks. 

 The Bank of Thailand said the total NPLs in the Thai financial system stood at 17.6 percent of total loans. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar bobbed around 1.8110-1.8120, caught between a softer yen and recent gains in the baht and the rupiah. 

 Analysts believe given the restrictive forex trading environment in Thailand and Indonesia, players were using the Sing dollar as a proxy. 

 Dealers said the Sing's upside was capped around 1.8100 on dollar buying by local corporates and the downside was around 1.8140 where hedge funds and local banks were seen selling the dollar earlier in the week. 

 Many analysts see 1.8200 as a strong near-term support on fears of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso drifted around 50.50 with some peso selling interest given the baht's recent gains and ahead of the weekly policy meeting of the central bank's monetary board on Thursday. 

 Manila dealers said the market was also keeping an eye on developments on the political front. 

 President Gloria Arroyo said on Tuesday she was considering imposing martial law in the troubled southern island of Basilan where Muslim rebels are holed in with U.S. and Filipino hostages. 

 A slower than expected rise in the May consumer price index has raised expectations of further monetary easing with the central bank saying overnight rates may fall to 8.25 percent if annual inflation averages around 6.25 percent. 

 The overnight borrowing rate is now at 9.0 percent and lending rate is at 11.25 percent. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was flat in light offshore trade as Seoul markets were closed for the Memorial Day holiday. 

 The currency has been tracking the yen closely, though it could feel downward pressure from foreign investors' net sales of 107.6 billion won worth of local stocks on Tuesday. 

 On the non-deliverable forward market, the one-month won was at 1,293/95 and the six-month was at 1,302/05. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 Dealers expected another rangebound day for the Taiwan dollar as the central bank was likely to keep the currency in its recent range. The bank was seen intervening at 34.02 and 34.14 in the past few days. 

 It opened a touch firmer at 34.037 against Tuesday's close of 34.043, but later slipped alongside the yen. 

 However, it was expected to be underpinned by fund inflows to the local stock market after the government announced stimulus measures on Monday to support the stock market. 

 Foreign investors bought a net T$1.27 billion in shares on Tuesday, accumulating a net T$2.76 billion over the last four sessions. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah held onto its recent gains, with sentiment improving ahead of a special impeachment session in August. 

 Jakarta dealers said players were optimistic that President Abdurrahman Wahid would soon be kicked out of office. Parliament has censured him twice on charges of corruption and incompetency. 

 However, analysts said the rupiah's gains were limited due to Jakarta's mercurial political scene and the threat of violence from Wahid's more fanatical supporters.

title: Emerging  FX  - Rangebound despite jumpy yen and baht.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 6 (Reuters) - Asian currencies opted for the safety of their recent ranges on Wednesday as the yen and Thai baht see-sawed. 

 The Thai baht fluctated from a high of 44.74 to back past the 45 mark amid speculation the central bank was buying dollars in order to stem the currency's rise and shore up reserves. 

 Bank of Thailand declined to comment on the talk. It also said it would delay the implementation of new disclosure laws, adding to the uncertainty that had helped support the baht along with fears of new restrictions on foreign exchange trading, and higher interest rates. 

 Singapore dealers took a dour view on the latest developments in Thailand, saying they feared the offshore baht market was seeing its last days. 

 "If they (BOT) keep messing around, then it's going to go the way of Indonesia, where everyone had enough of the central bank changing its mind and just got out," said a European bank dealer. Meanwhile, the yen slipped on renewed concerns over the stagnant Japanese economy and a firmer euro. 

 Seoul markets were closed for a public holiday and will re-open on Thursday. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was on the backfoot as players rushed to cover their short dollar positions after the central bank said it would delay new forex trade reporting rules, which were set for July 2. 

 After hitting a 44.74 high, its best level since March 30, the baht slipped past the 45 level again to hit a low of 45.31. 

 Singapore dealers said there was speculation the Bank of Thailand was buying dollar around 44.80 in order to slow the baht's rise and build up its reserves. The bank later declined to comment on the talk. 

 But dealers saw the dollar's rally as short-lived given the uncertainty over central bank policy. 

 Fears of possible new regulations and higher interest rates, and confusion over the new reporting rules have sent the baht higher as offshore players bailed out of dollar longs. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar settled at 1.8120 after a volatile session saw it slip to 1.8130 from 1.8070 earlier. 

 The main catalyst was the dollar/baht, with dealers reporting U.S. funds buying back dollar/Sing from 1.8070. 

 A survey of economists by the Monetary Authority of Singapore showed the country's economy is expected to grow 3.5 percent, at the lower end of the government's revised official forecast of 3.5 to 5.5 percent. 

 It also showed the weakness in the Sing dollar was likely to persist this year but the median exchange rate stood at 1.8000. Respondents expected the median exchange rate to strengthen to 1.770 in 2002. 

 The Sing dollar has lost more than four percent since the beginning of the year when it was at 1.7365. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso erased gains to slip to 50.72 from 50.50 earlier against 50.59 late Tuesday. 

 Manila dealers said a local bank alone bought $20-30 million at 50.55-65 on behalf of corporates. A foreign bank was also spotted buying $5-10 million at 50.55. 

 They added investors were still cautious as Muslim rebels holding hostages in the southern Philippines said a U.S. missionary captive had been injured in clashes with troops. 

 Such concerns pushed stocks down for the third straight session, also bruising sentiment for the peso. 

 But dealers said hopes for a rate cut given benign inflation data earlier this week underpinned the peso at 50.80. 

 The policy-making Monetary Board meets on Thursday. 

 The overnight borrowing rate stands at 9.0 percent and the lending rate at 11.25 percent. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah edged up to a session high of 11,120 before heavy local corporate dollar demand pulled it to levels around 11,200. 

 Jakarta dealers said the rupiah had been gaining on speculation President Abdurrahman Wahid may step down peacefully before impeachment hearings in August. 

 The rupiah is expected to spike higher if Wahid resigns but analysts say any gains would be temporary given the country's poor economic conditions. 

 Moody's said the political and social turmoil eroding government's ability to implement economic policy were not limited to events surrounding the presidency. 

 However, it kept a stable outlook on its B3 foreign currency country ceiling for bonds and notes. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar slipped by a hair's breadth due to the softer yen, but kept within a tidy range of 33.940-34.090. 

 Fears of central bank intervention prevented the Taiwan dollar from straying too far. 

Singapore dealers said the bank has been spotted on both sides of the market to keep the currency within a tight range. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was stable in dozy offshore trade as Seoul markets were closed for a public holiday, and will re-open on Thursday. 

 Bank of Korea will hold its monthly monetary policy setting meeting on Thursday. A recent Reuters poll showed economists unanimously seeing the bank holding its overnight call rate steady at five percent due to inflation fears. 

 On the offshore non-deliverable market, the one-month won was at 1,289/90 against 1,293/95 earlier in the day and the six-month was at 1,298/1,300 against 1,302/1,305.

title: Emerging  FX  - Yen helps, but local news hinders.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 29 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies held their ground with the help of the steadier yen late Tuesday, but local politics and poor economic data threatened to topple them out of their recent ranges. 

 Korea received confirmation of its slowdown with April industrial output falling by 1.3 percent on month against expectations of a 0.6 percent decline. 

 Politics continued to dominate Southeast Asian markets, with the Indonesian rupiah nervously eyeing Wednesday's key parliamentary session, which is expected to bring President Abdurrahman Wahid one step closer to impeachment. 

 Meanwhile, the baht see-sawed when the cabinet announced the sacking of Bank of Thailand Governor Chatu Mongol Sonakul, who had been engaged in a row with Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra over low interest rates. 

 The yen was steady against the dollar with investors eyeing London and New York trade for direction. Both markets were closed on Monday for public holidays. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht bounced up to around 45.50 after a dip following the government's decision to sack the central bank governor. 

 It touched a session low of 45.64 as soon as the news broke, mainly due to one U.S. investment bank covering short dollar positions taken earlier in the day. 

 But soon the market started to price in a rise in baht funding costs as interbank money market rates rose in anticipation of a hike in key rates and some state-linked companies were seen selling dollars. 

 Chatu Mongol was replaced by Pridiyathorn Devakula, chief of Thailand's Import-Export Bank and a leading supporter of the argument that higher rates were needed to kick-start the economy. 

 However, government officials were quick to deny talk of rate hikes saying the change of central bank chief would not affect monetary policy. 

 The incoming governor said the market should decide the appropriate level of interest rates, adding that the bank would ensure Thai monetary and fiscal policy were in line, to kick-start the economy. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah recovered to around 11,300 from lows of about 11,620 thanks to subdued corporate dollar demand and profit-taking in a market heavily long of dollars. 

 However, the relative calm could soon be disrupted, with parliament poised to decide on a special legislative session to impeach Wahid, who has been censured twice over charges of corruption and incompetency. 

 Wahid and other government officials have warned of violence if efforts to impeach him move ahead. Most protests so far have been conducted by Wahid's supporters. 

 Charts showed the dollar/rupiah has been on a downward trend since February 26, with support around 11,150. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was holding up near its session highs around 1,290 as month-end dollar sales by exporters trickled in through the day. 

 The dollar sales also helped the won off a low of 1,300 touched after industrial output data came in worse than expected and foreign funds, which had been selling local stocks for the past several sessions, came in to buy dollars. 

 April output fell a seasonally adjusted 1.3 percent month-on-month, against a 0.4 percent rise in March as exports limped and domestic consumption came off. 

 The April current account surplus fell to $634.8 million from $1.81 billion in March largely due to a 9.9 percent year-on-year fall in exports. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar recovered a bit as central bank intervention prompted profit-taking on the dollar's three percent rise on Monday. 

 Singapore dealers said offshore players took profit on their long dollar positions in early trade, and were waiting for the market to stabilise before taking on fresh dollar positions. 

 "The market really overshot itself on Monday," said a European bank dealer in Singapore. 

 Charts showed the dollar/Taiwan was venturing back from extremely overbought territory, with a 14-day relative strength index reading of around 73 against Monday's 98. 

 However, dealers said the Taiwan dollar's gains were likely to be capped just below the 34 level as the central bank is viewed as tolerating a weaker currency in its bid to boost Taiwan's flagging economy. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar clambered back to around 1.8100 having hit lows of 1.8150 earlier, as regional currencies benefited from the firmer yen. 

 Dealers said local banks which bought the U.S. dollar earlier began selling at around 1.8150, raising worries about possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 They added some interbank players were keen to buy the U.S. dollar on dips around 1.8080, limiting the Sing dollar's upside. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso recouped losses to 50.53 from early lows of 50.88. 

 Manila dealers said players took profit on their long dollar positions at 50.65-70 as the yen firmed, but car importers and foreign banks were looking to buy the dollar on dips at 50.30-50. 

 The market kept a wary eye on the fate of 20 hostages held by Muslim rebels since Sunday in the southern Philippines. 

 Local radio reports said the rebels threatened to kill their captives if they came under military attack. 

 Dealers also eyed a special Congressional session to pass a key power reform bill, seen as a litmus test of President Gloria Arroyo's commitment to economic reforms.

title: Emerging  FX -Yen losses hurt, politics grip rupiah.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 28 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were caught in the yen's downdraft late on Monday, which provided players with an excuse to add to their long dollar positions, dealers said. 

 The euro strengthened at the expense of the yen after talk of central bank intervention kept investors on alert in a market thinned by holidays in London and New York. 

 Political concerns also added to the region's woes. Indonesian President Abdurrahman Wahid warned in a nationally televised speech that any attempts to oust him would break Southeast Asia's most populous country apart. 

 In Thailand, the interest rate tussle between the government and central bank dragged on. A local newspaper reported that the government was preparing to order the central bank to force up deposit rates by 1.5 percentage points to spur spending. 

 But Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra denied the report, saying he had never ordered the central bank to do so. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah wilted past 11,500, briefly hitting one-month lows of 11,720, as Indonesia's leadership crisis dragged on. 

 The market showed little reaction to President Wahid's comments, which stopped short of carrying out his threat to declare a state of emergency. 

 Wahid is scrambling to save his presidency as parliament is set to meet on Wednesday to decide whether to press ahead with a special impeachment session of the top legislative body. 

 Jakarta dealers said the rupiah escaped further losses because local corporates had little appetite for dollars around these levels and state banks were also spotted selling dollars around 11,650. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht settled in a well-worn 45.56-45.62 range, caught between buying by government-linked exporters and selling from offshore banks, Bangkok dealers said. 

 The continuing battle between the government and central bank over interest rates weighed on sentiment. 

 Finance Minister Somkid Jatusripitak said the government would decide on the best level for interest rates after the central bank reports on its policy review on June 4. 

 Deposit rates currently stand at around two to three percent, with lending rates at seven to eight percent. Thai banks are unwilling to lend given their mountain of non-performing loans. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar struggled in the wake of poor economic data, hitting 32-month lows of 34.50 as the central bank let up its usual dogged defence in late trade. 

 Singapore dealers said the central bank sold up to $1.5 billion to slow the currency's fall, beginning its intervention early in the session around 33.495. But it later let the local dollar go in the face of heavy demand for dollars and the disappointing economic data. 

 After the close, the bank said it would enter the market to "maintain order" if necessary, attributing the local dollar's sharp fall to "untrue rumours". 

 While it had been bracing for bad news, the market was still glum over first quarter gross domestic product data issued after the close on Friday. The economy grew by a mere 1.06 percent on year, against forecasts of 3.25 percent. 

 The top economic planning agency said earlier in the day the economy slowed in April with no recovery in sight. Its index of leading indicators in April slipped 0.5 percent on month to 93.3. 

 Looking ahead, the Taiwan dollar could see some relief as the market is heavily long of dollars. Charts showed dollar/Taiwan looking hugely overbought, with a 14-day relative strength index reading of 98. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso dipped against Friday's 50.50 close, though it was off its day's low of 50.96. Local corporates seeking to repay foreign debt bought the dollar on dips towards 50.60. 

 Manila dealers said it was also weighed by ongoing political uncertainty coupled with weekend news of gunmen believed to be Muslim rebels seizing 20 people in a tourist resort in the southern Philippines. 

 The market was also eyeing a special Congressional session to debate a key power reform bill, viewed as a litmus test of the government's commitment to reform. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar was in limbo, stuck in a tight 1.8080-1.8118 range over the course of the day, but dealers said the mood was hurt by growing tension in Indonesia and the Philippines. 

 Local banks and U.S. names were offering the dollar at around 1.8110, stirring jitters about possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, which admitted it had intervened in the market earlier this month to support the Sing dollar. 

 "At any rate, people want to buy the dollar with all sorts of reasons from the Philippines, Indonesia to Taiwan, but they can't because of intervention fears," a European bank dealer said. 

 Given such fears, dealers expected the Sing dollar was unlikely to weaken beyond 1.8180 in the near term. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won closed near the top end of its Monday trading range of 1,293.2-1,298.0 despite the yen's retreat, buoyed by exporter dollar offers and some fund inflows. 

 But the upside was capped amid caution ahead of major economic data this week, including April industrial output on Tuesday and the May consumer price index on Thursday. 

 Economists polled by Reuters forecast industrial output fell 0.6 percent last month from March because of dwindling exports and sluggish domestic demand. 

 Inflation is expected to be tame due to seasonal factors. 

 "We expect negative month-on-month headline inflation for the first time this year. Declines in fruit and heating oil prices are likely to be the main course," Salomon Smith Barney said. 

 "Quite stable CPI figures should be favourable to the bond market. But headline inflation tends to be modest in May because of the seasonal stabilization in agricultural food prices," the bank said in a report.
