title: Emerging  FX  - Treading water, Japan data eyed.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 28 (Reuters) - Asian currencies pulled back early Monday as fears of intervention took away the yen's gains in a market thinned by holidays in London and New York. 

 The euro got a new lease on life as talk of central bank intervention kept investors on alert after it hovered just above six-month lows against the dollar earlier last week. 

 Gains in regional currencies last week were mostly due to the yen's rise, which was propelled by the euro's weakness rather than any improvement in Japan's economic fundamentals. 

 The market was focused on Japan's April industrial output due at 2350 GMT Monday. Economists polled by Reuters expected the data to show a fall for the second straight month. Elsewhere, local politics in Bangkok and Jakarta clouded the Thai baht and the Indonesian rupiah. 

 Investors were likely to stick to long dollar/baht positions as the Constitutional Court holds hearings on whether to uphold a ruling that Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra failed to correctly declare his assets during the 1990s. 

 The rupiah retained its bearish tone ahead of Wednesday's special parliamentary meeting, which could set in motion President Abdurrahman Wahid's impeachment. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar edged down to 1.8080 as players bought the dollar after disappointing output data released at the weekend. 

 Singapore's manufacturing output dipped 0.8 percent in April from a year ago after rising 6.4 percent in March, though it rose 6.1 percent on a three-month moving average. 

 Electronics output fell 8.8 percent in April from a year ago, on top of a five percent fall in March. 

 Dealers said local banks were keen to buy the Sing dollar at 1.8100, 1.8130 and below, reminding the market of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 The MAS admitted earlier this month it had intervened in the market to support the Sing dollar. Dealers expected it to intervene again if the Sing dollar breached 1.8150. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso slipped to 50.80 from 50.50 late on Friday in extremely thin morning trading. 

 "You want to buy the dollar, but you can't because no one is offering," a Manila dealer said. 

 Investors were upset by news that gunmen believed to be Muslim rebels seized 20 people including two U.S. missionaries on Sunday on a tourist resort in the the southern Philippines. 

 Reflecting jitters and underlying political uncertainty, four foreign brokerage houses have either ceased or suspended operations in the Philippines this year. More are expected to follow suit. 

 Socio-economic Planning Secretary dante Canlas said late on Friday he expected annual inflation to remain flat in May, and economic growth in the first quarter should be around 2.3-3.0 percent. The government is due to release inflation data for May in two weeks. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar edged closer towards the 33.50 mark, depressed over much lower than expected first quarter gross domestic product growth. 

 After the market's close on Friday, the state statistics agency said Taiwan saw growth of only 1.06 percent on year, against forecasts for 3.25 percent. 

 The government also lowered its GDP target for 2001 to 4.02 percent from a previous forecast of 5.25 percent. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah headed south in thin early trade, hitting one-month lows, with little relief in sight ahead of Wednesday's parliamentary meeting. 

 Parliament is expected to decide on whether to take the next step towards impeaching President Abdurrahman Wahid and call upon a special session of the top legislative body. 

 Meanwhile, a presidential spokesperson said Wahid, who was censured twice by parliament, was considering a state of civil emergency if parliament pressed ahead with impeachment. 

 However, it is unclear whether his senior ministers or the military woud support such a move. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won edged down on a softer opening of the local stock market but dealers in Singapore said the downside should be limited by continued equity-linked inflows and General Motors' expected takeover bid for Daewoo Motor. 

 They said Korean media reports suggested a GM delegation would reach Seoul on Monday and might announce the bid soon. 

 However, players were likely to tread cautiously amid uncertainty about the direction of the yen and ahead of some key economic data due this week. 

 April industrial output and current account data are due on Tuesday, the May producer price index on Thursday and May trade figures on Friday. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht pulled back below a key psychological level of 45.50 as importers and interbank players bought the dollar in the absence of fresh baht-supportive leads. 

 Dealers in Singapore said players were reluctant to buy the baht as it was not clear what the outcome of the court hearing on Prime Minister Thaksin would be even though some analysts believed his chances of surviving the case and holding on to his job now looked brighter. 

 Charts showed the dollar/baht was still trapped in a protracted consolidative phase which started around April 10. 

 The market is also focused on further development of the state-run Thai Asset Management Corp (TAMC) which will buy upto 1.2 trillion baht worth of bad loans from banks. 

 It is expected to get the formal green light this week and to start operations in June.

title: Singapore Dlr Lower Late; Tracks Yen, Regionals
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was lower late Monday, tracking weaker regional currencies and the yen, dealers said. However, intervention fears capped the local currency's downside. 

 Around 0816 GMT (4:16 a.m. EDT), the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.8115, up from S$1.8058 late Friday in Asia. It traded between S$1.8080 and S$1.8123 Monday. 

 The U.S. dollar opened higher, following late Friday's gains in London and New York. After a brief dip early in the day, it resumed its ascent across Asia, dealers said. 

 Dealers said European and U.S. banks and investment houses were the main buyers of U.S. dollars Monday, while local banks acting on customer orders and one U.S. bank were the main sellers. 

 Fears of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore to keep inflation in check prevented market participants from testing the immediate resistance at S$1.8130. 

 With April inflation at the top of the 1-2% tolerance band, the central bank is expected to resume intervening on the U.S. dollar's moves toward S$1.8200. 

 The U.S. dollar remain well supported at S$1.8080, dealers added. 

 Prices of benchmark Singapore government bonds ended mostly steady to a touch lower in thin trading. 

 Bond prices have held steady for the past two weeks as participants are comfortable with their positions and expect negligible downside to domestic interest rates. 

 "Prices were quoted slightly lower because of the higher rates, but hardly one or two trades were done today," a dealer said. 

 In the money market, the overnight rate eased from Friday's 3%, but remained above 2% for most of the day due to a weaker Singapore dollar. Term rates edged higher for the same reason. 

 Interest rate swaps ended narrowly mixed in a very thin market, with shorter-dated swaps gaining the most, while the seven- and 10-year swaps eased a touch. 

 The yield on two- and five-year bonds ended flat at 2.29% and 2.96%, respectively. 

 At the longer end of the curve, the yield on the seven-year bond was flat at 3.33%, while the yield on the 10-year bond rose one basis point to end 3.56%.

title: Singapore Dlr Dn Late, But Off Low; Local Bks Buy US Dlrs
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was lower against the U.S. dollar late Friday, but off its intraday low, dealers said. 

 Around 0834 GMT, the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.8058, up from S$1.8029 late Thursday in Asia. It traded between S$1.8020 and S$1.8080. 

 The U.S. dollar opened higher, tracking its gains against the yen, and rose further on buying by Singapore banks to fulfill corporate orders, dealers said. 

 However, the U.S. currency retreated after U.S. banks and investors sold long-U.S. dollar positions. A large local bank also joined in the selling to cut losses on the significant long positions it had built earlier in the day. 

 "Around S$1.8060, a big European bank also joined the selling and pushed (the U.S. dollar) into the S$1.8040s (by late afternoon)," said a senior dealer at a European bank in Singapore. 

 Dealers said the U.S. dollar's gains, for now, are expected to be capped at S$1.8080 on intervention fears. 

 In a research note, Singapore's DBS Bank said the Monetary Authority of Singapore may intervene further to defend the local dollar if inflation continues to trend higher following a 2% rise in Singapore's April consumer price index. 

 April inflation is at the top of the MAS' 1%-2% tolerance band. 

 Dealers said that, while in the short term, renewed yen strength could push the U.S. dollar lower against Asian currencies, the currency would likely find support from local companies around S$1.8000. 

 Prices of benchmark Singapore government bonds ended mostly steady to a touch lower in thin trading. Bond prices have held steady since last week as participants are comfortable with their positions and expect negligible downside to domestic interest rates. 

 Interest rate swaps ended higher, tracking a weaker local dollar. 

 In the money market, the overnight rate rose above 3% on pre-weekend fund demand before easing slightly in late afternoon trading. 

 Yields on two-year bonds rose one basis point to 2.28%, while five-year bond yields ended flat at 2.95%. 

 At the longer end of the curve, the yield on the seven-year bond was flat, at 3.33%, while the yield on the 10-year bond rose one basis point to end 3.55%.

title: Emerging  FX  - Unsteady, but still rangebound.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 21 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were 

 unsteady early Monday due to lingering unease over the Morgan 

 Stanley Capital International reweighting of its indices. 

     But analysts said the reweighting would have a limited 

 impact on markets as it had been largely priced in already. 

 They noted the announcement made on Saturday had few surprises. 


    The dollar was flat against the yen	  in early Asian



trade, providing some relief for regional currencies. It was



also little changed against the euro , which hit



five-month lows on Friday.



With few fresh factors in sight, regional currencies were



likely to stay fenced in their recent ranges. Analysts say



Asian markets were now looking for further clues as to where



the economy of the United States, its largest export market,



was headed in the second half.



In the meantime, there was some major economic data from



the region due later in the week. Taiwan will issue its first



quarter current account data on Monday, April industrial



production, export data and jobless rate on Wednesday, and



first quarter gross domestic growth on Friday.



    Korea is expected to issue first-quarter GDP on Friday.



    SINGAPORE DOLLAR	



    The Sing dollar dipped more than a half cent to 1.8125 from



late Friday's 1.8057, pressured by the lower yen.



    Dealers said players took profits on short dollar



positions, but the Sing's downside was supported by U.S.



investment banks actively selling the dollar at 1.8120.



    Singapore's weighting in the MSCI's All Country World Free



Index fell to 0.26 percent from 0.38 percent, but the market



has shown little reaction as the move was well flagged.



    Analysts said fears of possible intervention by the


Monetary Authority of Singapore were still intact, especially



at levels above 1.8150.



    THAI BAHT	



    The baht drifted off to 45.60 from 45.42 late on Friday.



    Bangkok dealers said Singapore-based banks bought the



dollar from 45.40, but rice exporters were offering the dollar



at 45.55.



    They added local companies were keen to buy the baht at



below 45.50.



    The Bank of Thailand said late on Friday it did not expect



a decision by the government to raise its planned 2001/2002



budget deficit would create debt financing problems for the



country.



    The government approved a plan to raise the budget deficit



to 3.5 percent of GDP from 2.7 percent planned earlier.



    PHILIPPINE PESO	



    The peso also edged down in line with weaker regional


currencies, opening at 50.40 against 50.33 late on Friday.



    Manila dealers expected companies with dollar debt are



looking to buy the dollar from 50.20-30.



    Finance undersecretary Juanita Amatong said the government



plans to sell between $500 million and $700 million worth of



bonds in the United States, Japan and Europe next month.



    The National Treasurer said the foreign borrowing would be



a crucial part of the government's mid-year financing



programme. The country expects its budget deficit to reach 145



billion pesos this year.



Political uncertainty also weighed on the peso. Unofficial



results showed President Gloria Arroyo's coalition was holding



its lead in the fight for 13 senate seats.



Analysts have said Arroyo's coalition must win nine of the



contested Senate seats to secure a majority and ensure passage



of vital economic reform measures.



KOREAN WON -2



The won was flat as it trotted alongside the yen, though



sentiment towards the currency may be lifted by cheer in the



local bourse over MSCI's higher weighting for Korean shares.



But analysts said any real gains from the MSCI reweighting



would be slight as it had been long anticipated, and fresh



foreign fund inflows due to the higher weighting would be



staggered. Korea's weighting rose by 3.3 percent in the MSCI



emerging market index.



However, with little new in the market, the won was



unlikely to break its recent range. Since May 7, it has kept



within a narrow range of 1,294-1,310.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH



The rupiah succumbed to familiar complaints of thin dollar



liquidity and local corporate dollar demand amid political



wrangling.



    The currency was straddling the 11,400 mark, with little



relief in sigh as the country's political crisis dragged on.



    The latest political scuttlebutt over the weekend in



Jakarta was that President Abdurrahman Wahid planned to declare



a state of emergency in order to repel a bid to impeach him.



    However, a spokesman later denied Wahid would take such a



measure. A cabinet meeting was also held on Sunday, with the



two main players of the current political drama conspicuously



absent - Wahid and his deputy and political rival, Megawati



Sukarnoputri.



TAIWAN DOLLAR



The Taiwan dollar drooped past 33 against Friday's close of



32.948 to the dollar.



    The market was upset by a forecast from a research house



that saw the local dollar at 38 to the dollar.



    Analysts have said they expected the currency to weaken



given Taiwan's slowing economy and heightened export



competition. However, most analysts do not see the Taiwan



dollar falling past 35 to the dollar.



But Taipei dealers said they spotted the central bank


selling dollars in order to prevent steeper falls in the local


currency.



    Hopes for foreign fund inflows and exporters' dollar sales



were also expected to underpin the local dollar.

title: Emerging  FX  - Aided by steady yen, U.S. data.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 18 (Reuters) - A steady yen continued to provide support to Asian currencies early Friday and further help was expected from encouraging U.S. data and Wall Street's overnight performance. 

 In early trade, the yen was off overnight highs but far from lows around 124 seen earlier in the week, aided by option plays, recent gains in the Nikkei, and doubts over Japan's tolerance for a weaker currency. 

 But analysts warned speculation on the impact of changes to the MSCI equity indices on Saturday could result in outflow of funds from Japanese stocks in favour of U.S. markets. 

 A surprise fall in U.S. first-time jobless claims to their lowest level in two months buoyed hopes of a recovery in export-dependent Asia's largest market. 

 The weekly claims fell by 8,000 to 380,000, signalling resilience of the labour market - keenly watched by analysts for its links to consumer spending which accounts for two-thirds of overall economic activity in the U.S. 

 The Nasdaq rose 1.26 percent and the Dow 0.29 percent as computer giant Hewlett-Packard reported a quarterly profit higher than market estimates. 

 Markets will now watch for any clues from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's speech to bankers later Friday and to an economic club on May 24. 

 Meanwhile, no surprises were expected from the second day of the Bank of Japan's policy meeting. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar kept a firmer tone at just above 1.8050, showing little reaction to news gross domestic product rose 4.5 percent on year in the first quarter, a shade below the government's advance estimate of 4.6 percent growth. On an annualised seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter basis, first quarter growth was down a sharp 11 percent against a 10 percent growth rate in the fourth quarter. 

 The Ministry of Trade and Industry said the second quarter would weaken further and Singapore might experience a technical recession, or two consecutive quarters of negative growth, but this did not change its full year forecast. 

 The Sing dollar continued to be supported by fears of further intervention following the Monetary Authority of Singapore's confirmation earlier this week that it had sold the U.S. dollar when the Sing dollar hit fresh 11-year lows of 1.8265 last week. 

 Dealers said players were merely liquidating their long U.S. dollar positions, with little fresh buying of Sing dollars in sight. They added European banks were looking to buy the U.S. dollar at around 1.8020-30. 

 But analysts doubted the Sing dollar would extend gains in the mid term, given gloomy economic fundamentals. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was a tad higher at 45.30 thanks to the firmer yen and the regional currencies. 

 Bangkok dealers said players liquidated their long dollar positions after the Bank of Thailand's move to tighten disclosure rules on baht trading for non-resident accounts from July 2. 

 Also positive for the baht, the government said it would cut corporate tax for companies listed on the Thai bourse to 25 percent from 30 percent as part of efforts to revive the sagging stock market. 

 Dealers said oil importers were looking to buy the U.S. dollar at around 45.20-25. Baht funding costs in the offshore market were nearly flat, with the one-month forward rate at 8/13 satang per dollar against 5/15. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso eased to 50.30 as local banks covered their short dollar positions. 

 Manila dealers said importers were looking to sell the peso at 50.00-10, but buying orders from shipping companies were supporting the downside at 50.20-30. 

 The Philippines' trade surplus jumped to $1.297 billion in the first quarter from $731 million a year ago. 

 Political uncertainty lingered, as no clear winner had yet emerged in the race for control of the Senate. Unofficial results showed President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo's People Power Coalition on course to win eight of the 13 Senate seats on offer. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won edged up touching a high of 1,294 on the back of a steadier yen and as Wall Street's overnight gains helped the local stock market. 

 However, dealers in Singapore said an uncertain economic outlook and expected pre-weekend profit-taking in stocks were likely to prompt dollar buying on dips. 

 They said dollars bids were already emerging beyond 1,300, and were expected to cap the won around 1,290-1,295. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar inched up with the yen and on expected gains in the local stock market after Wall Street's rise. 

 But trade was likely to be within the 32.93-32.96 range, as players were unlikely to push the Taiwan dollar much higher on fears of central bank intervention. 

 Dealers in Singapore said Thursday's widely expected rate cut would raise hopes of more foreign inflows into the stock market. 

 The central bank lowered the discount rate to 3.75 percent and the accommodation with collateral rate, which banks pay when using government bonds as collateral for central bank loans, to 4.125 percent. 

 It was the sixth rate cut since late December, bringing the total easing to a full percentage point, with Thursday's quarter point cut twice as large as any of the previous three. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah nudged lower but was expected to stay within its recent 11,300-11,450 range despite rising political tensions, given fears of central bank intervention. 

 Parliament is due to reconvene on May 30 when an impeachment hearing is expected to begin against President Abdurrahman Wahid for his alleged involvement in graft scandals. 

 Dealers in Singapore said first quarter GDP data due later in the day was unlikely to impact sentiment, with the market more concerned about political developments. 

 Meanwhile, the IMF praised Indonesia's move to submit revised 2001 budget assumptions to parliament, saying this would pave the way for the release of a delayed $400 million loan. The cabinet on Thursday approved the revised figures, which are likely to be presented to parliament on Monday.

title: Singapore Dlr Higher Late; Tracks Yen, GDP Impact Muted
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was higher late Friday, but off its intraday high, as it tracked the yen in a listless session, dealers said. 

 The release of expectedly weak first-quarter growth data and a bearish outlook for the economy failed to hurt the local currency much, as market participants were yet to recover from heavy intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore last week. 

 "The market would have loved to buy U.S. dollars, but most were still licking their wounds inflicted during the acknowledged MAS intervention of (last) week," Bank of America said in a research note. 

 Around 0841 GMT (4:41 a.m. Friday EDT), the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.8069, down from S$1.8095 in Asia late Thursday. 

 The U.S. dollar opened lower, hitting an intraday low of S$1.8040, as it fell below Y123. 

 The U.S. currency rose slightly on the weak Singapore growth data, but most of its partial recovery came in the wake of renewed yen weakness. The dollar climbed to as high as Y123.41. 

 Singapore revised its estimate for economic growth in the first quarter to 4.5% from an advance estimate of 4.6% issued in April. 

 Significantly, the data showed that growth momentum, based on an annualized, quarter-on-quarter basis, turned negative for the first time since the Asian crisis, down by a sharp 11%, from 10% growth in the fourth quarter. 

 The government retained its economic growth forecast for 2001 at an already-revised 3.5%-5.5%, but added that global economic outlook is still bearish. 

 Ministry of Trade & Industry Chief Economist Tan Kong Yam said that while quarter-on-quarter growth momentum could contract again in the second quarter, overall year-on-year growth is expected to remain positive in the second quarter of this year. 

 Prices of benchmark Singapore government bonds ended flat to a touch higher as market participants focused on buying off-run issues, or older bonds that are close to maturity, that have been lagging benchmark prices, dealers said. 

 Overall, trading in Singapore government bonds was very light, and the weak growth data and outlook generally supported prices.

title: Emerging  FX -Boosted by Wall St,  central bank  moves.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 17 (Reuters) - Asian currencies edged higher in early trade on Thursday as strong gains on Wall Street provided a psychological boost by raising hopes for more inflows. 

 The Dow Jones Industrial average rose 34.95 points or 3.15 percent to close above the key 11,000 mark for the first time since September 14. 

 Market participants were also reluctant to buy the dollar against some currencies as they were unnerved by recent actions by central banks. 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore confirmed to a local newspaper on Wednesday that it had intervened in foreign exchange markets last week to support the Sing dollar. 

 In Thailand, the central bank said on Wednesday it would tighten disclosure rules on baht trading for non-resident accounts from July 2 to curb speculation on the local currency. 

 And Bank Indonesia said it expected to keep conducting "prudent and measurable" intervention in the foreign exchange market to prevent excessive hikes in interest rates which are already at 21-month highs. 

 BI has been gradually raising rates in a largely unsuccessful attempt to stem the rupiah's losses. But critics said such moves would hurt the state budget and the troubled banking sector. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was trading around two-week highs after the central bank said it would soon take more steps to stave off speculation. 

 Dealers said players rushed to pare long dollar positions, although some bargain hunting was likely to emerge below 45.20. 

 They said the next key target for the baht is 45.06 which it has failed to breach since April 19. 

 On the credit rating front, Fitch IBCA, Duff & Phelps said on Wednesday it had no plans to change Thailand's sovereign ratings and stable outlook despite the regional and global slowdown. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar climbed above 1.8100, thanks to scattered buying by interbank players early in the morning. 

 Dealers were ever more wary of further intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, given its rare confirmation that it sold the U.S. dollar last week. Finance Minister Richard Hu also spooked dealers by saying the amounts involved in recent overseas acquisitions by local companies were not large enough to move the Sing dollar. 

 That fear helped the Sing dollar clamber back to 3-= week highs, off 11-year lows of 1.8265 hit last week. 

 And some dealers expected further liquidation of long dollar positions after the issue of April non-oil exports data, due at 0430 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters expected on a 1.8 percent rise against a 2.1 percent contraction in March thanks to a low base effect and the weaker Sing dollar. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was loitering around the 11,300 level with players reluctant to trade given the country's volatile politics. 

 President Abdurrahman Wahid said earlier in the week he expected to be impeached, though he added that he would continue fighting and would also run for the 2004 presidential polls. His spokesman later denied he had said he expected to be impeached. 

 Meanwhile, Indonesian political leaders have said an impeachment session seemed inevitable. 

 On the economic front, Finance Minister Prijadi Praptosuhardjo said on Wednesday the cabinet would discuss changes to the 2001 budget and submit them to parliament soon. 

 Those revisions were expected to be handed down to parliament in mid-May, and need to be ratified for the IMF to review Jakarta's progress on reforms and resume lending. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO The peso edged up to 50.09 against Wednesday's local 50.14 close, helped by firmer regional currencies and the yen. 

 Manila dealers said energy and power companies were looking to buy the dollar at around 49.80, otherwise staying on the sidelines to wait for more attractive levels. 

 Dealers said the prospect of a rate cut by the central bank also helped lift the mood. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said the Monetary Board was biased to cut key interest rates following the U.S. rate cut. The board holds its weekly meeting later on Thursday. 

 The Philippines' overnight borrowing rate is currently at 9.5 percent and the lending rate at 11.75 percent. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 A firmer yen lifted the Taiwan dollar, which ended at a six-week low of 32.957 on Wednesday, pushing it back the right side of 32.90. 

 The market was viewing the central bank's recent dollar-buying as an effort to guide the currency lower in order to maintain Taiwan's export competitiveness amid slowing demand. 

 For the past few weeks, the bank has kept the local dollar in a tight range of 32.85-90, but allowed the currency to close past 32.90 for the first time since April 30 on Tuesday. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won recovered some ground thanks to the firmer yen. 

 An early rally on the local bourse also lifted sentiment towards the won with the market hoping for further foreign funds' equity-linked inflows. 

 Even though Korean shares ended lower on Wednesday, foreign investors were net buyers, purchasing a net 16.6 billion won worth of shares. They bought a net 5.2 billion won worth of shares in early trading on Thursday. 

 However, the won was unable to hold onto its earlier high of 1,301.5. For the past two sessions, it has been unable to break resistance of around 1,302 convincingly as local importers sought dollars on dips.

title: Emerging  FX  - Buoyed by yen, Wall St gains.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 17 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were buoyed in late trade on Thursday by euphoria over robust gains on Wall Street, the yen's firmer footing, and caution over moves by some regional central banks. 

 But the dollar's consolidation was expected to be short-lived as its fundamentals remained relatively sound compared with other major currencies. 

 "I just can't imagine the yen and the euro strengthening against the dollar on a sustained basis at this juncture given fundamental pictures in Japan and the euro zone are not that bright," said a dealer at a major Asian bank. 

 "In emerging Asian markets, the dollar is pretty much in favour. I don't expect the Sing dollar to poke above 1.8000 or the baht above 45.00. There are lots of companies out there who will gladly pick up the dollar around those levels," he said. The market is focused on U.S. weekly jobless claims data, due at 1230 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters forecast that 395,000 people appled for unemployment benefits in the week ending May 12, up from 384,000 the previous week. 

 Elsewhere, Singapore's non-oil domestic exports fell 1.2 percent on year in April, against expectations of a 1.8 percent rise. April was the second straight month of decline, confirming market views that Singapore's economy continued to weaken. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar zipped up more than half a cent to 3-= week highs of 1.8073. 

 The main catalyst for the latest rise was growing fears of further intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, which confirmed it had sold the U.S. dollar last week. 

 "Our recent comment on having intervened in the market last week was made to reiterate our unchanged S$ policy, notwithstanding short-term M&A flows," the MAS told Reuters. 

 The Sing dollar has lost nearly four percent since the beginning of the year in part due to M&A-linked capital outflows, which are estimated to be up to $14.5 billion. 

 Singapore's first quarter economic survey is due out at 0000 GMT on Friday. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso edged up to 50.05 at one stage before buying by oil companies pushed it back to 50.26. 

 The Philippine central bank cut its overnight rates by 50 basis points following the U.S. rate cut earlier this week. This will bring the borrowing rate to 9.0 percent and the lending rate to 11.25 percent. 

 Analysts said the central bank might cut rates further next month if the U.S. Federal Reserve eased again. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht managed to stay around 45.30, after being beaten down by dollar orders from importers and companies when it tried to break above 45.15. 

 Bangkok dealers said the market had largely factored in news of the central bank's plan to further tighten disclosure rules on baht trading for non-resident accounts from July 2. 

 "I think what the market is concerned about is not the new regulations themselves but the central bank's gesture. After all, this is just a modification of the existing rules," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in Bangkok. 

 "The amount of money in the non-resident accounts is around $420 million which is not substantial," he said. 

 Baht funding costs in the offshore market moved left, with players unwinding dollar/baht positions in the forward market. The one-month rate was quoted at 5/15 satang per dollar and three-month at 30/45. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah enjoyed some gains as players unwound their long dollar positions due to slack corporate demand. 

 Jakarta dealers said a local company sold around $30 million through state banks, prompting interbank players to follow suit. 

 Market turnover was estimated around $150 million, which dealers said was close to the average seen in recent sessions. 

 But they added the rupiah's outlook was still dim given the tangled economic and political problems Indonesia faces. 

 First quarter gross domestic product data is due on Friday. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won trailed the firmer yen, with sentiment getting an additional boost from rallying local stocks. 

 While the yen remained the dominant influence, the won cheered over foreign funds' inflows headed for the local bourse. Foreign investors bought a net 28.3 billion won worth of local stocks for the day, though they remained net sellers of 53.9 billion won worth so far this week. 

 However the currency was unable to push through the 1,300 level, last touched on May 14. 

 The market showed little reaction to news the unemployment rate fell to 3.8 percent in April from 4.2 percent in March. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar ended at 32.952, below its opening of 32.946 due to the central bank's active U.S. dollar buying in what analysts see as a drive to keep exports competitive. 

 But the downside was underpinned by a steadier yen and Wall Street-inspired gains in the local stock market. 

 Taiwan stocks raked in 1.21 percent gains, dovetailing a sharp rise on Wall Street. Foreign investors bought Taiwan shares worth a net T$1.22 billion on Thursday after selling a net T$299 million in the previous session. 

 The central bank announced at an impromptu news conference that it was cutting key rates by 0.25 percentage points, its sixth easing since December.

title: MAS confirms S$  intervention , policy unchngd-paper.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 16 (Reuters) - The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) sold U.S dollars on the foreign exchange market last week in support of the weak Singapore currency, the Business Times (BT) newspaper reported on Wednesday. 

 "MAS confirmed in writing to BT yesterday that it sold US dollars in the market last week - a departure from its usual practice of not commenting on its actions," the paper said. 

 The action followed strong demand for U.S. dollars against the Singapore dollar, linked to recent merger and acquisition flows and market expectations of those flows, BT said. 

 The newspaper quoted the central bank saying: "MAS will continue to do so when necessary to offset any market impact of such corporate demand for U.S. dollar against the Sing dollar." 

 The MAS also confirmed to the newspaper that its policy for a modest and gradual appreciation of the Singapore dollar remains unchanged. 

 "This policy is based on our medium term assessment of the economy, not short-term economic or inflation developments," the MAS said in its statement. 

 The Singapore dollar edged higher to 1.8150 on Wednesday, up more than one cent from the fresh 11-year lows around 1.8265 hit last week. 

 The Sing dollar has lost more than four percent since the beginning of the year.

title: Emerging  FX  - Steadier as Fed decision meets hopes.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 16 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were mixed early Wednesday following a widely expected interest rate cut by the U.S. Federal Reserve. 

 But analysts said with the U.S. seen nearing the end of its easing cycle, players in the region will focus on regional problems again as the global downturn drags on. 

 The Fed cut the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 4.0 percent, its lowest level in seven years. It also cut the more symbolic discount rate by the same amount to 3.5 percent. 

 The statement announcing the cut, the fifth 50 basis point cut so far this year, said it saw excessive weakness as the main threat to the economy, and repeated concerns about falling investment spending and weak corporate profits. 

 Analysts said slower investment spending was especially pronounced in the tech sector, to which most of Asia is exposed. 

 A Reuters poll following the cut showed most primary dealers expecting the pace of easing to slow at the Fed's next meeting on June 26-27. 

 The yen saw its earlier gains slip away, while the euro was little moved from overnight levels. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar firmed to 1.8150 from 1.8186 late Tuesday. 

 Dealers attributed the gain partly to comments by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. "(The) MAS intervened last week to keep the Singapore dollar within its policy band," the MAS told a local newspaper. 

 The MAS is believed to have sold at least $500 million when the Sing hit fresh 11-year lows of around 1.8265. 

 It also said the policy to allow the Sing to gradually appreciate is based on its medium-term assessment of the economy, and said it would intervene when necessary. 

 "Not surprising, because everybody in the market knew it came in," a European bank dealer said. "But people are using this as an excuse to take profits." 

 He added better-than-expected March retail sales data also offered reasons to liquidate U.S. dollar long positions. 

 April non-oil domestic exports data is due on Thursday. A Reuters poll forecast a 1.8 percent on-year rise from a 2.1 percent contraction in March. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah held onto levels above 11,500, though its near-term outlook was still grim. 

 While the market remained long on dollar, Jakarta dealers have said local corporate demand for dollar amid the country's turbulent politics was strong. 

 There is also talk that around $3-$5 billiion in foreign debt will be due by mid-June, adding further pressure to the rupiah. 

 President Abdurrahman Wahid said on Tuesday he expected to be impeached. But he also made clear that he would not go without a fight, which would throw the country into a fresh crisis. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 Uncertainty about the outcome of Monday's elections, seen as a test of President Gloria Arroyo's popularity, was likely to keep the peso trapped within the 50.00-50.50 range. 

 Manila dealers said most players believed Arroyo's candidates will get most of the crucial 13 Senate seats but will fall short of a definite majority. 

 Meanwhile, the central bank said it would consider the inflation trend in deciding whether to lower its key overnight rates following the U.S. rate cut. 

 The overnight borrowing rate is currently at 9.5 percent and the lending rate at 11.75 percent. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was marginally firmer, but was still in a familiar range as players trimmed dollar longs. 

 The market took heart from the Fed's latest cut, which many believed would jump-start the sagging U.S. economy - a major market for exports from Asia. 

 Dealers said investors took news of the cabinet raising budget deficit for October 2001-September 2002 to 200 billion baht from 150 billion baht with a grain of salt. 

 "In theory, a bigger stimulus package should be good news," said a Bangkok dealer. 

 "But I guess the market was not excited because the amount is not that big. Moreover, the market wants to know how the government will channel the increased liquidity to the real economy." 

 Singapore dealers expected the baht to loiter in the 45.40-45.50 range. Baht funding costs in the offshore market was steady at 10/15 satang for dollar for the one-month forward rate. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was steady, drifting in a thin market after opening at 1,303.0 versus the Tuesday's close of 1,303.7. 

 The currency is likely to be caught between a softer yen and hopes of M&A inflows, with U.S. automobile giant General Motors expected to make an announcement next week on its talk to buy certain assets from Daewoo Motor. 

 Its upside is likely to be capped by recent foreign funds selling of local stocks. Foreign investors sold 95.1 billion won worth of local shares on Tuesday and around 1.5 billion won in early trade. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar slipped as the yen failed to hold onto its earlier gains. 

 Analysts have said that of the regional authorities, the Taiwan central bank was one of the most likely to follow the Fed in its easing cycle. So far this year, the Taiwan central bank has slashed rates by 75 basis points, still less than the 250 basis points that the Fed has cut. 

 While a rate cut typically would hurt the currency as it makes local assets less attractive, the market could view further easing by the Taiwan central bank positively as it seeks to boost economic growth. 

 But the market was expecting any sharp moves in the Taiwan dollar to be counteracted by the central bank.

title: UPDATE 2-Singapore downplays M&A impact on  currency .
text:
SINGAPORE, May 16 (Reuters) - Singapore on Wednesday played down the impact an estimated outflow of up to US$14.5 billion resulting from overseas acquisitions would have on the local currency. 

 "I don't think the amounts are sufficiently large to move the Singapore dollar in a significant way," the Minister of Finance, Richard Hu, said in Parliament on Wednesday. 

 But he said the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), would take any short-term impact into account. 

 The finance minister's statement followed recent weakness in the Singapore dollar against the U.S. unit on the foreign exchange market, which traders have linked to merger and acquisition flows and market expectations of these flows. 

 Singapore Telecommunications announced in March a planned purchase of Australia's second largest telco, Cable & Wireless Optus Ltd , worth up to US$8.7 billion. 

 When asked about whether there was any change in the terms of the proposed acquisition of Optus, Hu said: "I'm not aware of any significant change." 

 SingTel, currently 78 percent owned by the government, is seeking approval from Australian authorities for its takeover of C&W Optus, which is 52-percent owned by Britain's Cable & Wireless Plc . 

 Separately, DBS Group , in which the government owns 38 percent, has mounted a bid worth up to US$5.8 billion for Hong Kong's Dao Heng Bank . 

 MAS INTERVENES TO SUPPORT SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The MAS, in a rare departure from a policy of no comment, confirmed to a local newspaper, the Business Times, on Wednesday that it has been selling U.S dollars in support of the weak Singapore currency. 

 "MAS confirmed in writing to BT yesterday that it sold US dollars in the market last week - a departure from its usual practice of not commenting on its actions," the paper reported on its front page on Wednesday. 

 The newspaper quoted the central bank saying: "MAS will continue to do so when necessary to offset any market impact of such corporate demand for U.S. dollar against the Sing dollar." 

 The MAS also confirmed that its policy for a modest and gradual appreciation of the Singapore dollar remains unchanged. 

 "This policy is based on our medium term assessment of the economy, not short term economic or inflation developments," the MAS said in its statement. 

 The Singapore dollar, which has lost more than four percent since the beginning of the year, edged up to 1.8125/35 0850 GMT, up from fresh 11-year lows hit last week at 1.8265. 

 OVERSEAS ACQUISITIONS OF STRATEGIC INTERESTS 

 Hu said the proposed purchases by Singapore government-linked companies of both Optus and Dao Heng Bank were long term strategic business moves. 

 "Hong Kong is clearly one market, (which) for obvious reasons, is a must for DBS since they are going to be a regional player," Hu said. 

 The government has been encouraging local firms to grow beyond the confines of the Singapore economy for some time. 

 Hu said both acquisitions were such moves, and they would enable them to tap regional opportunities and become more than Singaporean companies. 

 SingTel's expansion plans hit snags twice last year as bids for stakes in Hong Kong's C&W HKT and Malaysia's Time Engineering fell through on perception that the firm was controlled by the Singapore government. 

 In an effort to shake the perception, the eighth largest telecom firm in Asia said last month the Singapore government had given up its special share which offered veto rights over major corporate decisions. 

 Hu said the government did not interfere in the commercial decisions of government-linked firms. 

 "Their soundness (acquisitions) has to be judged over time by the performance of SingTel and DBS, and not by the immediate reaction of the stock market as reflected in their share prices." 

 Hu also defended both acquisitions which were seen too high for the price of growth. 

 "When you buy controlling shares in a large operation, generally you have to pay a substantial premium," he said, adding that the size of the premium was a judgement the management had to take and it was not in the government's interest to challenge.

title: Emerging  FX -Fed cuts soothe some, but yen weighs.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 16 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were mostly firmer in late trade on Wednesday after interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve raised hopes of economic recovery in the world's major growth locomotive. 

 In a statement that followed the cut, the fifth 50 basis point reduction so far this year, the Fed repeated concerns about falling investment spending and weak corporate profits. 

 But the positive impact of the cut was countered by a weaker yen which retraced to its two-week lows around 124 amid talk of Japanese investor demand for overseas assets. 

 Local factors also played a key role in lifting some currencies, particularly the Singapore dollar and the Thai baht. 

 The Sing dollar made strong gains after the Monetary Authority of Singapore confirmed it intervened last week to offset the impact of strong M&A outflows. Dealers said the confirmation, which is unusual, served as a notice that it would not tolerate further slippage in its trade-weighted currency. 

 The Thai baht lurched higher after the Bank of Thailand said it would further tighten disclosure rules on the baht to stave off speculation. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht lept above 45.40 on news the central bank was planning to further tighten disclosure rules on baht trading for non-resident accounts from July 2. 

 Bank of Thailand spokesman Bandid Nijathaworn said financial institutions would need to give more information about spot, forward, and swap transactions, derivative transactions, equity or debt instrument deals between them and non-resident accounts. 

 Bangkok dealers said market participants rushed to cut losses by unwinding long dollar positions after the baht breached above 45.40, although the dollar retracement was met promptly by demand from companies and importers. 

 Baht funding costs in the offshore market also eased further as demand to borrow the baht to fund dollar holdings ebbed. The one-month forward rate was quoted at 9.5/17.0 satang per dollar, but there was not much trade done as the spread was wide. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar firmed as local banks offloaded U.S. dollars following comments from authorities reaffirming their commitment to a tightening monetary bias. 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore confirmed, in the local press, it intervened last week to offset the impact of an M&A inspired hike in corporate demand for the U.S. dollar. 

 Finance Minister Richard Hu told parliament the amounts involved in recent overseas acquisitions by local companies were not large enough to move the Sing dollar. 

 Dealers said local banks led the U.S. dollar sales and were followed by players already seeking to trim long positions. 

 "The near-term trading range could be 1.8100-1.8140 but that is contingent to the yen not weakening significantly beyond 124," a chief dealer of a European bank in Singapore said. INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah hovered around 11,400 with the market eyeing warily President Aburrahman Wahid's comment that he would not quit and would in fact fight the next presidential polls in 2004. 

 On Tuesday, Wahid told a seminar he expected to be impeached by parliament but on Wednesday his spokesman denied he made the comment. 

 Jakarta dealers said trading conditions were thin with most activity led by state banks active on both sides of the market. 

 However, most players kept to the sidelines as heads of parliamentary factions met to discuss a possible change in leadership and timing of any impeachment hearing against Wahid. 

 Meanwhile, Bank Indonesia said it would continue to intervene to support the rupiah and avoid excessive hike in interest rates. 

 The central bank also said the Fed rate cut could have an impact on its weekly SBI certificate auction, which saw the one-month rate reach 16.31 percent from 16.26 percent last week. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won edged lower in line with the falling yen, touching a two-week low of 1,310.2, where some export and equity-related inflows capped the downside. 

 Dealers said hopes of foreign direct investment inflows from the potential sale of Daewoo Motor Co. and Hynix Semiconductor to foreign investors kept sentiment supported. 

 The consumer confidence survey for April also came in better than the previous month but dealers in Singapore said they were more worried about the economy of Korea's biggest export market. 

 With a recovery in the U.S. still unclear despite the Fed's aggressive rate cuts, the won was expected to stay depressed. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso ended at 50.14 after reaching a high of 50.06 from lows of 50.21. 

 Manila dealers said local banks bought the peso earlier, but foreign banks and IT companies were looking to buy the U.S. dollar at 50.10-20. 

 The government said the preliminary January-April budget deficit was 36.717 billion pesos, lower than its target of 38.3 billion for the period. 

 President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo said the Philippines was aiming to bring down its budget deficit to 130-145 billion pesos this year from its initial estimate of 225 billion pesos. 

 Analysts said the government needs to consolidate its chronic deficit urgently, otherwise it would inflict more damage on the economy given that total public sector debt is approaching 80 percent of GDP. 

 The central bank said it would consider the inflation trend in deciding whether to lower its overnight rates following the U.S. rate cut. The overnight borrowing rate is currently at 9.5 percent and the lending rate at 11.75 percent. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar fell to six-week troughs of 32.996, tracking the yen lower. Dealers said U.S. investment houses bought the dollar following the TAIEX's poor showing. 

 Taiwan's central bank is expected to cut its interest rates, following the Fed's move on Tuesday. 

 In April, the central bank cut key interest rates by 0.125 percentage points, bringing the discount rate to 4.0 percent and the collateral rate to 4.375 percent.

title: WRAP: Singapore Dlr Up As MAS, Govt Talk Tough On Policy
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar rebounded Wednesday after the government reiterated that it won't tolerate excessive currency weakness arising from merger and acquisition-related outflows. 

 Breaking from tradition, the Monetary Authority of Singapore confirmed what many in the market already suspected - that it intervened last week to bolster the Singapore dollar after the currency fell to a new 11-year low of S$1.8268 to the U.S. dollar. 

 The MAS also warned of further interventions to offset any currency weakness arising from corporate demand for U.S. dollars to fund overseas acquisitions and it repeated its standing policy allowing "a gradual, modest appreciation of the trade-weighted Singapore dollar." 

 That policy is based on its "medium-term assessment of the economy, not short-term economic or inflation developments," the MAS noted. 

 Separately, Finance Minister Richard Hu told parliament that recent overseas acquisitions by Singapore Telecommunications Ltd. (P.SGT) and DBS Group Holdings Ltd. (P.DBS) won't be large enough to hurt the Singapore dollar. 

 "I don't think the amounts are sufficiently large enough to move the Sing dollar in a significant way," Hu said, adding that the MAS will continue to iron out short term volatility arising from the two deals. 

 Taken together, the comments prompted foreign exchange traders to cover short positions in the local currency. Recently, many analysts had speculated that the MAS might have quietly altered its position on the local dollar to one tacitly approving a modest depreciation in hopes that a weaker currency would offset the negative impact on exports of slowing economic growth overseas. 

 The timing of the remarks caught many traders off guard, as they came just before key April trade data Thursday and revised figures for first quarter gross domestic product Friday. Both sets of data are expected to provide further evidence of Singapore's economic slowdown. 

 While the statements are expected to ease pressure on the local currency in the near term, some analysts say that a sharp economic slowdown here might persuade the MAS to ease its monetary policy stance at its next review scheduled for July. 

 Meantime, the remarks appeared to signal that MAS wasn't happy with the recent pace of the local currency's decline. The Singapore dollar has been weakening all year, and the pace of depreciation picked up last week after the MAS said inflation isn't likely to rise in the near term. 

 Market participants had interpreted this comment as a hint that the MAS would abandon its moderately tight monetary policy stance, since inflation management is the sole declared objective of its monetary policy. 

 The dollar began the day trading around S$1.8165 and fell on the MAS acknowledgment of last week's interventions. Then, after the remarks from Hu, the local currency rose further, pushing the dollar down to S$1.8128 from S$1.8146 immediately before the comments. 

 Around 0800 GMT the Singapore dollar was quoted at S$1.8128 to one U.S. dollar compared with S$1.8186 late Tuesday. 

 The stronger local dollar caused interbank money market rates to ease slightly. Government bond prices rose marginally. 

 A growing number of Singapore corporations have been looking to make overseas acquisitions to diversify and expand their businesses. This puts downward pressure on the local currency, as these companies need to buy dollars or other foreign currencies to fund these deals. 

 In March, SingTel successfully bid for the purchase of Australia's Cable & Wireless Optus (A.CWO) in a deal valued up to A$17.3 billion. Last month, in a deal valued around S$10 billion, DBS won a bid to purchase Hong Kong's Dao Heng Bank (H.DHB).

title: Emerging  FX  - Waiting for the Fed.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 15 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were on the back-foot early Tuesday as the dollar rose on hopes an anticipated Fed rate cut would help boost the economy. 

 But trading was likely to be subdued due to caution ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting later in the day. The market is widely expecting the Fed to cut the federal funds rate by 50 basis points, which would bring it to four percent. 

 The yen ceded ground to the dollar amid these expectations, adding pressure to regional currencies, while the euro was around one-month lows. 

 Analysts predicted that if the Fed cuts rates, the dollar will continue to flex its muscles, although its future strength relies on how the U.S. economy is shaping up in the second half. 

 Treasury Secretary Paul O'Neill said earlier he was not worried about a recession, nor about currency values. 

 While the FOMC is the big economic event this week, there were also key regional and political developments in store. 

 Manila markets re-opened after Monday's key elections and Singapore will issue key economic data, including April non-oil exports data and the first-quarter economic survey. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won stumbled over a lower yen, although it was finding some support. 

 Reports that three U.S. funds were interested in buying the managerial rights and a stake in Hynix Semiconductor and a widely anticipated announcement from General Motors on its talks to take over parts of the bankrupt Daewoo Motor kept sentiment towards the won buoyed. 

 As with the rest of the region, the won was likely to see a quiet session ahead of the FOMC meeting. A rate cut in the U.S. was seen as beneficial to Korea as it would further hopes for a pick-up in growth in the U.S., Korea's largest export market. 

 However, the Bank of Korea is unlikely to follow the Fed's easing given inflationary pressures. The central bank held off on a rate cut earlier this month due to a rise in inflation. 

 THAI BAHT The baht edged down to 45.55 from 45.44 late on Monday. 

 Bangkok dealers said the mood was defensive on the weaker yen and Sing dollar which encouraged offshore dealers to sell the baht. They added government-linked companies and electronics exporters were moderately offering the U.S. dollar at 45.60. 

 Thailand's central bank said late on Monday it was not worried about pressure on the Thai baht despite speculation the Malaysian ringgit could be allowed to devalue in future. 

 Commerce Minister Adisai Bodharamik said his ministry would review its export target for 2001 taking into account a recent slowdown in the global economy. In March, the Commerce Ministry cut its forecast for exports in 2001 to 9.46 percent from 11.3 percent. 

 The market kept a wary eye on the Constitutional Court's hearing of a graft case against Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra later on Tuesday. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was basically steady edged up and was likely to gain some more ground as Monday's poll went through without a major hickup and raised hopes President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo's supporters will win enough seats to ensure smooth governance through her term. 

 Dealers said the market perception was that Arroyo's supporters will win eight of the 13 Senate seats and a decent majority in the 262 House of Representatives. 

 However, final election results will not be available for several days and that would infuse some uncertainty. 

 Allegations of fraud and rigging traditionally follow polls in the Philippines and litigation into such matters usually drag on for months. 

 Dealers said the trading range for the day should be within 50.00-50.50, but players will be on the watch for any bad news to quickly go dollar long. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar hovered around the 1.8200 mark as overnight losses of the yen and euro encouraged players go U.S. dollar long. 

 Dealers said fears of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore was likely to keep players cautious when treading beyond the 1.8200 mark and they will also be on the watch for any trading cues from the March retail sales data due Tuesday. 

 Demand for the U.S. dollar was expected to be strong at around 1.8170-1.8180 range, where local banks were selling U.S. dollars on Monday. 

 Most U.S. dollar offers are now expected to have lined up at 1.8225-1.8230. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was trapped in a narrow range, caught between equity-linked foreign inflows and importer dollar demand. 

 The currency opened unchanged at 32.882 before dipping to 32.890. Demand from foreign funds later lifted it to 32.887 at 0122 GMT. 

 Foreign investors have been net buyers of local stocks since April 30, buying a total T$34.982 billion worth of shares as of Monday. 

 The yen's retreat and the central bank dollar-buying intervention should cap the Taiwan dollar's upside at 32.82, dealers said.

title: Emerging  FX  - Take a breather ahead of big day.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 14 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were sticking to the safety of their recent ranges early Monday ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting. 

 Market players were likely to hold off on taking fresh positions before the FOMC meeting on Tuesday. A Reuters poll of U.S. primary dealers showed them almost unanimously expecting a 50 basis point cut from the Fed. 

 Positive data from the U.S. last Friday might brighten the session for regional currencies as Asia looks to the U.S. for any pick-up in growth. U.S. April retail sales rose 0.8 percent while the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index climbed to 92.6 in May. 

 However the euro's travails may dampen sentiment towards the Singapore dollar while the yen offered little guidance as it barely budged against the dollar. 

 This week is also an eventful one in the region. Manila markets were closed for Senate and local elections, which are viewed as a key test of President Gloria Arroyo's popularity. 

 Singapore will issue key economic data later this week, including April non-oil domestic exports on Thursday and the first quarter economic survey on Friday. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar kept a softer tone at 1.8170 against 1.8125 late on Friday. 

 Dealers said various names hesitantly bought U.S. dollars early, but the market was still on alert for possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 They added the MAS was most likely to come in once the Sing dollar breached 1.82, where moderate stop-loss U.S. dollar buying orders were said to be lined up. 

 Last week the MAS was believed to have sold at least US$500 million when the Sing dollar hit fresh 11-year lows near 1.8270. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was quoted slightly lower offshore with domestic markets closed for congressional and local elections. Trading will resume on Tuesday. 

 Arroyo hopes to bolster her administration by winning control of the Senate after she swept to power in January when former president Joseph Estrada was ousted by a "people power" revolt. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 Hopes for foreign direct investment lifted the won's spirits in early trade as positive news on the corporate front emerged. 

 Optimism that General Motors Corp. would soon announce a deal to buy some of the assets of the bankrupt Daewoo Motor boosted sentiment last week. 

 And a local newspaper reported that debt-ridden Hynix Semiconductor may sell managerial rights and a stake to three U.S. investment funds. 

 But local corporates were still showing an appetite for dollars on dips below 1,300. Trading was also cautious ahead of the FOMC meeting. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 Dollar bulls continued to dominate the rupiah market as negative political developments outweighed hopes the IMF might soon resume lending to Jakarta from its $5 billion loan programme. 

 President Abdurrahman Wahid on Friday defied opponents, refusing to either hand over more power to his popular deputy or answer a second parliament censure over two graft scandals. 

 Political leaders and some cabinet ministers have been pressing for power sharing between Wahid and Vice President Megawati Sukarnoputri to end the political gridlock. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said demand for the U.S. currency remained robust and they expected dollar buying at any retracement, with 12,000 seen as a near-term target. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was steady with foreign inflows and central bank support likely to keep it bound within a 32.88-32.92 range. 

 However, dealers in Singapore said the Nasdaq's lower finish on Friday, poor economic data last week, and a fire in an office complex in northern Taiwan's Eastern Science Park over the weekend would hurt sentiment. 

 The fire gutted several tech companies' offices including many subsidiaries of Acer Group which said the fire caused over $20 million in damage. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht edged down in line with other regionals but dealers in Singapore said the lack of fresh domestic leads would keep it trapped within a 45.40-45.60 band. 

 They said export-related inflows and unwinding of dollar longs by offshore players, following the Singapore dollar's rise last week, had supported the baht. 

 But sentiment was depressed by the poor economic outlook and shades of political uncertainty as a court hearing resumes on Tuesday against Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra, accused of not fully declaring his assets. 

 An upside break of 45.40 was likely to push the baht up to 45.20, beyond which demand for the dollar was believed to be strong, a dealer at a European bank in Singapore said.

title: Emerging  FX  - Directionless, Fed, US data eyed.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 11 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were a mixed bag late Friday as the market was driven by domestic leads while players kept a low profile ahead of April retail sales data at 1230 GMT and Tuesday's Federal Reserve rate-setting meeting. 

 The market has largely factored in another 50 basis point rate cut, but debate will continue over how much more the Fed will need to cut to stimulate U.S. economy. 

 The U.S. is a major market for exports from Asia and any move that to keep its economy growing is positive to Asian currencies. 

 Economists polled by Reuters forecast U.S. April retail sales rose 0.2 percent overall after a decline of 0.2 percent in March. 

 In the region, the Philippine peso hovered in a snug range, with activity muted ahead of congressional elections on Monday. 

 The Singapore dollar recouped some lost ground on talk of renewed intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, but gains were stunted by persistent demand for the U.S. dollar to fund overseas asset purchases by local companies. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso traded in a narrow 50.45-50.55 range for most of the day helped by easing fears of violence ahead of Monday's Senate polls and on an overall lack of dollar demand. 

 Total turnover was a mere $117.5 million, compared with Thursday's $137 million. 

 But dealers in Manila said the peso's upside was capped by interbank players and importers seeking dollars on dips. 

 With most players already long of dollars, a growing perception the polls would pass peacefully resulted in some unwinding of those positions. 

 Philippine financial markets will be closed on Monday for the election. Trade will resume on Tuesday. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar edged down in thin trading to 1.8140 from early highs of 1.8120. 

 Dealers said European banks and U.S. funds took profits on long U.S. dollar positions, but importers and corporates were looking to sell the Sing dollar at 1.8120. 

 They said the market was wary of further MAS intervention, given speculation they had sold at least $500 million in the last two sessions. The MAS said on Thursday it does not comment on its market operations. 

 Speculation is rife whether or not the MAS is going to shift its tightening monetary stance to neutral to weather a slowdown. The Sing dollar has fallen in recent sessions to levels analysts believe to be beyond the MAS' tightening policy band. 

 "I think the MAS was tactical if they did intervene because it has to introduce some sort of uncertainty in the market," a U.S. bank analyst said. 

 "If people are sure that its monetary stance is neutral, which in reality it is, no one would hold the Sing dollar because the interest rates are lower than the U.S. yet the currency is depreciating. It makes no economic sense." INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah eased but kept off its session low of 11,260 after state banks were spotted selling dollars near 11,200, the 38 percent retracement of the dollar's steep April 26-May 1 slide. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said initial dollar buying was sparked by news of a late Thursday bomb blast in a dormitory in the suburbs in which two people died. 

 However, fears of intervention and relatively subdued dollar demand from corporates tempered the rupiah selling spree. 

 The market largely ignored comments by the IMF's spokesman who said the government's proposed fiscal package which targets a budget deficit of 3.7 percent could form a good basis for restarting talks on stalled lending. 

 Dealers said the market had keenly tracked the twists and turns in Jakarta's relations with the IMF and would react only after a decision is taken on disbursement of a $400 million loan tranche suspended since December. 

 Meanwhile, central bank governor Sjahril Sabirin said the bank was not certain if domestic interest rates already around 21-month highs would be cut or raised. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was locked in a tight 45.40-45.53 range, wedged between exporter dollar offers and a lack of demand for the baht. 

 Some Bangkok dealers said dollar/baht looked set to break out of its recent consolidative phase and head higher. 

 Data released on Friday showed the external account remained weak. Although Thailand managed to eke out a trade surplus of $38 million in the first quarter, a finance ministry official said its trade balance in April would be in deficit. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won hovered around the 1,300 mark supported by export and equity related inflows. 

 But dealers in Hong Kong said interbank players worries over the yen, which retreated from its recent highs against the dollar, kept the won's upside capped. 

 Interest was subdued ahead of the U.S. retail sales data and the Fed's policy meeting. 

 They said talk General Motors was planning to make an announcement on its talks to buy part of the bankrupt Daewoo Motor also kept players cautious. 

 Local newspapers quoted Korean officials saying the deal was in the final stages. Dealers said a successful sale of Daewoo was likely to help the won in terms of both flows and sentiment. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar edged up to 32.87 from 32.91 earlier thanks to buying by U.S. banks. 

 Dealers said firmer stocks also lifted sentiment, with the benchmark TAIEX ending up more than two percent on buying by state-linked funds. 

 Analysts said the Taiwan dollar might get a boost if Taiwan's weighting in Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI)'s global indices was increased on May 19. 

 A local newspaper reported the planned adjustment to Taiwan's weighting would bring in an additional US$1.3 billion annually over the next five years.

title: Singapore MAS seen curbing Sing dlr drop - dealers.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 10 (Reuters) - Suspected intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) in recent days is cementing fears the central bank may have lost patience with recent exchange rate weakness, analysts said on Thursday. 

 Dealers said the Singapore dollar reached highs of around 1.8170 to the U.S. dollar after the central bank was spotted selling dollars around 1.8220/30. It was quoted at 1.8187/97 by 0815 GMT. 

 The MAS had no comment. "We do not normally comment on our market operations," said an MAS official. 

 Given estimates of aggressive overseas expansion by Singapore firms, worsening external economic conditions and rising political risks in the neighbourhood, drawing a rigid line in the sand may prove a bit difficult. 

 But some analysts believe an aggressive rejoinder to the Sing dollar's drop to 11-year lows around 1.8270 early this week was aimed at putting to rest speculation the MAS was shifting its monetary stance from a policy favouring a gradual appreciation. 

 Dealers believe the central bank was behind rather heavy U.S. dollar sales, led by local banks, late Wednesday that pushed the Sing dollar up to 1.8190 and was also active on Thursday. 

 Several smoothening operations mostly in London and New York trading time had been spotted since the Sing dollar breached the 1.82 level against the U.S. dollar in early April, they said. 

 A currency strategist at a major local bank said because of genuine dollar demand, the central bank had kept a low profile despite the Sing dollar drifting far from 1.8000-1.8050 - what he believed to be the weaker end of the MAS policy band. 

 "But they would certainly discourage the market from taking this as a shift in its stance," he said. 

 He said rising interbank offer rates in the money market also indicated the central bank was draining liquidity, in another effort to bolster the Sing dollar. 

 The on-and-off speculation on the MAS's stance of a "gently appreciating band" picked up after the MAS said last week inflation was not a near-term threat from the weakening currency. 

 "The Singapore dollar is being impacted by both flows and sentiment...so drawing too many rigid lines in the sand may not be appropriate," said David Simmonds, senior currency strategist at Salomon Smith Barney. 

 "But there must be a limit to it (decline) or otherwise it does require a close scrutiny of the monetary policy," he added.

title: Emerging  FX -Caught in yen's downdraft, Fed watched.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 10 (Reuters) - Asian currencies moved lower early Thursday after the yen slipped to one-week lows against the dollar on stock losses and waning optimism about Japan's new government. 

 Fresh economic data from Japan indicated that an economic recovery might still be elusive. Lending by Japanese banks fell 3.4 percent on year in April, the 40th consecutive month of decline. The wholesale price index also fell 0.1 percent on year in April. 

 Market players were likely to keep a low profile ahead of the May 15 Federal Open Market Committee meeting. Most analysts expected the Fed to cut key rates by another 50 basis points. 

 Local factors were also weighing on regional currencies. Uncertainty in the run-up to the Philippines' Senate elections on Monday kept the dollar well-bid agains the peso. 

 The Singapore dollar continued to be dampened by talk of merger and acquisitions, though rumours that the Monetary Authority of Singapore intervened on Wednesday should cap its downside. 

 Meanwhile, the Asian Development Bank warned that Asia would face slower growth over the next two years, but said fears of a new regional crisis were overstated. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar eased past 1.8200 after hitting a high of 1.8190 late Wednesday for the second session in a row, on talk of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 Dealers said heavy selling of dollar by local banks around 1.8250-60, with U.S. funds joining in later, sparked speculation of intervention late Wednesday. 

 Local corporates and some foreign banks were still chasing the dollar around 1.8220, and dealers said dollar demand was stronger near 1.8200. 

 But they added wariness over intervention would cap the Sing's downside, keeping it within the 1.8210-1.8260 range. 

 However, players who believe local companies need to buy more dollars to hedge their recent investments abroad would attempt to breach 1.8267 touched Wednesday. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won shadowed the yen's movements, but exporters' dollar sales and foreign investors' equity-linked inflows were expected to cap its downside. 

 However, the won has been unable to break resistance of around 1,293, a level last seen on March 21 when it fell past 1,300. Dealers said there was genuine dollar demand from local importers waiting to buy dollar on dips towards 1,295. 

 Analysts said in the absence of any big moves in the dollar/yen, the won was relegated to stay within narrow ranges. 

 Indeed, charts showed volatility in the won has fallen by over 40 percent since May 2 as the price action has narrowed increasingly in recent session. However, analysts also noted the won has been stronger than its 14-day moving average. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht ticked down from 45.59 late Wednesday, tracking the softer yen. 

 Bangkok dealers said trading was lacklustre as offshore dealers were on the sidelines. 

 They added the baht was supported around 45.65 by buying interest from food and garment exporters, while foreign banks were keen to sell around 45.48-50. 

 The market showed little reaction to Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra's comments that Thailand's economy is expected to grow 3.5-5.0 percent in the near term. 

 The Bank of Thailand has forecast GDP growth of 3-4.5 percent in 2001, against 4.3 percent in 2000. But the bank said in late April the economy would expand by 2.5-4.0 percent this year. 

 Thailand's Constitutional Court will reach a verdict by August on whether Thaksin is guilty of deliberately concealing some of his wealth. If found guilty, Thaksin will be banned from political office for five years. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah continued to loiter around the 11,000 mark, enjoying the relative calm in Indoneisa's usually stormy political scene. 

 However, the lack of dollar inflows and sinking sentiment over the country's economic and political woes prevented the currency from making any substantial gains. 

 Indeed, Bank Indonesia said late Wednesday economic growth in the second quarter was expected to come in at 3.8 percent, slower than the first quarter. Indonesia's economy has been badly hobbled by the weak rupiah as shaky politics have blocked economic reforms, stalled the IMF's $5 billion latest lending programme, and discouraged foreign investment. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was pressured by worries ahead of the May 14 Senate polls, and dealers expected it to hit lower levels given the lack of dollar supply. 

 They said some exporters' dollar offers were expected around 50.80, but sentiment was bullish on dollar given the uncertainty over the outcome of the polls, which are seen as a test of President Gloria Arroyo's popularity. 

 The central bank said late Wednesday gross international reserves as of end-April slipped to $14.5 billion from $14.7 billion the previous month due to payments by the government of maturing external debt. 

 The bank's monetary board will hold its weekly meeting later in the day, but most analysts expected it to keep rates steady ahead of the Fed's May 15 meeting. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar nestled in its recent range, with trading expected to remain listless. 

 Dealers in Taipei noted late Wednesday some outflows from foreign funds, which could pressure the local dollar lower if they pick up steam. 

 However, players have continued unwinding their long dollar positions around 32.90, a level that the market believes the central bank is defending. 

 Charts showed volatility in the Taiwan dollar has remained below one since April 19.
