title: Emerging  FX  - Firmer, bracing for US data, Fed.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 10 (Reuters) - Asian currencies recouped some ground in late Thursday trade on the back of a steadier yen, with some players trimming long dollar positions ahead of key U.S. data and the Federal Reserve's meeting next week. 

 The market was awaiting the release of weekly U.S. jobless claims data at 1230 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters estimated on average the number of new jobless claims totalled 417,000 last week against 421,000 a week earlier. 

 "The market has been quite long of dollars. Players seem reluctant to build fresh positions ahead of the data and the Fed's meeting. Asian currencies should move within a narrow range in the runup to May 15," said a senior dealer at an Asian bank. 

 News Asia was moving closer to concluding currency safety net deals backed by Japan which would guard against a repeat of 1997/98 regional crisis also provided some psychological support for the currencies, the dealer said. 

 Japan announced it had struck a $3 billion swap deal with Thailand, a $2 billion agreement with Thailand and a $1 billion facility with Malaysia. 

 The Singapore dollar gained amid rumours the Monetary Authority of Singapore was in the market to intervene again after a similar move on Wednesday. 

 The Indonesian rupiah was out of sync with its regional peers, losing nearly 1.50 percent on the day, as renewed political tension triggered corporate buying of dollars. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar bounced back more than half a cent to 1.8175 in a tense session from lows of 1.8241 on suspected central bank intervention, dealers said. 

 Dollar sales by a U.S. bank at around S$1.8220/30 in thin lunchtime trading spurred talk the Monetary Authority of Singapore was in the market after Wednesday's suspected intervention to pull it back from a low of around 1.8267. 

 The MAS declined to comment on the talk. "We do not normally comment on our market operations," an MAS official told Reuters. 

 The Sing dollar has been pressured mainly by prospects of further M&A-related capital outflows, falling to fresh 11-year lows around 1.8270 earlier this week. 

 Speculation is rife whether or not the MAS is going to shift its tightening monetary stance at a policy review in July. 

 Some say the MAS would shift its policy to neutral, guiding the Sing dollar lower to buoy the export-oriented economy. Others argue the Sing dollar on a trade-weighted basis was already slipping into a neutral policy band, removing the need for them to further ease their stance. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The Indonesian rupiah eased to one-week lows amid hightened political tensions and after a meeting of key politicians due on Friday was postponed. 

 However the downside was capped at around 11,250-11,270 where Jakarta dealers said state banks were seen selling dollars. 

 Dealers said the shaky political situation after the second censure of President Abdurrahman Wahid by parliament and poor economic outlook would continue to weigh down the rupiah. 

 They said the delay of the meeting, expected to come up with a power sharing formula to ease tension, disappointed the market. 

 Local newspapers also quoted army chief General Endriartono Sutarto warning Wahid not to sack parliament. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht barely moved in listless sideways trading, stuck in a tight range over the course of the day. 

 Bangkok dealers said petrochemical importers were looking to sell the baht at around 45.50, but buying by exporters was underpinning it near 45.60. 

 The Thai central bank said it was not worried about inflation in 2001 and would keep its forecast range of 0-3.5 percent for inflation this year despite fluctuating oil prices. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso ended slightly higher from Wednesday's 50.65 close helped by some export-related inflows and a lack of overall dollar demand. 

 Dealers said the peso gapped down at the open on expected central bank dollar buying, which they believed had pulled the peso down late Wednesday. 

 It touched a high of 50.47 where importers and players wary over Monday's Senate polls were seen bidding for dollars. 

 The polls widely viewed as a referendum on President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo's polularity, were also seen as key to the Philippines' credit rating outlook. 

 The head of Standard and Poor's sovereign ratings John Chambers said if the president did not get a strong mandate, governability would be an issue for her for the rest of her term. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won bowed slightly due to a softer yen, but stayed in a tight 1,304.5-1,308 range as the yen's movements were minimal. 

 Since the beginning of the week, the won has been trapped in increasingly narrow price action. Dealers said while local importers have been seeking dollars on dips, exporter dollar sales have capped the won's losses. 

 Foreign investors' stock purchases have also provided underlying support for the won. Foreign investors bought a net 80.97 billion won worth of shares on Wednesday. 

 But the yen was still the dominant influence, and analysts say without major movements in dollar/yen and few fresh local factors, the won was likely to stick to narrow ranges. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar drooped with the softer yen, but stayed well within its recent range of 32.86-32.90. 

 With the central bank recently intervening on both sides, dealers said interest in the market was dwindling, and the Taiwan dollar would likely be trapped in its recent range for some time. 

 Analysts say Taiwan's slowing economy also signalled it was unlikely for the curreny to strengthen and some expect the central bank to let it weaken. 

 "The continued slowing both in monetary growth as well as bank lending also point to tighter domestic liquidity ahead," said Standard Chartered Bank in a research note. 

 "The sluggishness in the economy's near term outlook will hence keep the TWD rangebound for now with TWD gains capped at 32.80 in coming weeks."

title: Asia Markets - Mixed, poor U.S. data weighs.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 9 (Reuters) - Most Asian equities were mixed 

 on Wednesday in cautious trading after lower U.S. productivity 

 data and a jump in labour costs raised concerns about inflation 

 and a slowing economy. 

     Productivity in the first quarter in the United States fell 

 for the first time in six years, but unit labour costs posted a 

 bigger-than-expected gain, the largest since the last quarter 

 of 1997. 


    In Tokyo, the benchmark Nikkei average	   fell for the



second straight session as investors sought more details on



Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi's much-hyped reforms.



    "It's time now to see a follow-through (on reforms)," an



equity analyst in Tokyo said.



    The Lower House was due to hold a question-and-answer



session later in the day on Koizumi's debut policy speech made



on Monday. The opposition camp was expected to attack him for



being short on concrete details.



"He's got to show results within 100 days. But we know



nothing happens overnight in Japan, except for earthquakes,"



the analyst said.



Japan is due to hold an election for the Upper House by



late July. Speculation is rife the ruling Liberal Democratic



Party might call for an early election for the more powerful



Lower House to use Koizumi's sky-high popularity.



The Nikkei's dip weighed on the yen , which slipped



to 121.84 at one point but worries about an evident U.S.



economic slowdown underpinned it.



M&A VS MAS



The Singapore dollar kept a softer tone at around 1.8240



against the U.S. dollar, suffering from prospects of further



merger and acquisition-related capital outflows.



The latest discomfort came from media reports that United



Overseas Bank had offered to buy Hong Kong's HKCB



Bank for US$692 million. HKCB denied the talk but



dealers said it was enough to sour the Sing dollar's prospects.



Analysts said the weakening Sing dollar and a lack of



aggressive intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore


suggested it would shift its monetary policy to neutral from



tightening at its mid-year review in July.



But some said the current monetary stance already suggested



a neutral policy setting given the Sing dollar's exchange rate



against a trade-weighted basket of currencies, which includes



the yen and euro.



"Singapore doesn't need to be tightening monetary policy at



this stage and in my view will not do so," David Simmonds,



senior currency strategist at Salomon Smith Barney, told



Reuters Television.



He said on a trade-weighted basis, the Singapore dollar was



pushing through what he perceived as the MAS' "neutral"



parameters.



Simmonds said he expected the MAS to reiterate over the



next week or two that it was not returning to a loose monetary



policy.



"During this period of intense M&A related-noise in any



case it's wise not to be drawing too many rigid lines in the



sand."



PHILIPPINES EYES RATE CUT



In the Philippines, hopes for a rate cut boosted the debt



market, especially on the short end .



The Philippine central bank holds its weekly monetary



policy meeting on Thursday. The bank has said it was more



biased to cut rates to buoy the economy, rather than cutting to



defend the fragile peso .



    The key overnight borrowing rate is now at 9.5 percent and



lending rate at 11.75 percent.



    Analysts said lower rates would help the Philippines to



service its mountain of foreign debt totalling $52.06 billion



at the end of 2000.



    But they added the market kept a wary eye on Senate



elections next Monday, which weighed on overall sentiment.

title: Emerging  FX  - Steady on yen, lack of domestic cues.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 9 (Reuters) - Asian currencies held within their recent ranges late on Wednesday, helped by a lack of fresh domestic leads and a steady yen. 

 Even the more volatile rupiah and peso traded within a narrow band as markets waited for a May 11 meeting of top Indonesian politicians and the May 14 Senate polls in the Philippines. 

 Analysts said the yen's retracement from around 124 levels in late April was supporting most regionals on the downside but their upside was capped by persistent signs of weakening growth in the U.S. - Asia's largest export market. 

 The latest data indicating a further slowing included a drop in productivity and a rise in labour costs. 

 For more clues on the U.S. economy, markets will focus on Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greespan's speech at a banking conference on Thursday and on Friday's April retail sales report. 

 The events will set the tone ahead of the Fed's May 15 policy meeting where it is widely expected to cut another 50 basis points off its 4.5 percent funds rate. 

 The yen was under pressure in early European trade, helped by a fall on the Nikkei and as the euphoria over new Japanese Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi faded. 

 The euro traded in a tight range near its three-week lows against the dollar. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar was sandwiched between fears of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore and talk of M&A outflows, which prevented a significant rebound from its 11-year lows. 

 Dealers said most of the day's trade was within a 1.830-1.860 range with U.S. names and local banks buying dollars on dips. 

 Analysts said last week's comments by the MAS and poor economic data had encouraged players to probe weaker levels. 

 They said the risk of the Malaysian ringgit being repegged lower was another factor weighing on the Sing dollar. 

 The ringgit is believed to form a sizeable component in the trade-weighted basket the MAS uses to manage the exchange rate. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht edged higher against the dollar, thanks to exporter dollar sales and foreign inflows to Thai assets, dealers in Singapore and Bangkok said. 

 The currency drifted in a snug 45.52-45.62 range, in the absence of strong domestic leads. But it was expected to be top-heavy in the near term due to poor fundamentals. 

 A finance ministry official said on Wednesday Thailand switched to a monthly trade deficit in April after surpluses in the previous two months. 

 Based on about 85 percent of trade information for April, the deficit stood at US$56 million. Consumer confidence also fell in April from the previous month, according to a university survey. 

 In the forward market, dealers said there was good demand for dollar/baht outrights in three-and six-month tenors. The three-month rate was quoted at 45/60 satang per dollar, and the six-month rate at 80/110. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 Falling local shares and worries over the U.S. economy nudged the won slightly lower as it spent most of the session glumly following the yen. 

 With dollar/yen stalling, the won has been mired in a narrow range of 1,295-1,305 since the beginning of the week. 

 Dealers said unless the yen made any significant moves, the won was likely to continue trading in a narrow range, trapped between local importers' dollar bids and foreign investors' equity-related inflows. 

 On the non-deliverable forward market, the one-month won was at 1,302/3 against 1,301.8/2.8 late Tuesday and the three-month was at 1,306/7 from 1,306/7. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah loitered just under the 11,000 level, plagued by the usual suspects of a lack of dollar inflows and Jakarta's volatile politics. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said while local corporate dollar demand still lurked, players were unwilling to take fresh long dollar positions as a resolution to the current political crisis may be reached soon. 

 Major political parties are due to meet on Friday, fueling talk a compromise may be reached to determine the future of President Abdurrahman Wahid, who could possibly face impeachment. Bank Indonesia warned late Wednesday that economic growth was likely to be slower in the second quarter while inflation was set to rise. The country's economic problems have been compounded by the weak rupiah and persistent political instability. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso closed lower at 50.65 against the open of 55.44 as gains inspired by overseas workers' remittances were countered by dollar bargain hunting as the market remained nervous ahead of the congressional election on Monday. 

 The market was factoring in potential rate cuts after central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said last week that it was biased towards cutting key interest rates. 

 The central bank has cut its benchmark interest rates by 550 basis points since mid-December, more than reversing a 400 basis point hike in October which was aimed at shoring up the peso. 

 But analysts said those aggressive cuts might not be enough to boost the economy, and it was important for the government to quickly shift from rhetoric into action. 

 "Clearly, low domestic interest rates alone may not be enough to spur growth. However, the ball is no longer in the hands of monetary authorities," Jojo Gonzales, head of strategy and economics at Merrill Lynch, said in a report. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar closed a touch lower on Wednesday after gaining on the back of foreign fund inflows in the past seven sessions. 

 Dealers said dollar buying in NDF markets weighed on the local currency, but profit taking at 32.90, the top end of its recent range, helped limit the downside. 

 UBS Warburg said poor export data released on Tuesday kept offshore interest in dollar/Taiwan dollar forwards and it expected the spot rate to trade above 32.90 in the next few days.

title: Asian  Currencies  Mostly Dn;Singapore Dlr At Mercy Of M&As
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- Most Asian currencies drifted slightly lower late Wednesday, but remained hemmed in within narrow ranges, as they mirrored the yen's movements, dealers said. 

 Resisting the yen's pressure, however, the Singapore dollar and the Thai baht were stronger. 

 The Singapore dollar took centerstage on renewed concerns that Singapore Telecommunication Ltd.'s A$17 billion bid for Australia's Cable & Wireless Optus (A.CWO) might be scuttled. 

 A report by the Melbourne Age newspaper that the Australian government will block SingTel's planned takeover of C&W Optus, unless the U.S. grants export licenses for military satellite technology, resurrected such fears. 

 The deal, which has contributed to the U.S. dollar's recent strength against the Singapore currency, led to a sharp pullback in the U.S. dollar to around S$1.8200 in early Asian trade. 

 Given the magnitude of the deal - it would be the largest overseas acquisition by a Singapore company - the local dollar has been sensitive to any news of its progress. 

 "The market keeps vacillating about the SingTel-Optus deal," said Mansoor Mohi-uddin, a regional currency strategist at UBS Warburg. 

 As the concerns ebbed, the U.S. dollar quickly regained its footing. Interbank participants scooped for bargains, even before SingTel stepped in to say it was confident the deal will go through, following talks with Australian and U.S. government officials on its acquisition of C&W Optus. 

 "The pullback triggered an opportunity to buy cheap dollars," said a dealer at a U.S. bank. 

 A large local bank, which has been snapping up U.S. dollars in recent sessions, unloaded the currency in late trade, pushing it down to S$1.8216 at 0910 GMT Wednesday. 

 Late Tuesday, the U.S. dollar was higher at S$1.8238. 

 Fears of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore - which dealers believed had intervened to smooth the local dollar's decline last Friday and earlier this week - also kept participants wary of pushing the Singapore dollar down too aggressively. 

 "There's a hint of repetition about today's (Wednesday's) Singapore dollar story," Bank of America said in a research note. "The world and his dog wants to buy dollar-Sing, but there is a whiff of the authorities at S$1.8250 and above." 

 A marginal rise in Malaysia's international reserves as of April 30, and reassurance by a senior government official that the government has no plans to review the ringgit peg for now assuaged fears of an imminent devaluation of the currency. This also contributed to the Singapore dollar's sharp rebound in early trading, market watchers said.

title: Singapore  Dlr Dn Late,But Off Low;  Intervention  Suspected
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was slightly lower late Tuesday on continued corporate demand for U.S. dollars, but came off its early low amid suspected intervention on behalf of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, dealers said. 

 Around 0819 GMT, the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.8244, up from S$1.8234 late Friday in Asia, but was lower than its intraday high at S$1.8265. 

 Singapore markets were closed Monday for a public holiday, but in offshore dealings, U.S. dollar hit a new 11-year high of S$1.8268 against the Singapore currency in thin, illiquid trading. 

 The U.S. dollar opened around S$1.8160 in Asia Tuesday and rose quickly to S$1.8265 in early trades before retreating on suspected intervention through a large local bank, dealers said. 

 For the remainder of the day, the U.S. dollar traded between S$1.8236 and S$1.8250, with its upside capped by intervention fears and a slightly stronger Thai baht.

title: Emerging  FX  - Steady yen helps, U.S. data awaited.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 4 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were steadier early Friday as a buoyant yen sparked hopes that countries in the region might not need to keep their currencies weak to stay competitive in export markets. 

 But yen-inspired gains were expected to be counteracted by U.S. jobless claims released overnight that showed record corporate layoffs, raising fears the worst might not be over. 

 The market is now focused on the April U.S. employment report due at 1230 GMT, which will give a clearer picture of the labour market. 

 Employment is closely linked to consumer confidence - the linchpin in the U.S. economy, which is the biggest market for exports from Asia. 

 Economic data in the region was also not encouraging. Singapore's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) for April showed a reading of 46.2 percent, compared with 47.4 percent in March. But position squaring ahead of a long weekend holiday in several centres should help underpin the regional currencies as the market is generally long on dollar. 

 Markets in India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand will be closed on Monday to celebrate Buddha's birthday. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won broke 1,293 resistance, though importers' dollar bids brought it off the high so far of 1,287. 

 Analysts said a clean break of 1,293, last seen on March 21, paves the way towards 1,284, which is the 62 percent Fibonacci retracement of the dollar's rise from February 21 to April 4. 

 However, the market has so far hesitated from really testing key resistance given the yen's modest gains and thin trade. 

 Analysts have also said the won's rise might be short-lived given Korea's slowing economy. Finance Minister Jin Nyum said earlier the economy was expected to grow by 5 percent in 2001, adding "artificial" measures were needed to achieve that. 

 The OECD said on Thursday it forecast 4.2 percent growth for the Korean economy in 2001, with a U.S.-led rebound possible if vital corporate reforms continue to be pursued. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar bobbed around 1.8200 after hitting a 1.8218 low overnight on what was believed to be M&A-related flows. 

 Dealers said fears of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore would cap the Sing's downside but more signs of a weaker economy were likely to dampen sentiment. 

 Singapore's Purchasing Managers' Index for April stood at 46.2 percent, from 47.4 percent in March. However, the electronics sector gained a marginal 0.6 point, which indicated a possible bottoming out. 

 The PMI followed government surveys of outlooks in the manufacturing, commerce and services for April-September that showed deteriorating sentiment towards business conditions. 

 Dealers said some local and foreign banks were still looking to buy dollars, possibly bringing about a test 1.8220, which the market belives would be defended by the MAS. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was struggling to stay above 11,000, with persistent local corporate dollar demand amid Indonesia's slippery political scene. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said the market continued to prefer holding dollars given the political uncertainty shrouding the country. Parliament recently handed President Abdurrahman Wahid a second censure, and if his reply is not viewed as satisfactory, impeachment proceedings could be started. 

 Analysts said Jakarta's thorny politics was holding up key reforms, including budget revisions needed in order to receive a long-delayed $400 million loan from the IMF. 

 The government said late Thursday it had agreed to recommendations by an independent panel on changing central bank law, which had been a sticking point with the Fund. It did not give further detail. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was treading water, with demand for it tapering off after one big bank in Singapore was spotted buying a large amount of the currency on Thursday. 

 Equity-linked inflows also supported the currency, with foreign investors turning net buyers of local stocks since April 27, according to data from the Stock Exchange of Thailand. 

 But the market was unlikely to push the baht aggressively in either direction ahead of a long weekend holiday. Thai financial markets will be closed on Monday and Tuesday. 

 The one-month forward rate was steady at 6/10 satang per dollar in the offshore market and -9.5/-9.0 satang in the onshore market. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was likely to feel some pressure as Moody's Investors Service said it was concerned about the Philippines negative rating outlook after the state of rebellion imposed by the government to crush opposition protests. 

 Moody's said on Thursday it had maintained the Philippine's Ba1 foreign currency rating as it believes the country is amply cushioned against external economic shocks over the near term. 

 But it added that unresolved political uncertainties will adversely affect the country's longer-term economic prospects. 

 Dealers in Singapore said with the market slightly short of dollars after the peso's gains in the past few sessions, a volatile session could be expected. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar opened higher at 32.868 against the Thursday's close of 32.890 on the back of follow-through buying linked to investment in local stocks. 

 Dealers said the upside could be limited by the central bank, which has been in the market lately to slow the currency's gains. Some believe the authority is likely to keep it at 32.82-32.85 in the near term. 

 The market awaited April consumer price data due on Monday. March CPI rose 0.44 percent on-year. The central bank is also scheduled to release end-April foreign exchange reserves figures on Monday.

title: Singapore Dlr Dn Late; Revisits 11-Yr Low
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar fell further late Friday, revisiting its recent 11-year low of S$1.8245 against the U.S dollar on strong U.S. dollar buying led by local banks on behalf of companies. 

 Dealers said a central bank statement that Singapore's inflation rate was unlikely to rise in the near term, despite the weak Singapore dollar, helped precipitate the local currency's decline. 

 However, the U.S. dollar retreated from its 11-year high amid intervention fears and was quoted at S$1.8234 at 0838 GMT (4:38 a.m. EDT), up from S$1.8201 late Thursday in Asia. 

 Reversing their earlier buying spree, local banks subsequently sold U.S. dollars in late Asian trading, suggesting that the selloff was likely at the central bank's behest, dealers said. 

 The last suspected intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore occurred last week when the U.S. dollar first hit its 11-year high. 

 At 0925 GMT (5:25 a.m. EDT), the U.S. dollar was quoted at S$1.8202, little changed from late Thursday. 

 The U.S. dollar opened lower in Asia on selling by European banks in the wake of a stronger yen. But its early decline was short-lived, as a large local bank, which has been an aggressive buyer this week, resumed buying U.S. dollars on behalf of companies and for merger and acquisition-related outflows. 

 The U.S. dollar's early rise was punctuated by sales from U.S. and European banks executing sell orders on behalf of clients. 

 A second wave of U.S. dollar buying emerged following a statement by the Monetary Authority of Singapore that inflation was unlikely to rise further near-term and that domestic price stability isn't threatened by a weaker local currency. 

 Market participants interpreted the statement as a hint that the MAS may ease its moderately tight monetary policy stance at its next scheduled review in July, a senior dealer at a European bank in Singapore said. 

 Inflation, as measured by the Consumer Price Index, rose 1.8% from a year ago in March and was up 0.2% from February. The March inflation rate was at the high end of the MAS' 1% to 2% tolerance band. 

 With local banks leading the buying, market participants were emboldened to bid the U.S. dollar higher to its recent 11-year high, inviting the suspected intervention. 

 The MAS usually doesn't comment on its market actions. 

 Long Bonds End Higher 

 Prices of longer-dated government bonds ended higher, tracking overnight gains in U.S. Treasurys on expected poor U.S. unemployment data later Friday, and on a further contraction in Singapore's Purchasing Managers' Index for April, dealers said. 

 The April PMI fell 1.2 percentage points to 46.2%, indicating that manufacturing activity in Singapore contracted for the third consecutive month. 

 The yield on the two-year bond was flat at 2.29%, while the five-year bond ended one basis point lower at 2.99%. 

 On the longer end of the curve, the yield on the seven- and 10-year papers fell by two basis points each, to 3.38% and 3.57%, respectively.

title: Emerging  FX -Firm as dlr consolidates, US data eyed.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 3 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies were firmer in late trade on Thursday as market participants trimmed dollar longs in the face of a firm yen and pending U.S. job data. 

 Japan's Golden Week holidays thinned trading volumes in major currencies. Markets in much of Southeast and South Asia will be closed for a public holiday on Monday and dealers said players were squaring positions, fearing they might be caught on the wrong side when trading resumes on Tuesday. 

 Analysts expected regional currencies to stay in tight ranges ahead of the U.S. government's weekly jobless claims data at 1230 GMT and the April unemployment report on Friday. 

 The U.S. is a key market for Asia's exports and any news that points to its ability to absorb goods from the region is supportive to the currencies. 

 "Although consumer spending has been quite resilient so far this year, recent jobless claims have risen rather sharply," said Syetarn Hansakul, economist at WestLB in Singapore. 

 "This raised fears of an employment-led downturn. Any sharp rise in unemployment in April would dampen consumer confidence and that could adversely affect Asian currencies," she said. 

 The Singapore dollar bucked the trend on Thursday, slipping under the weight of dollar demand linked to M&A activities as local companies seek to expand by buying into overseas firms. 

 The Philippine peso made good gains after street protests to support jailed former president Joseph Estrada were brought rapidly under control earlier this week. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar slipped to session lows of 1.8213 having spent most of the day orbiting a tight 1.8160-1.8194 range. Dealers said local banks and U.S. names sold the Sing dollar against the U.S. dollar and the Australian dollar, fanning talk they were still executing orders for a deal by Singapore Telecommunications to buy Australia's Optus . 

 The Aussie/Sing dollar cross , which has been in a steep uptrend channel since April 24, reached three-month highs of 0.9498 on Thursday. 

 Dealers expected firm support for the Sing dollar around 1.8200 to the U.S. dollar on fears of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 But analysts said the Sing dollar might face fresh downward pressure if Singapore's Purchasing Managers' Index for April, due on Friday, reinforced concerns about a slowing economy. 

 In March the PMI index shrank to 47.4, contracting for the second straight month for the first time since January 1999. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso extended its gains, reaching a high of 50.10, up nearly three percent from 15-week lows of 51.60 early Wednesday. 

 Manila dealers said power companies and oil firms were looking to buy the U.S. dollar around 50.20, but the broader market was keen to book profit on long dollar positions. 

 Analysts said the market was keeping a wary eye on the political situation, especially Senate elections on May 14, when President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo needs to capture enough seats to ensure a solid majority. 

 The central bank kept key overnight rates unchanged, a move widely expected by the markets. The overnight borrowing rate is currently at 9.50 percent and lending at 11.75 percent. 

 Philippine merchandise exports fell for the second consecutive month in March, pointing to slower growth in the economy in the first quarter compared to the end of last year. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won climbed past 1,300 thanks to the firmer yen, but importers' persistent dollar bids stopped it from testing the key resistance level of 1,293. 

 With the yen only making modest gains, dealers said the market was reluctant to test 1,293, last touched on March 21 when the dollar broke through 1,300. 

 They added if the yen rallied above 121.30, then the market might find the resolve to test 1,293. 

 Settlement of stock purchases by foreign funds gave the won a boost. Foreign investors have bought an impressive net 463.6 billion won worth of local stock in the past three sessions. 

 But analysts said for now, the won's rise remained precarious given slowing external demand for Korea's exports. Recent data showed exports fell by 9.3 percent on year in April. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht inched up further on continued trimming of dollar longs by players caught short in the offshore market, Singapore dealers said. 

 Singapore and Hong Kong names led the dollar sales but local corporate dollar demand limited the baht's upside. 

 "The baht is tracking the yen much closer as there is a lack of fresh local leads and that is making a lot of foreign players a bit uncomfortable with their dollar longs," a dealer at a European bank in Singapore said. 

 He said players were also squaring off before a long weekend. Thai financial markets will be closed on Monday and Tuesday for the birthday of Buddha and for Coronation Day. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah fluctuated within the 11,000-11,300 band with some export-related inflows causing trimming of dollar longs early and local corporate dollar demand capping the upside. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said speculation embattled president Abdurrahman Wahid was losing support also kept players cautious. 

 They said the market was keenly watching the political situation after parliament handed Wahid a second censure for his alleged involvement in graft scandals. 

 Local media reported Wahid's ministers told him to hold his tongue and share power with other political parties through a cabinet revamp if he wanted to survive in office. 

 Wahid has a month to reply to the parliamentary rebuke and if his reply is not found satisfactory, impeachment proceedings could be initiated. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar trod familiar ground, spending the session in the week's range so far of 32.858-928. 

 Hopes for foreign equity inflows and a firmer yen helped it rack up some gains earlier in the day, but it soon surrendered these amid wariness over central bank intervention. 

 Taiwan's central bank has been recently spotted in the market buying dollars to cap its currency's rise, in what analysts see as an effort to keep exports competitive given slowing demand from the U.S.

SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Singapore dollar was slightly stronger against the U.S. dollar late Friday in choppy trade, a day after it touched a new 11-year low against the U.S. unit. 

 Trading was volatile as some players sold their long U.S. dollar positions ahead of a meeting of the Group of Seven leading industrialized nations' finance minister and central bankers. 

 Around 0800 GMT (4.00 a.m. Friday EDT), the U.S. dollar was trading at S$1.8180, down from S$1.8243 late Thursday in Asia. 

 The pair opened at around S$1.8190 on buying by a large local bank, but fell to the intraday low of S$1.8185 as some foreign investors cleared long positions ahead of the weekend. 

 But the pair rose above S$1.8200 in late trading as the yen began to lose ground against the U.S. dollar, traders said. 

 Fears that the Monetary Authority of Singapore would intervene again to support the Singapore dollar also capped the U.S. dollar's gains. 

 The central bank apparently intervened late Thursday after the pair peaked at the new 11-year high. Earlier this month, the MAS had reiterated that it would intervene to smooth out volatility in the currency market. 

Singapore government bond prices rose Friday as investors parked their funds in the safer instrument, ahead of the G7 meeting of finance ministers and central bankers this weekend and amid rising political uncertainty in Indonesia. Yields move in the opposite direction to prices. 

 The yield on the two-year paper fell two basis points to 2.30%, and the yield on the five-year paper also fell two basis points, to 3.03%.

text:
0215 GMT - The Philippine peso was well submerged under the 51 per dollar level as the market fretted over a huge rally by supporters of former president Joseph Estrada. 

 - Estrada arrested on Wednesday on economic plunder charges - punishable by death - and thousands now gathered near where he is being held.

 - Local corporate dollar demand expected at 12,100 amid ongoing political upheaval.

title: Emerging  FX  - Easier in holiday-thinned trade.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 16 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were easier late on Monday, but activity was confined to familiar range as holidays in several centres kept interest thin and volumes low. 

 Most Asian markets reopened after a three-day break but Hong Kong, Sydney and much of Europe were still closed for the Easter break. Thai markets were also still shut for Songkran. 

 Analysts expected volumes to pick up from Tuesday, but the overall trend remained unchanged. 

 "Until the market is convinced that risk of the yen falling to much weaker levels is over, most players in the region will prefer to stay long of dollars," a chief dealer of a European bank in Singapore said. 

 Japan competes with key Asian countries in export markets and also absorbs a chunk of the region's exports. 

 Analysts said the release of poor economic data in line with the expected slowing of exports and growth across the region was also likely to keep sentiment depressed. 

 Singapore is due to release March non-oil domestic exports data on Tuesday after lowering its growth forecast for the year last week. Most analysts expect exports to contract after a 5.4 percent rise in February. 

 The Bank of Japan's downgrade of its view of the economy in its April report had little impact on the yen as the view had been widely expected. 

 Both the yen and euro were also rangebound in a holiday-thinned market with the dollar getting some marginal support from tension in the Middle East after Israel's air raid on Syrian positions in Lebanon earlier in the day. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah led regional loosers on Monday as dollar sales by state banks were badly upstaged by strong corporate demand. 

 Jakarta dealers said state banks sold around $10-15 million but that was not enough to halt the rupiah's slide. 

 One oil company was heard placing a big dollar buying order while foreign banks were also active in bidding for the dollar, they said. 

 Optimism over a potentially positive outcome from the IMF visit was overshadowed by news of the World Bank scrapping a $300 million loan to the country, partly due to its failure to meet certain requirements. 

 "Now the market hopes that the IMF visit would lead to the disbursement of its loans for the sake of other creditors' confidence in Indonesia. The country's public-debt profile is in virtual default," said a dealer at a European bank in Singapore. Meanwhile, Bank Indonesia kept its indicative intervention rates in the rupiah interbank money market unchanged at 12.625 percent for the overnight rate and 13.375 percent for the seven-day rate. The intervention rates are among the central bank's tools to influence liquidity in the market. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was stuck in a tight range just beyond the 50 mark, with regional weakness keeping the dollar well bid while a lack of corporate dollar demand capped the downside. 

 Dealers in Manila said with a holiday in Bangkok and lack of a clear signal from the yen, most corporates preferred to stay on the sidelines. 

 Meanwhile, the central bank said key policy rates were likely to stay unchanged until the release of inflation data on May 5 and the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting on May 15. 

 The bank's overnight borrowing rate is currently at 10.0 percent while the overnight lending rate is at 12.25 percent. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht came off its lows in late trade after being wedged in a tight range for the whole session as the onshore market was closed for the four-day Songkran holiday. Trading will resume on Tuesday. 

 The dollar retained its bid tone, although market participants were reluctant to push or mark it up too high against the baht, fearing the central bank's latest disclosure requirements would further dent dollar demand. 

 The central bank has said that from May 1, banks will have to provide details on foreign debt exposure and repayment obligations when their clients buy dollars from them. 

 The one-month offshore forward rate was quoted at 10/15 satang per dollar while the onshore rate was quoted at -9.9/-9.0 satang. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won held off its lows as fears of central bank support and possible equity-linked fund inflows limited the downside, but the soft yen left players keen to buy the dollar on dips. 

 Foreign investors remained net buyers of Korean shares on Monday, picking up a net 1.3 billion won worth, but their purchases were well below Friday's 69.1 billion won as the Easter holiday and expectations of a softer Nasdaq dampened interest. 

 Dealers said there was no sign of direct or indirect central bank intervention on Monday, but the market remained on guard after the authorities' recent aggressive efforts to curb the won's fall. 

 Data released on Monday showed forex reserves fell to $93.64 billion on April 15 from $94.44 billion at end-March, partly due to a $300 million repayment to the IMF. 

 But the central bank declined comment on whether the drop in reserves was also due to recent intervention, which dealers estimate at around $700-$800 billion. 

 On the economic front, the seasonally adjusted jobless rate held steady at 4.2 percent in March and analysts said it could stay above four percent for the year as the economy slows and corporate restructuring continues. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was overshadowed by lingering pessimism over the yen and expectations of poor trade data, due on Tuesday. 

 Analyst forecasts for the March data ranged from marginal gains to a contraction, with a Reuters poll producing an average forecast of a 2.87 percent on-year drop in non-oil domestic exports after February's nominal 5.4 percent rise. 

 Dealers said overall the market still favoured the U.S. dollar, but it was wary of central bank intervention after the central bank said earlier this month it was sticking to a tightening bias. 

 The impact of $5.8 billion DBS-Dao Heng acquisition deal ran out of steam as the market awaited further developments. One dealer said DBS had bought dollars actively in the past few weeks, indicating it might have already covered most of the cash required for the planned takeover. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar nudged lower in line with the yen and won but dealers in Singapore said fears of the central bank, which was believed to be active in early trade kept the currency in its recent tight range. 

 They said the central bank intervention at around 32.95 was not aggressive but was enough to signal its intention. 

 A dealer at a European bank in Singapore said the Taiwan dollar was unlikely to break the 32.88-32.98 range in the near term unless the yen made a major move. 

 A lower finish on the local stock market and last week's downgrade of the trade outlook kept sentiment depressed.

title: Emerging  FX  - Lifted by firmer yen before holiday.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 12 (Reuters) - The firmer yen bumped Asian currencier higher in light trade late Thursday ahead of the Easter break. 

 This report will not appear on Friday, April 13, due to the Easter holiday in most of Asia and the Songkran holiday in Thailand. Please see and for reports on the Korean won and Taiwan dollar. 

 The yen extended its recent gains, taking advantage of speculation over U.S. Treasury Secretary Paul O'Neill's commitment to the strong dollar policy. Those gains lent particular support to the North Asian currencies. 

 The dollar was earlier upset by media reports the U.S. National Association for Manufacturers will meet with O'Neill later this month to complain about the strong dollar. 

 In the meantime, the euro edged slightly higher. 

 However, analysts said the outlook for the yen and regional currencies was still cloudy at best, given slowing external demand and the limping tech sector. 

 On the domestic front, Korea's finance ministry said earlier it would expand its foreign exchange reserves and use dollar/won forwards to stabilise the forex market. 

 And the Bank of Thailand said it was content with the current level of the baht. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won extended its gains alongside the yen, with wariness over possible central bank intervention also helping. 

 Dealers in Singapore said stop-loss dollar sales were triggered around 1,330 and 1,322. "The market was quite long on dollar anyway. So the yen and the concerns over the central bank are good reasons to bail out of these positions," said a dealer at a European bank in Singapore. 

 Korean authorities continued to harden their line towards the foreign exchange market. The Finance Ministry said it would push local banks to repay borrowings owed to the central bank in order to boost reserves. 

 It did not elaborate how it intended to use dollar/won forwards to stabilise the forex market, nor whether that included the offshore non-deliverable forward market. 

 But dealers said the market largely ignored the rhetoric, given the lack of detail. A currency analyst also said the onshore forward market was relatively small. 

 Separately, Finance Minister Jin Nyum said the government would not step into the market to support the won unless it saw panic or speculation, adding however that it would coordinate any action with the central bank. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht traded in a tight range with low volumes for most of the day as players avoided taking aggressive positions ahead of a long weekend. 

 Financial markets in Bangkok will be closed from April 13-16 to celebrate the Songkran festival that marks the Thai New Year. They will reopen on Tuesday. 

 Dealers in Bangkok said a firmer yen and fear of central bank intervention kept most players from taking long dollar positions. 

 But analysts said poor fundamentals and continuing equity outflows suggested the baht will weaken in the medium term. 

 The Bank of Thailand's assistant governor Chetthavee Charoenpitaks said the central bank was satisfied with the current level and stability of the baht, which he attributed to stability in the yen. 

 He declined to respond when asked whether a recent strengthening of the baht was due to central bank intervention. 

SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar extended gains to above 1.8030 with trading volume picking up in the afternoon after U.S. names sold dollar/Sing as the yen probed two-week highs. 

 Dealers said investment banks and local banks were keen to buy the dollar at 1.8025-30, with others squaring their positions ahead of the long weekend. 

 The market will now focus on the release of non-oil domestic exports on Tuesday, with a poor figure expected to hound the Sing dollar to decade troughs of 1.8235 hit on April 2. 

 But analysts said despite no improvement in the grim economic outlook, fears of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore would support the downside at 1.8180 for now. 

 In February, non-oil domestic exports rose a worse-than-expected 5.4 percent on year from nine percent in January. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was a shade higher from late Wednesday levels after touching a low of 50.15 in light and sporadic offshore trade. 

 Markets in Manila were closed for the Easter break and will reopen on Monday. 

 Dealers in Singapore said only a few banks were squaring their positions before the Easter holidays and given low volumes, the moves were exaggerated. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar rode the yen's coat-tails, poking above 32.90 as players trimmed long dollar positions after the yen probed two-week highs against the dollar and the euro. 

 Dealers said they had not heard of any central bank intervention in the Taiwan market on Thursday. 

 Recent gains in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index , which is taken as a strong barometer for the island's exports, also boosted sentiment, they said. 

 Foreign fund buying of local stocks also underpinned the currency. On Wednesday, they bought shares worth a net T$1.961 billion, ending an eight-session net selling streak of T$21.751. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah came off an intraday high of 10,380 due to dollar demand from a multi-national company and state banks in a thin pre-holiday market. 

 But its downside was underpinned by hopes the IMF team's visit to Jakarta would lead to the disbursement of a $400 million loan delayed since last year. 

 "We do not think this visit will result in an LOI (letter of intent), but are encouraged that the likelihood of one is increasing," said an IDEAglobal report. 

 "However, the overall picture still remains tenous...IMF is also concerned about budget deficit and says market may not have priced in possibility of deficit running out of control," it said. 

 The rupiah's steadier tone has eased pressure on the central bank to directly or indirectly prop up the local currency. 

 Bank Indonesia on Thursday kept its intervention rates in the rupiah interbank money market unchanged. The intervention rates are among the central bank's tools to manage liquidity.

title: Emerging  FX  - Climb with yen's help,c.bank worries.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 11 (Reuters) - Asian currencies eked out gains early Wednesday, buoyed by the steady yen and persistent worries over central bank intervention. 

 The yen held onto recent mild gains, thanks to the lingering effects of Finance Minister Kiichi Miyazawa's cautionary remarks on Tuesday. 

 But the euro was the biggest loser, with concerns the European Central Bank may hold rates dragging it down. Dealers said losses in euro/yen were weighing on the dollar/yen as well. 

 Korean foreign exchange authorities were spotted selling dollars in the market on Tuesday, keeping up recent direct intervention. In contrast, Taiwan's central bank capped their currency's gains on Tuesday while Thai and Singapore authorities were largely absent. 

 But with players still on the look-out for possible intervention, the market was happy to carry on unwinding dollar longs. Wall Street's overnight gains were also lifting the mood on local bourses, with the improved spirits spilling into the foreign exchange markets. 

 However, analysts pointed out Tuesday's downgrade of Singapore's 2001 growth forecast and Taiwan's 2001 export growth forecast indicated tough times ahead for regional currencies as Asia feels the impact of the U.S. slowdown. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar bounced more than a cent to 1.8060 from Tuesday lows of 1.8200, after fears of intervention encouraged profit-taking on long dollar positions. 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore said on Tuesday it was keeping its policy bias towards a gradual appreciation of the local dollar and was ready to intervene to keep it within its policy band. 

 Players, who had speculated the MAS might have shifted its bias to neutral, were unwinding dollar longs, but were looking to buy on dips to 1.8020-30, dealers said. 

 "I don't think there is significant change in sentiment. It's a good chance to buy cheap dollars," a European bank dealer said. 

 But the Sing might reverse course if Hong Kong's Dao Heng Bank confirms talk Singapore's DBS Group is set to make a bid for it in a deal valued up to $5.78 billion. 

 A spokeswoman for Dao Heng said it will likely make an announcement later in the day. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht chalked up modest gains to 45.37 from Tuesday's low of 45.71, thanks to offshore banks unwinding long dollar positions as the yen and the Sing firmed. 

 But dealers said they were seeking to buy dollar on dips to around 45.30 given weak economic fundamentals and potential political risks. 

 Lawyers for Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra denied on Tuesday accusations he hide assets and argued his wife was responsible for handling his business affairs. 

 Thailand's Constitutional Court heard its third day of evidence on Tuesday to decide whether to uphold a ruling Thaksin filed false asset returns when he was a minister in the 1990s. 

 If the court confirms the ruling, Thaksin faces a five-year ban from politics. 

 Baht funding costs offshore were vitrually flat, with the one-month rate at 17/25 satang per dollar from 17/45 Tuesday. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won edged higher on the back of gains in U.S. equities and a firmer yen. 

 The KOSPI rose over 2 percent at the open, helped by the Nasdaq's 6 percent rise and a 9.45 percent gain in the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's semiconductor sub-index 

 Dealers in Singapore said given recent intervention by the authorities, players were avoiding long dollar positions for now. 

 But analysts said with doubts still hanging over the yen's outlook and prospects of a turnaround in electronics sector demand, the dollar was likely to maintain its safe haven status. 

 "With global economic prospects deteriorating and importers remaining unhedged any dips in the dollar are likely to be only temporary," said Mansoor Mohi-uddin, currency strategist at UBS Warburg, maintaining a dollar/won near-term target of 1,400. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar nudged up further, taking heart from the firmer yen and won as well as gains on Wall Street. 

 But dealers in Singapore said the central bank was likely to cap any sharp rise in the local dollar. 

 Tuesday's trade data suggested Taiwan's economy was slowing in line with the U.S. and because of weak domestic demand. 

 The Ministry of Finance said on Tuesday exports in March fell 1.8 percent on-year, while imports were down 13.1 percent, leading to a slash of 2001 export growth forecast to just 0.5 percent, against an earlier forecast of 4.21 percent. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah clamoured higher with local corporate dollar demand falling quiet as an IMF team began its review of Jakarta's progress in economic reforms. 

 Dealers said the market was likely to be thin with players riveted on the 12-14 day review conducted by the IMF team. 

 The Fund said late Tuesday in Washington the long-awaited mission would have to assess some outstanding issues before a delayed $400 million loan could be approved. 

 Approval of the loan and a new letter of intent with the IMF are key to triggering a $5.8 billion debt rescheduling with the Paris Club of official creditors. 

 Among the issues that have yet to be resolved between the Fund and Jakarta is the controversial plan to change central bank law. Indonesian leaders have been elusive as to whether they will stick to the plan, which the IMF fears may compromise the central bank's short-lived independence. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was gained some ground on the back of firmer regional currencies and dollar remittances from overseas workers ahead of the Easter break. 

 Manila's forex market will close at noon on Wednesday and will re-open on Monday. 

 An IMF official said late Tuesday the Philippines would likely see its economy grow by around three percent this year. 

 Markus Rodlauer, who is leading an IMF mission currently in Manila, added that the Fund generally agreed with the government's economic targets, stressing the particular importance of meeting the deficit target.

title: Emerging  FX -Clouded by easier yen, bleak outlook.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 10 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were stuck within recent weak ranges early Tuesday as the dollar made gains against other major currencies overnight. 

 Fear of central bank intervention was likely to keep players on their toes, though a weaker yen and increasing evidence of slowing growth would leave demand for the dollar intact on dips, analysts said. 

 A steadier yen combined with verbal and actual intervention by Asian central banks in the past few sessions has kept most currencies off their recent lows. 

 However, some of the regionals have sustained more damage on conflicting comments by officials and politicians. 

 Analysts said with key U.S. economic data including retail sales and the producer price index for March expected later in the week, markets might adopt a cautious approach. 

 In early Asian trade, the yen was struggling the wrong side of 125 as fresh economic data confirmed the market's negative view on the prospects for the Japanese economy. 

 The Bank of Japan said on Monday the March domestic wholesale price index dropped 0.5 percent from last year, the steepest fall in two years. 

 The euro was also under pressure ahead of the European Central Bank policy-setting meeting on Wednesday. Most analysts expect at least a 25-basis point cut in the bank's 4.75 percent benchmark rate. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was steady in early trade on wariness about central bank intervention and dealers in Singapore expected authorities to keep it within a 1,340-1,345 range. 

 The Bank of Korea sold an estimated $200 million on Monday after a sale of upto $500 million on Friday following weeks of verbal threats on the won's declines in line with the weak yen. 

 But dealers said the central bank was more worried on the yen/won cross rate and some believed the interventions were intended to keep the cross rate at around 10.60. 

 "The central bank has become more aggressive after the cross rate went as high as 11 last Thursday," a dealer at a European bank in Hong Kong said. Yen/won was last quoted at 10.69/74. 

 Korea competes with Japan in a number of export markets. 

 The won's declines against the dollar, however, have inflated import prices that rose 0.8 percent in March from the previous month. Export prices rose 1.8 percent in March. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was clinging to 10,800 as the market waited for an IMF team to begin reviewing Jakarta's economic reforms on Wednesday, a crucial step towards a new letter of intent, which would secure the release of a delayed $400 million loan. 

 The letter would also trigger a $5.8 billion debt rescheduling deal with the Paris Club of official creditors. 

 But analysts have cautioned against high expectations as the IMF and Jakarta may still have differences over controversial proposals to change central bank law. 

 A senior economics official said on Monday the goverment agreed in principle with an independent panel's review of the central bank reforms. He did not elaborate. 

 Last week, Attorney General Marzuki Darusman said the government would stand by its insistence that the entire central bank board resign when the changes took effect. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was expected to come under pressure with local importers seeking dollars ahead of the Easter break. 

 Markets in Manila were closed on Monday for the Valour Day holiday and will be closed again on Thursday and Friday for Easter. 

 Given the dearth of fresh domestic factors, the peso has been tracking other regional currencies, which have been hobbled by the U.S. slowdown and softer yen. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar crept down to touch the 1.82 mark in early trading, putting it perilously close to decade lows of 1.8235 hit last week. 

 The latest upset was caused by a worse-than-expected growth figure for the first quarter and a bigger-than-expected cut in Singapore's 2001 growth forecast. 

 The government said the economy grew just 4.6 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 2001, due to a significant slowdown in the manufacturing sector. A Reuters poll of 10 economists had predicted 5.9 percent growth. 

 It also cut the growth forecast for 2001 to 3.5 to 5.5 percent from five to seven percent. 

 Some dealers said the market was caught short of U.S. dollars and players were scrambling to cover their positions. 

 But they saw no sizeable orders related to news Singapore's DBS Group was set to make a bid for Dao Heng Bank in a deal valued at up to $5.78 billion. Analysts emphasised that bears were merely using the news as an excuse to further bid up dollar/Sing. 

 "While DBS are likely to have already covered their currency exposure, the news added to the constant flow of Singaporean corporates looking to acquire overseas investment," said UBS Warburg currency strategist Mansoor Mohi-uddin said in a report. 

 THAI BAHT The baht was riveted to a tight 45.65-45.75 range in early morning trading after rumours of central bank intervention and hefty profit-taking on U.S. dollar longs pushed it off 37-month lows of 45.85 on Monday. 

 But Bangkok dealers said local banks were keen to buy the U.S. dollar on dips at 45.50-55. 

 Baht funding costs in the offshore market were a tad firmer, with the one-month forward rate at 37/47 satang per dollar from 30/60 late on Monday. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was edging closer to the support level of 33.00, which dealers expected it to breach due to the weaker yen and expectations of poor trade data, to be released at 0245 GMT. 

 Some analysts expected March trade data to show negative year-on-year export growth. The island recorded a trade surplus of $1.059 billion in February. 

 A comment by central bank governor Perng Fai-nan that the exchange rate needed to be flexible and reflect changes in the global financial environment was likely to keep the currency on the defensive, dealers said. 

 They said players were still looking to buy the U.S. dollar on dips to 32.90, with stops placed at 32.85.

title: Emerging  FX  - Firmer as central banks lurk.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 10 (Reuters) - Asian currencies clawed towards the stronger end of their recent ranges late Tuesday as the market kept a wary eye on central banks. 

 The Singapore dollar, Thai baht, and Korean won staved off further losses as fears of intervention ruled the market. 

 Dealers said Thai and Korean authorities had again intervened in defence of their currencies, continuing a recent trend, while the Monetary Authority of Singapore reaffirmed its current monetary policy bias towards tightening. 

 The yen's mild rebound following cautionary remarks from a Finance Minister Kiichi Miyazawa also helped the regionals keep their footing. 

 But they were unable to muster enough strength to break past key resistance levels, with the yen still looking fragile over the longer term. 

 Adding more woe to the regional outlook, Singapore, one of Asia's sounder economies, turned in a weaker than expected first quarter performance, with growth of 4.6 percent on year against expectations of 5.9 percent. 

 The city-state also revised downwards its 2001 growth forecast to 3.5-5.5 percent from 5-7 percent due to the slowdown in the U.S. and global electronics sector. 

 Taiwan's economy also showed more symptoms of a slowdown with March exports falling 1.8 percent on year and imports down a substantial 13.1 percent. The Ministry of Finance cut its 2001 export growth forecast from 4.21 percent, adding import growth "should be negative." 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won reclaimed ground in late trade, helped by Korean authorities who were spotted selling dollars around 1,336 won. 

 The government has been intervening directly in the market in recent sessions to push the dollar/won lower after several weeks of verbal intervention. 

 Given the intervention and the accompanying reluctance to hold dollar longs, analysts said dollar/won may retrace to 1,330. 

 The dollar/won's daily chart showed it was still within an uptrend channel that started on February 21, with support around the 1,330 level. 

 Dealers in Singapore said there was some genuine demand for dollars from Korean importers and offshore parties that capped the won's gains. 

 They added that trade had thinned out due to wariness over increased government activity and the rangebound dollar/yen. 

 "These levels are really hard to play because you're not quite sure whether the market is waiting for another big move in dollar/yen or for a big correction (in dollar/won)," a dealer at a European bank said. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar edged up to 1.8132 in afternoon trading, after hovering at 1.8140-60 from earlier lows of 1.8200. 

 Sporadic U.S. dollar bids from foreign and local banks ran into fears of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore especially after it reaffirmed its tightening bias. 

 The MAS also said it stood ready to intervene if necessary to keep the Sing dollar within its policy band. 

 The MAS's comment came after the government announced a lower-than-expected growth figure for the first quarter and a bigger-than-expected cut in Singapore's 2001 growth forecast. Yet dealers expected the Sing dollar to soon revisit 1.8180 and 1.8200 lows on the back of burgeoning M&A activities which point to capital flows out of Singapore. But they saw no big orders related to talk DBS Group was making a bid for Dao Heng Bank in a deal valued at up to $5.78 billion. 

 "The talk is still very much up in the air and we haven't heard of any confirmation. On top of that, DBS is a bank. I think they are clever enough to hedge their currency exposure," a currency strategist said. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah edged higher from its session low of 10,875 as a lack of local corporate demand for dollars prompted banks to trim their dollar longs. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said corporates were reluctant to bid dollars above 10,800 ahead of the start of an IMF review of Indonesia's performance on economic reforms on Wednesday. 

 The review is seen as a step towards resumption of IMF lending, stalled since December after the Fund said Jakarta failed to meet certain programme targets. 

 However, the rupiah's rise was capped at around 10,740 where some local banks were seen buying dollars. 

 Dealers said state banks were spotted selling dollars in early trade but given the small amount sold, most dealers suspected they were not acting on behalf of the central bank. 

 The Finance Minister said he saw no significant problems affecting the IMF review as all the key requirements demanded by the IMF had been met. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso firmed off a session low of 50.25 on inflows of overseas workers' remittances, bunched up with only two working days in the week. 

 Philippine markets were closed on Monday and will go on Easter break from Thursday. Trading will resume on Monday. 

 Dealers in Manila said the dollar inflows mostly coming from local banks prompted others to trim their dollar longs and sent importers to the sidelines. 

 As expected, the central bank left key interest rates steady at its weekly policy meeting. The overnight borrowing rate stands at 10.0 percent and the lending rate at 12.25 percent. 

 Governor Rafael Buenaventura said the bank was not in the market to support the peso and attributed its recent weakness to regional declines and not to its easing policy. 

 A government source said the first quarter deficit was likely to come at around 37.054 billion pesos, below previous estimates of 48.552 billion. The Philippines has a 2001 budget deficit target of 145 billion pesos, against last year's 136.11 billion. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht traded in a narrow range in the afternoon following rumours the central bank might have intervened in the offshore spot and forward markets through a U.S. name. 

 Fears of intervention upstaged negative local factors. 

 Consumer confidence in the Thai economy fell for the second straight month in March from the previous month, according to a survey by the University of Thai Chamber of Commerce. 

 The commerce ministry also cut its 2001 export growth target to 9.45 percent year-on-year from 11.30 percent earlier and an actual 19.5 percent rise in 2000. 

 Baht funding costs offshore eased, with the one-month forward rate at 17/45 satang per dollar against 37/47 in the morning. TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar firmed slightly as most players opted for the sidelines. 

 With the yen holding above 125 and dollar selling in other Asian non-deliverable forwards, dealers said there were few incentives for the market to take on dollar longs. 

 However, further evidence of Taiwan's slowing economy kept a lid on the local dollar's upside. 

 The finance ministry slashed its 2001 export growth forecast to 0.5 percent from 4.21 percent after the release of data showing a 1.8 percent on year fall in exports in March. Imports fell 13.1 percent on year in March.

title: Singapore 's MAS: Ready To  Intervene  To Keep SGD In Band
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The Monetary Authority of Singapore said Tuesday it has not changed its policy of allowing a gradual, modest appreciation of the trade-weighted Singapore dollar within a policy band, as stated in its monetary policy Statement of Feb. 2001. 

 "Although the trade-weighted Singapore dollar has weakened since then, it has remained within the policy band. MAS stands ready to intervene if necessary to keep it within the band," central bank said. 

 "The recent weakness of the Singapore dollar, especially against the U.S. dollar, has prompted speculation that MAS has shifted its policy stance on the exchange rate. This is not so," it added. 

 Following is the full text of MAS' statement: 

 The downward revision in GDP growth forecast for 2001 from 5%-7% to 3.5%-5.5% reflects the deteriorating outlook for the external environment. The downturns in the U.S. economy and in the global electronics industry have been deeper than expected. Our less optimistic assessment of Singapore's prospects therefore reflects a cyclical fall in external demand, rather than deterioration in our export competitiveness. 

 The recent weakness of the Singapore dollar, especially against the U.S. dollar, has prompted speculation that MAS has shifted its policy stance on the exchange rate. This is not so. 

 MAS manages the Singapore dollar exchange rate against a trade-weighted basket of currencies, and not against any single currency. MAS has not changed its policy of allowing a gradual, modest appreciation of the trade-weighted Singapore dollar within a policy band, as stated in the MAS Monetary Policy Statement of Feb. 2001. Although the trade-weighted Singapore dollar has weakened since then, it has remained within the policy band. MAS stands ready to intervene if necessary to keep it within the band. 

 MAS will review its policy stance in July, and will be making a statement on monetary policy then.

title: Emerging  FX -Rangebound on yen,  intervention  fears.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 9 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were rangebound, not far from their recent lows on Monday, in the face of intervention threats and uncertainty about the near-term direction of the yen . 

 More warnings from Japanese officials against excessive exchange rate weakness kept the yen supported the firm side of 125 to the dollar for most of the day, making players wary of pushing the regionals lower. 

 But most analysts expected the dollar to move ahead again on continued safe haven flows after a brief period of consolidation. 

 "The dollar is basically in a consolidation phase and there is some uncertainty on how long it will remain in this phase. So for the time being there is some respite for other currencies," a chief dealer of a European bank said. 

 The rest of the region was also rife with talk of central bank intervention as finance officials and politicians kept up their verbal routine. 

 Korean foreign exchange authorities were spotted selling dollars via onshore banks at around 1,343.00, continuing last week's aggressive intervention. 

 However, comments by Thai officials worked the other way, taking the baht to a new 37-month low. 

 The euro managed to hold its day highs around $0.9040 amid concerns over the U.S. economy after March payrolls data released on Friday showed the steepest monthly fall in ten years. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht perked up after rumours swirled in the market that the central bank stepped in to prop up the currency at 45.80-45.85. 

 The central bank said earlier it was monitoring the baht closely, but reiterated the baht weakness was caused by the soft yen and other external factors. 

 Dealers said the baht fell to intraday lows of 45.85 partly due to a remark by Commerce Minister Adisai Bodharamik that a weak baht was helping exports. 

 "The market's interpretation of it was the government was willing to tolerate a weaker baht," said a Singapore dealer. 

 Meanwhile, Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said Thailand had no plan to impose monetary controls to stem losses in the baht which hit fresh 37-month lows on Monday. 

 The one-month forward rate in the offshore market eased slightly to 30/60 satang per dollar from around 40/50 satang in the morning. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won moved within a tight range, helped by a steadier yen and on dollar selling intervention by the Bank of Korea. 

 Dealers in Seoul said the central bank sold an estimated $200 million via onshore banks at 1,342.0 won in the morning and 1,343.0 in the afternoon. 

 But they scoffed at Monday's operation, which came on the back of an aggressive $400-$500 million intervention last week. 

 However, a bearish outlook for the region reinforced by weak U.S. March payrolls data and the KOSPI's fall following the Nasdaq's losses on Friday, kept sentiment depressed. 

 Analysts said the market would keep an eye on more data from the U.S. including retail sales and the producer price index for March due later in the week. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar remained under selling pressure due to the regional trend and talk of a major local bank planning to buy a bank in Hong Kong. 

 Dealers said players had bid up the dollar on reports that DBS Group , Southeast Asia's largest bank, was set to make a bid of up to HK$45 billion ($5.78 billion) for Hong Kong's Dao Heng Bank . 

 Otherwise, the market was awaiting flash data on January-March growth and the government's revised 2001 growth forecast to be released on Tuesday. Economists polled by Reuters expected the economy to grow 5.9 percent in the first quarter. 

 "The official 2001 economic growth forecast - currently at 5-7 percent - is expected to be revised downwards," said a DBS report. 

 "However, this should not have any material impact on the forex and equity markets which have largely priced in the slower growth," it said. 

 The Reuters poll produced an average forecast of 4.6 percent growth in 2001. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was wedged in a narrow range, with foreign banks trimming long dollar positions and state banks buying the dollar, dealers said. 

 One Jakarta dealer said Bank Indonesia, the country's central bank, was heard entering the market to sell a small amount of dollar at 10,850. 

 The market expected a long-awaited visit by the IMF to Indonesia this week would give the ailing rupiah some reprieve. 

 The visit should pave the way for disbursement of a $400 million loan delayed by the IMF since late last year and trigger a $5.8 billion debt rescheduling deal with the Paris Club of official creditors. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was trapped within a tight range on U.S. dollar selling by players wary of central bank intervention. 

 Dealers in Hong Kong said exporters sold U.S. dollars as the Taiwan dollar eased towards its session low of 32.95 fearing the central bank may not allow the currency to test the 33 level. 

 On Friday, the central bank capped the Taiwan dollar's gains at 32.90, leaving it confined to a narrow range. 

Central bank governor Perng Fai-nan said on Monday the Taiwan dollar rate should reflect changes in the international financial environment. 

 Dealers said sentiment was weighed by a fall in the TAIEX and the continued deadlock between China and the U.S. over a spy plane and its crew detained by Beijing. 

 The market will be watching for March trade balance data due on Tuesday. A Reuters poll showed an average of $759 million surplus expected for March, compared with a surplus of $1.059 billion in February. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was steady with only a few small offshore deals reported as markets in Manila were closed for the Valour Day holiday. Trade will resume on Tuesday. 

 Dealers in Singapore said a weak outlook for the yen and other regional currencies would continue to keep the peso pressured as exporters and overseas workers held back dollars. 

 Importers would also be seeking U.S. dollars because of a shorter week with Philippine markets again closed on Thursday and Friday for the Easter break.
