title: S.E Asian  currencies  still on slippery ground.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 23 (Reuter) - Southeast Asian currencies remained on slippery ground on Wednesday after coming under renewed pressure as the Thai baht slid to new lows. 

 Poor market liquidity and wide spreads added to market volatility as players turned increasingly nervous ahead of an Asian central bankers meeting in Shanghai on Friday. 

 Dealers said expectations the meeting might produce some form of coordinated intervention to counter the speculative onslaught on the region's currencies kept the dollar in demand. 

 "The big issue for the market at the moment is this meeting in Shanghai as there is the possibility of concerted intervention or a statement that they are willing to join hands to support currencies," said Chiang Yao Chye, economist at CIBC Wood Gundy in Singapore. 

 The Thai central bank intervened to stem the baht's slide as it was pulled down by heavy commercial demand for dollars. 

 "We noticed the central bank intervened to stop the baht's fall at around the 32.50/32.60 to the dollar level," a senior dealer at a local bank in Bangkok said. 

 The baht hit a record low at one point with some dealers reporting transactions at as low as 32.60 to the dollar. At 1050 GMT, it was quoted at 32.250/32.550 onshore and 31.500/31.550 offshore. 

 Dealers attributed the sharp plunge in the onshore market mainly to sales by importers seeking dollars to pay their bills and by corporations needing the dollar to repay foreign loans. 

 They said the central bank did not need to sell large amounts of dollars to curb the fall because the pressure was mainly from local players trading in small amounts. 

 A senior Thai central bank official attributed the baht's weak tone to poor first-half earnings reported by local banks and finance companies. 

 The Singapore dollar succumbed to fresh selling after comments by Finance Minister Richard Hu which players treated as yet another signal to buy the U.S. dollar. 

 Hu told parliament Singapore dollar's exchange rate was determined by market forces and its recent appreciation against its neighbours, especially the baht and Indonesian rupiah, did not pose a significant threat to its competitiveness. 

 "Our exchange rate policy should not be guided by short-term expediency considerations. We always focus on managing the exchange rate of the Singapore dollar on a trade-weighted basis with a medium-term perspective," Hu said. 

 The Singapore dollar fell to a low of around 1.4690 to the U.S. dollar after the comments, compared with 1.4645 earlier. 

 The Malaysian ringgit was hit by fresh waves of selling by offshore U.S. banks despite talk that the central bank had intervened to sell dollars around 2.6350/70 ringgit. 

 The ringgit was quoted at 2.6355/85 to the dollar against a morning low of 2.6230. 

 "We are not sure if there is any intervention at all. The said banks could be taking their own positions," a dealer at a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur said. 

 The Indonesian rupiah remained weak after being dragged down by the slump in the baht. Spot rupiah was at 2,587/97 against an opening of 2,570/80. 

 "We saw some central bank intervention at the 2,580 level which helped boost the rupiah to 2,540 level in late morning, but uncertainty in Thailand kept the dollar tone biddish," a U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said. 

 "If the rupiah could break the 2,500 resistance level, then there is potential for a strong comeback. But if it falls below the 2,600 level, speculators would launch an attack to test the band again," a local bank dealer said. 

 The Philippine peso fell on commercial demand for dollars, closing at 28.50 to the dollar against 28.15 previously.

title: Southeast Asian  currencies  fragile despite lull.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 22 (Reuter) - Southeast Asian currencies showed signs of succumbing to renewed pressure in late Tuesday trade after making a brief recovery earlier in the day. 

 Dealers said the dollar's surge to a 71-month high of 1.8071 marks in afternoon trade also weighed on Asian currencies. 

 They said early gains in the Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar were driven by funds cashing in on the dollar's sharp rise, but did not reflect a change in sentiment. 

 "People who were long were just taking profit. I believe this regional currency weakness is not over yet," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore. 

 The market is awaiting the results of an Asian central bankers meeting in Shanghai later this week. 

 "This wave of contagion hitting the regional currencies will be a relatively long running affair," said Desmond Supple, head of Asian currency research at BZW Asia. 

 Supple said the central bankers meeting could yield strong verbal support for the region's currencies, but added that he did not expect it to result in actual coordinated intervention. 

 "There's a broad-based reassessment of risk-reward valuations in the region. Given that genuine funds are leaving as well as speculators, that significantly increases the cost to the real economy of any intervention," he said. 

 The Indonesian rupiah bounced back as offshore players triggered stop-loss dollar sales below the 2,600 level in afternoon trade, dealers said. 

 The rupiah was quoted at about 2,590 to the dollar at 0920 GMT after rising as high as 2,5670 against 2,600 around midday. 

 "We didn't hear of any intervention today. The dollar was trading near the high of the band so people just got cautious," the Singapore dealer said. 

 The Indonesian central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,378/2,682 after the rupiah became the latest victim of a speculative attack on Monday. It plunged about 150 points to a historic 2,665 low against the dollar before staging a marginal recovery on central bank intervention. 

 But dealers said the dollar was likely to encounter strong buying interest on any moves towards the 2,550 level. 

 In Malaysia, the ringgit slipped back a notch to 2.6230 to the dollar against 2.6200 earlier. 

 Dealers said a further drop towards 2.65 was likely despite expectations Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad would intensify his criticism of speculative attacks on the ringgit. 

 News reports quoted Mahathir, due to return to Malaysia on Tuesday after a two-month absence, as saying there may have been a political agenda behind recent attacks on regional currencies. 

 Bank Negara Malaysia said its reserves had fallen to 61.9 billion ringgit as at July 15 against 70.7 billion a fortnight earlier, reflecting its recent efforts to defend the ringgit. 

 The Singapore dollar slipped back beyond the 1.46 level against the U.S. dollar in line with weakness in the ringgit. 

 Dealers said the currency was likely to head for 1.47/1.48 to the U.S. dollar despite positive export data and optimistic comments about the economy from government officials on Monday. 

 "In the short term, this is not so much about Sing dollar weakness as it is U.S. dollar strength," a dealer said. 

 The Thai baht weakened, partly due to rumours that Thai opposition parties were planning to bring a no-confidence motion against the government, dealers said. 

 "It's just natural for the opposition to create trouble with the current financial crisis in Thailand," said one. 

 The Philippine peso ended weaker at 28.15 to the dollar from 28 previously despite central bank sales of about $5.5 million during the day, Manila traders said.

title: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals post further losses.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 18 (Reuter) - Regional currencies racked up further losses in Friday afternoon trade as funds continued to pile into the U.S. dollar in a market rife with rumours. 

 Dealers said liquidity remained very low and spreads wide, exaggerating currency movements. 

 "Liquidity continues to be a problem so it takes just a few (million) dollars and this market can push it around," a treasury manager at a U.S. bank in Singapore said. 

 He said there was talk of Asian central banks gearing up for concerted intervention in the face of heavy speculative attacks on regional currencies since the de facto devaluations of the Thai baht and Philippine peso earlier this month. 

 "There have been all sorts of rumours going through the markets. My own opinion is it could just be people caught short trying to cover back," he added. 

 The U.S. Treasury and the International Monetary Fund are on high alert over financial turmoil in emerging markets worldwide, which has sent stocks and currencies plunging, the Washington Post reported on Friday. 

 The newspaper quoted officials as saying they were worried the turmoil could slow growth in some of the world's most vibrant economies, which have become key markets for U.S. exports. 

 In Malaysia, the ringgit remained weak after sinking to a fresh three-year low of around 2.6080 to the U.S. dollar on selling by offshore funds. 

 It was quoted at 2.6060/90 at 0845 GMT against 2.5970/6000 around noon. 

 Dealers said the apparent absence of Bank Negara Malaysia from the market, despite talk it had checked rates around the 2.6000 level earlier, contributed to the ringgit's slide. 

 Another senior trader at a Singapore-based bank said dollar/ringgit could face some resistance around 2.6120. 

 The ringgit has fallen more than three percent this week partly due to a perceived change in stance by Malaysian authorities towards allowing market forces to determine the exchange rate. 

 The Singapore dollar recovered some equilibrium after sinking to a new 30-month low of around 1.4665 against the U.S. dollar. 

 Speculation that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) had intervened to stem the currency's slide caused players to turn cautious, dealers said. 

 "We heard the MAS were up at the 1.4635 level but there's no confirmation," a dealer said. "Ultimately, I don't believe the MAS is too worried about dollar/Sing at these levels." 

 The Singapore dollar was quoted unchanged from its noon levels of 1.4605/15 at 0845 GMT, against an early high of 1.4550/60. 

 Dealers said the traditionally robust currency was being affected by declines in regional currencies and a perception the MAS would condone some weakness in it. 

 "The MAS will look at it in terms of percentages with the neighbours," a dealer said, referring to the de facto central bank's policy of monitoring the Singapore dollar against a trade weighted basket of currencies. 

 "They would be uncomfortable if all the neighbours weakened and the Sing dollar did not move," he said. 

 The Indonesian rupiah fell to a new low of 2,502 to the dollar on spillover weakness. 

 The currency had earlier recovered briefly after falling to a low of 2,497 as offshore players sold it during the Jakarta lunch break. 

 Indonesian President Suharto was quoted as saying he had asked the country's top finance officials to monitor the situation and take steps against currency speculation. 

 In Thailand, the baht continued to weaken on commercial dollar demand before a long weekend but its slide was relatively muted, dealers said. 

 The baht was quoted at 30.350/450 to the dollar onshore at 0830 GMT and 30.300/400 offshore. 

 A Singapore-based dealer said dollar/baht was likely to move up slowly towards the 30.50 level, with buying interest expected below 30.00. 

 The market showed little immediate reaction to news that Japan and Thailand had agreed to cooperate to promote stability in currency markets, using measures including intervention.

title: Singapore Dlr/Short-Term -2: Economists Mixed On Direction
text:
However, the unexpected weakness in the local currency in recent days has divided economists on exactly how much weaker the Singapore dollar will get in the medium-term and what sort of recovery it will make by the end of the year. 

 An average forecast based on a poll of 13 economists by Dow Jones indicates the U.S. dollar will have retreated again, to reach S$1.4340 by the end of the year. The forecasts range from S$1.4100 to S$1.4500. 

 'The Singapore dollar can go down quite (a bit) lower ... even lower than S$1.48. This is because of the short term sentiment and it has nothing to do with the fundamentals,' said the chief economist at a Singapore bank. 

 Other differ. 'It's quite unlikely for the (Singapore) dollar to go (lower) to S$1.48,' says J.P. Morgan economist Ong Sin Beng. 'The Singapore dollar is underpinned by strong fundamentals,' he says. 

 'If you look around the region, we're the only country with a strong current account surplus. You don't see that elsewhere,' Ong says. 

 Market analysts agree that one major uncertainty is whether the Monetary Authority of Singapore, the city-state's central bank, will intervene to curb the currency's current weakness.

title: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals weak and weary.
text:
* Malaysian ringgit recovers from 33-month low on talk of Bank Negara intervention overnight. Seen vulnerable to more weakness. 

 * Indonesian rupiah shows muted reaction to comments by central bank governor, firms partly on expectations of tighter liquidity due to tax payments. 

 * Thai baht subdued as market loses interest after confirmed central bank intervention on Monday. 

 * Philippine peso remains under pressure. 

 * Singapore dollar still weak but sluggish. 

 SINGAPORE, July 15 (Reuter) - Southeast Asian currencies continued to be afflicted by poor sentiment on Tuesday as comments from central bankers and government officials sent mixed signals to the market. 

 In Malaysia, the ringgit regained some poise on talk Bank Negara had intervened in offshore markets overnight and possibly early on Tuesday, after the currency slid to a 33-month low of 2.5700 against the U.S. dollar. 

 Dealers said speculative funds sold the ringgit down to its lowest level since October 1994 after Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday the ringgit was still within a "reasonable range". 

 "There's speculation that Negara was in at the 2.5700 top through agents in Sydney time, as well as in London and New York," said a senior dealer at a European bank in Singapore. 

 He said U.S. funds were likely to now push the currency towards 2.6000 to the dollar, although the rise could slow as the market was already long of dollars. 

 Comments by Anwar on Tuesday that Malaysia would allow the exchange rate to be determined by market forces were expected to weigh further on the ringgit, dealers said. 

 "Buying of dollar/ringgit is still very strong. Immediate target is 2.58. If it rebounds from there, it could go back below 2.53," another European bank dealer said. 

 The ringgit was at 2.5565/95 to the dollar at 0350 GMT against 2.5310/30 at its close in Kuala Lumpur on Monday. 

 Indonesian central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono's comments that he saw more scope for interest rate cuts if inflation fell, had a muted effect on the rupiah, dealers said. 

 "The market is moving more in response to the liquidity situation, which is a bit tight because some tax payments are due," a Singapore-based dealer said. 

 "At the moment, the rupiah is the only currency being spared by speculators. But once speculation in the ringgit has subsided, they will look towards the rupiah," he added. 

 He said there was a line-up of corporate orders for the dollar below 2,440 but rumours that state banks were looking to sell aggressively above 2,460 were limiting rupiah weakness. 

 Spot rupiah was at 2,446.0/49.0 at 0350 GMT against an opening 2,450/55. 

 The Thai baht had a subdued morning, largely due to a lack of interest after the Bank of Thailand (BOT) confirmed it had intervened to support the currency on Monday. 

 The BOT said the baht had fallen about 15 percent since it switched to a managed float on July 2 from the previous system of pegging the baht to a basket of currencies. 

 "The speculators got what they wanted with the de facto devaluation. And there are a lot of stale longs in the system putting a cap on the dollar/baht above 30," a Singapore dealer said. 

 But he said the dollar would be bought on any dips as Thailand's financial woes had not ended. 

 The baht was quoted at 29.920/29.970 to the dollar in domestic markets at 0350 GMT and at 29.850/950 offshore.

 He added, however, that the authorities were likely to be comfortable with some weakness in the currency, especially in view of the U.S. dollar's steep climb against the mark in recent days. 

 The Philippine peso recovered some ground but remained weak on the second trading day after its effective devaluation. 

 The peso was quoted at 29.000/30.000 at 0350 GMT against an opening at around 30 to the dollar.

title: Stg/mark easily holds above three marks in Asia.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 14 (Reuter) - Sterling was holding at levels comfortably above three marks in quiet Asian trading on Monday after its surge above the three mark barrier in European trade on Friday, dealers said. 

 At 0400 GMT it was quoted in Asia at 3.0045/55 compared with late London quotes of around 2.9975 marks. Earlier on Monday it hit a high of 3.0090, before drifting back. 

 On Friday, sterling hit a peak of 3.0010 marks in London, its strongest level against the German unit in over 6-1/2 years. 

 Sterling has been bolstered by rising interest rates, a strong economy and its safe haven status amid turmoil generated by approaching European Economic and Monetary Union, set for launch in January, 1999. 

 Base U.K. lending rates were nudged up for the third month running last week to 6.75 percent and analysts say there are more interest rate rises in the pipeline. 

 However, Germany has an economy that is stuttering at best and a much lower interest rate regime, which makes its currency unattractive to foreign exchange market traders. 

 Three month sterling deposits are around seven percent while the same rate for the German mark is about 3-1/16 percent. 

 "Three marks was always the target for sterling and it's made it," said the head of trading at a European bank in Singapore. 

 "I'm not a natural sterling bull at the moment, but I'd hate to be fighting the market on this one," he added. 

 The sterling trader at another European bank in Singapore said his philosophy would remain the same for the pound as when it was approaching three marks. 

 "It worked all the way up from 2.50 marks or so. You just buy on the dips and take profit when it gets ahead of itself," he said. 

 Trading in Asia was not especially active on Monday morning, he said. 

 "There's still a lingering feeling that the Old Lady (the Bank of England) won't exactly be happy to see sterling above three marks -- it's a pretty crucial psychological level," he said. 

 "Certainly there's been no sign of any intervention, but it's definitely a background factor since the market out here is so thin," he added. 

 The head of trading said he expected to see sterling/mark head to around 3.0500/0600 in the near future -- assuming no central bank intervention.

title: Southeast Asian  currencies  under siege.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 14 (Reuter) - Southeast Asian currencies were hit by waves of selling on Monday as uncertainty following the Philippine peso's effective devaluation last week spread like wildfire through the region. 

 In Malaysia, the ringgit fell to a 16-month low of 2.5500 to the dollar in early trade amid Bank Negara Malaysia's failure to intervene aggressively, dealers said. 

 The ringgit was quoted at 2.5375/95 to the dollar at 0400 GMT against 2.5042/52 at its Kuala Lumpur close on Friday. 

 "It's crazy," a European bank dealer in Singapore said. 

 "Because of the story of the Philippine peso, which they devalued last week, the market is expecting the ringgit and rupiah to follow suit," she added. 

 Another European bank dealer in Singapore said Bank Negara was heard to have sold dollars around the 2.5500 ringgit level. "But I think Negara was in just to slow down the fall rather than stop the flow," he said. 

 Dealers said the market was still long of dollars, leaving room for the ringgit to head lower. 

 They said Bank Negara may be allowing market forces to dictate the spot's value rather than defending the ringgit aggressively in the face of heavy selling interest. 

 Dealers estimate the Malaysian central bank spent over $1 billion to support the ringgit last week. 

 In Indonesia, the rupiah rebounded from its early lows as offshore players began unloading dollars. 

 Dealers said offshore players seemed to be trying to cash out from the market after they drove the rupiah to a low of 2,469.0 on Monday morning. 

 "I think some feel that the rupiah is low enough for a buy back, reversing the market trend," a local bank dealer in Jakarta said. 

 But another local bank dealer said the rupiah buying was initiated by some state banks and followed through by offshore players, driving the rupiah to a high of 2,445 before operators bought some dollars back. 

 The rupiah was quoted at 2,453.0/58.0 at 0400 GMT against an opening 2,451.0/55.0. 

 "Bank Indonesia (BI)'s band widening last week is not helping to strengthen the rupiah. With BI having the lowest reserves, the rupiah will be the next currency to attack," a Singapore-based dealer said. 

 The central bank widened its intervention band to 12 percent from eight percent last Friday, in what was seen as a move to pre-empt possible turbulence in the rupiah after speculative attacks on the peso and baht. 

 In the Philippines, the peso fell to a low of 29.75 to the dollar in thin trade as banks remained wary after the central bank's move on Friday to allow the peso-dollar rate to trade within a wider band. 

 Volume was a light nine million dollars after two-and-a-half hours of trading on Monday. 

 The central Bank of Thailand (BOT) intervened to stem the baht's fall in domestic markets, selling dollars at the 30.75-30.80 baht level, dealers said. 

 "The central bank intervened through a small local bank by selling the dollar at around 30.75-30.80," a European bank dealer in Bangkok said. 

 A BOT spokeswoman declined to say whether the central bank had intervened in the market. 

 Commercial dollar demand and lingering jitters from the peso slide pushed the baht to new lows. The currency was quoted at 30.500/30.800 to the dollar in the domestic market at 0400 GMT, after the intervention, against 30.00/30.60 late on Friday. 

 "The amount of intervention was insignificant. But it capped the baht at around 30.80," the dealer said.

title: Singapore dollar surges as funds dump U.S. dollars.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 10 (Reuter) - The Singapore dollar shot up in late afternoon trade on Thursday on stop-loss sales by funds that were long the U.S. dollar, dealers said. 

 "Some stops were triggered below 1.4350. They could be very huge, especially by U.S. funds, which have been very long the U.S. dollar," a European bank dealer said. 

 The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4295/305 to the U.S. unit at 0710 GMT against a morning low of 1.4367. 

 U.S. funds had been building long dollar/Sing positions since last week as anxieties about regional currencies spread following the Thai central bank's shock move to a managed float of the baht. 

 "I think it's a healthy correction. I would buy the (dollar/Sing on) dips to see it back above 1.44," the dealer said, adding that dollar/Sing should remain supported around 1.4290/1.4300. 

 She said the Singapore dollar had been pushed up alongside a sharp rise in the ringgit as Malaysian interbank rates surged due to expectations of a liquidity squeeze. 

 "Dollar/Sing has followed dollar/ringgit for the past few days. I think the Sing is being dragged by the ringgit move," she said, adding that the ringgit was pushed up by a sudden rise in the Kuala Lumpur overnight interbank rate. 

 The ringgit was quoted at 2.4900/05 to the dollar at 0910 GMT after firming to 2.4875 against 2.5005/10 in the morning. 

 The overnight rate rose to a high of 45/50 percent on sudden tightening of liquidity in the banking system as a result of Bank Negara's massive intervention in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday to support the ringgit. 

 Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers said it could mop up anything between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit from the system. 

 Settlement of Tuesday's intervention is on Thursday.

title: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals dampened by dollar bulls.
text:
* Baht eased on strong commercial demand for the dollar 

 * Ringgit pressured but supported by fears of Bank Negara's presence to cap dollar rise at 2.5250 

 * Rupiah softens after government's deregulation package did not contain any band widening 

 * Singapore dollar stays weak on U.S. dollar demand. 

 * Taiwan dollar weak but off lows on central bank intervention

 * Peso takes breather, seen at desired range. No signs of central bank intervention

SINGAPORE, July 8 (Reuter) - Bulls dominated the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, pressuring most Asian currencies and prompting efforts by some central banks to shore their currencies. 

 Almost a week since the Thai government announced a managed float exchange rate system, the baht remained weak against the dollar amid persistent commercial demand for the dollar. 

 Local importers and foreign loan borrowers who needed the the dollar for payment on imported goods and loan repayments were among dollar buyers, dealers said. 

 The baht was trading at 29.130/230 against the greenback compared to 28.90/29.00 on late Monday. 

 The Bank of Thailand set its reference rate at 28.922 to the dollar against 28.578 on Monday. 

 In the offshore market, the baht traded at 28.700/900 against 28.50/80 on Monday. 

 Dollar buying by hedge funds pressured the ringgit but upside on the dollar was capped by fears of Bank Negara's presence at 2.5250 ringgit to the dollar. 

 "There has been a lot of buying of dollar by hedge funds but Negara is waiting at the 2.5250 level. It will be very tight today, maybe 2.5240/50," said a delaer with a Eruopean bank in Singapore. 

 At 0400 GMT, the ringgit was trading at 2.5240/50 to the dollar. 

 Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar. Singapore operators were buying dollars after Indonesia's economic deregulation package did not contain the widely-speculated widening of the dollar-rupiah band, removing some of the arguments for going short in dollars. 

 "There is no fresh factor to trade on. The package contains nothing about the band," the dealer said, adding that players were covering part of their short dollar positions. 

 Spot rupiah was at 2,433.0/33.5 at 0225 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.00/31.75. Tomorrow and today rupiah was at 2,432.75/33.10 and 2,432.25/32.75, respectively. 

 Analysts said sentiment remained positive because the deregulation package could stimulate the stock market which had posted several record highs in the past few days. 

 A dealer in Singapore said overall trading was quiet, with a biddish tone on the dollar against the baht seen causing a slight weakening of the rupiah. 

 "It's a quiet day. In the swap market, rates are trapped in a narrow range because of a two-way market," he said. 

 The Singapore dollar weakened further on continued dollar buying by U.S. funds, dealers said. 

 The local currency briefly tested 1.4385 before firming to 1.4372/82 at 0400 GMT. 

 "It's moving in tandem with dollar/yen," said a dealer with a local bank. He added he did not expect further firmness in dollar/Sing unless dollar/yen rises sharply. 

 Elsewhere, the Taiwan dollar remained weak but recovered from an eight-year low against the greenback after the central bank emerged to fend off speculation. 

 After hitting a low of 27.935 to the dollar, the Taiwan dollar was seen trading at 27.912/915 to the dollar at 0400 GMT. It was expected to range between 27.90-94 on Tuesday. 

 The Philippines peso stablised after recent hectic trade following Thailand's move to a managed float exchange rate system. The peso traded within a tight range of 26.383/385 in the morning. There was no evidence of intervention by the central bank on Tuesday.

title: Singapore dollar slips as speculators move in.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 8 (Reuter) - The Singapore dollar continued to head south against its U.S. counterpart on Tuesday largely on the back of sales by U.S. funds, blamed for the recent sell-off in regional currencies, dealers said. 

 "The funds are trying to attack all the currencies in the region," a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore said. 

 He said the rest of the market was mostly squared up in the Singapore dollar but U.S. funds were still extending their long dollar/Sing positions. 

 The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4386/96 to the U.S. dollar at 0820 GMT against its opening 1.4358. It briefly hit a low of 1.4405 on selling from London-based parties. 

 The domestic currency has been under siege since late last week after Thailand's shock move towards a managed float exchange rate system. 

 Dealers said large U.S. funds, which had bet on a devaluation of the Thai baht, were turning on other Southeast Asian currencies to test how far they could be pushed. 

 "I think dollar/Sing can go to its last high of 1.4500/20," the U.S. bank dealer said. 

 He added that most players were not afraid of intervention by the de facto central bank ahead of that level, unless the Singapore dollar moved sharply. 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) typically intervenes to stem sudden movements in the domestic currency. 

 Jacqueline Ong, economist at research firm I.D.E.A., said the Singapore dollar's traditional "safe haven" status among regional currencies could have undergone a slight shift with Singapore authorities endorsing a more modest appreciation of the unit. 

 "In the past, we've always assumed a strong Sing dollar policy from the government. But recently (Finance Minister) Richard Hu said there's no need for the Sing dollar to appreciate that much if inflation stays under control," Ong said. 

 "To the extent that foreign inflationary pressures become more muted, our exchange rate does not have to appreciate as much as it did before," Hu said in a speech in March. 

 Ong said players were unlikely to go aggressively into the Singapore dollar despite regional uncertainties due to a belief the MAS would intervene to prevent its sharp rise. 

 "Although we're sure now that the local authorities don't want the Sing dollar to be strengthening so fast, they definitely do not want it to weaken to like 1.45 overnight," she said. 

 She said a gradual move in the Singapore dollar towards 1.45 would probably be acceptable to local authorities, as long as the U.S. dollar also strengthened towards 115 yen.

title: Singapore Dollar Falls Vs U.S. Dlr Early On Heavy Selling
text:
SINGAPORE (AP-Dow Jones)--The Singapore dollar is lower against the U.S. currency in early trading Tuesday. 

 The U.S. dollar rose strongly against the Singapore dollar at the start of trading on a combination of U.S. fund buying and interbank technical trading, say bank traders in Singapore. By 0230 GMT (10:30 p.m. EDT), volumes of US$150 million to US$200 million had been traded, traders estimated. 

 Much of the buying interest came from a single U.S. fund which Monday failed to fully fill a large order to buy at S$1.4360 according to one trader at a local bank. 

 The buying pressure pushed the U.S. dollar up to an early high of S$1.4385, leading traders to expect it to test the S$1.4400 level during the day. 

 The U.S. currency encountered selling interest and fell from its high, however, prompting traders to speculate that the Monetary Authority of Singapore, Singapore's de facto central bank, was selling U.S. dollars at the S$1.4385 level to smoothe exchange rate volatility. 

 'This looks like the MAS. They don't like sudden weaknesses, or sudden strengths,' said a trader at a leading Singapore bank. 

 The overall trend remains upward for the U.S. dollar against the Singapore dollar, traders say. The move has developed in part because investors are allocating assets away from South East Asia as a whole, and in part because traders are still concentrating on Singpore's relatively weak May trade figures, which showed a 1% fall in non-oil exports. 

 At 0245 GMT (10:30 p.m. EDT) the U.S. dollar is trading at S$1.4378, up from S$1.4366, its level in late trading Monday. 

 The ringgit is trading at S$0.5695, higher than S$0.5690 late Monday, but capped at S$0.5700 as long as the U.S. dollar is capped at 2.5250 ringgit by likely Bank Negara intervention, say traders.

title: Battered traders still steer clear of Thai baht.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 4 (Reuter) - Trading volume in the baht has been minimal since the Thai government stunned markets on Wednesday by adopting a managed float system that effectively devalued the currency. 

 The move followed weeks of turmoil in Thailand's financial markets, with the baht under attack in May from overseas speculators concerned over the economy, a slump in the stock market and the shaky political backdrop. 

 Since then, coordinated central bank intervention, the imposition of capital controls and a sharp rise in interest rates left many speculators badly burned, and most want to keep a low profile until there is less volatility. 

 "I'm not interested at the moment. I'll want to let it all settle down before I go back in," the head of trading at a European bank said. 

 The baht has stabilised after plunging by nearly 20 percent in offshore markets on news of the managed float. On Friday, the Bank of Thailand allowed its new daily reference rate for the currency to weaken slightly to 28.189 to the dollar from 27.383 on Thursday. 

 In offshore markets, the baht was quoted at around 28.650/28.800 early on Friday. But the European trader noted that dealing spreads were still exceptionally wide with some banks quoting as much as a big figure (one baht) spread. 

 Wide spreads, where the bid and offer rate are far apart, are a sign a dealer does not want to be caught out on either side. 

 "That's a plain signal they're (dealers) not too interested either," he said. "But eventually things will slide back and the market will behave a little more normally. Then I'll have a look." 

 The baht's nemesis came on May 14 when it sank to 26.600 per U.S. dollar from an opening 25.920 as foreign speculators, including hedge funds, moved in for the kill as talk swirled of a possible baht devalution. 

 "At that stage the market was going crazy and the world and his wife seem to want to get involved and go short baht both spot and forward," said one Singapore based trader. "It was seen as a one-way-street." 

 But the authorities returned the market's volley with joint intervention by the Thai and Singapore central banks, and while volume in spot dried up, the forward market was still roaring ahead as a severe shortage of baht saw forward rates romp higher. 

 With the speculators already squeezed, the Bank of Thailand then introduced capital controls which prevented offshore players from raising baht in the spot market to either cover their short positions or take out fresh ones. 

 The two-tier market was then born as offshore traders were starved of liquidity and the dollar/baht rate strengthened dramatically as investors scrambled to cover their shorts. 

 From the 26.600 per dollar level the baht reached at the height of the attack, it subsequently rallied to 22.10 per dollar as demand for baht offshore far outpaced supply. 

 Hungarian financier George Soros, the man who made $1 billion during the 1992 sterling crisis, was rumoured to have taken a $4 billion short baht forward contract, although many traders doubt his position was, or is, that big. Soros himself said "there have been some exaggerated rumours". 

 By then, battered and bloody speculators had either lost a lot of money or were having sleepless nights over short positions they were hanging on to. 

 The dramatic announcement of the managed float on Wednesday this week allowed the baht to sink below the 28.00 per dollar level, which may seem like good news for the offshore punters. 

 But it came too late for many who had lost money by cutting and running after covering their short positions soon after the Bank of Thailand's successful defence of the baht. 

 Traders are still unsure of just how the new currency regime will work and as they lick their wounds, volume is likely to remain extremely light until further details are forthcoming. 

 "I'm fed up with the whole affair. There's very little liquidity and frankly I don't trust a thing that the (Thai) authorities say any more," a trader at a European bank said. 

 He added that the events of the last two days seemed to have mentally drained a lot of dealers. "Everyone's just looking forward to the weekend. It's a real Friday feeling today, especially with the States out for the Fourth of July." 

 "I'm taking a long lunch today."

title: U.S. funds batter Singapore dollar - dealers.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 3 (Reuter) - The Singapore dollar, traditionally a safe haven during Southeast Asian currency volatility, came under attack on Thursday from U.S. funds, dealers said. 

 It continued to slide in late afternoon trading as the U.S. funds tested its "safe-haven" status and interest rates in the city state fell. 

 By 1100 GMT, the Singapore dollar was trading around 1.4343/53 to the dollar compared to about 1.4300 on Wednesday. "The further weakness in the afternoon is basically because the Singapore interest rates came off," a dealer with a local bank told Reuters. 

 Singapore's overnight interbank rate declined to around two percent on Thursday against 2-11/16 percent on Wednesday. 

 Dealers said U.S. funds continued to test how low Singapore's currency could go against the U.S. dollar. 

 Buying from various parties emerged after the Singapore dollar broke 1.4315/20 to the dollar and stop-losses were triggered. 

 "U.S. funds are still buying the dollar against the Sing. At this rate, I think we could see the Sing going to 1.4355 to the dollar soon," said another dealer with a U.S. bank. 

 "People think the Singapore dollar won't be attacked because of its safe-haven reputation. But these U.S. funds are testing this reputation," a dealer with a European bank said. 

 "All the Americans want to do is to test the various stops to see how low the Sing dollar would go. They want to see how the weak shorts will be triggered out," he said. 

 Dealers said the U.S. dollar rose against the local currency after a British party emerged to buy on behalf of some U.S. funds from 1.4310 onwards. 

 "The Americans were buying the dollar against the Sing since late New York last night and they are just continuing to test all the stops," a dealer with a U.S. bank said. 

 He said the first stop at 1.4320 was tested and triggered and now U.S. funds were looking to test the next resistance at 1.4355.

title: Singapore dollar safe-haven status under attack.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 3 (Reuter) - The Singapore dollar, traditionally considered a safe haven during Southeast Asian currency volatility, came under attack on Thursday from U.S. funds, dealers said. 

 "People think the Singapore dollar would not be attacked because of its safe-haven reputation. But these U.S. funds are testing this reputation," a dealer with a European bank told Reuters. 

 "All the Americans want to do is to test the various stops to see how low the Sing dollar would go. They want to see how the weak shorts will be triggered out," he said. 

 At 0429 GMT, the Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4317/27 to the dollar. It had held fairly steady at around 1.43 on Wednesday despite strong pressure on several regional currencies triggered by the de facto devaluation of the Thai baht. 

 Dealers said the greenback rose against the Singapore dollar after a British party emerged to buy on behalf of some U.S. funds from 1.4310 onwards. 

 "The Americans were buying the dollar against the Sing since late New York last night and they are just continuing to test all the stops," a dealer with a U.S. bank said. 

 He said the first stop at 1.4320 was tested and triggered and now U.S. funds were looking to test the next resistance at 1.4330 and 1.4340. 

 Some dealers said the Singapore currency's "safe-haven" reputation was fairly vulnerable this time due to a weak stock market and an economy whose growth had slowed. "Previously, the Singapore dollar, with the strong economy, was seen as a good buy every time something bad happens in the region. It's not so now. I would tend to be neutral on the Singapore dollar," said the dealer with the European bank. 

 Most other regional currencies were battered on Wednesday after Thailand announced a managed float exchange rate system, where the baht value would be determined by market forces. 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), Singapore's de facto central bank, does intervene in the open market but it usually does not comment on its position, said dealers.

title: "Safe-haven" Singapore dollar gains on Baht float.
text:
SINGAPORE, July 2 (Reuter) - The Singapore dollar saw some healthy buying against the U.S. currency on Wednesday thanks to its status as a "safe-haven" currency, dealers said. 

 The move was in contrast to most of the other Southeast Asian regional currencies, which were reeling from Thailand's move to float the baht, they said. 

 Thailand's Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya shocked the Asian currency markets earlier on Wednesday with an announcement that the country's exchange rate would be subject to a managed float, in which the baht's value would be set by market forces with immediate effect. 

 "We saw quite a bit of selling of the dollar against the Sing following news of the Baht float," a dealer with a European bank said. 

 "The Sing dollar is believed to be a safe-haven and whenever there is any uncertainty in the region, it will be the best bet," said a dealer with a U.S. bank. 

 Dealers said activity on the dollar/Sing was "orderly" and not volatile like in some other regional currencies. 

 "The dip in the dollar against the Sing was very fast and it quickly went back up to Tuesday's levels again," another dealer with a U.S. bank said. 

 At 0755 GMT, the Singapore dollar was trading at 1.4296/06 to the dollar after hitting an early low of 1.4285 and a high of 1.4300. It was well-supported at 1.4285/90 to the dollar, dealers said. 

 They said there were no signs of intervention in the open market by Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the de facto central bank.

title: Thailand Baht Stabilizes Offshore After Nearly 14% Plunge
text:
SINGAPORE (AP-Dow Jones)--The Thai baht has stabilized in early afternoon trading in the offshore market after earlier falling by nearly 14% against the U.S. dollar on the news that the Bank of Thailand is abandoning its currency peg in favor of a managed float system. 

 Offshore trading is fitful with bid/offer spreads as wide as 2% to 3%. Onshore trading activity, meanwhile, is completely non-existent, say traders at Thai banks, with spreads up to 10% being quoted. 

 At 0715 GMT (3:15 a.m. EDT) the dollar is quoted at 28.75 baht in the offshore market, relatively little changed from levels around 28.50 baht at 0130 GMT, but 16% above its level in offshore trading late Tuesday. 

 At the same time swap rates in the offshore market are down sharply after traders sought to dump baht and square their positions, a move which allows hedge fund speculators to unwind open long dollar forward positions at a profit, according to traders. 

 One month forwards are quoted at a premium of 40 satang compared to 75 satang Tuesday, while the three month forward premium is at 120 satang down from 225 satang Tuesday. 

 'It will take the market time to adjust to developments. At the moment no one wants to be in the market. Everyone is just waiting for London to come in to see what happens then,' said one regional currencies trader at a Singapore bank. 

 Liquidity in the offshore market is still extremely restricted, however, prompting one senior trader at a Thai bank offshore to forecast that the baht will rally from present levels on scarcity of supply. 

 The prohibition on domestic Thai banks providing baht to foreign participants unless they can demonstrate an underlying business transaction remain in force, despite the jettisoning of the currency peg. 

 The details of how the Bank of Thailand is to implement its new foreign exchange policy are yet to be made fully clear, but the Thai trader expects a 'Singapore-type system.' 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore actively manages the Singapore dollar's level against an undisclosed basket of currencies, intervening to maintain what it sees as acceptable levels. 

 The Thai trader estimates that the Bank of Thailand is targeting a ceiling for the U.S. dollar of between 30 baht and 31 baht. 

 'Any higher than that and the central bank will be intervening in the market,' he said.

title: ASIAN EXOTICS - Tighter liquidity bolsters baht.
text:
* Thai baht strengthens as U.S. dollar weakens and amid tighter liquidity at home. Most dealers still reserving judgement on success of new finance minister 

 * Indonesian rupiah eases slightly but held steady by reports of dollar sell-orders just below current trading range 

 * Malaysian ringgit steady after overnight weakness amid rumours of central bank intervention

 * Singapore dollar gains on U.S. dollar weakness and against ringgit sales 

 SINGAPORE, June 24 (Reuter) - The Thai baht firmed on Tuesday as the U.S. dollar weakened against the other major currencies and amid tighter local liquidity. 

 Dealers said trading activity was thin as most dealers still prefered to stay on the sidelines to see how the new finance minister fared. 

 "People are still waiting to see what will happen next," said one Thai baht dealer in Singapore. "We don't expect a devaluation, but you never know." 

 Thanong Bidaya was appointed finance minister on Friday following the abrupt resignation of Amnuay Viravan after disagreements with political rivals. 

 In the offshore market, the baht was quoted at 24.800/25.100 to the dollar at 0400 GMT, compared with 24.900/25.100 on Monday. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the market remained quiet as most players appeared to square their positions ahead of the month-end. 

 In the domestic market, the baht firmed to 25.850/25.910 early against 25.950/26.050 late on Monday on the U.S. unit's weakness abroad and easing demand for the dollar, dealers said. 

 "Dollar demand eased this morning. But some players still bought the dollar to cover positions ahead of the mid-year period," said one dealer at a European bank. 

 The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.78 per dollar against 25.81 on Monday. 

 The Indonesian rupiah eased against the dollar in slow trading on Tuesday, dealers said. 

 Spot rupiah was last quoted at 2431.00/32.00 at 0320 GMT against an opening of 2429.50/30.50. 

 "The dollar/rupiah appears capped at 2432 now as the market believes there are some heavy sell-orders at that level," said a dealer in Singapore. 

 He said the current bottom for dollar/rupiah was around 2429.50/2430.00. 

 The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,424/2,616 and its conversion band also at 2,424/2,472 on Monday. 

 The Malaysian ringgit fell against the dollar overnight amid rumours of intervention by Bank Negara in London. The ringgit fell again to below 2.5200 in Sydney but quickly recovered. 

 "Dollar/ringgit was pushed up to 2.5215 in Sydney but came back down quickly," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur. "It triggered stop-loss dollar sales around 2.5190/00." 

 By 0400 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5170/80 a dollar. It closed at 2.5150/60 in Kuala Lumpur on Monday. 

 Dealers said fears of central bank intervention again capped the dollar's rise. 

 In Singapore, the local dollar strenghtened through the morning to stand at 1.4267/77 at 0400 GMT after early trade at 1.4280 to the dollar. 

 It also rose against the ringgit, with the Malaysian currency bid at 0.5667 from 0.5673/5 in early trade.

title: Singapore pledges to continue to defend Thai baht.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 19 (Reuter) - Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Thursday Singapore would continue to help Thailand defend its baht against speculators. 

 "We will continue with what we have been doing, which is to collaborate with the Thai central bank, but as you have seen so far the Thai authorities have managed quite a lot," Hu told reporters on the sidelines of a conference on project financing. 

 "I think there is no doubt that the present glitch (in Thailand) is a temporary one," he said following the resignation of Thai counterpart Amnuay Viravan. 

 On May 14, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said it had intervened jointly with the Bank of Thailand in the foreign exchange market to defend the baht against speculators. 

 MAS, effectively Singapore's central bank, rarely admits intervention in the market. 

 MAS deputy managing director Koh Beng Seng told reporters two days after the intervention that the move to defend the baht against speculators was effective. 

 But Amnuay's resignation on Thursday triggered another tumble of the baht in Asia, triggering a wave of hedging against other regionals, dealers said. 

 Some dealers said news that Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee also planned to resign would prompt more selling of baht. 

 The baht was pushed down to 26.300 against the dollar in late morning, but revived to 25.150/659 at midday. 

 Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said a new finance minister would be appointed on Friday but kept financial markets guessing as to who it might be. 

 -- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3080)

title: Singapore Dollar Drifts Higher Late In Light Trading
text:

title: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht firms as BOT widens controls.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 11 (Reuter) - The Thai baht firmed in offshore markets on Wednesday as the dollar hit lows not seen in almost seven months against the yen and the central Bank of Thailand (BOT) tightened its grip on speculators, dealers said. 

 The baht was quoted at 23.850/23.900 to the dollar at 0440 GMT in the offshore market compared with 24.050/24.250 late on Tuesday. It was at 25.720/25.730 in the domestic market against 25.743/25.753 late on Tuesday. 

 The BOT set the mid-rate at 25.71 per dollar versus 25.72 on Tuesday. 

 "The market is still very short of baht so there will be selling interest on any uptick in the dollar/baht," a European bank dealer in Singapore said. 

 She said the central bank's latest move to cut off baht supply to foreigners through the stock market was also causing more selling of dollars for baht. 

 The BOT asked bank custodians on Tuesday not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks sought by foreigners in a move to plug loopholes for foreigners to raise offshore baht. 

 The central bank also said non-resident investors selling Thai stocks must be paid only in foreign currencies and the payment be made promptly to specific investors. 

 Signs that the capital controls imposed by Thai authorities since the baht came under speculative assault in mid-May were going to stay in place for some time yet fuelled jitters in the market, dealers said. 

 Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday that current capital control measures introduced by the authorities to curb speculation in the baht were temporary, but more permanent ones would be announced soon. 

 A senior BOT official told Reuters the central bank was working on measures to institutionalise the current controls to fend off future speculation, but did not provide a time frame. 

 In Indonesia, the rupiah showed a firmer bias amid tight money market liquidity but dealers said activity was confined to a narrow range. 

 "Trading is better than Tuesday but volume remains low. In fact the general view hasn't changed yet, with offshore slightly long in rupiah forwards," a Singapore bank dealer said. 

 Spot rupiah was at 2,427.50/28.00 at 0440 GMT against an opening of 2,428.0/29.0. 

 Dealers said trade was driven by relatively tight liquidity, keeping the dollar under pressure. Overnight money was traded at 13.0/14.0 percent. 

 Dealers were mixed over the impact of the weakening dollar against the yen on dollar/rupiah rates. 

 A U.S. bank dealer said some seemed to attribute the rupiah's strength to the fall in dollar/yen but others were looking at the potential impact on Indonesia's budget, which would be negative if the yen continued to rise. 

 Indonesia has set a dollar/yen exchange rate of 110 for its 1997/98 budget starting April. 

 The dollar slipped to 110.97 yen in early Tokyo trade, its lowest level since November 20, 1996, on concerns about Japan's growing trade surplus. 

 The Malaysian ringgit recovered from its overnight lows as exporters sold the dollar near its highs. 

 "Exporters are selling the dollar around 2.5150 and this is capping the dollar/ringgit's rise," a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur said. 

 Strong dollar buying by two U.S. hedge funds at the 2.5100 level pushed the dollar/ringgit to a high of 2.5160 in thin overseas markets on Tuesday. 

 Dealers said many funds were still short dollars and were looking to cover their positions. 

 Across the border, the Singapore dollar's rise was thwarted by local bank buying of the U.S. dollar, raising fears of central bank intervention. 

 "Dollar/Sing will be under pressure but I think the local banks are around at the 1.4180 level. I would favour selling any rallies to 1.4220/30 or above to see an eventual test of the low end of 1.4100," said a dealer. 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore typically intervenes in forex markets through major local banks to stem sharp rises in the local dollar.

title: Singapore Dollar Flat As Funds Sell, Locals Buy
text:
SINGAPORE (AP-Dow Jones)--The Singapore dollar is unchanged against the U.S. currency in early trading on Wednesday. 

 At 0215 GMT (10:15 p.m. EDT Tuesday) the U.S. dollar is quoted at S$1.4200, unchanged from levels Tuesday afternoon. 

 After dipping to a low of S$1.4193 in late trading, on what one trader at a Singapore bank described as 'massive stop losses going through', the U.S. dollar stabilized in the morning. 

 'The sellers are still out there. Funds are still getting out of their long dollar/Sing positions,' warns a trader at a leading U.S. bank in Singapore. 

 Local corporations are still buyers at levels below S$1.4200, so if that level is breached the U.S. dollar is likely to fall no further than S$1.4180, he said. 

 'We are looking at a very tight range,' he says. 

 Also damping the possibility of further Singapore dollar appreciation are traders' and institutional investors' fears that the Monetary Authority of Singapore will intervene in the market should the U.S. dollar resume its fall. 

 The MAS was widely rumored to have bought U.S. dollars via local banks after the currency's 100 point fall against the Singapore dollar on Monday.

title: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht dips as overseas demand eases.
text:
* Thai baht eases as offshore demand subsides. Some bargain hunting interest in dollar seen at current levels. 

 * Singapore dollar firmer but off its highs on perceived central bank intervention after heavy overnight sales of Malaysian ringgit/Sing dollar cross. 

 * Malaysian ringgit slightly firmer on dollar sales by exporters and corporate interests. 

 * Indonesian rupiah steady as market seeks new leads with liquidity conditions providing sole point of interest. 

 SINGAPORE, June 10 (Reuter) - The Thai baht shed some of its recent strength on Tuesday as demand abated in offshore markets, dealers said. 

 "Dollar selling (for baht) in offshore markets has eased. Some offshore players think it's an opportunity to buy the dollar at the current rate," a foreign bank dealer said. 

 "We may see a base forming for the dollar just below 24.00 baht for now," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said. 

 Bangkok dealers said there was less selling pressure on the dollar in offshore markets as some foreign investors had acquired baht to cover short positions by selling Thai stocks late last week. 

 Thailand's two-tier baht system, imposed around mid-May to cut off baht supply to speculators, was expected to remain in place for a few months. 

 On Tuesday, the central Bank of Thailand (BOT) told  local brokerages informally not to handle big lot stock transactions with foreigners in its latest move to cut offshore players' access to the baht, brokers said. 

 Senior BOT officials were not immediately available for comment. 

 The baht was quoted at 24.200/24.300 to the dollar at 0435 GMT in offshore markets against 24.150/24.250 late on Monday. In the domestic market, the baht was traded at 25.730/25.735 against 25.740/25.750 late on Monday. 

 The BOT lowered the baht/dollar midrate to 25.72 from 25.75 on Monday as the dollar weakened against the major currencies. 

 The Singapore dollar was off its highs, partly due to perceived intervention by the local monetary authority, after the domestic unit shot up against the U.S. dollar on heavy hedge fund sales of the ringgit/Sing cross overnight. 

 "Dollar/Sing traded to as low as 1.4170 last night. But this morning the central bank seems to be around," the U.S. bank dealer said. 

 "Local banks have been bidding aggressively around the 1.4200 level so we should see it remaining supported," he said. 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the de facto central bank, typically intervenes in forex markets through major local banks. 

 Dealers said the ringgit/Sing cross had fallen to an overnight low of 0.5635 as hedge funds, which were long, unloaded their positions. 

 "There was a big sell order on ringgit/Sing in London. When that happened dollar/Sing collapsed and dollar/ringgit shot up," a European bank dealer in Singapore. 

 The cross was quoted at 0.5663/70 at 0435 GMT and was seen trading within a new range of 0.5650-0.5675 for the time being. 

 The Malaysian ringgit firmed slightly against the U.S. dollar but dealers said its gains were limited by selling interest in the ringgit/Sing cross and activity was confined to a narrow range. 

 Another Singapore-based European bank dealer said there were some Malaysian exporters selling dollars at 2.5090 and speculators were picking up dollars around 2.5070. 

 "If the 2.5110 level holds for the next couple of days, then we should see dollar/ringgit moving down," the dealer said. 

 He said the selling of dollar/Sing was mainly by U.S. funds, which had built up positions in anticipation of the New York Commodities Exchange (NYCE) launching futures contracts on Asian currencies against the U.S. dollar. 

 The NYCE said on Monday it was delaying the launch of a Sing dollar futures contract, partly due to expressions of concern from the MAS. 

 "This is causing many to dump dollar/Sing," he said. 

 Futures contracts on the Thai baht, ringgit and Indonesian rupiah are expected to be launched on June 26. 

 Singapore has long restricted internationalisation of its currency and keeps a tight rein on trading of the Singapore dollar. 

 In Indonesia, the rupiah was relatively steady amid a dearth of fresh leads after the country's May 29 general election. 

 A U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said offshore operators were still long on rupiah in the forward market although there were attempts to square positions at any opportunity. 

 She said many operators were also seen trying to establish fresh outright positions, keeping the market in range trading. 

 Spot rupiah was at 2,428.50/29.50 at 0435 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.0/29.5. 

 "Sentiment is mixed. There is no clear trend yet," a Japanese bank dealer said, adding that the market was desperate for fresh news after slowing down sharply in the past few days. 

 Dealers said rupiah liquidity was a bit tight, with overnight money traded at 12.0/13.0 percent, but attention was focused on the liquidity outlook for Friday.
